you are not true renunciants, for you are all categorized within the realm of the asuras. As for the Way of ultimate truth, it is not..."

They seek it through contentious debate, using vigorous and resonant rhetoric to crush the heterodox paths. Yet, as for the successive transmission from Buddha to Buddha, there is no other intent than this.

Even if there are verbal teachings, they fall within the scope of transformative ritual. As for the Three Vehicles and Five Natures, or the causes and effects of humans and devas—these do not apply to the Perfect and Sudden Teaching.
Furthermore, the youth Sudhana never sought out faults; O Great Virtue, do not misapply [the teaching].
The mind is like the great ocean, which does not harbor a corpse; it simply carries it along as it intends to travel across the world. One creates the obstacle of views, which obstructs the mind.
When the sun rises without clouds, it shines brilliantly throughout the heavens; when there is no film before the eyes, there are no flowers in the sky.
"O practitioner of the Way! If you wish to accord with the Dharma, simply do not give rise to doubt. When expanded, it encompasses the entire Dharma-realm;

when withdrawn, not even a single hair's breadth exists. It is vividly and clearly manifest, never lacking anything. The eyes do not see it; the ears do not hear it. What thing would you call it? An ancient said:
'To describe it as a single thing is to miss the mark. You need only look for yourself. What else is there?"
"Ma! Even speaking of it, there is no end. Each of you must exert yourselves.

"No, it would not. "Then please, Master, provide a turning word on my behalf. The Master then asked, "Is this not too much?
Huangbo said, "Why do you not say, 'Come back tomorrow for another meal'? The Master said, "What is the use of saying 'tomorrow'? I will eat right now! Having said this, he gave him a slap.
Huangbo said, "This madman has come here again to pull at the tiger's whiskers. The Master then let out a shout.
[The two masters] went out. Later, Guishan asked Yangshan, "What was the intention of these two venerable elders? Yangshan said, "How about you, Master?
Guishan said, "Only by raising children does one come to know a father's compassion. Yangshan said, "Not so. Guishan said, "And what do you say, child?
Yangshan said, "It is very much like inviting a thief to ruin the family."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk gave a shout; the Master bowed and invited him to sit. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
When the Master saw another monk approaching, he held up his whisk; the monk prostrated, and the Master struck him. Seeing yet another monk approach, he again held up his whisk;
the monk paid no heed, and the Master struck him as well.
One day, while the Master was attending a vegetarian feast at a donor’s house together with Puhua, the Master asked, "A hair swallows the vast ocean;
a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or is it simply the nature of the fundamental substance? Puhua kicked over the rice table. The Master said:
"Too coarse," said Master Linji. Puhua replied, "What kind of place is this that you speak of coarse and fine?
The next day, the Master again went with Puhua to attend a vegetarian feast. He asked, "How does today’s offering compare to yesterday’s? Puhua, as before, kicked over the dining table.
The Master said, "You have succeeded, indeed, but it is too coarse. Puhua said, "Blind fellow! What do you mean by 'Buddha-dharma'?"
"How coarse or fine? The Master then stuck out his tongue.
One day, the Master was sitting with the Elder Mudata of Heyang inside the earthen stove in the monks' hall. Thereupon, he spoke.
Every day, Puhua wandered through the streets acting like a madman. When the Master asked him, "Tell me, are you an ordinary person or a sage?
before he had even finished speaking, Puhua entered. The Master then asked, "Are you an ordinary person or a sage?
Puhua said, "Now tell me, are you an ordinary person or a sage? The Master then gave a shout. Puhua pointed his finger and said, "The bride of He'yang; the wooden pagoda."
"The wife’s Chan—Linji, that little fellow, actually possesses one eye. The Master said, "This thief!
Puhua said, "Thief! Thief! and then went out.
One day, Puhua was eating raw vegetables in front of the Sangha Hall. When the Master saw him, he said, "You look very much like a donkey.
Puhua then brayed like a donkey. The Master said, "You thief! Puhua replied, "Thief! Thief! and then went out.

Puhua was constantly roaming the streets and markets shaking his bell, saying: "If it comes from the bright side, I strike from the bright side; if it comes from the dark side, I strike from the dark side;
if it comes from the four quarters and eight directions, I strike with a whirlwind; if it comes from empty space, I strike with a continuous barrage. The Master sent an attendant to observe him.
As soon as the attendant saw him speaking thus, he seized him and asked: "What if it does not come in any such way? Puhua— [implied: struck him.]
Toukai said, "Tomorrow there is a vegetarian feast at Dabeiyuan. When the attendant returned and reported this to the Master, the Master said, "I have always harbored doubts about this fellow."
An elderly practitioner visited the Master; having never before engaged in formal social greetings, he asked, "Is it right to prostrate, or is it not?
The Master gave a shout. The elderly practitioner then prostrated. The Master said, "What a fine bandit! The elderly practitioner replied, "A bandit! A bandit!"
He then went out. The Master said, "Do not say that there is nothing wrong. While the Head Seat was standing in attendance, the Master asked, "Is there still a fault?
The Head Seat said, "There is. The Master said, "Is it a fault on the part of the guest, or a fault on the part of the host?
The Head Seat said, "Both have faults. The Master said, "Where does the fault lie? The Head Seat then went out. The Master said, "Do not say there is nothing."
This was excellent. Later, a monk recounted this to Nanquan, who said, "Official horses trampling one another.
The Master once entered a military camp to attend a meal. At the gate, he saw an officer. Pointing to a pillar, the Master asked, "Is it ordinary or is it sacred?
The officer was speechless. The Master struck the pillar and said, "Even if you could have spoken, it would still have been nothing more than a wooden peg."
He entered, and the Master asked the head monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I went to the prefectural city to sell yellow millet.
The Master said, "Did you sell it all? The monk said, "I sold it all. The Master drew a line in front of him with his staff and said, "Can you sell this too?"
"Is it like this? The Master then shouted; the Teacher then struck him. When the head cook arrived, the Master brought up the previous words.
The head cook said, "The monastery manager does not understand the Master’s meaning. The Master asked, "How about you? The head cook then bowed; the Master likewise struck him.
A presiding master (zuozhu) came to visit him. The Master asked the presiding master, "Which sutras or treatises do you lecture on?

The master replied, "I am a man of shallow learning, but I have roughly studied the *Śata-dharma-śāstra*. The Master said, "There is a person who has clearly realized the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings."

There was a man who asked, "Regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, are those who understand them the same as those who do not? Or are they different? The Master said, "Those who understand them are the same;
those who do not understand them are different. Le Pu, who was serving as the attendant, stood behind the Master and said, "Seat-Master," and then [the Master] replied, "Yes."
"What place is this? Speak of their sameness or speak of their difference. The Master turned his head and asked the attendant, "And what about you?
The attendant then gave a shout. As the Master was seeing off the presiding lecturer, he returned and asked the attendant, "Was that shout just now yours directed at me, the old monk?
The attendant replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him.
The Master heard that the second-generation Deshan was about to give a teaching, saying: "If you can speak it, thirty blows; if you cannot speak it, thirty blows.
The Master ordered Lepu to go and ask: "Why do you give thirty blows even if one can speak it? He told him, "Wait for him to strike you;
catch hold of the staff and push him away once. See what he does then. Lepu went there and questioned him exactly as instructed.
Deshan struck him. Baizhang caught the staff and gave it a push. Deshan then returned to his quarters.
Baizhang followed back and reported this to the Master (Nanquan). The Master said, "I have always suspected this fellow. Nevertheless, do you see Deshan?"
As he was about to offer a comment, the Master struck him.
One day, Attendant Wang visited the Master; they went together to look at the monks in front of the Sangha Hall. He asked, "Do the monks in this hall study the sutras?
The Master said, "They do not study the sutras. The Attendant asked, "Then do they practice Chan? The Master said, "They do not practice Chan."
The attendant said, "If he neither studies the sutras nor practices Chan, what exactly is he doing? The Master said, "I am teaching him entirely to become a Buddha or a Patriarch.
The attendant said, "Though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract. What then?"
The Master said, "I thought you were just a common layman.
The Master asked Xingshan, "What is the white ox on the open ground? Xingshan said, "Hūṃ. Hūṃ. The Master said, "Mute! Mute!
Xingshan said, "How about you, Elder? The Master said, "This beast!"
The Master asked Lepu, "Since the beginning of time, one person has practiced the staff and another has practiced the shout. Which of these is more intimate?
Lepu replied, "Neither is intimate. The Master said, "What is the point of intimacy? Lepu then shouted. The Master struck him.
When the Master saw the monk approach, he spread his two hands wide. The monk remained silent. The Master asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said:
"The whole lump cannot be split open; I give you two coins. Dajue arrived for an audience.
The Master raised his whisk. Dajue spread out his sitting mat. The Master threw down the whisk.
Dajue folded up his sitting mat and entered the Sangha hall. The assembly of monks said, "Is this monk perhaps a relative of the Master? He does not prostrate."
He bowed but did not receive a blow. When the Master heard of this, he had Jue summoned. When Jue came out, the Master said, "The assembly says you have not yet consulted the Elder.
Jue said, "I do not presume to inquire," and then returned to the assembly.

When Zhaozhou was traveling on pilgrimage, he visited a master. Upon encountering the master while he was washing his feet, Zhaozhou asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The master replied, "It happens to be the time when the old monk is washing his feet. Zhaozhou stepped forward and made a gesture as if listening.
The master said, "You want another ladleful of foul water poured over you? Zhaozhou then went down.

The Senior Monk Ding arrived for an audience. He asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master stepped down from his rope seat, seized him, gave him a slap, and then pushed him away.
Ding stood there dazed. A monk standing nearby said, "Senior Monk Ding, why do you not prostrate?
Only then did Ding prostrate, whereupon he suddenly attained great enlightenment.

Which of these is more intimate? Luopu said, "Neither is intimate. The Master said, "What is the place of intimacy? Luopu then shouted; the Master then struck him.

Da-jue folded up his sitting mat and entered the Sangha hall. The assembly of monks said, "Could this monk perhaps be a relative of the Master?"

The Twelve-Faced Avalokiteśvara faces straight ahead. The Master descended from his corded seat;

The Master raised his staff and struck him; Magu caught it, and they grappled each other as they entered the abbot’s quarters. The Master then questioned a monk.
"Sometimes a single shout is like the precious sword of the Vajra King; sometimes a single shout is like a golden-maned lion crouching on the ground;

"Ho! The Master raised his staff and said, "Speak further! Speak further! The nun shouted again, and the Master struck her.

Longya asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Hand me the meditation board. Longya handed the meditation board to the Master; the Master took it and struck him.
Longya said, "I will let you strike me as you please, but there is no meaning of the Patriarch in that. Later, Longya...
Dongshan Ya arrived at Cuiwei and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Cuiwei said, "Hand me the meditation cushion.
Ya immediately handed the cushion to Cuiwei. Cuiwei took it and struck him. Ya said, "If you wish to strike, then strike as you please."
"However, there is no meaning of the Patriarch. After Ya resided at the monastery, a monk entered his room to request instruction, saying:
"When you were traveling on pilgrimage, you visited two venerable elders; did they approve of you or not? Ya said: "If they approved, they approved profoundly;
however, there was still no meaning of the Patriarch. At Mount Jing, there were five hundred followers, yet few came to seek instruction. Huangbo sent the Master [Yaoshan] there.
Jingshan said to the Master, "When you arrive there, what will you do? The Master replied, "Once I have arrived there, I shall naturally have my own expedient means.
When the Master reached Jingshan, he girded his waist and ascended to the Dharma Hall to see Jingshan. Just as Jingshan raised his head, the Master let out a shout.
As Jingshan was about to open his mouth, the Master swept his sleeves and departed. Shortly thereafter, a monk asked Jingshan about this monk.
"What was it that you just said? he asked, and then gave a shout at the Master. Jingshan said, "This monk has come from Huangbo’s assembly.
Do you wish to know? Ask him yourself. At that time, more than half of Jingshan’s five hundred followers dispersed.
One day, Puhua went into the marketplace and begged people for a *zhiduo* (a monastic robe). Everyone gave him one, yet Puhua would not accept them all.
The Master ordered the head of the monastery to purchase a coffin. When Puhua returned, the Master said, "I have finished making a *zhiduo* (monastic robe) for you.
Puhua immediately took it upon himself and went through the streets, shouting, "Linji has made me a *zhiduo*.
I am going to the East Gate to pass away. The people of the market vied with one another to follow and watch him. Puhua...
He said, "I have not yet come today; tomorrow I shall go out through the south gate to pass away. Thus it was for three days, and no one believed him.
On the fourth day, with no one following to watch, he went alone outside the city and entered his own coffin by himself. He asked a passerby on the road to nail it shut.
Immediately, news spread abroad, and the people of the market vied with one another to go there. When they opened the coffin, they saw that his entire body had vanished, leaving nothing behind but—
He heard the sound of bells ringing faintly in the air as they departed.
When Master Xinglu was first at Huangbo’s assembly, his conduct and practice were pure and singular; the Head Seat then sighed and said, "Although he is but a junior monk,"
He was different from the others, so the Head Seat asked him, "How long have you been here, Senior? The Master said, "Three years.
The Head Seat said, "Have you ever asked questions? The Master said, "I have never asked questions; I do not know what there would be to ask. The Head Seat said:
"Why do you not go and ask the Abbot, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master then went;
before his question had even ended, Huangbo struck him. The Master came back down, and the Head Seat asked, "How was your inquiry?"
The Master said, "Before my question had even finished, the Abbot struck me. I do not understand. The Head Seat said, "Just go and ask him again.
The Master went back and asked again; Huangbo struck him once more. Thus he asked three times and was struck three times.
The Master came and said to the Head Seat, "I am fortunate to have received your compassion, allowing me to inquire after the Abbot's health. Three times..."
He asked questions and was struck three times. He lamented his own karmic obstacles for failing to grasp the profound meaning, saying, "I shall now take my leave.
The Head Seat said, "If you are going, you must first take leave of the Abbot. The Master bowed and withdrew.

The Head Seat went first to the Abbot's quarters and said, "That young man who questioned us was truly in accordance with the Dharma. When he comes to bid you farewell, please receive him with skillful means."
Later, he carved it into a great tree to provide shade for all people under heaven.
The Master then took his leave of Huangbo, who said, "You must not go elsewhere; you should go to Dayu at Tancheng in Gaoyang."
"I shall certainly explain it for you. The Master went to Dayu. Dayu asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Huangbo.
Dayu asked, "What words did Huangbo say? The Master said, "Three times I asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, and three times I was struck.
I do not know whether I was at fault or not. Dayu said, "Huangbo..."
"With such earnest and grandmotherly concern, you have been brought to utter exhaustion for my sake, yet you still come here to ask whether you have committed an offense or not.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "So it turns out that Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma consists of nothing more than this!

Daoyu grabbed him by the collar and said, "You bed-wetting little devil! Just now you were asking whether you had committed an offense or not, and now you say that Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma consists of nothing more than this!"
"The Dharma has no children. What principle have you seen? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The Master struck Daoyu three times under the ribs.
Daoyu pushed him away and said, "Your teacher is Huangbo; it is none of my business. The Master took his leave of Daoyu and returned to Huangbo.
When Huangbo saw him coming, he asked, "This fellow comes and goes back and forth; what is there to do?"
[The Master] finished his period of attendance. The Teacher said, "It was simply because my grandmotherly heart was so earnest.

Then the attendant duties were concluded, and [Nanquan] stood in attendance. Huangbo asked, "Where have you come from? Nanquan replied, "Yesterday, I received your compassionate command and went to visit Dayu;
that is where I have come from. Huangbo asked, "What words did Dayu say? Nanquan then recounted the previous conversation. Huangbo said, "How did you manage to get this fellow to come here?"
[The Master] said, "I will wait for the pain and give you a blow. The Master said, "What do you mean by 'waiting'? Eat right now! He then struck him with his palm.
Huangbo said, "This madman has come here to pull the tiger's whiskers. The Master then gave a shout. Huangbo said:
"Attendant, lead this wind-crazed fellow to the hall for practice. Later, Guishan raised this story and asked Yangshan, "At that time, did Linji gain the power of Dayu or the power of Huangbo?
Yangshan replied, "He not only knows how to ride the tiger's head, but he also understands how to strike the tiger's tail.
While the Master was planting pine trees, Huangbo asked him, "What are you doing planting so many trees in the deep mountains?"
The Master said, "First, it serves as a scenic feature for the mountain gate; second, it serves as a banner for later generations.
Having finished speaking, he struck the ground three times with his mattock. Huangbo said, "Even so, you have already received thirty blows from me.
The Master again struck the ground three times with the mattock and made a sighing sound. Huangbo said, "My school has reached..."
"You shall greatly flourish in the world. Later, Guishan raised this remark and asked Yangshan, "At that time, Huangbo entrusted his teaching to Linji alone;
was there anyone else? Yangshan replied, "There was, but the years have been so remote that I do not wish to mention it to you, Master.
Guishan said, "Even so, I still wish to know. You simply go ahead and mention it. Yangshan—
Shan said, "A single person points south; the command shall prevail over Wu and Yue. When encountering a great wind, it will immediately cease" (this was a prophecy concerning Venerable Fengxue).
Once, while the Master was attending on Deshan, Deshan said, "I am weary today. The Master said, "Why does this old fellow talk in his sleep? Deshan then struck him.
The Master overturned the rope bed, whereupon Deshan desisted. Later, while the Master was working together with the community to hoe the earth, he saw Huangbo approaching.
He stood leaning on his hoe. Huangbo asked, "Is this fellow tired? The Master said, "The hoe has not even been lifted; what is there to be tired of? Huangbo then struck him.
The Master caught the staff and gave it such a shove that Huangbo fell over. Huangbo called for the Rector, saying, "Rector! Rector!"
"Help me up! The rector stepped forward to support him, saying, "How can you, Master, tolerate such an impertinent madman?
As soon as Huangbo rose, he struck the rector. The Master was hoeing the ground and said, "In other places they perform cremation;
here, we bury everyone alive at once. Later, Guishan asked Yangshan, "What was the meaning behind Huangbo striking the rector? Yangshan replied:
It is said: "The real thief has run away; the trackers are beaten. One day, as the Master was sitting in front of the Sangha Hall, he saw Huangbo approaching.
He immediately closed his eyes. Huangbo then made a gesture of intimidation and returned to the Abbot’s quarters. The Master followed him to the quarters to offer his thanks.
The Head Seat was standing in attendance by Huangbo’s side. Huangbo said, "Although this monk is but a junior,..."
[The Master] replied, "I knew there was such a thing. The Head Seat said, "The Old Monk’s feet do not touch the ground, yet he testifies for this youth.
Huangbo slapped him across the mouth. The Head Seat said, "If you had known, you would have understood.
When the Master saw Puhua, he said, "When I was in the South delivering a letter to Mount Gui, I knew that you were already staying here waiting for me."
"I have come. And I have come. I have obtained your assistance. I now wish to establish the fundamental tenets of Huangbo;
you must by all means help me to bring this to completion. Puhua bowed respectfully and departed. Ke Fu arrived later, and the Master addressed him in the same manner.
Fufu also respectfully descended. Three days later, Puhua ascended again to inquire after him, saying, "What did you say, Master, the day before yesterday?
The Master raised his staff and struck him down. Again, three days later, Kefu also ascended. Upon inquiring after him, he asked:
The Master struck Puhua the day before yesterday; why was that? The Master likewise raised his staff and struck him down.
In the Master’s assembly, two fellow students asked one another: "Setting aside the middle and lower capacities, I ask you, elder brother, to speak a single phrase.
One said, "As soon as you intend to ask, you have already missed it. The other said, "If that is so, then I shall go and pay my respects to you, elder brother. The former replied, "..."
When the Master heard that robbers had arrived, he ascended the hall and said, "If you wish to understand the Guest-Host phrase of Linji, go ask the two Chan monks in the air.
He then descended from his seat. A monk came forward and asked, "Is it right to prostrate, or is it not? The Master then shouted.
The monk prostrated. The Master said, "This thief. The monk also said, "This thief," and then departed.
The Master said, "Do not say that all is well. The Head Seat was standing in attendance; the Master looked back at him and asked, "Is there any fault here? The Seat said, "There is. The Master said:
The guest commits a fault; the host commits a fault. The Seat-holder said, "Both commit faults. The Master asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Seat-holder then went out.
The Master said, "Do not say it is 'no matter' (wúshì). Later, a monk reported this to Nanquan. Nanquan said, "Official horses trampling one another.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk gave a shout. The Master then gestured for him to sit. The monk—
As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. When another monk approached, the Master raised his whisk; the monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
When yet another monk approached, the Master again raised his whisk; the monk paid no heed, and the Master struck him as well.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who study the Way must be extremely careful and discerning. When guest and host meet, there is immediately an exchange of words;

sometimes he manifests his form in response to things, or acts with his whole being; he may wield the power of expedient means through joy or anger, or manifest half his body, or ride upon a lion, or ride upon an elephant king.
If there is a truly authentic student, they will immediately shout. First, [the master] picks up [the challenge]."
He brought out a basin of glue. The "Good Knowledgeable One" (the teacher) failed to recognize it as an external trap;
he stepped onto that trap and began to pose and feign. The student then shouted at him again. The former person refused to let go. This is a terminal illness.

It cannot be cured by medical treatment. To call this "the guest looking at the host" means that either a good spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) does not bring forth the essential substance, but simply seizes [the student] according to the point of their inquiry;
when the student is seized, they refuse to let go even unto death. This is "the host looking at the guest."
There may be a student who brings a single pure object before a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).
When the spiritual friend recognizes this object and seizes it to hurl it into a pit, the student says, "Excellent, spiritual friend! The spiritual friend then says, "Alas!
You do not distinguish between good and evil. The student then prostrates; this is called "the host looking at the host. Or there may be another student...
Clad in shackles and fetters, he went before a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra). The friend further placed another layer of shackles and fetters upon him, and the student rejoiced;
neither could distinguish between them, so they called it "the guest looking at the guest. "Virtuous One," the mountain monk says:

all that I have raised is for the purpose of discerning demons, selecting the extraordinary, and knowing the false from the true. When the Master arrived at Minghua, Minghua asked: "Why do you come and go?"
The Master said, "You have merely worn out your straw sandals. Huizhao asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, "Even this old fellow does not recognize the head of the matter.
He then went to Fenglin. On the road, he encountered an old woman who asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "I am going to Fenglin.
The woman said, "It happens that Fenglin is away at the moment. The Master asked, "Where has she gone? The woman then walked off. The Master [was left there].
The Master called out, "Venerable! The monk turned his head. The Master then walked away.
When the Master ascended the hall, a monk came forward. The Master gave a shout; the monk also shouted. The monk then bowed. The Master struck him. He then asked a monk:
"Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Dingzhou. The Master raised his staff. The monk hesitated; the Master struck him immediately. The monk did not accept this.
The Master said, "In the future, you will encounter those with clear eyes. Later, the monk went to visit Sansheng. As soon as he brought up the previous conversation, Sansheng struck him.
The monk hesitated; Sansheng struck him again. The Master frequently used the shout (*he*) in response to stimuli, and the disciples under his guidance also learned it.
The Master shouted. The Master said, "You all learn my shout. Now I ask you:
suppose one person comes out from the eastern hall and another comes out from the western hall, and both shout simultaneously—can you distinguish guest from host here?"
"How would you go about dividing it? If you cannot divide it, do not learn to shout like this old monk hereafter.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Sometimes I first illumine and then act; sometimes I first act and then illumine; sometimes illumination and action are simultaneous;
sometimes illumination and action are not simultaneous. When there is someone present who first illumines and then acts, that is 'first acting and then illumining.'"
There is a Dharma that exists wherein illumination and function are simultaneous; it drives the plowman’s ox and snatches the food from the hungry man;

it beats the bones to extract the marrow and applies needles and awls with piercing force. When illumination and function are not simultaneous, there is questioning and answering, the establishment of guest and host, the mixing of water and mud, and responding to conditions to engage with beings.
If one is a person of transcendent capacity, they should "lift up and go" even before the question has been raised.
It was still slightly lacking. When a monk came, the Master raised his whisk; the monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
Another monk came, and the Master again raised his whisk; the monk paid no heed, and the Master struck him as well. Yet another monk came for an audience;
the Master raised his whisk, and the monk said, "Thank you, Master, for your instruction," whereupon the Master struck him too. While the Master was sleeping in the hall, Huangbo came down...
He came to see him. [Baizhang] struck the head of the sounding board once with his staff. The Master raised his head; seeing it was Huangbo, he went back to sleep.
Huangbo struck the head of the sounding board once again, then went up to the upper quarters where he saw the Head Seat sitting in meditation.
He said, "The junior monks in the lower quarters are actually sitting in meditation; what are you doing here, indulging in such deluded thoughts? The Head Seat replied, "This old fellow—"
"What? Huangbo struck the wooden board once and immediately went out. Later, Guishan asked Yangshan, "What was the meaning of Huangbo entering the Sangha hall?
Yangshan said, "Two colors, one match. One day, during a communal work session, the Master was walking behind.
Huangbo turned his head and, seeing that the Master was empty-handed, asked, "Where is the hoe? The Master—
Yangshan said, "There is one person who has already taken it away. Huangbo said, "Come closer; let us deliberate on a matter together. The Master approached.
Huangbo held up his hoe and said, "This very thing—no one in the world can lift or grasp it.
The Master snatched it from his hand, held it up, and asked, "Why is it now in my hands? Huangbo— [remained silent].
He said, "Today there is a great communal labor for all; let us return to the monastery. Later, Guishan asked Yangshan, "The mattock was in Huangbo’s hands;
why was it taken away by Linji? Yangshan replied, "The thief is the petty man."
In wisdom he surpassed the gentleman. When the Master was sent by Huangbo to deliver a letter to Guishan, Yangshan was serving as the guest prefect at that time.
Upon receiving the letter, he asked, "Which of these is Huangbo’s, and which is for the messenger? The Master then gave him a slap.
Yangshan held him back, saying, "Brother, since you understand such matters, let it be. Together they went to see Guishan, who then—
Question: "Brother Huangbo, how many followers do you have? The Master said: "Seven hundred. Miaoyan said: "Who acts as their leader? The Master said:
"I have already sent word to him just now. The Master then asked Miaoyan: "How many followers do you have here, Preceptor?
Miaoyan said: "One thousand five hundred. The Master said: "That is too many! Miaoyan said: "Huang..."
"Brother Heshang, you are not lacking either. When the Master took his leave of Mount Gui, Yangshan saw him out and said, "In the future, you shall go north;
there will be a place for you to dwell. The Master said, "How could such a thing be? Yangshan said, "Just go.
Later on, there will be someone to assist you, elder brother. This person will have a beginning but no end; he will have a start but no finish. Afterward, the Master...
Upon arriving at Zhenzhou, Puhua was already there. When the Master entered the world [to teach], Puhua assisted and supported him.

Not long after the Master had taken up residence, Puhua departed from his physical body in its entirety. Later, while the Master was traveling to Huangbo during the midsummer retreat, he saw the Abbot reading a sutra.
The Master said, "I thought you were such a person; it turns out you are just an old monk who hides black beans. After staying for several days, the Master took his leave.
Huangbo said, "You arrived after the summer retreat has begun, yet you are leaving before it ends. The Master replied, "I came only briefly to pay my respects to the Master.
Huangbo then struck him and drove him away. The Master traveled several li, but feeling doubtful about what had transpired, he returned.
The end of summer retreat. One day, the Master took his leave of Huangbo. Huangbo asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "Not south of the River;
I am going straight back north of the River. Huangbo struck him. The Master grabbed him and gave him a slap across the face.
Huangbo laughed heartily and called to his attendant, "Bring the meditation board and the desk from our late teacher Baizhang. The Master said, "Attendant, bring some fire! Huangbo—
Huangbo said, "Even so, you must simply take it with you; in the future, you will sit upon the tongues of all people under heaven.
Later, Guishan asked Yangshan, "Did Linji fail Huangbo? Yangshan replied:
"Not so," said Guishan. "How about you, my son? Yangshan replied, "Only by knowing gratitude does one understand how to repay it.
Guishan asked, "Among the ancients of old, was there anyone like this or not?
Yangshan said, "There was, but because the times were so distant, I did not wish to cite him as an example for you, Master. Guishan said, "Even so, I still wish to know."
"Son, simply bring it forth and look. Yangshan said, "As for the assembly at the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, when Ānanda praised the Buddha, he said:
'To offer this profound mind to every dust-mote world is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness. Is this not an act of repaying kindness? Baoshan said, "So it is, so it is.
When one's insight is equal to the teacher, one lacks half the teacher's virtue; only when one's insight surpasses the teacher is one fit [to receive the transmission]."

The Transmission. When the Master arrived at the head of Bodhidharma’s stupa, the custodian of the stupa said, "Venerable Sir, shall you first pay homage to the Buddha, or shall you first pay homage to the Patriarch?
The Master said, "I pay homage to neither the Buddha nor the Patriarch. The custodian asked, "What kind of karmic enemy are the Buddha and the Patriarch to you, Venerable Sir?

The Master then shook out his sleeves and departed. While traveling on pilgrimage, the Master arrived at Longguang. When Longguang ascended the hall for the discourse, the Master stepped forward and asked: "Not..."
He sharpened his blade. "How can one achieve victory? he asked. Daguang sat upright in his seat. The Master said, "A great *kalyāṇamitra*—do you have no skillful means?
Daguang stared at him with wide eyes and said, "Huh? The Master pointed his finger and said, "This old fellow has met his defeat today.
Upon arriving at Sanfeng, Master Ping asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Huangbo. Ping said, "Does Huangbo have..."
"What words? The Master said: "Last night, the Golden Ox met with calamity; even until now, no trace of him is seen. Píng said:
"The golden wind blows through the jade flute; who is it that knows this sound? The Master said: "Directly penetrating ten thousand layers of barriers, he does not dwell within the clear void.
Píng said: "Your question, my son, is far too lofty. The Master said: "A dragon gives birth to a golden phoenix chick; it charges [forward]..."
He shattered the azure lapis lazuli. Baoping said, "Sit for now and drink some tea. He asked again, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master said, "Longguang.
Baoping said, "How is it at Longguang these days? The Master then went out. Upon arriving at Daci, Daci was sitting inside the abbot’s quarters.
The Master asked, "What is it like when one dwells uprightly in the abbot's room? Daci said, "The cold pines are of a single hue; a thousand years of separation. Wild... [text ends].
"The old man plucks the flower; ten thousand nations are in spring. The Master said, "Ancient and modern, eternally transcending the essence of perfect wisdom;

the three mountains lock away ten thousand layers of barriers. Cui then shouted. The Master also shouted. Cui asked, "What is this? The Master shook his sleeves and went out. He arrived at Huayan in Xiangzhou.
Huayan leaned on his staff and made the gesture of falling asleep. The Master said, "Old monk, why are you dozing off? Huayan said, "..."
The Zen master Jiaxiang was quite different from the others. The Master said, "Attendant, prepare some tea and bring it for the Abbot to drink.
Yan then called the Rector, saying, "Seat this venerable one in the third position. When he arrived at Cui峰 (Cui-feng), Feng asked, "Where have you come from?"
The Master said, "Huangbo has come. Feng said, "What words or phrases did Huangbo have to instruct people?
The Master said, "Huangbo had no words or phrases. Feng said, "Why is there none? The Master said, "Even if there were, there would be no place to bring them forth. Feng said, "..."
[The Master] simply raised [his staff] and looked at him. The Master said, "A single arrow passes beyond the Western Heaven.
At Xiangtian, the Master asked, "Neither ordinary nor holy—please, Master, speak quickly. Xiangtian said, "I, this old monk, am just like this.
The Master then shouted, "What are all these bald-headed monks looking for here? A bowl? At Fenglin, Fenglin asked, "May I ask you something? The Master said, "Why not?"
[The Master] said, "One might as well gouge out one's own flesh to make a wound. Lin said, "The sea moon is clear and casts no shadow; the wandering fish is alone in its delusion.
The Master said, "Since the sea moon casts no shadow, how can the wandering fish be deluded? Lin said, "Observing the wind, one knows the waves rise; gazing at the water, the wild sail drifts.
The Master said, "The solitary wheel shines alone as the rivers and mountains fall silent; with a single laugh, heaven and earth are startled. Lin said, "I leave it to you."
"Three inches of brilliance illuminates heaven and earth. Try saying a single phrase when the moment arises. The Master said: "When meeting a swordsman on the road, you must present your sword;
unless you are a poet, do not offer up your verse. Fenglin then desisted. The Master then offered this verse:
"The Great Way is beyond all likeness; go as you will, west or east. Stone-fire cannot catch up; lightning-flash finds no passage. Miaoyan asked Yangshan: "Stone-fire..."
It is beyond reach; even a flash of lightning cannot penetrate it. Regarding the various sages of antiquity, what did they take as the person?
Yangshan said, "What is your intention, Master? Miaoyan said, "As long as there are words and explanations, there is no real meaning. Yangshan said, "Not so."
Guishan said, "How about you, my son? Yangshan replied, "In official matters, even a needle cannot pass; in private affairs, carriages and horses may go through.
Upon arriving at Jin’ou, the Ox saw the Master coming; he gripped his staff crosswise and sat crouched right in front of the gate.
The Master struck the staff three times with his hand and returned to the first seat in the hall. When the Ox came down and saw him, he asked, "Regarding the mutual relationship of guest and host..."
[The two monks] saw each other, both maintaining their dignified deportment. [One monk asked: "Elder, from where have you come? You are far too impolite. The Master said, "What did the Old Monk say?
As the Ox was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him. The Ox made a gesture as if falling over; the Master struck him again. The Ox said, "Today, I am not in luck.
Miaoyan asked Yangshan, "Between these two venerable elders, is there a winner and a loser? Yangshan—

Shan said, "If you win, you win the whole; if you lose, you lose the whole. When the Master was about to pass away, he sat upright and said, "After my extinction, you must not let my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye be extinguished.
Sansheng stepped forward and said, "How would we dare let the Master’s Treasury of the True Dharma Eye be extinguished?
The Master said, "In the future, if someone asks you, what will you say to them? At this, Sansheng suddenly—
"Hai! The Master said, "Who would have known that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would perish at the hands of this blind donkey?
Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away.
*Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xinghua* (Sixth generation descendant of Nanyue, successor to Linji).
The Master’s name was Cunjian. He first visited Linji, who appointed him as his attendant. Linji asked, “Where have you come from?
He replied, “From Luancheng. Linji said, “May I ask you a question? He replied, “A novice precept-holder does not understand. Linji said:
"To shatter the Great Tang Dynasty and find a person who does not understand—such a one is hard to find! Go to the hall!
The Master asked, "Just now, did you intend to humiliate that newly arrived monk? Ji said, "Who am I to concern myself with whether he is humiliated or not?
The Master said, "You, Master, only know how to pelt a dead sparrow on the ground; you do not know how to use a turning phrase to cover it over. Ji said, "..."
"What do you say to this? The Master said, "Please, Venerable Sir, act as the newcomer. Jie then said, "A newly ordained monk does not understand.
The Master said, "Rather, it is my own fault. Jie said, "Your words conceal the sharp point [of the sword]. As the Master hesitated, Jie struck him.
When evening arrived, Linji said to the Master, "Today when I questioned the newly arrived monk, it was like striking a dying sparrow on the ground or hitting it right in its nest;
yet as soon as you produced a word, I shouted and struck him as he soared into the blue clouds. The Master said, "The grass bandit has been utterly defeated.
Linji struck him again.
On the day the Master opened the hall, he held up the incense and said: "This one stick of incense is originally for my elder brother, Sansheng.
Yet Sansheng was too solitary for me; thus, I ought to have inherited the Dharma from Dayue. But Dayue was too distant for me.
It was at the place of Sansheng that I realized the phrase of 'host and guest. Had I not met my elder brother Dayue, I would have surely missed the mark for my entire life."
Receiving the staff at the place of Great Enlightenment, I have seen the principle by which my late master Linji received the staff under Huangbo.
This single incense offering is for my late master Linji.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Today, I ask nothing of how or what; I simply invite you to enter directly with a single blade, and Xinghua will bear witness for you.
At that time, Elder Minde came forward and prostrated. As soon as he rose, he gave a shout. The Master also shouted.

Emperor Tongguang was traveling through Hebei. Upon returning to the temporary palace in Weifu, he held regular morning audiences.
After the officials of the Bureau of Monks had finished their audience, the Emperor asked his attendants, "Is there anyone of great virtue in this region? A close minister replied, "Just now—"
The monks brought as members of the Registry were all men of virtue. The Emperor said, "This is merely virtue in the pursuit of fame and profit.
Are there no men of true Way and virtue? A close minister reported, "There is an Elder Xinghua here; he is truly a man of virtue. The Emperor then summoned him.

The Emperor extended the legs of his *fukuto* (head-wrap). The Master said, "As for the treasure of a sovereign, who would dare to appraise its value?
The Emperor’s countenance was greatly pleased, and he bestowed upon the Master purple robes and a title. The Master declined them both. The Emperor then presented a horse for the Master to ride.
The horse suddenly startled and fell, whereby the Master injured his foot. When the Emperor heard of this, he issued a decree for medicine to treat him.

He did not recognize it. The Master said, "The 'Leprous-footed' Dharma Master can speak it, but he cannot practice it.

The Epitaph for the Stupa of Chan Master Linji Huizhao:
The Master’s name was Yixuan; he was a native of Nanhua in Caozhou. His secular surname was Xing. From childhood, he was exceptionally brilliant; as he grew older, he...

His filial piety was renowned. Upon shaving his head and receiving full ordination, he resided at lecture halls where he thoroughly investigated the *Vinaya* and extensively studied the sutras and śāstras.
Suddenly, he sighed and said, "This is the medical prescription for saving the world; it is not the principle of a separate transmission outside the teachings.

He immediately changed his robes and traveled to various regions. First, he visited Huangbo, and next, he called upon Dayu; the dialogues and exchanges from these encounters are recorded in his *Xinglu*. Once...

Having received the seal of approval from Huangbo, he soon arrived at a small temple situated by the Hutuo River at the southeast corner of the city of Zhenzhou in Hebei, where he served as the abbot;
it was there that Linji derived his name. At that time, Puhua was already there, feigning madness and mingling with the crowd, such that neither sages nor commoners could fathom him.
Upon the Master’s arrival, Puhua assisted him. During the Master’s peak period of propagation, Puhua cast off his physical body entirely.
This indeed fulfilled the prophetic prediction of Yangshan’s "Little Śākyamuni. Just as war broke out, the Master departed.
The Grand Marshal Mo Junhe converted his residence within the city into a monastery, naming it after Linji, and invited the Master to reside there.
Later, the Master shook out his robes and traveled south to Hezhou. There, the Provincial Governor, Attendant Wang, received him with the etiquette due to a teacher. He resided there for some time.
Ji came to Xinghua Temple in Daming Prefecture and resided in the Eastern Hall.
The Master was free from illness, yet one day he adjusted his robes, sat upright, and after concluding a dialogue with Sansheng, passed away in silence.

This was on the tenth day of the first month of the eighth year of the Xiantong era of the Tang dynasty (the Dinghai year). His disciples enshrined the Master’s entire body in a stupa to the west of Daming Prefecture.
In the northern corner: Imperial posthumous title, Chan Master Huizhao; stupa name, Chengling.

The monk then approached. The Master said: "I am calling for someone from Zhejiang; what business is it of yours, a man from west of the river?
Question: "What is the true meaning of Caoxi? The Master said: "When you meet a swordsman on the road, you must present your sword; if you are no poet, do not offer your verse."

Verse. At that time, there was a presiding master (zuozhu) who asked: "I have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, but I do not yet know the matters of the School of the Patriarchs (Zongmen).

I beg the Master to provide me with the essential framework. The Master said: "When it comes to the matters of the School of the Patriarchs, what is there that is difficult to say? You have just asked about the old monk’s nostrils. Above your head is vast and below your feet is vast. What does the school of the Teachings (Jiaojia) call this? The Master continued: "The Teachings speak of the 'Three Thousand Worlds in a Single Thought-moment' (yixin sanqian).

But tell me, where does that single thought-moment arise from? If you can answer this, then you will understand the School of the Patriarchs. The presiding master remained silent. The Master struck him once and said: "You have been sitting on a mountain of gold for thirty years, yet you still do not know how to spend it! He then left the hall.
[The Master] said, "The school of teaching has no such intent.
He drove them away with his staff and ascended the hall, saying, "All of you, hurry up! Hurry up! This old monk is seventy-nine; look, I am about to depart!"
A monk then asked, "Where will you go after a hundred years? The Master said, "Thirty years from now, someone will speak of this.
[The monk] asked, "Who is worthy to wear Kāśyapa’s upper robe? The Master said, "Shaking out my many-year-old tattered rag-robe;
its frayed half flies away with the clouds. Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Sometimes it hangs [upon the tree]."

[The Master] placed it upon his shoulder. "This is superior even to the people of this age wearing brocade robes. A questioner asked, "One wears clothes and eats food all day long; how can one avoid wearing clothes and eating food?
The Master said, "Wear clothes and eat food. The questioner replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, then wear clothes and eat food.
A Dharma Master asked, "I do not ask about the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings; how [is it otherwise]?"
"This is a matter within the Gate of the Patriarchs. The Master said, "I, the old monk, have entered into your alms-bag.
The host asked, "Why is the Master in the student’s alms-bag? The Master said, "What are you going to offer? Bring me some betel nut and cardamom quickly.
The host asked, "What is it that the Master lacks? The Master said, "This thief is defeated today! The host stepped forward and said, "The student..."

Just as he entered the monastery, he requested the Master’s instruction. The Master said, "Appointing according to one's capacity. The student stepped forward and said, "I, this disciple, seek counsel from the Abbot.
The Master rebuked him, saying, "You fellow who leans on fences and feels for walls! You could not even serve as a village headman in a hamlet of three households.
Later, as the Master was returning from a meal, a monk approached him and asked for alms money. The Master said, "I received thirty coins at the meal."
[The Master] spoke. The monk said, “I request you to do so. The Master said, “Though the giver may never grow weary, the receiver should know contentment. A question was asked:
“Regarding the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, I request the Master to provide its essential framework. The Master said, “Bring it forward, and I shall provide you with its framework.

The monk stepped forward and said, “I request the Master to speak it now. The Master said, “Demolish the eastern fence to patch up the western wall. There was a monk named Zongchan who consulted the Master, saying, “Master, please instruct me.”
The Master said, "Stop. The monk stopped immediately. The Master scolded him, saying, "You do not even know the name. He added, "If you can explain it, I shall judge you.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Chan was unable to respond. A lay official asked, "Can one breath turn over the entirety of the Great Tripitaka?"
The Master said, "What silk cloth do you have? Bring it here quickly! A questioner asked, "An ancient said there is 'one path to ultimate realization.

What is this one path to ultimate realization? The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! This notice of yours is difficult for me to encounter here. Both the brush and the ink—both legal documents—are settled at once.
The questioner stepped forward and said, "What fault have I committed? The Master then struck him and drove him away. Another asked.
"Since the time of the ancient masters, have there been any distinctions or divergent paths—principles that are difficult to comprehend?
The Master said, "There are. The student asked, "What is this principle of distinctions and divergent paths that is so difficult to comprehend?

The Master said, "I shall wait until you have passed through sixty kalpas over three lifetimes before you can believe it. The student asked, "I have only recently entered the monastic community; I beg the Master for instruction."
The Master said, "You do not understand how to ask. The student asked, "How about you, Teacher? The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows; go out and take them yourself.
A monk asked, "In all the lands of the ten directions, there is only the One Vehicle Dharma.
What is this One Vehicle Dharma? The Master said, "If you did not ask, I would not know. Since you have asked me, I know it."
The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! Where did you get this question from? The monk was speechless.
Another monk asked, "To speak is to shake heaven and earth; not to speak is to be free from even a single thread of attachment.
Is it speaking? Or is it not speaking? The Master said, "What are you saying? When the monk repeated his question, the Master said, "This fellow who tells empty lies! [The monk] stepped forward.
The monk said, "I am here. The Master said, "To speak is to shake heaven and earth. That you have spoken thus—" The monk said, "Yes.
The Master brandished his whisk and struck him, saying, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! You come here to frighten me!

A monk asked, "Please provide us with the essential framework of the meaning of the Teachings. The Master said, "Just ask, and I shall tell you. The monk pressed on, "I request you to speak now. The Master said, "Buddha."

Incense was being burned within the hall; [the Master] joined his palms at the triple gate. A questioner asked: "I, a student, have a question; I do not know whether you, Master, will permit it or not.
The Master said: "Truly, when a thief comes, one must strike; when a guest comes, one must look upon them. The questioner pressed:
"I do not know how you, the Monk, would speak to this? The Master said: "This thief cannot strike you. A questioner asked: "The Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings..."
"How is it attained? The Master said, "It is attained by responding to the capacity [of the student]. [The student] asked, "I request the Master to provide a turning word.
Is this possible? The Master said, "It is possible. [The student] pressed further, "Please speak it now! The Master grabbed his staff and drove him away.
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Come forward, you who will not be deceived. A monk stepped forth and responded with an assent. The Master said:
"I have just spat a lump of dung into your throat to choke you; I have spat it into your eyes to blind you. How can you say you are not being deceived?

Later, while the Master was reading the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, a monk asked: "Master, what sūtra are you reading? The Master replied: "Without duality, without division; without distinction."
"Because there is no severance. Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Even my reciting of the sutras would not be permitted.
A lay official asked, "Does the Master follow the teachings or not? The Master said, "Shaving the head with light and washing the bowl clean—how could this not be following the teachings?
Once, during a meal, a lay official asked, "I request the Master to bestow his food upon me. The Master said, "The three virtues and six flavors."
[The Master] offered it to the Buddha and the Sangha. "Hūṃ. Hūṃ. Bring it here quickly! This old monk wishes to eat. A secular official said, "I request that the Master bestow wealth upon me.
The Master said, "The disciple bestows wealth; the Master bestows the Dharma. First comes the old monk, then the Buddha.

Again, a secular official asked, "Today my disciple has opened the *Kangyur* (the Treasury of Scriptures). I beg the Master for a single phrase to provide the essential framework for this treasury. The Master said, "This..."
[The monk] asked, “It is difficult to find [one who can answer]. The Official said, “Please provide the essential outline. The Master said, “Playing the lute for a cow.

Later, while the Master was reading a sutra, a monk asked, “What sutra is the Master reading? The Master said, “The *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*; the ‘Chapter on the Cremation’ (*Te-p’i-pin*) is at the very end. [The monk] asked, “Why is that?”
"What is the discourse that transcends the Buddhas and surpasses the Patriarchs? The Master suddenly took up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "I call this a staff;
what do you call it? The monk was speechless. The Master again showed him the staff and said, "The discourse that transcends the Buddhas and surpasses the Patriarchs—is that what you asked about?
The monk was speechless. Because Jiaoshan had borrowed an axe, the Master called out to him.
The youth brought the axe head. Having brought it, he stood before the Master and said, "There are no marking lines yet;
let us first chop the rough parts. The Master then shouted. He called the youth again, saying, "Come, come! What is this axe of yours? The youth then made a gesture of chopping.
The Master said, "You cannot chop off the head of your father in the house. The Master then cited Huangbo: "And..."
Shangyu said, "The old monks of the world all say that the 'single breath of the Way' resides within me.
Whether I let you go or whether I do not let you go, it is all within me. A monk then asked, "What is the single breath of the Way?
The Master said, "Appointing one to office according to their capacity. The monk asked, "What is not letting go of the single breath of the Way? The Master said, "To subdue."
May you graciously accept this offering. Question: What is Chan? The Master said: "A fierce fire frying oil. Question: Not discriminating among anything.

"Please, Master, provide the essential framework of the Buddha-dharma. The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth; beasts, donkeys, and horses. The monk asked, "Why do they not understand?
The Master said, "If you were held fast by me, they would have to be smashed to pieces. The monk said, "Master, you must not always speak thus.
The Master said, "I do not believe you when you say they are not smashed to pieces. A monk asked, "Having recently entered the monastic community, I beg the Master for instruction."

[The monk] said, “It is so. The Master said, “You have recently entered the monastic community. The monk replied, “Yes. The Master said, “One’s heart should not betray others, and one’s face should show no shame.
The monk replied, “I do not understand this. The Master said, “Come closer; I will explain it to you. The monk approached. The Master said, “Go.”
The Master ascended the hall. The assembly stood in attendance. The Master shouted, "Go out! but the assembly did not leave.
The Master shouted again, and the assembly remained bewildered. The Master raised his staff and drove them all down at once.
The Master was reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* when a monk asked, "What sūtra is this? The Master said, "Great clouds of radiance;
azure clouds of radiance; purple clouds of radiance. What kind of cloud is that over there?
The monk said, "That is a black cloud to the south. The Master said, "It must rain today. He then added, "I thought he was a lion cub, but it turns out he is..."
"A little mouse.
He ascended the hall and said, "Is there anyone who can come forward and kick over this meditation seat? A monk came forward and responded with an affirmative "Yes. The Master said:
Coming from the north, he cast his hook to catch whales and giant fish; yet at the very moment of casting it down, he caught nothing but a frog.
A monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Give me back the second segment. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The third segment is different;
ten thousand *li* away is Yuzhou. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Tear out his nostrils. A monk asked, "What is... (The Master said,) "...tear out his nostrils."
"A single phrase that is like a tangled vine. The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are your question. He asked further, "How does one grasp the main thread and handle it?
The Master said, "When it comes to me, ask. He asked, "If supported, there are the heavens and the earth; if not supported, not even a hair's breadth is encountered—at such a time, what then?
The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! I have never seen such a thing. The Master then asked, "First, leap three thousand miles; then, turn upside down."
[The Master] said, "Stepping back eight hundred [paces]. How do you do? The student said, "Yes. The Master said, "First, let me issue a formal reprimand; I shall give this fellow a good beating.
He added, "Come, come! I will engage you in some idle talk. The universe and the great earth are supported [by it]; tell me, how deep is the water of Lake Dongting?
The student stepped forward and said, "It has never been measured. The Master said, "Is that so? And what about the water of Lake Dongting?"
"How is it? The student replied, "It is precisely because of the present age. The Master said, "You do not even understand this entanglement," and struck him. [The student] asked.
The great assembly gathered like clouds. [A monk] asked, "What is it that we should discuss together? The Master said, "How so? [The monk] asked, "I do not ask about the Flower Treasury Ocean;
what is the path that leads upward? The Master said, "Welcome, welcome."
The Master, citing a saying from an ancient, asked the assembly: "What kind of matter is accomplished by the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings?
A monk said, "Today the entire assembly has been invited for a communal work; it is no small matter. The Master said, "Do not bring it out.
The monk said, "We are beating the drum to eat the midday meal (yao-shi). The Master said, "Do not pick it up. The monk said, "The Master is so [direct]!"
“Daodao” (Repeatedly). The Master said, “I also only want you to speak like this. A monk asked, “What is the phrase for ‘encountering obstacles wherever one goes’?
The Master said, “I also only say it. The monk pressed further, “How do you say it? The Master said, “HŪṂ! HŪṂ! The arrow has already traveled a hundred thousand li beyond the Western Heavens;
now it waits within the land of the Great Tang. A monk knocked on the door and asked, “If one’s own matter is not...”
Ming asked, “I beg the Master for instruction. As soon as the Master opened the door, the monk prepared to open his mouth to speak, whereupon the Master struck him across the mouth with his hand.
The monk asked, “What is the point of entry for a student? The Master said, “One cannot be understood. The monk pressed further, “I do not understand.”
The Master said, "These words will circulate widely thirty years from now. A monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
The monk further asked, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Shaking out my many years of worn-out patchwork robe, its tattered half flies off with the clouds.
The Provincial Head Monk of Muzhou and a multitude of great virtuous ones invited the Master to ascend the hall. The Master—

He asked for the Sangha Director (Sengzheng). The Director responded with an assent. The Master said, "The Prior (Jiansi)? The Director replied, "He is not here. The Master said, "The Chief Administrator (Dujian)?
The Director replied, "He is not here. The Master said, "The Senior Seat (Shangzuo)? The Director replied, "He is not here. The Master said, "These three cases are not the same;
this is the first. The subsequent text is long; we shall meet tomorrow. No need for further words; I take my leave and depart. He then rose.
The great virtuous ones were at a loss. The Master raised [the point], saying:
"An ancient said: 'To gather them together is up to me; to tear them apart is also up to me. A monk asked:
"What is it like to tear them apart? The Master said: "Bodhi, Nirvana, True Suchness, and Liberation. Three times nine is twenty-seven. Give it back to me!"
The first tally arrived. He said again, "The very mind is Buddha. I have spoken thus for now; what do you say?
The monk said, "I do not speak in that way. The Master said, "The cup falls to the ground; the plate shatters into seven pieces. The monk said, [silently].

"How do you clench [your hands]? The Master then sat with his hands folded. One day, the Regional Inspector of Muzhou asked, "What is the matter of the Zen school? The Master said, "Come closer, come closer. The Inspector came forward. The Master said, "How can you speak such empty falsehoods? The Inspector was speechless. The Master then asked, "Whom have you studied under? The Inspector said, "I have studied under such-and-such a person. The Master said, "He is like a dried-up well; he has nothing left to give you. The Inspector was again speechless. The Master said, "If you wish to understand the Way, you must first abandon all conceptualization. If you do not abandon it, you will never attain liberation. The Inspector was again speechless. The Master said, "The Buddha Dharma is not something to be grasped by the mind or intellect. It is beyond words and letters. You must realize it for yourself within your own nature. The Inspector was again speechless. The Master said, "If you wish to see the Buddha, look at your own face before your parents were born. If you wish to hear the Dharma, listen to the sound of the wind in the pines and the rain on the bamboo. The Inspector was again speechless. The Master said, "If you wish to enter the Way, you must first cut off all attachments. If you do not cut them off, you will be bound by them. The Inspector was again speechless. The Master said, "The Way is not far away; it is right here before you. Do not seek it elsewhere. If you seek it elsewhere, you will wander in birth and death for countless eons. The Inspector was again speechless. The Master said, "If you wish to attain the Way, you must first abandon all views. If you do not abandon them, you will be caught in the net of views. "Venerable Master, where have you come from? The Master said, "What else? Shi said, "I have come to read the scriptures.
The Master suddenly struck the meditation seat once and asked, "In the scriptures, what is this called? Shi said, "It is not mentioned in the scriptures. The Master said, "The scriptures state:
'Managing one's livelihood and engaging in productive industry do not contradict the True Principle. What then? Shi had no reply. The Master [said]: "..."
He also struck the bed once and said, "Generally speaking, what do you call this? Shi replied, "I call it a bed.
The Master said, "This fellow who is sticky about his food! Once, while at a meal, the Imperial Secretary Chen Cao of Muzhou personally handed a steamed bun to a monk.
The monk reached out his hand to receive it, but the Secretary withdrew his hand. The monk was left speechless. The Secretary then [addressed] the assembly...
The official was sitting atop the pavilion of the military garrison when he suddenly saw several monks approaching. The official said, "How many monks are coming?
The Minister said, "It is not they. The official asked, "How do you know it is not they? The Minister replied, "Wait until they arrive here."
"I will test you. The monk then arrived. The Minister suddenly called out, "Upādhyāya! Upādhyāya! The monk turned his head, but remained speechless.
The Minister said, "I do not believe your words."
Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered, the Master said, "Suddenly! Suddenly! A monk came forward and said, "Please, let the assembly return to the hall.
The Master struck his meditation seat once and said, "It kills me with grief! The monk then turned his head, and the Master raised his staff and drove them all away at once.
A monk asked, "What is the direct shortcut to the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Three people, two people—do not ask."
The monk stepped forward and said, "I request that the Master speak. The Master said, "Three people, one indictment; you have all been brought before me.
The monk asked, "What is it like when a single word expresses everything? The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! You have struck the old monk right on his front teeth!

The monk continued, "I have already received the Master’s instruction. The Master said, "A fellow with a head but no tail. Qiantang is three thousand li from the capital. The monk was speechless. [Another] monk asked:
[The monk asked: "How is it when a single phrase is completely purified? The Master said: "I would pluck out your eyebrows and replace your eyelashes.
The monk was speechless. The Master said: "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! You liar who speaks empty words! [The monk] asked:

"What is the path that leads upward? The Master said: "In the morning look to the southeast; in the evening look to the northwest. [The monk] asked: "Without involving trivialities, please, Master, speak. The Master said: "Three."
The sections are different. We shall address the first now; as the subsequent text is extensive, we shall proceed on the coming day.

A question was asked: "What is the intent of the teachings? The Master said: "Give me back your question. He pressed further: "I do not yet know, Reverend, how you would speak. The Master said: [Silence].
"Hūṃ. Hūṃ. I dare not hope for anything extraordinary from you; you have not even accepted my words. A monk asked, "What is 'appointing to office according to one's capacity'?
The Master said, "Do not appoint. The monk pressed, "Why do you not appoint? The Master said, "They are of the same class as frogs.
Another monk came forward and requested, "Please, Master, speak. The Master said, "Do not disturb the common people. Raising children..."
"I know my father's kindness. Do you understand? The monk asked, "What is it that one knows only after raising a child—that the father is kind? The Master said, "A heart that does not betray others;
a face without shame. A monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. The monk pressed further.
"No. The Master said, "Tsk! This frog—how can it have such evil karma? A questioner asked, "I, this student, have a doubt; I beg the Master to resolve it for me.
The Master said, "A single palm does not clap loudly. The student replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A single thread cannot form a bundle."
[The Master] led him out himself. [The student] asked, "I beg the Master’s instruction regarding the direct shortcut. The Master said, "Someone already asked about this this morning.

[The student] pressed further, saying, "Setting aside for a moment what was asked this morning, please speak for me, Master. The Master said, "At the head of the triple gate, the market smiths and the *vajra*-bearers;
the little sons of foot-soldiers toss coins. [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the Teachings? The Master said, "A single question."
[The Master] did not raise it again. A question was asked: "What is the teaching of the one lifetime? The Master said: "Shang Daren. Qiu Yiji. [The questioner] asked again.
"What is urgent? The Master said, "I shall answer your question. [The monk] further asked, "What is the most urgent within the urgent?

The Master said, "In heart, he does not betray others; on his face, there is no color of shame. A question was asked: "Regarding the 'Eight Non-Accomplishments,' what are these scriptural passages?
The Master snapped his fingers once and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The infinite superior causes from all the lectures and praises above—look!
A frog leaps up into the sky; an earthworm dashes across the Eastern Sea. A question was asked: "What is the hawk? The Master... [remained silent].
[The Master] said, "This dead sparrow. The student asked, "What is the 'hawk's mechanism'? The Master said, "Yesterday there was a monk who chased it away;
today you have come here again. The student asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Master said:

The Emperor issued an edict demoting an official of the court. [The Emperor] asked: "What is the single phrase prior to the pivot? The Master said: "I shall ask you one question to let you grope for it.
[The Emperor] further asked: "Is it not just this? The Master said: "Playing the lute for a cow. [The Emperor] asked: "At the very moment of speaking, how is it?
The Master said: "Why have you fallen into speech? [The Emperor] further asked: "Where is the place where one falls into speech? The Master said: [Silence].
"Charged with the offense, he was sent to Yuzhou ten thousand *li* away to serve his sentence. The Master asked, "The assembly is gathered like clouds; what should we discuss?
The Master said, "Which monk has brought a question here? As the student raised his head, the Master struck him, saying:
The old monk, however, does not do it that way. [The student] asked, "I do not know, Master, how you would ask?

Washing rice with water. A question was asked: "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]? The Master said: "The text below is long. He also said: "I am ashamed that you have asked. The student pressed further:

[The student] quotes the scripture. The Master says, "When will you understand, even in a donkey’s year? [The student] asks, "What is the eye of the teachings? The Master says, "Appointing to office according to one's talent.
[The student] asks, "What is the eye of the patch-robed monk? The Master says, "In the morning look to the southeast; in the evening look to the northwest."
Ascending the hall, he said: “When Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva practiced the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he believed, accepted, and practiced it.
He then asked a monk, “What was I reciting just now? The monk replied, “The Master was reciting a sutra.
The Master struck him and said, “This old veteran has no heart that betrays others, yet his face shows no sign of shame. A monk asked, “What is the teacher of all Buddhas? The Master said:
"Nail, nail, dong, dong. Bone, low, bone, old. Jin said, "I beg the Master’s compassion.
The Master said, "I ask you: how do you speak the second phrase? Jin said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Truly so! Truly so!
While the Master was sitting, a monk suddenly asked, "Please, Master, speak. The Master said, "Suru suru svāhā. [The monk] asked, "What is..."
"The pivotal point for moving upward. The Master said, "He holds court in the kingdom of Silla, yet beats the drum in the kingdom of Great Tang.
Entering the hall, he said, "The mechanism of a flash of lightning is rarely encountered; for now, let us make our living in the village of the kiln-mold. A monk asked:
"What is it like to make a living in Mokyo Village? The Master said, "Take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.

The monk asked further, "What is it like when the lightning-like faculty is rarely encountered? The Master said, "It is indeed so. A monk asked, "When it is said that the three realms are mind-only and the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only, what then?
The Master said, "Teeth clashing against teeth; bring another question. The monk was speechless. The Master [continued].
He said, "The tongue has no bones. Again, he brandished his staff and made a stroke, saying, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said:
"Kak-kaku" (Cawing bird). Question: "Without falling into the profound mechanism (*xuánjī*), please speak. The Master said:
"In thirty years of traveling as a mendicant, I have never encountered such a question. He pressed further: "I ask the Master to answer this dialogue. The Master said:
