"What? The Master said, "What are you looking for here at this old monk’s place? Quickly, pay three prostrations. He added, "Come closer;
I have already been lecturing you with all sorts of nonsense. The student stepped forward and said, "I know that the Master fears I may not be sincere. The Master said:
"The staff is not here. [The Master] struck him thirty times with the handle of the broom. A monk asked, "What was the meaning of the ancients turning earth into gold?
The Master said, "I do not speak in that way. The monk pressed further, "How would you speak it, Teacher? The Master said:
Gold turns into earth. A student asked, "I have newly entered the monastery; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "Having eaten your fill of rice, why do you speak such nonsense and inverted words? The student replied, "If it is so, then all dharmas are unobtainable."
The Master said, "How do you understand my words? The student replied, "All dharmas are unattainable. The Master struck him.
A student asked, "I have recently entered this monastic community; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "Do not let me be buried by you."
The student stepped forward and said, "I beg the Master’s compassion. The Master said, "One arrow passes beyond the Western Heaven; one is not, two are not.
There was a senior lecturer of the *Lotus Sūtra* who came and asked, "Although I lecture on the sūtra, I do not understand its underlying meaning.
I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "Awakening is reality. The third and the first, the ninth and the seventh. Before one's face and behind one's back, they are identical."
“How much have you gone? The host said, “I do not understand. I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, “Pick it up! The host asked again.
The Master said, “Mahāprajñāpāramitā. The host further said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Follow local custom when entering a region.
The host asked, “What is the meaning of the teaching? The Master said, “The Wondrous Dharma King Kinnara; the Great Dharma Kinnara.”
King Nala. The Master said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Truly, you are like an unperforated iron hammer. Come forward. The Master approached him;
the Master reached out his hand and made a sweeping gesture through the air, then asked, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand."
The Master said, "It is not here.
He ascended the hall and said, "Recognize the humble, and it is noble. A monk then asked, "In a long street, is there still anything noble?"
The Master said, “There is. The monk asked, “How is it that it is precious on the long street? The Master said, “Old ginger! Old ginger!
The monk said, “If that is so, then I have purchased it. The Master said, “One or two *liang*—give me back my three *wen*!
The monk was speechless. The Master said, “Ho! Ho! You liar and fabricator! The Master asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk [remained silent].
The monk said, "I have come from Tiantai. The Master said, "I hear it is said that the Stone Bridge has been split in two; is this so?
The monk said, "From where did the Master receive this news? The Master said, "I took you for a guest from the peak of Huading, but it turns out you are a man from the village of Pingtian.
Because he saw a newly arrived monk, the Master said, "This old monk has never spoken a second word."
The Master tested the man. "Come closer. The monk then approached. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk said, "I beg the Master to discern this for me.
The Master said, "Today the clouds are somewhat high. He then asked the monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "The Master ought to know. The Master said, "I do indeed know.

The monk said, "But tell me, from where have I come? The Master said: [Note: The text provided ends abruptly with the Master's response. In the context of classical Zen records (gong'an), the Master’s final words would typically be a non-conceptual gesture or a paradoxical statement that cuts off the monk's intellectualizing.]
A pig leaps at a circle but cannot get out. [The Master] asks a monk, "Are you a wandering monk? The monk says, "Yes.
The Master says, "As soon as it hits, the frog croaks. The monk says, "I have not yet uttered a word. The Master says, "Come, come! How would you say it?
The monk says, "Has there ever been anyone who could stop it? The Master then strikes him. He asks another monk, "Where have you recently come from?"
[The monk] stood there. The Master shouted. The monk said, "Today the old monk has been shouted at by you. The monk shouted again.
The Master said, "After three shouts and four shouts, what then? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him and said, "This fellow who plunders empty space! [He then] asked another monk:
“From where have you come? The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, “You take the ancients as your own masters. The monk shouted again. The Master said, “The talk is broken.
The monk asked, “Where, sir, is the talk broken? The Master then struck him with his staff. He then questioned another monk.
“Where have you come from? The monk said, “I ask the Master to examine me. The Master picked up his staff and said, “What do you call this?
The monk said, “I ask the Master to examine it. The Master then struck him. He asked another monk, “Where have you come from? The monk said, [“From such-and-such”].
[The Master] knew that the monk had this question in mind. The Master said, "What is it like when there is one break, two breaks, and three breaks?
The monk said, "From where did the Master obtain so many breaks? The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! This fellow deserves thirty blows.
He asked another monk, "Where have you been staying during the summer retreat? The monk folded his hands and stepped back. The Master said, "The alms bowl."
“Inside, you have lost your spoon and chopsticks; beneath the sole of your straw sandals, you have lost an ancient coin. The monk said, “I am not like that.
The Master said, “We have been entangling ourselves with you long enough, yet you still do not understand. Come, come! Tell me truly: where did you spend the summer retreat? The monk said, “Jiangxi.
The Master said, “Out of consideration for your journey from afar, I shall give you thirty blows of the staff. [He] asked a monk: “What...”
“Where have you come from? The monk said, “From Mount Jing. The Master said, “How is it that you do not observe the five precepts?
The monk said, “Where does the fault lie? The Master said, “In my place, we do not admit śrāmaṇeras. Seeing a newly arrived visitor, the Master said, “He is particularly intolerable!
The monk was at a loss and stood to one side. The Master said, “Where did you get this bunch of wild hunters?”
"Stubborn fellow! Get out! He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk stared back at him with wide-open eyes. The Master said, "A fellow who trails behind donkeys and horses.
He asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "Someone just asked me that a moment ago.
The Master said, "Why did you fail? The monk said, "Don't be mistaken. The Master said, "Go out yourself and take it with you. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from?"
The monk said, "If you recognize it, you will know its place of origin. The Master shouted, "This shrimp is trying to make a living off Old Monk Ba!
The monk said, "Do not be mistaken. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows; go out and receive them yourself.
He asked another monk, "Have you come from north of the river? The monk said, "I have recently left Jiangxi. The Master said, "Spread out your sitting cloth and prostrate."
The monk performed three prostrations and, having finished his obeisance, departed. The Master said, "Not empty! Not empty! The monk turned his head back. The Master said, "Come! Come! Draw near!
'White' is 'black'—this is precisely where one must discern. The monk was speechless. The Master asked another monk, "How many new arrivals are there?
The monk replied, "Five. The Master said, "Like a collapsing wall or melting ice. The monk said, "The Master has never before asked such a question."
The Master said, "The thief uses the stolen goods as proof. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "I knew the Master would ask this question.
The Master said, "You liar who speaks empty falsehoods! The monk said, "Wherein lies the falsehood?
The Master said, "Who shall I have eat thirty blows for this? He asked another monk, "Where were you during the summer retreat? The monk said, "Wait for the Master [to finish speaking]."
"If there is a place where you dwell, tell it to the Master. The Master said, "A fox is not of the lion's lineage; a lamp is not as bright as the sun and moon.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Vulture Peak. The Master said, "In which hall does Nirvana reside?"
The monk remained silent. The Master asked again, "Where has Kāśyapa gone? The monk said, "I do not know. The Master said, "You empty-talking liar!
Sometimes, as soon as he saw a newly arrived monk, he would say, "This is a case already settled; I grant you thirty blows. The monk would ask, "What about me?
The Master would say, "Why does the Vajra at the triple gate raise his fist? The monk [remained silent].
[The Master] said, "Even Vajra was like this. He then struck him. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from?

The monk said, "One must know that there is that which does not involve traversing a journey. The Master then scolded him, saying, "As soon as you open your mouth, you let out the stench of excrement.
A monk came to visit the Master. The Master picked up a needle and said, "Pass through both nostrils at once. The monk said, "Do not be mistaken. The Master said, "HŪṂ."
"Hūṃ! Come forward. What did you just say? The monk said, "Master, do not be mistaken. The Master said, "In India they cut off heads and arms;
here, take this and go out yourself. Sometimes, when seeing newly arrived monks, the Master would say, "How is it that you do not observe the five precepts?
The monk said, "I have never yet attended to human affairs. The Master said, "This śrāmaṇera! [The Master] asked a monk, "What is it?"
[The Master asked: "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Wuzhou. The Master said, "Have you seen Dashi Fu?
The monk said, "I have not seen him. The Master said, "He is at Shuanglin Temple. [The Master] asked another monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk said, "From Wuzhou. The Master said, "That region produces many such people. [The Master] asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "On the road just now, I already..."
Someone asked, "Once it is realized, what then? The Master said, "Why does it dissolve like ice melting here?

The monk asked, "Where does my fault lie? The Master said, "A fellow who carries his own cangue and passes judgment upon himself. He asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, [silence].
"Where have you come from? The Master said, "I am being wronged. The monk said, "If the Master knows, that is enough.

The Master said, "Carrying a cangue through the legal proceedings," and struck him. He asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "Do not mistake this one question. The Master said, "Huh?"
[The Master] said, "From Jiangxi. The monk said, "Do not err. The Master said, "Whom would you have take thirty blows?
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk gave a shout. The Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly. The monk was at a loss; the Master struck him.
He asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "I know well that the Master has this one question. The Master said, "Seven loose, eight tight—this old monk!"
“Where are your nostrils? The monk said, “Why do you, Master, ask me about my own nostrils?
The Master said, “Hūṃ! Hūṃ! I grant you thirty blows. He asked another monk, “Where have you come from? The monk said, “From Lingquan.
The Master said, “Hūṃ! Hūṃ! I grant you thirty blows. He added, “Did you just say what you said? The monk said, “Yes.”
The Master said, "Why has the Vajra at the entrance of the three gates fallen to the ground? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "I took you for a true monk;
it turns out you are nothing but a frog. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "Please, Master, discern this for me."
The Master said, "Discern it beneath your own feet. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ!
Where is there no sovereign authority? He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "I have already answered the Master incorrectly.
The Master scolded him, saying, "Take a rope and bind Master Baoshou! The monk said, "What fault do I have? The Master said, "Go! He asked another monk:
“Where have you come from? The monk said, “From Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa. The Master said, “Recently, I killed all the monks in one gate.
Is this true or not? The monk was speechless. The Master said, “This is a frog. He asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk folded his hands and stepped forward.
The Master said, "How utterly disgraceful! The monk was speechless. The Master said, "This fellow who preys on empty air.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Jiangxi. The Master said, "Is rice expensive or cheap in Jiangxi? The monk said, "I have not entered the marketplace.
The Master said, "Out of consideration for your long journey, I grant you thirty blows of the staff. He asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Jiangxi."
[The Master] said, "Come forward. The Master asked, "How far is it from here to Jiangxi? The monk said, "It has never been measured. The Master said, "The pattern is already manifest.
[The Master] asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Jiangxi. The Master said, "Where did you spend the summer retreat?
The monk said, "At Yunju. The Master said, "What instructions were given there? The monk said, "Right now, what is there to say? The Master said, "This fellow..."
A monk approached from a high place. The Master said, "Why do you speak thus? The monk asked, "What do you mean by saying that?
The Master replied, "This is the genuine 'rice-cake' style for protecting old teachers. The Master asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Jiangxi.
The Master made a gesture of striking him and said, "How many straw sandals have you worn out? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Come, come! Have you ever passed through Mei Ling Pass?"
[The Master] said, "What? The monk said, "It has passed. The Master said, "Today is a fine autumn day. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Jiangxi.
The Master said, "Is there anyone here who does not eat rice? The monk said, "There is. The Master said, "This person is one who eats rice.
He asked a monk, "Why did you not answer when I asked you about what is upon your head? The monk said, "Where was it not [asked]?"
The Master said, "I am glad you have finally emerged. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Double-Tree Grove (Śāla Grove).
The Master said, "May I ask about what happened on the road? The monk asked, "What are you asking, Preceptor? The Master said, [nothing further].
"You have not even dreamed of 'The Great Man' (Shang Daren). Get out!

The monk examining the scriptures asked the second monk, "What scripture are you reading? The monk replied, "The Prajñā Sūtra. The Master said, "Hiding one's body inside the nostrils; [where is] the alms bowl?"
The spoon and chopsticks are hidden within; the skull is exchanged within the eyes. In which sutra is this expunged?
The monk said, "I do not know in which sutra it is expunged. The Master said, "Come, come.
Just as it is said in the Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, 'The wisdom of all-knowledge is pure,' is that so? The monk said, "It is. The Master picked up his staff and said, "Do you see this?"

[The Master said: "Ma. The monk said, "This is a phenomenon of form (*rūpa-dharma*). The Master said, "If someone were to offer food to a monk who is reading a sutra, you would likewise eat along with the crowd.

“Where have you come from? The monk said, “From Shuanglin Temple. The Master said, “What did Master Fu say?

The monk said, "From where did the Master receive this news? The Master said, "Both have lost it. There was one [who said]: "Both have lost it."

The visiting monk said, "That is so, but tell me, how do you answer for yourself? The Master replied, "A shrimp cannot leap out of its basket. He then asked another monk, "What was given today?"
"Are you the one who opens the sutra? The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Apply yourself well; do not let it go wrong. The monk said, "I will not let it go wrong.
The Master said, "You will enter hell as fast as a shot arrow. He asked another monk, "Have you ever lectured on the sutras? The monk said, "I do not understand."

He asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from the midday meal. The Master said, "Bring me the offering money. The monk replied, "The Master owes me some."
"What is missing? The Master said, "The frog is crying. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "I have come from the midday meal. The Master said:
A monkey is tied to a dew-pillar. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "I have come from the midday meal. The Master said, "Beating the grass and startling the snake.
He asked another monk, "Where have you been? The monk said, "I have come from the midday meal. The Master said, "Does the donor still possess eyes?"
The monk said, “I am at fault. The Master said, “Why did you follow me? The monk was speechless.
He asked another monk, “Where have you come from? The monk said, “I have come from the midday meal. The Master said, “With what will you repay the benefactor?
The monk said, “There is no need for further words. The Master said, “A pound does not equal two taels. The monk said, “This is a matter concerning the Master himself. The Master said, “Hūṃ!”
"Hūṃ! For now, I let you off with thirty blows. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "Master, do not ask such a question in vain.
The Master said, "What can you do about that single rope upon your head? The monk said, "Do not be mistaken. The Master said, "Adding shackles to a cangue.
He asked another monk, "Where have you been? The monk said, "I have come from the midday meal. The Master said, "The donor’s eyes are blind."
The Master saw a monk looking at him and said, "How many years have you been practicing? The monk said, "Please tell me, Reverend. The Master said, "Are you even forty-six yet?
The monk said, "Don't be mistaken. The Master said, "This dead frog! He asked another monk, "How much salt and vinegar did you eat today?
The monk lifted up his alms bowl. The Master said, "What a pity! That salt and vinegar is in the cowshed!"
While making his living, he asked an elder: "Why do you not seek a place to stay? The elder said, "Throughout the entire earth, a place to stay cannot be found.
The Master said, "Why is it that the rope is in my hand? The elder said, "If the Master speaks thus, it is acceptable.
The Master said, "It is not only the skull; even the nostrils have been pierced through. He asked another elder: "What is awakening?"
The Master said, "I see that you are one of those in the monastic forests who has many mouths and cannot hold them in.
Are you the *jueli* (Dharma teacher)? Jue said, "From where did the Master receive this news? The Master said, "Feel free to leap about as you please.

Jue said, "It is not that I am unable to speak. The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! You are becoming increasingly exposed in your failure. He added, "If I were to pose a single question, it would cause you to lose your life."
He lost his life. Jue said, "Master, you must not suppress the noble to make them base. The Master said, "Suru suru svāhā. He spoke again, saying, "Come, come!
Have you ever studied the scriptures? The scriptures say that for slandering this sutra, one incurs such a crime.
What is the meaning of the scriptures? Jue said, "The scriptures do not say there is an intentional meaning. The Master said, "Entering the earth..."
[The Master] held up his staff and said, "What is this? Jue said, "A staff. The Master said, "This fellow who clings to the boiling cauldron!
He asked a monk from Hebei, "There is a Venerable Zhaozhou there; have you ever been there? The monk said, "..."
"I have recently departed from there," [the monk] said. The Master asked, "What instructions did he give to his later disciples?
The monk said, "He would usually ask a newly arrived person, 'Where have you come from? If the monk replied, 'From the South,' Zhaozhou would say, 'Go and drink tea.
The Master then laughed heartily and said, "How shameful! He then asked, "As for Zhaozhou’s meaning, what was it? The monk said, "This too is..."
[The Master] said, "Zhaozhou has been splashed by you with a ladle of dung. The monk was speechless.
Seeing the monk taking his leave, the Master asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to Jingshan.
The Master said, "Suppose someone suddenly asks you, 'How would you say a single phrase that can shut their mouth? What would you do? The monk said, "I have a phrase. The Master said, "Go!"
The Master asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk said, "I am going to pay my respects at Mount Jing.
The Master said, "This old fellow would do well to have his skull shattered. The Master saw another monk and said, "He looks exactly like a Vinaya master; he will suddenly attain enlightenment."
A single arrow pierces through a skull for three thousand *li*. When the monk attempted to assume a posture of inquiry, the Master said:
"Suru suru svāhā.
This is the third examination of a Great Master who lectures on the Sūtras and Śāstras.

The Master asked the Sangha Director (Sengzheng). The Director assented. The Master said, "Do you lecture on the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*? The Director replied, "I dare not say so; I merely read the texts when I was young.
The Master picked up a sugar cake, broke it in two, and said, "What do you call this? The Director was speechless.

Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Master Muzhou, Volume Six of the *Recorded Sayings of Ancient Venerable Masters*.
The Master was a dharma heir of Huangbo. Initially, he resided at Guanyin Monastery in Muzhou, where he constantly maintained a following of over a hundred people for several decades.
Later, he left the assembly and lived in a room at Kaiyuan Temple, where he wove straw sandals to sell in order to support his mother;
thus, people of the time called him "Chen the Straw Sandal Maker. A small portion of his sharp-edged dialogues and recorded sayings is now collected here.
The Venerable Master of Muzhou, named Daorong, was a native of Yanzhou and surnamed Chen. His record of formal monastic training is not preserved.
He received the Dharma from the Venerable Master Huangbo Yun, being thus the fourth generation descendant of Mazu. He lived during the reigns of Emperors Xuanzong and Yizong of the Tang dynasty.

"How is it when one encounters the opportune moment? The Master said, "Your feet have already departed with your whole body.

[The Master] was lighting the lamp. The Master said, "Extinguish it. The monk moved from the east to stand on the west side. The Master said, "Wild fox spirit.
A monk asked, "What is it like when one ascends to the Nine Palaces [the throne] without wielding a single blade? The Master said, "A single staff controls the imperial street;

look back after the Great White Star has passed. A monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, "Eight petals, nine cracks. A monk asked, "What is the stupa? The Master said, "Eight petals, nine cracks."

An ordinary person. The Master said: "The hair is not combed; the face is not washed. Question: "What is it like when there are no clouds ten thousand miles away? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"One cannot pass even a single step. A monk asked, "Even the sword of Mohe Mo (Molai) is regretted as being dull; what of the matter of biting the arrowhead when facing the front?
The Master said, "If you cut it, you die. The monk then gave a shout. The Master struck his knee once. The monk shouted again. The Master raised his staff.
The monk said, "Old Monk, do not impose blind shackles or deliver blind blows! Take away the staff and strike this old monk instead; do not speak thus!"
[The monk] did not speak. The Master said, "Today, for no reason, this yellow-faced man from Zhejiang has caused a scene of frustration.
The monk said, "Old Monk, do not act like a monkey. [Another] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "How could it not be the Buddha?
[Another] asked, "To cherish the ancestral style and protect the Three Vehicles—what is the Way? The Master said, "What more do you expect to see in a dream?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "All the patriarchs and buddhas of the past have spoken exactly like this. At that time, a monk asked, "What did they say? The Master said, "How great!
A monk asked, "If a person of the highest capacity comes, will you still receive them, Master? The Master said, "I shall receive them. The monk said, "Then please receive me, Reverend.

The Master said, "This is the fault of this old fellow," and he immediately descended from his seat. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Harvest in autumn, [store for winter]."

[The Master] said, "The storehouse. A question was asked: "What is the true master of Baoying? The Master said, "The ladle is large; the bowl is small. A question was asked: "What is the water of Baoying? The Master said, "Clear.
[The questioner] said, "And what of the one who drinks it? The Master said, "Clear. A question was asked: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?

"What? The Master struck him. A monk asked, "Are the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "Minister Huang and Chancellor Li. The monk said, "I do not understand.

The Mute asked, "I request that the Master provide a definitive judgment. The Master said, "First cross the Muli River. He asked, "What is it like when one floats or sinks according to nature?

"How is it when practicing? The Master said, "A dot. He asked, "How is it when one ascends to the Nine-and-Five Throne without wielding even an inch of blade?

The Master said, "The season declines as the severe cold departs; flesh and bone grow thin and cold. [This was] while the Master was serving at Nan-yuan.
One day, the Head Gardener went to the garden, and Nan-yuan asked him, "How do you discuss 'a single blow' in the South?
The Master said, "We discuss it as something extraordinary. After a long silence, the Master then asked, "How do you discuss it here in this monastery, Preceptor?"
Nanyuan raised his staff and said, "The patience of non-arising beneath the staff; when facing the critical moment, do not yield to the Master.
At these words, the Master attained a sudden and great enlightenment. Nanyuan said, "You have come by the power of your vows to shoulder the Great Dharma;
this was no mere coincidence. Have you heard the words of Linji as he was about to pass away? He replied, "I have heard them. Nanyuan said, "Linji said: 'Who knows my True Dharma...'"
"The Eye-treasury was extinguished before this blind donkey. Throughout his life, he was like a lion; whenever he encountered a person, he would kill them.
Yet when he was about to die, why did he kneel and tuck his tail in such a manner? He replied, "As the time for the secret transmission drew near, the master himself was extinguished.
He asked again, "Why did Sansheng also remain silent? He replied, "He was a true son who had personally received the transmission upon entering the room."
"This is not like the common traveler outside the gate," Nan-yuan nodded in agreement. He asked again, "You speak of the four kinds of critical examination (*liaojian*). What dharma do you examine?
He replied, "If ordinary speech does not stagnate in ordinary sentiment, one immediately falls into the understanding of the sages. This is the great malady of students."
The former sages took pity on them and applied skillful means, like using one wedge to extract another. It was said: "What is it to take away the person but not the environment?
He replied: "A golden ball fresh from the red furnace; it shatters the iron face of the *jiaoluo*. Again he asked:

"What is it to take away the environment but not the person? He replied: "The straw mats have just been spread and the head is split open; amidst the first parting of the chaotic clouds, the shadow still lingers."
[The Master] remained silent. Again, he asked: "What is 'both person and environment being snatched away'? He replied: "Stepping forward with bated breath, one must be swift;
urging the whip against the harness, do not delay. Again, he asked: "What is 'neither person nor environment being snatched away'? He replied:
"I always remember the third month in Jiangnan, where the *shègū* birds cry and the hundred flowers are fragrant. Again, he asked: "Linji had three phrases. On that day..."
Question: "What is the first phrase? Linji said: "The seal of the three essentials opens; the vermilion dot is narrow.
Before you can even deliberate, host and guest are distinguished. The Master let out a shout as soon as these words were spoken. Question again: "What is the second phrase? Linji said:
"How could one who possesses wondrous understanding fail to resolve the questions of Asanga? How could Upāya fail to respond to the karmic capacity that cuts off the flow?
The Master said, "It was already wrong before you even asked. He asked again, "What is the third phrase? Linji said, "Just look at the puppets being performed on the stage;
their every movement depends entirely on the person inside pulling the strings. The Master said, "If it is exposed by clarity, it is no longer fit. Thereupon, Nanyuan considered him worthy.
Thus he served Linji, not failing the intentions with which his late master Xinghua had entrusted him.
The Master stayed for six years, and then Nan-yuan passed away. In the second year of the Changxing era of the Later Tang dynasty, he traveled south to the Ru River.
There he saw several thatched huts nestled against a mountain, looking like the home of fugitives. He asked an old farmer, "What place is this? The farmer replied, "The Old Feng."

At Xueji Temple, the world had long maintained the Vinaya precepts. When the abbot passed away and a famine occurred that year, the community abandoned the site and departed, leaving behind nothing but Buddhist statues, drums, and bells.
The Master said, "May I dwell here? A farmer replied, "You may. The Master then entered and took up residence.

During the day he begged for alms in the villages; at night he burned pine resin for light. Remaining alone for seven years, lay devotees renovated the site until it became a flourishing monastic center.

In the second year of the Tiānfú era of the Jìn dynasty, the governor of the prefecture heard of his reputation and received him with the utmost courtesy. On the first day of the Upper Yuan festival, he established the Nányuàn lineage.
In the second year of the Qiányù era of the Hàn dynasty, the governor transferred his post to Yǐngzhōu; the Master again fled from bandits and went to rely upon him.

The governor provided him lodging in the prefectural study hall, where the Master ascended the seat and said: "The Patriarch’s Mind-Seal is like the mechanism of an iron ox: when it departs, it leaves its imprint."
"Abide! Abiding is precisely the breaking of the seal. "It is simply this: neither going nor abiding. The seal is itself; the non-seal is itself.
At that time, the Elder Lu-po came forward and asked, "I possess the capacity of the Iron Ox; I request that you, Master, do not apply the seal to me. The Master said:

"Accustomed to fishing for whales and leviathans in the vast depths, I now sigh at the frog-like steps that stumble in the mud. While Lupei stood there lost in thought, the Master shouted, "Elder, why do you not offer a word?
As Lupei hesitated, the Master struck him with his whisk and asked, "Do you still remember the pivot of the dialogue?
Try to bring it forth. As Lupei was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the whisk. The Herdsman said:
"I know with certainty that the Buddha-dharma and the royal law are one and the same. The Master asked, "Governor, what principle have you perceived?
The Governor replied, "When it is necessary to cut, if one does not cut, one will instead suffer from the resulting chaos. Thereupon, the Master descended from his seat.

After the rebellion was quelled, there was a Grand Master Song in Ruzhou who offered his residence to be converted into a monastery, naming it Xinsi (New Monastery), and invited the Master to reside there. His Dharma assembly became preeminent throughout the land, and his disciples...
He arrived from afar. In the first year of the Guangshun era of the Zhou dynasty, the temple was granted the name Guanghui. The Master resided there for twenty-two years.
On the first day of the eighth month of the sixth year of the Kaibao era of the Great Song (the *guiyou* year), he ascended the seat and spoke this verse:
"The Way lies in seizing the opportune moment to save all beings; From distant lands, those who admire it come in a surging tide. In years to come, there will be an old man whose heart..."
He was like this: every day he offered incense and every night he lit lamps. On the fifteenth day, he passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.
On the day before, he had written a letter of parting for his patrons. He lived seventy-eight years and spent fifty-nine summer retreats in meditation.
Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Seven;
Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Eight:
The Recorded Sayings of Master Nian of Shou Shan in Ru Zhou (the ninth generation descendant of Nanyue, successor to Fengxue).
The Master’s name was Xingnian; he was the son of the Di family of Lai Prefecture. Upon entering the monastery, he ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddha-dharma has been entrusted to kings, great ministers, and powerful patrons, so that the Dharma may not be severed and the lamps may continue from one to another down to this day.
O Great Assembly, tell me: what is it that continues? After a long silence, he said: 'Today, it must be my elder brother Kāśyapa.'"

[The Master] first attained it. At that time, a monk asked: "What is different about this assembly at Mount Ling today compared to the one of old? The Master said: "Falling into pits and falling into ditches.
The monk asked: "Why is it so? The Master said: "Blind! A monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whom do you follow in the lineage of the ancestral wind? The Master said:
"Personally transmitted and shown before the cliff of Shaoshi. The monk said: "Please, let us hear one more note in a resonant voice."
The Master said, "I must have everyone know this now. A question was asked: "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "A single word cuts off the mouths of a thousand rivers; only before a ten-thousand-fathom peak does one attain the profound. A question was asked: "What is the realm of Shoushan?"
The Master said, "Leave it for everyone to see. A monk asked, "What is one within the realm? The Master said, "Have you even finished eating the staff yet?
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Wait for another time to eat the staff. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "At the edge of the city of King Chu, the Ru River flows eastward. The monk asked, "What is the intimate [instruction] for a student?"

[The monk] said, “At this place. The Master said, “On the final day of the fifth and ninth months, spring is encountered again. The monk asked, “Ultimately, what is the matter? The Master said, “Winter arrives;

it is the hundred-and-fifth day of the Cold Food Festival. [The monk] asked, “When the Minister of State stands by the seat, he prays that the Patriarchal lineage from the West will be proclaimed and exalted.

The Master said, “The King and his ministers have made three requests; today I respond. The myriad people enjoy their occupations and all are at peace. The monk said, “With [the Master],” [he continued].
"If that is so, then the clouds of compassion moisten everywhere, and all places are permeated. The Master said, "The rustic old man sings his songs, and everyone of these times joins in the chant.
He spoke again, "Venerable elders, there is not much to the Buddha-dharma; it is simply that you yourselves lack sufficient self-confidence."
If you can attain confidence within yourself, even if a thousand sages were to appear before you, they would have no place to set their teeth. Why?
It is simply because you have attained confidence for yourself and do not run outward in search of it; therefore, they cannot do anything about it.
Even if Śākyamuni Buddha himself were to arrive here, he too would receive thirty blows of the staff. That being so, as for the beginner and the one who has realized the ultimate...
"What principle do you rely upon for your study? Let me ask you all: have you yet attained such a state? After a long silence, he said:
"If you have attained such a state, you must act accordingly. There is nothing more to it. Be careful."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Where do all the sages of antiquity practice? The Master said, "Plowing the furrows and pulling the plow.

The monk asked, "What was the meaning of the ancients raising their mallets and brandishing their fly-whisks? The Master said, "On the solitary peak, there is no guest to lodge. The monk said, [further]...
“I do not yet understand your meaning,” [the monk] said. The Master said, “I am no one who sits waiting by a stump. [The monk] asked, “What is the path of Bodhi?
The Master said, “Five li from here to Xiang County. [The monk] asked, “As for that which transcends this, what is it? The Master said, “Coming and going is no easy matter.”

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is Shoushan? The Master said, "The eastern mountain is high; the western mountain is low. The monk asked, "What is it like to be among the people of the mountains?
The Master said, "It happens that the staff is not here. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "In the brazier there is fire, though no one stirs it; everywhere there is no trace, so wander as you please. The monk [bowed].
[The Master] said: "What is it like to be one on the Way? The Master said: "Sitting and watching the beauty of the mists and clouds; they do not equal the white clouds. [Someone] asked:
"At the place where all the sages have failed to reach, I request the Master to proclaim it. The Master said: "My spiritual light shines everywhere for ten thousand miles;
who dares to rival the sun’s disk? [Someone] asked: "When the body and mind of a student gather or disperse, what is it like? The Master said: "I do not hear [it]."
The sound of celestial music resounded. A monk asked, "How does one gather [the mind) back? The Master said, "Do not follow the shifting of the four seasons.

A monk asked, "What is it like when a Bodhisattva has not yet attained Buddhahood? The Master said, "Sentient beings. The monk asked, "What is it like after attaining Buddhahood? The Master said, "Sentient beings."
Sentient beings. A monk asked, "Before the awakening flowers have bloomed, how does one discern the reality? The Master said, "If it is not cold in winter, look after the end of the year.
The monk said, "Is this not it? The Master said, "Wrong. A monk asked, "When the six kingdoms have not yet been pacified, what is it like?
The Master said, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "And after they are pacified, what is it like? The Master said, "The great earth breaks into flames. A monk asked, "The Jewel..."
[The monk] asked, "How is it when the sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard? The Master said, "Whom do you resent? The monk said, "How is it after it has emerged from the scabbard?

The Master said, "One does not execute those who are innocent. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Execute! [Another monk] asked, "How is it when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard?

The Master said, "It is still tolerable as long as you do not begrudge [your life]. The monk said, "How is it after it has emerged? The Master said, "I humbly submit that [you are already dead]. (伏惟尚)

[The Master] said, "I grant you this. A monk asked, "What if one suddenly encounters the time of the lion's roar? The Master said, "Let the jackal howl as it pleases. The monk then shouted. The Master said, "As expected.

The monk shouted again. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. The monk bowed. The Master said: **Xiang.** A monk asked, "What if one suddenly encounters the time of the lion’s roar? The Master said, "Let the jackal howl as it pleases. The monk then shouted. The Master said, "As expected. The monk shouted again. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. The monk bowed. The Master said:
"You blind fellow! He spoke again: "Venerable elders, you must not shout blindly or shout recklessly.
Here, I have always told you: when there is a guest, there is always a guest; when there is a host, there is always a host. A guest is never two guests; a host is never two hosts.
If there were two guests or two hosts, they would simply be two blind fellows. Therefore, if I stand, you must sit."
"If I sit, you must stand; if I sit, we shall sit together; if I stand, we shall stand together.
Even so, when it comes to this point, you must keep your eyes wide open. If your gaze wavers for even an instant, you will be ten thousand miles away.
Why is this so? It is like looking at a horseman through a window; as soon as you hesitate, there is no connection.
All you venerable seniors, since you have set your minds upon this, you must be thorough and precise; do not seek empty flattery, for it will deceive you on another day or at another time.
If you all have something to ask, come forward; if you have nothing, take care.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said, "Pervading heaven and pervading earth.

The monk asked, "What is it like after it has emerged? The Master said, "A groundless field of sorrow. The monk asked, "If one kills one's father and kills one's mother, one repents before the Buddha."
[The monk asked: "If one kills the Buddha and kills the patriarchs, where can one repent? The Master said: "The water is ten feet deep. [The monk] asked:
"Transcending both the ordinary and the sage—please grant me a single phrase, Master. The Master said: "Do not wrongly blame this old monk. The monk said: "Thank you for your instruction, Master."
The Master struck him. [The monk] asked, "How is it before the fish-drum has sounded? The Master said, "Gazing at heaven, one does not see heaven. The monk said, "How is it after it has sounded?
The Master said, "Looking at the earth, one does not see the earth. [The monk] asked, "The Master is a great *kalyāṇamitra*;
why then do you go to Shoushan? The Master said, "I do not sit atop the solitary peak; I always accompany the white clouds in leisure. [The monk] asked, "Regarding the fourfold assembly..."
[The monk] surrounded [the master]. "What Dharma does the Master teach? The Master said, "Beating the grass is only intended to startle the snake.

The monk asked, "I do not yet know how you apply the hand. The Master said, "Just now, you nearly lost your life and body. [The monk] asked, "Without falling into the 'three inches,' I pray the Master will speak quickly.
The Master said, "When it comes to this point, even I cannot say anything. You, Reverend, speak! The monk said, "It still falls [into the trap]."

"Three inches. Please, Master, speak further. The Master said, "Shoushan has lost ground today. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Shoushan? The Master said, "A thousand flowers stand out in splendor;
a single leaf remains ever fragrant. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Better not to have such good things at all.
A monk asked, "When causes and conditions are not yet ripe, what then? The Master said, "Advance. The monk said, "When they are ripe..."
"What then? The Master said, "Withdraw. Question: "When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the winner? The Master said, "The winner loses."
The monk said, "What about when one cannot? The Master said, "Where is the pearl? The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "Vimalakīrti remained silent; what was the meaning of that? The Master said, "Rare is the guest who pierces his own ear; many are those who mark the boat's edge.
A monk asked, "What is the speech of Shoushan for leaving the body? The Master said, "Who can obstruct it?"
The monk said, "In that case, one may go with ease. The Master said, "If you go, I shall break your back.
The Master then said, "To attain intimacy, first of all, do not bring questions to ask. Do you understand? The question is at the place of the answer;
the answer is at the place of the question. If you bring a question to ask, I am already beneath your feet. If you hesitate, you are lost."
Negotiation. At that time, a monk came forward to prostrate, and the Master struck him. The monk asked, "What is it like when hanging one's staff in a secluded crag?
The Master said, "Wrong. The monk said, "Wrong," and the Master struck him again.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "All day long one is in a state of bustle; yet that matter is never obstructed. What is that matter? The Master said:
"A thousand flowers flourish atop the solitary peak; one walks upon ten-thousand-fathom crags. The monk said: "Is this not precisely where you, Master, benefit others?
The Master said: "The assembly sings and chants as they escort him away; across the thousand peaks he shall never return. The monk said: "Return!"
“How is it with the matter that has come? The Master said, “Even if my bones were ground to powder and my body shattered, I would still not have repaid [your kindness].
Once every three years, they send money and goods. The monk bowed. The Master said, “Heh! Heh! A monk asked, “All Buddhas emerge from this sutra.”

The monk asked, “I do not yet know from whence this sutra emerges. The Master said, “Lower your voice. Lower your voice. The monk asked, “How should it be received and upheld? The Master said, “One must by no means defile it.
The monk asked, “By performing what deeds and practices can one repay the four debts of gratitude and the three realms of existence? The Master said:
“Murdering and setting fires. The monk said, “In that case, he is a person of great deeds. The Master said, “How bitter and painful!
A monk asked, “After the World-Honored One’s parinirvāṇa, to whom was the Dharma entrusted? The Master said, “What an excellent question! No one can answer it.
The monk asked, “What is the ‘unspeakable speaking’ of the World-Honored One? The Master said, “Let the vast ocean change as it may; I shall never speak for your sake.”
[The Master] said, “It penetrates. A monk asked, “What is ‘Kāśyapa hearing that which cannot be heard’? The Master said, “A deaf man needlessly tilts his ears.
A monk asked, “An ancient said, ‘When you see form, you see the mind. Since all dharmas are formless, with what will one see?
The Master said, “When one house has business, a hundred houses are busy. The monk said, “I do not understand; I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, “Look after three days.”
[The Master] took [the staff]. A questioner asked: "When one enters the capital to pay court to the Sovereign, yet returns immediately upon reaching Tongguan Pass, what is this?

The Master said: "He is still a dull-witted fellow. A questioner asked: "When meeting a man who has attained the Way on the road, one does not respond with speech or silence. I wonder, with what then does one respond?"
The Master said, "In a mere flash, the three thousand worlds. The monk said, "If that is so, then even looking with one's eyes is unnecessary.

The Master said, "The imperial grace has not yet been encountered; once regret sets in, it is difficult to pursue. A monk asked, "What is it like when someone comes brandishing a Mohe-mo sword to take the Master’s head?
The Master let out a single sigh. The monk said, "How painful! The Master then struck him. A monk asked, "What is it like when one obtains a boat and crosses immediately? The Master—
[The Master] said, "He is still a dull-witted fellow. A monk asked, "If one were to borrow a question as a mere pretext, how would it be?
The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. A monk asked, "I have long been in poverty; I beg the Master for relief. The Master said, "No relief. The monk asked, "Why do you not relieve me?
The Master said, "Have you finished eating your blows yet? He struck him immediately upon these words. A monk asked, "What is the ancient [Way]?"

[The monk asked about] the Buddha-mind. The Master said, “A radish from Zhenzhou weighs three catties. [Another] asked, “What kind of thing is contained within the Dragon Palace and the Ocean Treasury?
I ask the Master for a unique distinction. The Master said, “It does not hang upon a three-inch tongue.

The monk asked, “Why does it not hang upon a three-inch tongue? The Master said, “Who knows that which is intimate after the phrase? [Another] asked, “If one does not fall into the *asaṃkhyeya* [kalpas], how does one cultivate and realize? The Master said, “Nearby.”
"Come forward; I will tell you. The monk stepped forward, and the Master struck him. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of Danxia covering his ears and Huangbo holding up his staff?
The Master said, "You do not ask while sitting in meditation; this would exhaust your entire life. The monk said, "Rarely encountered and difficult to meet;
I pray the Master will give me instruction. The Master said, "Do not let the bowl ring. A monk asked, "What is the substance of empty space? The Master said: "..."
"The old monk is under your feet. The monk asked, "Why is the Master under this student's feet?
The Master said, "I know you are a blind fellow. A question was asked: "As for the Master saying, 'The old monk is under your feet,' what is the meaning?
The Master said, "Lying across the body, one does not fear wading through mud and water; only those who recognize it know a true master. A question was asked: "As for..."
The Master said, "I know you are a blind man. What then? The Teacher said, "I offer you a treasure, yet you do not recognize it;
instead, you cause the blind man to fall into total blindness. A monk asked, "What is the center of the profound mystery?
The Master said, "If there are words, one must speak them. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Without words, even ghosts will be angry. A monk asked, "What is..."
“An eye of the patch-robed monk. The Master said, “This question is improper. The monk asked, “If it were proper, what then? The Master said, “It would be fit for such a thing.
A monk asked, “How can one leave behind all conditions? The Master said, “Once in a thousand years. The monk asked, “What about when one does not leave them behind?
The Master said, “Standing before the multitude. A monk asked, “What is it like before the Buddhas have appeared? The Master said, “Pick it up.”
The spoon does not grasp the chopsticks. A monk asked, "What is it like after seeing? The Master said, "While eating, one forgets the spoon.
A monk asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said, "One must not wrongly blame this old monk. The monk said, "And what is it like after he appeared?"
The Master said: "I shall present this to all people under heaven. A monk asked: "What is the phrase that transcends Vairocana and expresses the discourse of Śākyamuni?
The Master said: "Wondrous words are not many; to whom would one personally present these words? The monk asked: "What is it like when all is serene?"
The Master said, "If you have not clearly realized the truth of the mind-ground, it will be difficult to pass the barrier of Shoushan. As the monk prepared to offer a word, the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "What is a person who dwells in great peace and bliss? The Master said, "Not seeing a single dharma. The monk said, "By what means do you designate a person?
The Master said, "Thank you, Reverend, for grasping the meaning of my words. A monk asked, "What is a person who is always present? The Master said, "Running about in confusion."
"What are you doing? The monk asked, "How is it when not even a single hair has been raised? The Master said, "A traveler with pierced ears encountered on the road.

The monk asked, "How is it after it has been raised? The Master said, "There is no need for further hesitation. The monk asked, "Regarding this melody on the stringless lute, I request the Master’s rendition of its tones."
The Master remained silent for a long while and said, "Did you hear it? The monk said, "I did not hear it. The Master said, "Why did you not ask in a loud voice? [The monk] asked.
"The Great Compassionate One with a Thousand Hands and Eyes—what is the True Eye? The Master said, "Right then, it is blind. The monk asked, "After it is blind, what then?
The Master said, "Reaching for heaven and groping on the ground. A monk asked, "What is the mouth of the Master that preaches the Dharma?
The Master said, "It hangs on the wall. The monk asked, "If someone suddenly comes and asks, what then? The Master said, "Wait for me to take it down."
"When you return, I shall tell you. A monk asked, "If a student does not realize it here, and intends to go south, what then?
The Master said, "Quickly! The monk said, "But if one does not go in that manner, what then? The Master said, "Though you may meet [him] later, you will understand. [The monk] asked.
"What is the phrase that transcends both the ordinary and the sage? The Master said, "National Teacher An of Mount Song.
The monk asked, "Is this not the ultimate point of the Master himself? The Master said, "Master Let of Mount Nanyue. The monk asked, "What is the Master’s house style?
The Master said, "A puppet made of thread; there is someone pulling it. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has been pulled? The Master said: [silence].
"Subtle existence is beyond words; it cannot be measured. The monk asked, "What is 'subtle existence is beyond words; it cannot be measured'?
The Master said, "If there are words, one must obtain the phrase. The monk asked, "What is 'a puppet made of no thread, yet someone pulls the strings'? The Master said:
"One must first clarify the ancestral path before one’s descendants can find a place to dwell. A monk asked, "I am a student who has newly entered the monastery; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "Venerable brother, how long have you been in this old monk's assembly? The monk replied, "I have spent the winter and passed through the summer."
The Master said, "Do not misrepresent this to others. A monk asked, "If there is a person who comes having exhausted everything, will you still receive him?
The Master said, "Exhausting everything is fine; but who is that one person? The monk said, "The wind is high and the moon is cold.

The Master said, "How many people are sitting and lying in the Sangha hall? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "I have been deceived by this old monk. A monk asked, "The student seeks to go forth."
"How is the state of the world? The Master said, "Borrow water and offer flowers first as an offering; do not let it be too late that you must demand money for incense.
The monk said, "Matters of life and death are great. I beg the Master for a single memorial service. The Master said, "The traces have leaked through; there is no path left to flee."
The monk said, "In that case, he has caught you. The Master said, "Today I have arrived in Chang'an.

A monk asked, "The Tathāgata expounds the teachings of the Three Vehicles; I wonder what kind of teaching this is? The Master said, "Of a thousand words, not one hits the mark. The monk said, [and remained silent].
"Why is it that among a thousand words not one hits the mark? The Master said, "One who is not a person caught on the hook. A questioner asked, "All phenomena are empty;
how does one awaken to the principle of true emptiness? The Master said, "In the south, bamboo shoots sprout first; in the north, one wears a fur cloak."
The monk said, “Is it not that one must avoid falling into right and wrong? The Master said, “Look for yourself. A monk asked, “Do the lush green bamboo have Buddha-nature or not?
The Master said, “South of heaven, north of earth. The monk said, “In that case, you are investigating the principles of the Buddha.
The Master said, “North of earth, south of heaven. A monk asked, “What is it like before the bells and drums have sounded? The Master said, “Before you even ask.”
Ming asked about "striking after calling. As the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout. A monk asked, "What is the single lamp before Kāśyapa’s gate?
The Master said, "A solitary peak and a bright moon shine across the heavens; its nature is like a cold spring, pure to the very bottom.

The Verse on Guest and Host:
Having awakened through realization, one awakens from within delusion; delusion and awakening have never been distinct or divergent.

Only now do I know that from the beginning to the end, up until this very moment, there is no separate path connecting past and present. There is no separate path—do not ask others about it. To speak of past and present is merely to inquire about matters of the future.
The original is the host. Following others, one asks about guest and host; when the guest is recognized, it is entirely the host.
Guest within the host, host within the guest—they are employed interchangeably without confusion. Guest within the guest, host within the host—these two functions are used;
do not yield to the host. Grasping heaven and earth, act as the great host; allowing no room for deliberation, the entire body is severed. Only then can one be named the "host within the host."
I have composed three verses:
