[The student] asked, "What is the host within the host? The Master said, "Ten thousand miles away, no companion. [The student] asked, "What is 'taking the person but not taking the circumstances'?"
[The student asks about] the "object" (*viṣaya*). The Master says, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. [The student asks,] "What is 'seizing the object but not seizing the person'?
The Master says, "A foreigner loses his felt tent. [The student asks,] "What is 'seizing both the person and the object'? The Master says, "What Buddhas or patriarchs are there?
[The student asks,] "What is 'neither seizing the person nor seizing the object'? The Master says, "The question and answer are very clear. [The student] asks, "What is 'first illuminating, then..."
[The student] asked about "function" (*yòng*). The Master said: "A towering peakhead is struck by a great fire; within the city of Chang'an, not a breath of wind passes. [The student] asked:
"What is 'illumination and function occurring simultaneously'? The Master said: "On the towering peakhead there is no great fire; within the city of Chang'an no person travels. [The student] asked:
"What is 'illumination and function not occurring simultaneously'? The Master said: "Yesterday was the fifteenth; today is the sixteenth."

The eminent scholar Zhang Maochong asked: "Regarding the arrival of Kāśyapa Mātanga in the Han, the accounts have already become overly elaborate. As for Bodhidharma’s ‘single transmission,’ I beg the Master to provide instruction.
The Master said: "If winter were not cold, you would see it after the year has passed.

He asked: "The five eyes do not behold his countenance; the two ears do not hear his resonance. Is it within sound and form? Or is it beyond sound and form? The Master said: "From where does your question come?"
Question: "Looking for it, it is ahead; suddenly, it is behind. What, then, is this thing? The Master said: "It strikes right against your nostrils. Question: [Continues]...

"If one can transform things, one is identical to the Tathāgata. The myriad phenomena are 'things'; how can they be transformed? The Master said, "Having eaten your meal, you possess not a shred of intelligence.
A questioner asked, "Beating the mallet and raising the whisk are both merely words to stop a child's crying.
Raising an eyebrow or blinking an eye is not yet the mechanism of a true adept. What is the immediate, present utilization? The Master said, "The morning court session has already been dismissed."
He came out later in the evening. [The student] asked: "There is not a thread of silk to hang upon; the net of the Dharma is boundless.

Why, then, do you distinguish between delusion and awakening? The Master said: "Two buckets on one carrying pole. [The student] asked: "The mind follows the objects, and the objects follow the arising of the mind.

When both mind and objects are forgotten, where is that [state]? The Master said: "Wait until you have attained awakening before you will understand. [The student] asked: "Sentient beings have function; insentient things have no function. If..."
"What is the application of the insentient? The Master said, "The single-leafed door opens day and night. Question:
"The Dharma should even be relinquished, how much more so that which is not-Dharma. What is that which is not-Dharma? The Master said, "Eating porridge, eating rice. Question:
"In the river of craving, one floats and then sinks; in the sea of suffering, one emerges and then submerges. How can one emerge from this? The Master said, "Wrong."
Morning assembly. He addressed the assembly, saying: "The moon has not yet set, and the sun has already risen. All phenomena are still and silent; where is there anything that is not clear?
Since it is clear, how do you express this one phrase of clarity? After a long silence, he said: "The sun and moon shine upon the shadowless tree;
there is no need to hold it fast as one walks the streets."

Addressing the assembly: In question and answer, you must be taught so that the beginning and end are complete; otherwise, with a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail, you merely deceive yourself. Like a king wielding a sword, it depends entirely on the king’s intent;
like a mirror set upon a stand, it requires the cessation of all observation. To open one's mouth is already to travel thousands of miles;

to lower one's head in deliberation is to encounter ten thousand layers of gates. If you point to others without the true eye, how could it be anything less than becoming a jackal on your future path?
Ascending the hall, he said: "Morning after morning the drum resounds; night after night the bell tolls. All manner of people are gathered together—what further matter is there?
The sages of the past accomplished this very gate, and each of you venerable elders lacks nothing. I myself am already incapable of discerning good from evil;
yet you venerable elders wish to consume more pungent flavors and undergo further suffering."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When there is no matter, do not create one.

Return to the hall. Ascending the hall again, he said: "As soon as the bells and drums cease, host and guest are already distinguished. When the assembly comes together, both illumination and function are fully realized.
If you can understand it in this way, you will continue the lineage of the ancients; if you cannot understand it, you will truly be at a loss. Is there anyone here who understands?"
"Come forth and provide evidence before the assembly.
He ascended the hall and said, "Be careful not to miss it. He returned to the hall for tea.
Ascending the hall again, he said, "If you can utter the first phrase, it will burst forth from within the stone. If you can utter the second phrase, it shall be brought out by your inquiry."
"Come. If you can speak the third phrase, you will not even be able to save yourself.
Return to the hall. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you only obtain the root, do not worry about the branches. What is the root for you, venerable monks?
Is it coming and going, bowing to the Buddha and the stupa, entering the room and adjusting your robes, or indulging in joy and laughter? If you recognize this..."
"Are these four elements and five aggregates not the state of entering quiescence and stilling thought? Are they neither emerging nor entering, neither gathering nor dispersing?
Having understood this, you recognize the spirit. "What is the essence of the Venerable One? After a long silence, he said, "Return to the hall."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring scenery is mild and warm; all things are reviving and flourishing. The mountains are green and the waters are clear—truly a fit place for nurturing the Way.
For wandering Zen practitioners, this is most opportune. As for the ancestral style of the Buddhas, I am glad there is no interference with it. A monk stood in attendance.
The Master said, "I have already scattered sand into the eyes of you all. Now, I dare not fail to recognize good from evil.
[He] returned to the hall. A question was asked: "When it is cold, it is cold; when it is hot, it is hot. Is the cold one right? Is the hot one right? The Master said:
"The puppet on the end of the marionette pole is constantly being manipulated. [The student] asked: "Every day you open your sitting mat and spread out your alms bowl;

how do you repay the kindness of the donors? The Master said: "This one question of yours has nearly driven me to despair. [The student] said: "If that is so, then I shall thank you for your offerings."
The Master said, “What kind of power have you gained? The monk bowed. The Master said, “Tomorrow you shall have another meal.
He ascended the hall and said, “The spring scenery is mild and warm; the spring rain is universally moistening. All things sprout buds—where is there that does not receive this grace?
Tell me, how do you express the single phrase of receiving this grace? After a long silence, he said, “A drop of spring rain is slippery.”
[The Master said: "It is like oil. A questioner asked: "What is the Dharma-body of the student himself? The Master said: "Carrying firewood every day is no easy task.
The questioner said: "That belongs to the assembly. What is the student’s own [Dharma-body]? The Master said: "Sixty kalpas in three lifetimes. A questioner asked:
"Why are the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion here? The Master said: "What do you see? The questioner said: "In that case..."
[The monk] said, "Then there are the thousands, tens of millions, and billions of transformation bodies. The Master said, "For now, accept what was said before.
He then asked, "Why do you come up and go down? If you have something gained, you bury your brothers; if you have nothing gained, for what purpose do you come?"

Setting aside for a moment whether one attains it or not, what is this matter of the wondrous function before one’s eyes? After a long silence, he said: "Clouds cover the thousand mountains, their peaks unexposed;
raindrops fall before the street, gradually deepening. He then returned to the hall. A monk asked, "I beg the Master to point out the path of cultivation.
The Master said, "Kill people and set fires. The monk said, "Both of us are practitioners of the Way; why then do you speak thus?"
The Master said, "As expected, you do not practice. A questioner asked, "I request the Master’s essential instruction regarding the point of intimacy.
The Master said, "Do not forget. The questioner asked, "What is it like when one does not forget? The Master said, "There are three hundred and sixty days in a year.

The questioner said, "In that case, then one does not forget after all. The Master said, "What principle have you perceived? The questioner said, "Just now, I was thanking you for the tea. The Master said, [Silence].
"Not yet. [The monk] said, "Please, Master, speak further. The Master said: "Two communities share one Cold Food Festival.
Morning assembly. To the assembly: Before the moon has set, the sun has already risen. Sun and moon come and go without interval. I exhort you practitioners of Zen not to pursue them;
to pursue them is to needlessly give rise to doubt."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Beneath Fenghuang Mountain, the bells and drums resound with a roar. The house style of Shimen is proclaimed every morning.

When the assembly comes forward, host and guest are already distinguished. As soon as the mouth opens and the tongue moves, both illumination and function are fully realized. If you can realize it in this way—"
"Where are the Buddhas and Patriarchs? If you have not yet realized this, upon what do you rely to pass your days?
Setting aside for a moment whether you have realized it or not, what is the phrase where there are no Buddhas or Patriarchs? After a long silence, he struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Small Assembly. At dawn the drum is struck and we gather in the Dharma Hall; at evening the bell tolls and we meet in the Abbot’s Quarters.
I shall not ask about gathering in the Dharma Hall; what is the phrase for meeting in the Abbot’s Quarters?

[The Master] provides the answer on their behalf: "No wind passes through. A monk asks: "Is there anyone who does not repay the four debts of gratitude or the three realms of existence? The Master says: "There is. The monk says: "How so?"
"What is it like to not repay the four debts of gratitude within the three realms of existence? The Master said: "Casting off the hand, one lies upon the long street;

the realm of light and sound is not the ultimate intent. Question: "When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring flowers in their beaks as offerings? The Master said:

"When the fruit ripens and its fragrance wafts, the doves peck at it. [The student] asked: "After seeing [it], why does it not carry the flower away? The Master said: "When the myriad phenomena suddenly cease, ghosts and spirits are filled with sorrow.
[The student] asked: "Seeing and not seeing— are they the same or different? The Master said: "Mountains and rivers do not obstruct the path to the azure heavens;
wondrous function extends everywhere, flowing freely in all directions. A question was asked: "What is it like when one has personally reached the Treasure Mountain to seek the treasure?"
The Master said, "If you seek it and obtain it, you have missed the mark. [The student] asked, "After obtaining it, what then? The Master said, "Missed the mark, missed the mark.
He then continued, "To conceive a thought is to err; to stir a single念 (mental movement) is to deviate. Not conceiving and not stirring—this is precisely making one's living in stagnant water.
What is the turning phrase of a patch-robed monk? After a long silence, he said, "Hearing the drum roll at dawn, listen at dusk."

The sound of the bell. He ascended the hall and said: "Within the scenery of the three months of spring, the sun is warm and the breeze is harmonious. One walks along the waterside or sits in repose among the groves.

Beholding such a seasonal scene, the roles of guest and host are already distinguished. Should one open the mouth and move the tongue, both illumination and function are fully realized. If you can understand it in this way—"
[The Master] said, "Go! You have understood the host within the guest. But what is the host within the host? After a long silence, he said, "A single stream of the Ji River flows through Silla.
One day, he asked the steward, "The Qingliang Weir is dammed by you. But when a flood comes and the waters overflow the heavens, can it still be dammed?
The steward replied, "It is right here inside. The Master said, "With whom do you keep company? The steward was speechless. The Master then invited him [to stay].
The Master acted on behalf [of the guest]. He said, "It has passed through Silla. [The guest] asked, "If you, Master, were to encounter a flood so vast it reaches the heavens, could you dam it?
The Master said, "Above it supports the heavens; below it supports the earth. [The guest] asked, "What would you do when encountering the kalpa-fire blazing forth?"
The Master said: "Transversely emerging, vertically submerging.
He ascended the hall and said: "Mist rises from the four mountains; the great earth is pitch black; the sun and moon withdraw their light. At this very moment,"

"How do you distinguish the master? After a long silence, he struck the meditation seat and descended from it. When the Master had finished his bath and emerged, a monk asked, "Among the three bodies, which body is bathing?
The Master said, "I am tired. While escorting a deceased monk back and serving tea, [a monk] asked, "Where has the deceased monk gone after passing away?
The Master said, "The wind shakes the trees and they make a sound; the leaves fall and return to their root. After the student remained silent for a long while, the Master said, "Do you understand?"
[The monk] said, "No. The Master then poured three drops of tea [into his mouth]. [The monk] asked, "How can one obtain a human body?
The Master said, "I have always wished to take the body of a donkey."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Coming up and going down, and making requests for instruction—these are not without purpose. But what is the phrase that accords with the time and the season?
After a long silence, he said: "In the morning hear the sound of the drum; at night listen to the tolling of the bell. He then returned to the hall. A monk asked:

"Regarding the three vehicles outside the gate, when a student wishes to mount the ox-cart, how should it be? The Master said: "This is not yet the ultimate point. The monk asked: "What is the ultimate?"
[The Master] said: "The dog barks at empty sounds; the fool gazes toward the sun. A monk asked:
"At the head of a three-way fork, I do not know which path you instruct the student to take. The Master said: "Do not err."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The sound of the bell has just ceased, and the drum resounds; as bell and drum intersect, humans and devas gather. In the wondrous function of the moment, there is no separate dharma;
opening the mouth and moving the tongue, one manifests the Three Mysteries. In responding to the moment with illumination and function, one must be meticulous;
the shifting of guest and host is as swift as smoke. If you step forward further seeking the Buddhas and Patriarchs, by the time you deliberate, you have already been separated from the West."
Ascending the hall, he said: "A white cat with five toes and fierce claws; raised in the hall, it leaves no trace of insects.
This is clearly the method for securing one's position atop a tree; one must strictly avoid uttering words that permit an outsider. "What is the phrase that permits an outsider? he asked.
"Do not err. He ascended the hall and cited the words of Puhua. A monk then asked, "In the Beici Monastery there is a vegetarian feast; what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "When the sun is warm, one sits leaning against it; when the sky is cold, one does not raise one's head."
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you hear the sound of the bell, you follow the sound of the bell. If there is no sound of the bell, from where do you come?
If you do not come, where is the monastic community? Since you have come, what is your face? Even if you neither come nor go, you are merely making a living in stagnant water.
What is the monk’s sentence for letting out his breath? After a long silence, he said: "Zhen! (Adieu!)

[This is] important. Question: "How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said: "Eat porridge; eat rice. [The monk] said: "In that case, I shall go and lie down.
The Master said: "Go and lie down. Question: "Last night you turned one position; this morning you turn another position.
When both ends are turned simultaneously, what then? The Master said: "That is not yet the ultimate standard for a patch-robed monk. [The monk] asked: "What is the ultimate standard?"
The ultimate point for a patch-robed monk. The Master said, "At the end of spring, facing the early summer. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how is it?
The Master said, "Nine times nine is eighty-one."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Each and every one of you is a heroic man. So majestic and unchanging, what doubt could there be? Here before you, everything is as clear as the sun.

When the person extends or contracts, they manifest their own illness. Transcending this, one cannot find the path of the long sky; only through solitary liberation does the light of Chan allow for self-knowledge.
Though much learning and skillful means may discuss the past and present, to truly save beings, one must manifest the lightning-fast mechanism. It is excellent.
[The Master] said, "Go, go! The road to the Western Heaven is long, stretching over a hundred thousand miles.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Heaven and earth share the same root as I; the myriad things are one body with me.
Venerable elders, when the rector strikes the bell, do you feel pain in your hearts? If you do not feel the pain, you contradict the ancients. If you do feel the pain—"
"Why do you smile? [The Master said. "From now on, you must be thorough. A monk entered the room and asked, "At this very moment, is there still a teacher?
The Master said, "The lamp shines through the night; where is it not clear? [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, what is the matter?
The Master said, "Tomorrow is Cold Food Festival. [The monk] asked, "Regarding the ancient saying, 'A tuft of hair at a rapid water rapids'—"
“What is the meaning? The Master said, “The clouds part and the moon shines bright. Question: “What is the meaning of ‘the stone at the bottom of a rapid rapids’?
The Master said, “The roof collapses and the blue sky is revealed. [The student] said, “What is the meaning of ‘the roof collapses and the blue sky is revealed’?
The Master said, “Pervading from top to bottom.”
Small Assembly. Addressing the assembly, he said: "A bodhisattva who studies Prajñā must possess the eye of Prajñā.
If you do not possess the eye of Prajñā, you will be deceived by Prajñā. What is the eye of Prajñā of this assembly? Come forth and speak before the multitude.
After a long silence, he said: "It has sunk away. Be careful. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: [He remained silent.]

[The Master] said, "It comes out of your mouth and enters your ears. [The student] asked, "Is it not just this very thing? The Master said, "Clearly you hear; clearly you listen. A question was asked:
"Why is it that every morning the wind rises, yet there are no raindrops at all? The Master said, "It is simply because the Dragon King does not move his head.
[The student] asked, "Ultimately, what is the matter? The Master said, "Wait until the rain has fallen, and I will tell you. [The student] said, "..."
"It has rained. Why did you not speak, Master? The Master said, "This old monk is at fault.

[The student] asked, "What is 'both the person and the environment being taken away'? The Master extended both hands. [The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master snapped his fingers three times.

[The student] asked, "How does one distinguish the host throughout the twelve hours of the day? The Master said, "Put on your clothes and eat your food according to your station. [The student] said, "After having distinguished it, as for..."
"What? The Master asked. "What is the host? The monk was speechless. He then ascended the hall and said:
"To conceive a thought is already a deviation; to stir a single notion is already to go astray. To neither conceive nor stir—this is precisely to make one's living in stagnant water.
What is the place where a patch-robed monk turns himself around? As for the ancients speaking thus, do you understand?"
Is there a person here or not? If you say there is a person, I shall bind and kill you according to your words.
If you say there is no person, where does your intention lie? Therefore it is said: "The mind of nirvāṇa is easy to understand; the wisdom of differentiation is difficult to clarify. It is also said:
Knowledge and vision arise; knowledge is the very root of ignorance. When knowledge and vision are absent, seeing this is itself nirvana.
Even if you can attain clarity here, you have not yet possessed the eye of a patch-robed monk; you must be most meticulous.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The scenery of the three months of spring has faded, and the vermilion summer is about to arrive. This is the time for Zen practitioners to cease their travels and the hour to hang up one's staff at a secluded window.
Meeting beneath the trees, what should we discuss? After a long silence, he said: 'If one intends to point toward the path of a thousand differences...'"
A hundred thousand miles of returning light. Question: "How was it before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "Clouds disperse and the blue sky appears.
Question: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said: "The moon appears in the clear pool. Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: [Silence].
Crushed by chariots and trampled by horses. He asked, "What is it to be one on the Way? The Master said, "Sitting upright and lying horizontal. Entering the hall, he said:
"As soon as the incense smoke rises, it is known everywhere; the great assembly gathers like clouds. As for the ancestral vehicle of the lineage, it can only be thus.
If you can understand it in this way, you will seize the drum and snatch the banner, overturning the roles of host and guest, such that illumination and function are simultaneous."
The staff and the shout manifest together. Even if you understand it in this way, you are merely a host within the guest. What is the host within the host?
A monk then asked, "As soon as the incense smoke rises, it is known everywhere. I wonder, what is it like behind the Master’s mountain? The Master said, "I have told you; do you believe me?
The monk said, "I have come specifically to request your instruction. The Master then gave a shout. The monk said, "Master... [The Master] struck him.
The monk asked, "Why do you still avoid speaking of it? The Master said, "Blind! The monk bowed. The Master then said, "Within a single phrase, one must possess the Three Mysteries (san-xuan).
Within each Mystery-gate, one must possess the Three Essentials (san-yao). All the sages of antiquity fully possessed these Three Mysteries and Three Essentials.

If they did not possess the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, their efforts would all belong to the category of blind application. Since you are now able to apply yourself with such earnestness..."

"You must be thorough and attentive. After a long silence, he said: "I, a junior of Shimen, am clumsy and unskilled in all matters. I have stood here for a long time waiting for the prior; please return to the hall to rest. A monk asked:
"How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said: "Level. [The monk] asked: "How was it after he appeared in the world? The Master said: "Level."
The Master said, "Even. [The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand whether those who have appeared in the world and those who have not appeared in the world are one or two.

The Master said, "The wondrous function manifests according to the occasion; turning the light back depends solely on the person. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when the Great Matter has not yet been resolved? The Master said, "Urgent! [The monk] said, "..."

[The monk asked: "What is it like after the funeral arrangements are complete? The Master said: "Urgent. [The monk] asked: "What is profound discourse? The Master said: "Pointing toward the south of the wall. [The monk] asked:

"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Place your hands together at your chest. [The monk] asked, "What is the intent of this? The Master said, "Bow and step forward.
[The monk] asked, "If a fire breaks out in one place, you may deal with it as you wish; but what if fires break out simultaneously in all eight directions?"
The Master said, "Excellent. The monk asked, "Is there still a way to seek deliverance? The Master said, "If you seek deliverance, I will burn you to death.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Even if you do not seek deliverance, I will still burn you to death."
A great rain falls. He ascends the hall and says: "The morning sun is shrouded by clouds; the night moon withdraws its light.
Mist rises from the four mountains, and the great earth is utterly free of even a speck of dust. At this very moment, who is the master?

Although it is so, how can one deny that the thousand rivers compete to pour forth and the myriad streams flow from their sources, all at once encompassed by the great ocean? Do not say that it merely contains them all."
[The Master] finished speaking. But alas, he was driven by the current of the Ji River and passed through Silla.
He ascended the hall and said: "The golden crow sinks in the west; the jade hare rises in the east. Day and night revolve—when will there ever be an end?
Why not look at the position of true centrality where the sun is at its zenith in the south? Or rest upon your long couch at the hour of Zi (midnight) in the dead of night. Right.
At such a time, it may be said that the sentiments of a thousand sages have been exhausted and all images are entirely absent.

Nevertheless, even so, this is not yet the ultimate point. One must truly move and shift before it can be attained. Even if one manages to move and shift, one has merely gained the assent of Lopu and Guankui;

one has not yet gained the assent of those three saints and Xinghua. To open the mouth or move the tongue is already to fall into sickness; when the staff and the shout are applied according to the occasion—this is where it lies.
It is difficult to construct [a theory]. Blinking an eye, one must directly carry out the True Command (*saddharma-ājñā*).
Entering the hall, he said: "In the evening, look at the thousand households, their doors unbarred; from time to time, hear the sound of an autumn pestle, stroke by stroke.
How many travelers on the road have not yet returned? But once you have arrived home, what will you do? "All you venerable ones," he continued, "do not remain on the road; you must directly..."
Return home. If you are able to return home, you must simply treat your parents with intimacy; do not allow them to give rise to affectionate attachment. You must instead put your parents to death.
Once you have put your parents to death, you must then leave the household life. Having left the household life, you will then be able to be intimate with the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Although this is so, you must first eliminate the Buddhas and Patriarchs as well. Once you have put your parents to death...
Only when you have cast aside the Buddhas and Patriarchs can you possess even a grain of the understanding of a patch-robed monk;
yet, this is still not the full functioning of a patch-robed monk. After a long silence, he asked: "What is the full functioning of a patch-robed monk?

To kill one's father and mother, and to cast aside the Buddhas and Patriarchs—this is not yet the ultimate point for a patch-robed monk. As he stepped forward, intending to ask further how it was, [the Master said]: "The North Miao Mountains."

There were many below [in the assembly]. He ascended the hall and said: "Gathering here amidst clouds and mountains is intended for my lifelong purpose. Carrying my staff to various quarters, I intend to escape birth and death.
How can one spend the days in vain? Why do you not advance to deliberate upon this? If you wish to advance and deliberate, it is specifically..."
When the ground is discordant, he simply says, "Let it rest just as it is. Otherwise, one would further betray one's entire life; it is not at all like this.
Furthermore, where else could one set one's heart? After a long silence, he said, "Return to the hall."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When the dragon soars over the vast ocean, the fish and turtles hide their tracks; when the tiger roars from the high crag, the wild foxes withdraw their traces.
When the elephant king tramples, the jeweled shores all collapse; when the lion yawns, the hundred beasts vanish into hiding. When the phoenix spreads its wings, the myriad birds lose their nests.

Such is the ancestral style: those of middling or inferior capacity cannot approach it. Even Maudgalyāyana and Śāriputra, employing their wisdom and supernatural powers, [could not fathom it]. Gold...
As for the dhūta practice of wearing cast-off robes: when the Lord of Men (Śākyamuni) blinked his eyes, the śrāvakas could not fathom it, and how could those on the ten stages know?

When Śāriputra uttered a single word, the heavens immediately rained down flowers. How much more so regarding these many words spoken with such casual and disorderly talk! To pass through even a single thread of the Way, one must simply speak it forth from one’s own mouth.
Speak! Speak! Even if you were able to speak it, it would still be merely a conceptual approximation.
Ascending the hall, he said: "You eminent practitioners who investigate the mystery and superior men who travel afar must truly possess the eyes of a patch-robed monk. After a long silence, he said:
"Open your mouths and directly cause the sentiments of a thousand sages to be exhausted; let all conditions be unattached. Both father and mother are dead; guest and host are not established.
Even if you understand it thus, this is still but a small portion of a patch-robed monk's insight—it is not yet the total embodiment of a patch-robed monk."
"Enjoyment. "How is it that one enjoys with the whole body? After a long silence, he said, "Return to the hall for tea.
He ascended the hall and said, "Each of you, venerable seniors, has a bearing like a king; you must possess the eyes of a monk.
The mountains and rivers of the great earth do not obstruct the eye’s light—do not allow yourselves to be deceived by others. But tell me, what face does the King of Khotan present?"
At that time, a monk asked, "I have heard the Master say that mountains, rivers, and the great earth do not obstruct the eye’s light.
I wonder, what kind of face does the King of Khotan have? The Master said, "He does not go out the door. The monk asked, "With whom, then, does he share this path?
The Master said, "The most intimate is one's own kin."

This morning marks the Great Year; the peach-wood talismans have already been buried in the earth. Throughout the land, people tear open paper ingots.
Worldly sentiments mostly lose their proper place; I, this mountain monk alone, am filled with joy. Even if one were not thus, one would merely be plowing a field upon a grave.
To the assembly in winter, I shall speak for you a single phrase: all phenomena and their seasons—winter months are winter’s cold, and summer heat is summer’s heat.
Where is there no turning? Why labor so hard to establish [anything]? Whether established or not established, all words must be resolved.
If you further intend to ask "How?", what use is a blade of tempered steel at the bottom of a ship?
The assembly requested further instruction on the story of the three lifetimes at Mount Guishan. The Master replied with a verse:
"Last night at the third watch I had a dream: Mud oxen fought within the Cool River. At dawn I asked Old Man Guo;
He recognized Li the Bearded from South Village."
The Staff: I have a staff that spans the day, laid across my knees. Its large and small joints are distinct; from head to tail, it is one and the same.
Set down, it opens wide the great earth; held upright, it lifts up the myriad phenomena. If you encounter it in a bustling marketplace—
One who knows the music. Turning his head and striking the spine with a staff:

when illuminating and acting, he cuts off the path of heaven and earth; testing and breaking through, he causes the wise and the foolish to lose their courage and souls. Even if you were as eloquent as Su Qin wearing his jade pendants.
Seal. You must also surrender and await the imperial grace.
Only when you are captured alive until the end of your life, and then allowed to revive so that your remaining body may be preserved, will your surrender be manifest as a report to the world.
Even if they were to release you for the remainder of your years, would there be any understanding?

Illumination and function are simultaneous; beneath the staff lies the mystery. There is no room for deliberation, nor can the foolish or the wise exert themselves. The wheel and sword charge straight through the ranks of dragons and tigers;
horses are lost, men are slain, and blood fills the fields.
Illumination and function do not occur at the same time; few people understand this. Yellow leaves fall from the autumn sky; flowers fly as spring ends.

This verse praises the single shout that distinguishes guest and host: illumination and function operate simultaneously. If you can grasp the meaning within this, it will be like striking three o'clock at noon.

The Three Mysteries repay you for the teachings of all quarters. When the phrases of the Three Mysteries are not distinguished, one seeks to clarify the direct intent: in the tenth month, there is the sun of spring.
The Three Phrases.
The first phrase: The markings must be distinct and clear; do not be muddled. If you intend to step forward and ask "How is it?", the West has been transplanted here to this land.
The second phrase: Wondrous function applied according to the occasion without error. Do not engage with opening your mouth or moving your tongue;
you must clearly realize it beneath the staff. The third phrase: Question and answer are distinct and possess speech. Throughout all quarters—
All is well-discussed. Even a three-year-old child fears suffering.
Preface to the *Fengyan Collection* of Chan Master Cizhao of Shimen Mountain, from the *Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters*, Volume Nine.
When the Benevolent One appeared, it was like the autumn moon descending into a cold pond; when the Patriarchal intent came from the West, it was like spring thunder awakening hibernating creatures.
He cleared the deaf ears of living beings and pointed out the deluded head of Yanluo. Transcending the mundane and surpassing the holy, he was one who could truly "turn things.
Those who attained the Way were beyond counting in the world, and in every generation there have been extraordinary individuals who succeeded to the Dharma. Master [resided by] the Ru Water.
Throwing in the needle; standing in the snow at Shushan. He personally transmitted the ancestral seal and kept the Zen-sword secret within its scabbard.

When Governor Cha sent three letters of invitation, Master Yuan entrusted him with the seat of the One Vehicle. Wielding the precious sword that reaches the heavens, the spirits of the heretics were extinguished.

He shook his golden fur as he sprawled upon the ground, causing the jackal’s skull to split open. Even if one were to immediately establish the expedient means of "standing clear," shifting the roles of host and guest;

or if one were to seize the moment to cut off heaven and earth—who would then discuss Buddhas and patriarchs? With a shout, he clarifies the four kinds [of kōan]; with a staff, he manifests the three mysteries.

He illuminates the thousand differences, yet his function is not limited to a single phrase. Because of this, disciples gathered from afar and students arrived like clouds. The Master had thus revealed himself...
Regarding the *Cifeng* (Sharpness of Words): Zen practitioners have long been intimately familiar with its essential sayings. It has been compiled into two fascicles, titled *Fengyan*.
Although I, Guangpu, am fortunate enough to have heard it, I feel truly ashamed to compose this preface.
The Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Ten:
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shanzhao of Fenyang (Nanyue Lineage, Ninth Generation; Successor of Shoushan Nian).

The Master was a native of the Yu clan of Taiyuan. Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he traveled with staff in hand, staying briefly wherever he went, responding to conditions as they arose.

He struck [the ground] to express his realization. He had studied under seventy-one masters in succession before arriving at Shoushan. He asked, "When Baizhang rolled up his mat, what was the meaning?

Shoushan said, "The dragon’s sleeve sweeps aside, and the entire body is revealed. The Master asked, "What is your own meaning, Master? Shoushan said, "Where the Elephant King walks, there are no traces of foxes.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Rising from his prostrations, he said, "Ten thousand ages of the azure pool..."
"The moon in the realm of space: only after straining it again and again can one begin to know it. A questioner asked, "What principle did you perceive that led you to accept this for yourself?

The Master said, "This is precisely where I surrendered my body and life. Later, while traveling through the regions of Heng, Xiang, Xiangyang, and Mian, he was repeatedly invited by local magistrates to head famous monasteries.
He replied, "I am but a monk who constantly goes on alms-rounds; I have transmitted the Mind-essence of the Buddha."
This was no trivial matter. On eight separate occasions, he had been invited, yet he remained firm in his reclining posture and did not respond.

When Shoushan passed away, the monastics and laypeople of the Western Road dispatched the monk Qichong to invite him to serve as abbot. The Master closed his door and lay high upon his pillow. Qichong pushed open the door and entered, admonishing him, saying:

"The great matter of the Buddha-dharma outweighs minor matters of withdrawal. Fengxue feared he would fulfill the prophecy, and thus he worried that the essential teachings would fall into ruin. It is our good fortune..."

"Yet there was my former teacher. My former teacher has already passed away. You, who possess the strength to shoulder the Great Dharma of the Tathāgata—how can you wish for peaceful sleep at such a time?
The Master started up in alarm and, grasping Cōng’s hand, said, "Were it not for you, I would not have heard these words."
"Prepare the requisites; I shall depart. Having arrived, he sat in quiet meditation upon a single mat for thirty years, his feet never crossing the threshold.
Monastics and laypeople alike called him "The One from Fenzhou," not daring to address him by name.
While staying at Hou, he ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "In the gate of Fenyang sits a West River Lion, crouching right at the entrance.
As soon as anyone approaches, it bites them to death. What skillful means (*upāya*) is there to enter Fenyang’s gate and see Fenyang’s man?
If you see Fenyang’s man, you are fit to be a teacher of the Buddhas and patriarchs; if you do not see Fenyang’s man, you are all [lost]."
"This is the place where those who die on the ground stand. Is there anyone who can still enter now? You must enter quickly;
do not let your entire life go to waste. If you are not a guest of the Dragon Gate, take care not to suffer the 'dotted forehead' (rejection). Who, then, is a guest of the Dragon Gate?
He pointed his staff at them all at once and said, "Withdraw quickly! Withdraw quickly! Take care!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The former sages said: 'A single phrase must possess the three mysteries; each mystery must possess the three essentials.
Which phrase possesses these three mysteries and three essentials? Understand it quickly! Each of you should reflect for yourselves: have you attained a sense of stability yet?
When the ancients of old went on pilgrimage, if they heard a single kōan (cause-and-condition) that was not yet clear, they would go directly [to seek its meaning].
Below, food and drink lack flavor, and sleep and rest are uneasy. You must resolve this with the utmost urgency; do not treat it as a trivial matter.
This is why the Great Awakened Elder appeared in the world for the sake of the one great cause.

Consider that from antiquity until now, those who have traveled on pilgrimage have not done so to tour mountains or play by the water, nor to view the splendors of prefectures and capitals; every bit of clothing and every morsel of food has been for the sake of the Holy.

My mind was not yet fully enlightened; therefore, I traveled far and wide on foot to resolve profound mysteries, to transmit and propagate the teachings, to consult widely with those who had prior knowledge, and to draw near to those of high virtue.
This was all for the sake of continuing the lamp of the Buddha’s mind, to honor and flourish the ancestral lineage, to exalt the sacred seed, and to guide future practitioners.
To benefit oneself and others, I have never forgotten the traces of my predecessors. Is there anyone present now who would like to discuss this? Is there?
He immediately came out, and they deliberated together. A monk asked, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner? The Master said, "You are a wandering monk.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase for discerning a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "The sun rises in the west at the hour of Mao."
[The student] asked, "What is the phrase for when the true command is put into effect? The Master said, "Bringing it from a thousand miles away to present one's old face.
[The student] asked, "What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth? The Master said, "In the continent of Uttarakuru, long-grained rice grows; those who eat it are neither greedy nor angry.
He then said, "Use these four turning phrases to test the monks of the world. As soon as I see you come forth," [he would apply them].
“I have verified it. A student asked, “What is the place where the student exerts effort? The Master said, “Beating the Great Image at Jia Prefecture.
He asked, “What is the place where the student turns about? The Master said, “Watering the Iron Ox at Shan Prefecture.
He asked, “What is the place where the student is intimate? The Master said, “Playing with the Lion in West River. Then he said, “If anyone can understand these three...”
Verse: The Three Mysteries have already been explained; there remains the Three Essentials, which must be thoroughly realized—they are no ordinary matters.

For the sake of the assembly, I shall express them in verse: The Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials are difficult to distinguish; When one grasps the meaning and forgets the words, the Way is easy to approach.
A single phrase clearly encompasses the myriad phenomena; On the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums are fresh.
Ascending the hall, the Master said: “Fenyang has three secrets, which it is difficult for patch-robed monks to discern.
If you intend to ask how they are, I shall drive my staff right through your head. At that time, a monk asked, “What are the three secrets? The Master struck him. The monk bowed.
The Master said, “I shall express them all at once in verse. The First Secret: There is no fixed time for guidance; clever words cannot describe it. The clouds part...”

The moon in the blue sky: this is the second secret. Radiating light to distinguish the worthy and the wise; through questions and answers, the mind that benefits sentient beings is revealed, pulling out the wedge from the eye.
This is the third secret, spoken by a barbarian from the Western Regions. The water of the Ji River flows to Silla; in the northern lands, they use tempered steel.
He asked again: "Is there anyone who understands? Let those who understand come forward and convey a message. If you wish to know the distance, do not merely [rely on words]."

To spend one’s entire life merely memorizing words and phrases—what benefit is there in that? Do not stand here long; take care. Question: A cloth drum hangs before the hall; who is the one who knows it well? [The Master] says:
Stop the hoeing, pour out the wheat rice, and lie in the grass without raising your head.

Question: What is the site of enlightenment (dōjō)? The Master says: One cannot set foot upon it. Question: What is the Patriarch from the West? The Master says: [Stop the hoeing, pour out the wheat rice, and lie in the grass without raising your head.]

Regarding the intent behind [this question]: the Master said, "Piercing to the bone and piercing to the marrow. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Pervading heaven and pervading earth. [Thus ends the] question.
"One who truly cultivates the Way does not see the faults of the world. [The student] asked, "I do not understand what kind of faults they do not see.
The Master said, "The snow buries the night moon three feet deep; a boat travels ten thousand *li* on dry land. [The student] said, "What kind of mental activity is this, Master?
The Master said, "It is actually your own mental activity. [The student] asked, "Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, what is the True Eye? The Master...
[The Master] said, "Blind! [The monk] said, "If that is so, then two people are carrying a single staff. The Master said, "Singing a rustic song in a village of three households.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then you, the Master, are also inside it. The Master said, "Thank you for your persistence. [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s house style?
The Master said, "The Three Mysteries open the Right Path; a single phrase shatters the heterodox schools. [The monk] asked, "How about this?"
"This is the livelihood of the Upādhyāya. The Master said, "Usually I do not hold anything in my hands; I provide offerings for the monks of the five lakes. [The monk] asked, "I wonder what they eat?
The Master said, "Divine *sūkheta* rice is no more than a precious delicacy; with a single flavor of grain-soup, one is satisfied and rests."
Question: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "A new deity is further adorned by a shamaness.
[The monk] asked: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said: "An ancient shrine is revisited by a scholar's inscription.
A monk asked: "What is the source of the Great Way? The Master said: "Digging the earth to seek the blue sky. [The monk] said: "How can it be so? The Master said: "Recognize its profound mystery."
The Master raised the discourse on the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan) and said: "Do you understand the timing of the foundation of the Three Mysteries?
You must first grasp the intent of the ancients; only then will your own mind become clear. Furthermore, you will attain mastery in transformation and change, enjoying it inexhaustibly.
This is called the Buddha of Self-Enjoyment Body (Svabhoga-kāya), which does not rely on the teachings of others. Thus, one recognizes one's own livelihood. Therefore, Nan..."
Quan said, "When Master Wang was eighteen, he already knew how to make a living.
A monk then asked, "The ancients say that at eighteen they already knew how to make a living; I wonder what kind of living they made?
He replied, "Two water buffalo, with double horns and no halter. He added, "If you wish to understand this clearly, you must attain the Three Mysteries."
The essential intent: only then can one attain unimpeded enjoyment, seeking for oneself joy and fulfillment to bring one's life to its full expression.
Great men, do not let yourselves be self-defeating; if you are obstructed in every encounter, there will be no benefit or salvation for either side. To you all, I offer these verses:
The First Mystery: The Dharma-realm is vast and boundless; the myriad phenomena and all things are entirely contained within the mirror in their full perfection.
The Second Mystery: The World-Honored One asked Ānanda; Ānanda, having heard much, answered according to the facts, responding to the shape and capacity of the vessel. The Third Mystery:
Directly appearing before the Ancient Sovereign, beyond the four propositions and the hundred negations, Lǔ Zhì questioned Fēnggān, who then said: "This is the Three."
The Verse on the Three Mysteries: What is the essential meaning of these three mysteries? I shall instruct you directly so that you may discern them with clarity.
Do not merely claim at random, "I have personally attended upon the Master; he explained this to me. Such empty fabrications and deceptive speech only serve to delude others;
you will surely face the day when you are struck by the iron staff. Do not say I did not warn you! Furthermore, while picking chrysanthemums, he said to the assembly: "Gold..."
Flowers carpet the ground; jade stamens support the heavens. The bright sun hangs in the sky; heaven and earth shine with clarity. Clouds rise to bring rain; dew crystallizes into frost.
Without violating the principle of things, the Way is brought forth in a single phrase.

Is there anyone who can speak it? If you cannot speak it, there is a speck of dust in your eye; you must remove it before you may succeed. Therefore, Fengxue said: "If one establishes even a single..."
When a speck of dust arises, the state prospers and the village elders frown; when not a single speck of dust is established, the state perishes and the village elders are at peace.
If you understand this clearly, the *śrāmaṇera* has no share—it is entirely the old monk. If you do not understand this clearly, the old monk is precisely the *śrāmaṇera*.
The *śrāmaṇera* and the old monk can both awaken all people in the world, and they can also blind all people in the world.
“Do you want to know where the *ācārya* and this old monk are? [The Master] patted his two knees and said, ‘This here is the *ācārya*;
this here is the old monk. Now I ask you, venerable elders: are the old monk and the *ācārya* the same, or are they different?
If you say they are the same, then the elder is the elder and the old monk is the old monk. If you say they are different, then again...”
"The old monk is none other than you, O *śrāmaṇera*. If you can attain clarity regarding this, then within a single phrase there are the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials;
guest and host will be clearly distinguished, the affairs of your entire life will be settled, and the quest for the Way will be complete.

Thus Yongjia said: 'To grind one's bones and shatter one's body would not suffice as recompense; a single phrase, when realized, transcends ten billion worlds. He also said: 'The two halls of Linji..."*
One day, as they were seated together, both let out a shout simultaneously. A monk asked Linji, "Is there still a distinction between guest and host?
He replied, "Guest and host are clearly distinct. The Master composed a verse, saying: "The two Hall Heads are both masters; Within them, the principles seem to contend.
Guest and host are as clear as a mirror, Yet the Master points out the flowers before one's eyes. The Master thus proclaimed the essence of the school.
The *Cheng* (The Vehicle) states: "The profound and solemn [teaching] takes the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials as its primary concern;

this is the true essential manual of the Linji school. Fenzhou was located in Hedong, where the climate was bitterly cold; it was not uncommon for those standing there to lose their toes. Because of this, the Master discontinued the night assemblies.
One day, while sitting in meditation, a strange monk arrived riding on the clouds with a monk’s staff in hand. He asked, "For what reason has the Master ceased the night assemblies?"
"Thank you," the Master replied, citing the extreme cold as his reason for declining. A strange monk said, "Under your guidance, O Master, there are six men who will become great vessels.
I pray that you will not begrudge them the gift of the Dharma. Having spoken, he mounted a cloud and departed. The next day, the Master ascended the seat and recorded this in verse:
"The foreign monk with the golden staff’s radiance Came to Fenyang for the sake of the Dharma. Six men shall become great vessels; I entreat you to proclaim it for them."

[The Master] raised his voice: "From this night's assembly onwards, the practice shall never again be suspended. At that time, Chuyuan, Shouzhi, Huijue, Zhiyuan, Guquan, Qijiu, and others were all among those seated below;
they were renowned throughout the monastic community.
When the Master first opened the hall for the assembly, a monk asked: "At the single assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa personally heard the teaching. At this day’s assembly, who is it that hears it?
The Master said: "The great assembly listens attentively. The monk pressed further: "If that is so, then all living beings have someone to rely upon. The Master said:
"Were it not for ascending this precious throne, how could the ability of the six teachers be revealed? A monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does the school follow?"

"Who is it? The Master said, "Without passing through kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, one emerges directly before the Ancient Sovereign. [The student] further asked, "If that is so, then the prefectural city has hope.
The Master said, "The peaks of the Five Mountains are exquisite; the four seas all respond to the tide. A question was asked:

"Empty space is used as a provisional metaphor, and its name is manifested wherever it may be. I wonder, what kind of thing is this? The Master said, "It dwells among devas and humans, yet cannot be fathomed."
"Entering the earth, buried even deeper. The student said, "If that is so, then although this student does not understand, throughout kalpas I shall be entirely bathed in your grace.
The Master said, "Let the fine arms of the sword-wielder be left to their clamor; only when the belly is split open and the heart revealed is one truly enlightened."

The Master gave a small-scale discourse (xiaochan), saying: "Is there anyone who would like to ask a question? If so, come forward. A monk asked: "What is it like when the ice cracks and the fish scatter?
The Master said: "The water is clear, yet the fish do not appear; the long waves come and go of their own accord.

The monk pressed further: "In what position does the Dragon King reside? The Master said: "A golden palace exists everywhere; throughout heaven and earth, I alone am honored. The monk pressed further: "If that is so, then..."
“There is none who surpasses him. The Master said, “Who can excel at brandishing the sword? One must not wound oneself.
The Master then continued, “If you are one who can brandish the sword, even Fenyang would be at a loss. Do you recognize the sword? I shall explain it for you:
‘In the realm of the world there is no equal; throughout the land he walks alone. Take care! A monk asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master—
He said: "The many-year-old pine tree abounds in weathered bark; within the heart, there is naturally a single line of clarity. Question: "In all instances of question and answer,"

Guest and host each displayed their finest wonders. At Shaoshi, there was no word—how could the point be entrusted? The Master said, "In a crowd of a thousand people, it is rare to encounter such a question.
The student said, "Having come here across a thousand mountains and ten thousand waters, I have already received your compassionate grace; all matters are now settled."
The Master said: "When the sun is cut off, heaven and earth are dark; the myriad phenomena are all present before one's eyes. The student said:

"The official way does not admit even a needle, yet the private way allows for carriages and horses. [I], this student, prostrate. The Master said: "Do not prostrate. Wait for what time? [The student] asked.
"What is the matter prior to a single word? The Master said: "To clarify the essential meaning without falling into verbal explanations;

were even a hair’s breadth to move, there would be discrepancy. The student asked: "What is the matter subsequent to a single word? The Master said: "When two armies meet, there is no avoiding them. The student said:
"If that is so, then one has penetrated through skin and bone. The Master said: "Dragging it sideways and pulling it upside down, let it be as dust."
Man said, "I truly dare not fail the Master. The Master said, "Zhonghua was the most filial.
A student asked, "What is the Dharma-eye? The Master said, "It has already been blinded. The student asked, "I do not yet understand: what is the matter beyond this? The Master said:
Reaching for heaven and groping on the ground. A student asked, "I have long admired the full majesty of Fenyang; let him briefly display his golden mane for the assembly to see.
The Master said, "He will reveal it after three days. The student said, "If that is so, I shall retreat three paces. The Master said, "Come back again after one month.
A student asked, "The Patriarch’s Heart-Seal is beyond all verbal explanation; how is it when the moment of action arrives? The Master said, "Three."
"Looking at the journey from a thousand li away. Xue said, "If that is so, then I shall step back. The Master said, "Ten-thousand-fathom peaks do not depart from this very place.
A questioner asked, "When questions upon questions do not turn [the mind], what then? The Master said, "The dragon-horse receives the whip and gallops faster."
The imperial carriage bells resound over the Luo River. A student asked, "I have long admired the Lion of the West River.
Now that I have arrived, why do I not see him? The Master said, "Do you recognize the Lion? The student said, "If that is so, then the entire assembly may rejoice together. The Master said, "..."
Only when the brain splits open does one realize the urgency. A student asked, "Within the gateway of the True Dharma, what is the Master’s point of entry?
The Master said, "The myriad stars cluster around the night moon; it does not fall into the Purple Microcosm Palace. The student said, "If that is so, then the bright moon alone occupies the heavens.
The Master said, "It does not fail to illuminate those traveling at night."
The Master ascended the hall and said: "The fundamental Buddha-nature of all sentient beings is like the bright moon suspended in the sky;
it is only because of the obscuration of drifting clouds that it cannot manifest. A monk then asked: "When the bright moon is in the heavens, yet is obscured by a single cloud, what then?
The Master said: "The old monk has committed a fault; you must understand this, O Kalyāṇamitra. The student said: "If that is so, then [it is] divided..."

[The Master] said, "Discern clearly. The Master said, "Step back and do not reflect. A question was asked: "Taking a step, one traverses a thousand streams; seeking the source, the path grows ever more lost.
Regarding this single phrase within it, I pray the Master will prompt me toward it. The Master said, "A tree without shadow for a thousand years—today its branches and twigs are seen.
The student said, "Had I not submitted this question, how could I have encountered the Master’s pivotal function? The Master said, "A blind man looking [at forms]."

On the painted wall, he ascended the hall and said: "Now, those who preach the Dharma must act in accordance with the proper time and season. They must observe the faculties of beings to meet their needs, applying medicine according to the ailment.
If one fails to accord with the proper time and season, all such speech is termed 'untimely words. Therefore, it is said in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi Assembly: 'If you wish to know the Buddha-nature...'"

Regarding the meaning: one should contemplate the conditions of time and circumstance. Whether it be the clarity of sovereign and minister, father and son, or the distinction between the heterodox and the orthodox, the pure and the defiled—when these are clearly demarcated, it is called the "wild old man’s song.
The imperial Way is level and vast; the Buddha-dharma manifests before one. Seizing and releasing are at will; life and death are decided according to the occasion.

At times, the host is clarified within the guest; at times, the guest is clarified within the host; at times, the guest is clarified within the guest; or at times, the host is clarified [within the host].

The Lord of Lords. Sometimes it is combined with other elements; sometimes it is like a probing pole or a shadow-grass. Within a single phrase, there may be the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials.
Is there anyone who would ask? Come forward and discuss this with the assembly. At that time, a monk asked: "The gate of wisdom is difficult to understand and difficult to enter.
I, a student, do not comprehend it. I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "It is the truly authentic, selfless speech. You must seek it within the phrase."
"Clearly. The student said, "In that case, I thank the Master for personally opening the gate of expedient means. The Master said, "Do not forget this after ten thousand years. A question was asked:
"How is it when the numinous tortoise has not yet shown its signs? The Master said, "Laughing while rowing a boat upon the sea."
Raising the oar, he gazed upon the journey ahead. A question was asked: "The sweet dew water has been sprinkled repeatedly; why do the hundred grasses fail to sprout? The Master said:
"When the fields are parched, they cannot hold the water; what can the Dragon King do about it? A question was asked: "As the cold and heat grow ever more intense, on what shall the poor rely?"

The Master said: "Unadorned by private robes, one laughs joyfully all day long. The student said: "In that case, one would not be left exposed? The Master said: "One cannot hide in deep ravines; on the open ground, no form is displayed. A question was asked: "What is it like when one does not awaken to the Ancestor and does not believe in the Great Way?

The Master said: "Shatter the glass egg, and the phoenix chick emerges. The student said: [Silence] The Master said: "Unadorned by private robes, one laughs joyfully all day long. The student said: "In that case, one would not be left exposed? The Master said: "One cannot hide in deep ravines; on the open ground, no form is displayed. Question:
"What is it like when one does not awaken to the Ancestor and does not believe in the Great Way? The Master said: "Shatter the glass egg, and the phoenix chick emerges. The student said: [Silence]
"Today I have personally seen the Master," [the monk] said. The Master said, "From three thousand *li* away, you calculate the distance of the journey.

[The monk] asked, "What is it like when one rides alone on a single horse with a solitary spear, fighting independently of the group? The Master said, "Raising the hand, the bow is not grasped; lowering the head, the arrow is lost."
The student said, "The Master is a great spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra). Why do you act like this? The Master said, "A defeated general is not executed.

The student asked, "I, your disciple, wish to soar into the clouds and sky. Once there, how shall I act for the sake of sentient beings? The Master said, "The General beyond the frontier carries out his true commands;

The Master said, “The brains of all the beasts split open. A questioner asked, “‘Do not stand fixed in the two extremes; there is no need to settle in the middle path.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said, “Ivory comes from Guangnan. “I do not understand. Please, Master, point directly. The Master said, “Leather from the foreign lands.”
"A ball worth eight hundred coins. [The student] asked: "What is 'first illuminating, then acting'? The Master said: "Beating the drum for the Han dynasty;
singing the song of King Chu in harmony. [The student] asked: "What is 'first acting, then illuminating'? The Master said:

"Long Zu understood how to deploy a thousand stratagems; Han Xin was able to perform the feat of damming the waters. [The student] asked: "What is 'illuminating and acting simultaneously'? The Master said: "A long snake..."
The dykes and gates discharge the water simultaneously; Han Xin and Zhang Liang sing a great song. He asked: "What is it that illumination and function do not occur at the same time?
The Master said: "The Hegemon and the King have already returned to the Dark River; they raise the Golden Cock to celebrate Great Peace. He asked:
"It is not within, it is not without, and it is not in between. Where is it? The Master said: "White cotton cloth from India; the land of the East."

[The student] said, "Silk and cotton. [The Master] said, "I do not yet understand what these words mean. The Master said, "Mount Heng and Mount Wutai. [The student] asked, "How far apart are the City of Jewels and the Phantom City?

The Master said, "Lifting the foot and setting it down. [The student] asked, "When one applies oneself to the objects of the six sense-dusts, for which gate of skillful means does one find the ultimate destination?
The Master said, "Hengzhou’s *niuxi* (ginseng root) is known by all people under heaven. [The student] said, "If that is so, then [it is] compassion..."
A single utterance of sound opens the profound path; it causes the journey home to reach the very house at once. The Master said:

"The radish of Zhenzhou weighs three catties. A monk asked: "Among the three phrases, which one is the ultimate principle? The Master said: "Its form is revealed everywhere on the ground, yet in the end it is not seen.
The monk asked: "Is there still a place for one to settle oneself and establish one's life? The Master said: "Throughout one’s entire life, it is always the sky above."
The Epilogue. Yang Dainian and Prince Li engage in dialogue with the Master. Question: "Amitābha’s transformation of the world lies in the West;
Bodhidharma’s transmission of the mind came to the Eastern Land. When the barbarian arrives, the Han appears; when the water reaches, the channel forms. Mount Wutai remains serene yet towering."
The hundred grains flow toward the central sea in vast abundance; the nature of the single spirit manifests form by relying upon its environment.
Amidst the three realms of existence, upon what does one rely to establish one's destiny? The Master said: "The immortal has no wife; the jade maiden has no husband. Yang said:
"A nun who has shaved her head will never again give birth to a child. The Master said: "The iron ox of Shanfu can roar; the Great Image of Jiazhou recites the Mahā."
Li said: "Leaping sideways onto the mountain peak. The Master said: "Riding an ox without wearing boots.
Li asked: "Xuansha did not cross the ridge; Baoshou did not ford the river. Śāriputra visited fifty-three spiritual friends;
Huiyuan gathered eighteen monks and laymen. Xuefeng went up to Touzi three times; Zhiyi lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra* for ninety days. These six—"
"Is this fellow a jackal howling, or is he a lion’s roar? Speak! Speak! The Master said, "The water is so swift that the fish find it hard to move;
the peaks are so high that birds do not perch. Yang said, "The Great Sage of Sizhou. The Master said, "To add more mud upon the earth is yet another layer.
Li said, "Gold coins are covered upon the tongue. The Master said, "At midnight the music and song stir; who can recognize the true sound?"
He asked again: "Fengxue transmitted the seal; Nanyuan passed on the robe. Master Zhao propagated the teaching in the West River region, while Master Song led his disciples at Binglei.
Thus, the purport of the Southern School flourished greatly in the northern lands. Now tell me, from whose grace and power did these two masters receive their transmission?"
The Master said: "I do not enter the lotus pond to bathe; I am too lazy to travel to the Snowy Mountains. Yang said: "Ten thousand bodhisattvas within the Cool Mountain. The Master said:

"The assembly of sages gathered at the Vimalakīrti conference. Li said: "Carrying dry firewood on one's back, one encounters a wild fire. The Master said: "The mouth is the gate of calamity. [Question:
"In the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, one penetrates above the sun and moon; in the Fourth Dhyāna, one avoids the disaster of wind and fire."
Three crossings, driving the great ox-cart; facing you, grasping the seal of the total提 (ti).
The monkey has a single-sided ancient mirror; the cat has ten-thousand-mile divine light. Who is it that directly takes this up? The Master said:
"In the morning look to the southeast; in the evening observe the northwest. Yang said: "The cat and the white ox, however, know there is [something]. The Master said: "Drowned in the tomb."
"Head-weeds. Li Yun said, "A cooking oil cauldron in the moon. The Master said, "The waist-belt of a stone man. He asked again, "All Buddhas are entirely within this;
to move is to lose one's body and life, and to look upon it is to be blind at both ends.

At the moment of deliberation, there are thousands of mountains and ten thousand waters. Even if you understand it directly, you are still sitting in a pit of charcoal. Is there anyone who does not spare their eyebrows?"
Mao said, "He has come to deliver a message. The Master said, "A hundred fragments in disarray. Yang said, "In my whole life, I have never spoken falsely. The Master said, "You must still say it.
Li said, "A rabbit emerging from its burrow caught in a snare. The Master said, "Unobstructed in the east and west;
attaining mastery in the north and south. He then added a verse: "A single word just uttered penetrates the Dragon Court, Agitating Mount Sumeru and the Emperor of Heaven."
Śāriputra was startled. The Buddhas of the three periods of time sat down all at once; a puppet on a staff twitches its eyes. Yang replied:
"This year’s peach and plum are sweet and fragrant; for a thousand pieces of gold, one may buy a single fruit to taste. A gourd for storing medicine drags a rat's tail."

The orifice is small and narrow; it is difficult to hide within. The Master replied: "A peach pit from a thousand years ago has never been known to have fragrance. Though spring arrives many times, it is hard to find one to taste it.
The numinous tortoise drags its tail to erase its tracks; yet when it carries its young in the sand, it is even harder to hide.
Yang replied again: "Mañjuśrī is on Mount Wutai; the Arhats dwell in the caves of Tiantai. I ask you, Purple Hu—"
"A single dog. How is it that Puhua was a donkey? The Master replied: "Suddenly hearing the lion’s roar, the majesty of the elephant king is brought forth.

Holding fast the path of the holy and the ordinary, who would dare lift an eyebrow? To deliberate for as many kalpas as grains of sand, or to stir a thought, is to be separated by a thousand diverging paths.
In the blink of an eye one has gone to another realm; one has already been plastered with ash. Yang replied again: "Sitting within a spider's web."
The insects dare not pass; last night there were three feet of snow. All the birds have suffered from hunger. The fruit ripens and the branches bow low;
the geese are so fat they break the bamboo steamer lids. I ask you, Nun of Mount Moshan: how does she compare to Liu Tiemo? The Master answered again:

The mountain is high and few can climb it; the sea is deep and its bottom cannot be seen. The woodcutter needlessly wears out his shoes; the fisherman has no reason to boast of the water. Having said this, he fell silent.
"Transcending ten billion [worlds], he gathers them back to Vimalakīrti. If one seeks a fellow traveler, they would not have recognized each other for kalpas on end.
The Master composed this verse of the fundamental source: "Looking left and looking right, it is a blur at twilight; stretching out his hand and returning, it is already revealed.
But tell me, what is the phrase that reveals? Yang said: "Right at the moment of killing someone, the blind man sticks his head out. The Master said: [He has spoken.]
With both feet slightly off the ground, he stands empty-handed with his hands crossed over his chest. Lin says: "The left whiskers and right hair conceal patterns.
The Master says: "Fame and profit have already spread throughout the world; a young girl rides a cow backward. The Master speaks again:
"When Vimalakīrti remained silent and Mañjuśrī praised him as excellent—if I, this old monk, had been there, I would have given each of them thirty blows. Now tell me, what about these two elders?"
"Where does the fault lie? Yang said, "His head would split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree.
The Master said, "Kāśyapa did not raise his fist; Ānanda did not join his palms. Li said, "It is like a young calf before it has grown horns.
The Master said, "In haste, he clenched his fist and struck the gavel. The Master spoke again: "The scriptures have clear evidence: 'The Buddha-body pervades the entire Dharma-realm.'"
"The old monk today fills the entire dharma-realm. Where is the Secretariat Director right now?
Yang said, "A single piece of coarse cloth skirt, with knees protruding. The Master said, "Wide-mouthed cloth trousers and a three-foot staff. Li said, "..."
"A load of river water is worth three coins. The Master said, "One sees only the moisture on the tip of the nose; one does not see the dampness behind the crown.
When Minister Zheng visited Chan Master Fenyang Shanzhao during a tea conversation, the Minister said, "I have composed a verse to present to you, Master.
The verse says: 'Do not let yellow paper blind your eyes; The blue clouds naturally provide their own shade. Do not take the learning of the mundane And bury your true nature beneath it.'"

"The Patriarch’s Mind. He further said, "Use this verse alone to test the elders throughout the land. Fenyang said, "If that is so, then Fenyang is also inside it. Guobu said, "Carrying the cangue, he passes through the legal proceedings.

Zhao said, "There will be no further interrogation. Guobu said: The Patriarch’s Mind. He further said, "Use this verse alone to test the elders throughout the land. Fenyang said, "If that is so, then Fenyang is also inside it. Guobu said, "Carrying the cangue, he passes through the legal proceedings. Zhao said, "There will be no further interrogation. Guobu said:
This is a case of double meaning. Zhao said, "If you know, you have attained it. After a long silence, Zhao let out a sigh.
Huibao said, "Wenbao! Wenbao! Zhao asked, "Where are you? Huibao said, "I cannot even get to breathe;
how can I bear his saying that the Elder has been detained here? Zhao asked, "What kind of talk is this? Huibao said, "It is true. Zhao said, "Not so."

He was granted leave to depart. The head of the community said, "I request a verse from you, Master. Zhao replied, "I am not practiced in this. Nevertheless, he took up brush and ink and wrote on the paper:
Seeking a secluded path through the wild weeds, The rock pines spread their shadows far and wide. How many seekers of the profound mystery Have lost their original mind!
While the Master was under the assembly at Shoushan, one day he asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Shoushan replied, "Chu (the state of Chu)."
By the side of the royal city, the river Er flows to the east. It was here that the Master attained great enlightenment and composed three verses on the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan), saying:
"If you must use it, you must use it directly; let not the mind and intellect waver. When the lion roars at three years of age, the fox species vanish from the ten directions.

I possess the nature of True Suchness (Tathatā), as if hidden behind a curtain. Break through the gates of the six sense-doors, and the seal of Vairocana is revealed. This is the true bone [of the teaching].

"The Vajra-body may be praised; with a single sweep away of the six sense-objects, there is forever no obstruction. The vast and empty world takes emptiness as its essence; within that essence, non-action is truly arriving home.
At that time, Shoushan heard of this and invited the Master for tea. He asked, "Did you compose those three verses yourself? The Master replied, "Yes.
Shoushan said, "Suppose someone were to instruct you to manifest the thirty-two marks [of a Buddha]?"
"How is it? the Master asked. The Mountain said, "I am no wild fox spirit. The Master said, "Save your eyebrows.
The Mountain said, "How many have you dropped, monk? The Mountain struck the Master on the head with his bamboo staff and said, "This fellow will go on to act recklessly hereafter.
Afterward, when the Master took his leave of the Mountain, the Mountain entrusted him with his staff. Having received it, the Master spoke this verse: "Master," [he began].
Still leaning on his staff, [Zhaozhou] pierced through the dragons and elephants; the家风 (family style) of Linji had fallen into my palm.
Sanshan said, "Do not involve me in this. The Master struck him with his sitting mat. Sanshan said, "As expected, you have involved me. The Master said, "Today I have caught this old thief.
Sanshan said, "It seems you have gained the advantage, yet it seems you have lost the advantage."
