The Master said, "How can it compare to the spring breeze, idle everywhere? [Question: "What is the white ox on the open ground? The Master said, "Under the moon, there is no need for color. [Question: "What does it eat? The Master said, "From ancient times to the present, no one has been able to chew it. [Question: "I ask the Master to answer the question. The Master said:
"The old monk ought to act thus.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "To conceive a thought is already a deviation. A monk then asked, "What is it like when one does not conceive a thought?

The Master struck him three times and said, "Is it that I, the old monk, am failing you, O *dānapati*? Another asked, "In all instances of question and answer, one falls into the realm of the mental faculty (*manas*)."
[The student] said, "It does not fall within the scope of the mental faculty (*manas*). How would you respond, Master? The Master said, "Ask. The student said, "I request the Master to speak.
The Master said, "Do not engage in right and wrong here. [The student] asked, "When the Dragon Girl personally offered [the Buddha] the [lotus], what did she offer with?
The Master made a gesture of offering with both hands."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "In this place, the Buddha-dharma is such that what is difficult is easy, and what is easy is difficult.
Elsewhere, it is difficult to see but easy to recognize; here with me, it is easy to see but difficult to recognize. If you can understand this, you may roam freely throughout the world.
Suppose someone were to ask where you have come from; if you were to tell them you have come from Zhaozhou, you would be slandering Zhaozhou."
"The Way does not come from Zhaozhou; furthermore, it obscures one's own self. How, then, will you all respond to him?
A monk asked, "When everything one encounters is slander, how can the Master avoid being slandered? The Master said, "If you say you are not slandering, you have already slandered.
A monk asked, "What is the path of correct cultivation? The Master said, "If you understand cultivation, then you have attained it. However,"
Failing to understand how to practice, they immediately fall into the trap of cause and effect. It is further said:
"I teach you that if someone asks, simply say to them, 'Zhaozhou has come. If they suddenly ask what Dharma Zhaozhou preached, simply say to them, 'When it is cold, I say it is cold;
when it is hot, I say it is hot. If they ask further about anything other than this matter, simply say:"
[The Master] asked, "What matter? [The monk] asked again, "What Dharma does Zhaozhou speak? The Master said to him, "When the Master came, he did not instruct me to deliver a message.
If you, Venerable One, wish to know Zhaozhou’s affairs, simply go and ask him yourself.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when one disregards what precedes and follows? The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment the disregard of what precedes and follows: whom are you asking?"
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Kāśyapa transmitted it to Ānanda; tell me, to what person did Bodhidharma transmit it? A questioner asked:
"As for the Second Patriarch obtaining the marrow, how was that? The Master said: "Do not slander the Second Patriarch. The Master continued: "Bodhidharma also had these words:
'He who is outside obtains the skin; he who is inside obtains the bone. Tell me, what about one who is even further inside?"
“What have you attained? The questioner asked, “What is the principle of attaining the marrow? The Master said, “Just recognize the skin;
in my place, even the marrow is not established. He asked, “What is the marrow? The Master said, “At this rate, you have not even touched the skin.”
Question: "So majestic and imposing—this is surely the Master’s 'right position,' is it not?

The Master said: "Do you know anyone who does not approve of this? The student said: "If that is so, then there must be another position. The Master said: "Who is the one who is different? The student said:

"Who is the one who is not different? The Master said: "Call out as much as you wish. Question: "When a person of the highest caliber is given a single push, they turn immediately. But when a person of the lowest caliber comes along—"

"How is it? The Master said, "You are the highest of the high; you are the lowest of the low. The monk said, "I request the Master to provide an answer. The Master said, "The answer has no master yet.

The monk said, "I have come from seven thousand *li*; do not act with a calculating mind. The Master said, "Based on this one question of yours, would it not mean that your calculating mind has failed?
This monk departed after staying for only one night. Question: What about one who comes from a collateral line and does not inherit? Like...
"What? the Master asked. "Who? the student replied. "Whom do you ask about? the Master asked. "One who does not come from the collateral line," the student replied.
The Master stroked him with his hand and asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said, "Do not deceive yourself.
He asked, "True Suchness and ordinary or holy beings are all but dream-talk; what, then, is the true word? The Master said, "I shall say no more than these two."
The student said, "Setting aside those two for a moment, what is the true word? The Master said, "Oṃ buraṇ phaṭ. The student asked, "What is Zhaozhou?
The Master said, "The East Gate, the West Gate, the South Gate, and the North Gate. The student asked, "What is concentration (samādhi)? The Master said:

“Indeterminate. The student asked, “Why is it indeterminate? The Master said, “A living thing. A living thing. The student asked, “What is it like when one does not follow after the various states of being?
The Master said, “It should be thus. The student said, “Is this not precisely the fundamental matter of the student? The Master said, “It is.”
"It is following. It is following. A question was asked: "In the past, for thirty years one drew a bow and released two arrows, yet could only shoot half a sage.
Today, I ask the Master to shoot the whole. The Master then rose and departed.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "The ultimate Way is without difficulty; it is only that one dislikes making discriminations. As soon as there are words, there is discrimination;
there is clarity. Yet I, this old monk, do not abide within clarity. Do you still cherish it or not? A student asked:
"Since the Master does not abide within clarity, what is it that you cherish? The Master said: "I do not know either. The student said: [I do not understand.]
"Since the Master does not know, why do you say it is not within clarity? The Master said, "You may ask about the matter as you wish;
having finished your prostrations, withdraw."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "The Dharma is fundamentally unborn; now it is without extinction. Do not even say that speaking is birth and silence is extinction.
But tell me, how do you understand this principle of being neither born nor extinguished? A monk asked, "Is it not already neither born nor extinguished?
The Master said, "This fellow only recognizes dead words. A monk asked, "The Ultimate Way is without..."
“Difficult. It is only that it dislikes discrimination. As soon as there are words, there is discrimination. How do you, Master, instruct people?
The Master said, “Why do you not quote the words of the ancients in full? The student said, “I have only managed to reach this point. The Master said, “It is precisely this:
‘The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination.’”
Ascending the hall, he said: "Studying the sutras is within birth and death; not studying the sutras is also within birth and death.
How, then, do you all manage to escape? A monk then asked: "What is it like when neither is retained? The Master said:
"If it is real, one immediately attains it. If it is not real, how could one possibly escape birth and death? Question: "When the edge of a sharp sword is keen, what is it like?
The Master said: "I am the sharp sword. Where is its keenness? Question: "When a great peril arrives, how does one avoid it?
The Master said: "It is exactly so."
The Master ascended the hall. After a long silence, he asked, "Has the entire assembly arrived yet? A monk replied, "The entire assembly has arrived.

The Master said, "I shall speak only when one more person arrives. The monk said, "Wait until no one else arrives, and then you may speak to the Master. The Master said, "It is difficult indeed to find such a person."

The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "When the mind arises, all manner of phenomena arise; when the mind ceases, all manner of phenomena cease. How do you all understand this? A monk then asked:
"What is it like at the moment when there is neither arising nor ceasing? The Master said: "I grant you this one question.
Later, while in meditation, the Master remarked: "It is clear, yet not yet clear; the darkness is fading and the dawn is about to break. Where are you?"
"Neither at either end," the monk said. The Master said, "If that is so, then it must be in the middle.
He said, "If it is in the middle, then it is at either end. The Master said, "How long has this monk been here with me making such talk?
He cannot get out of these three phrases. Even if he were to get out, he would still be within the three phrases. You—"
“How is it? The monk said, “I have mastered the three phrases. The Master said, “Why did you not speak this way earlier?
A monk asked, “What is universal penetration? The Master said, “Depart from the Diamond Meditation.”

The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Monks of the patched-robes school must directly cut off the heads of the Reward-Bodies and Transformation-Bodies Buddhas before they can succeed. A questioner asked:
"Who is it that cuts off the heads of the Reward-Bodies and Transformation-Bodies Buddhas? The Master said: "It is not within your realm."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold. A monk then asked:
"What form or appearance is present before one's eyes that would allow a student to behold it? The Master said: "It does not matter whether you are south of the Yangtze or north of it.

The monk said: "Does the Master have no expedient means to help people? The Master said: "What was the question just now? [The monk] asked: "Having entered the Dharma-realm, do you still know there is [something more]?"
[The student] said, “There is not. The Master said, “Who enters the Dharma-realm? The student said, “If it is so, then one does not even know where to go upon entering the Dharma-realm.
The Master said, “It is not cold ashes or dead wood; flowers and brocade manifest, and there are a hundred kinds of existence.

The student said, “Is this not the functioning within the place of entry into the Dharma-realm? The Master said, “What connection is there? [The student] asked, “If it is the ground of the principle of ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*):”
"From where did you get that? The Master said, "Please, Venerable, recite it once more. [The student] asked, "When the myriad objects arise together, is there anything that cannot be deluded by them?
The Master said, "There is. The student asked, "What is that which cannot be deluded? The Master said, "Do you believe that the Buddha-dharma exists?
The student said, "I believe the Buddha-dharma exists. The Master said, "The ancients have already spoken of this; how [do you understand it]?"
The student said, "This delusion cannot be grasped. The Master said, "Why do you not ask the old monk? The student said, "I have already asked.
The Master said, "It is a delusion. A question was asked: "I wonder, is there still a proximity between the ancients and people of today?
The Master said, "They are indeed proximate, yet they are not of one and the same substance. The student said, "Why are they not the same? The Master said, "The Dharma-body does not speak."
Fahui asked, "The Dharma-body does not preach the Dharma; does the Master not have a person [to preach]? The Master said, "I answer within the realm of wisdom.

Fahui said, "How can you say that the Dharma-body does not preach the Dharma? The Master said, "Within the realm of wisdom, I rescue your father; he simply will not show his head. A question was asked:
"When practitioners do not see one another, is there still mutual accommodation? The Master said: *Note: The final response to the last question is omitted from the source text.*
The Master said, "I can fathom their mutual reversals. The student said, "If you cannot fathom them, what is there to reverse?
The Master said, "Not being so is your own self. The student said, "Does the Master yourself also admit to being fathomed? The Master said, "People are drawing closer."
"The Way is becoming increasingly distant. The student asked, "Why did the Master hide himself away? The Master said, "I am now speaking with you right here.
The student asked, "How can you say it is not becoming distant? The Master said, "It should be understood in this way."

The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Those whom one succeeds in transforming and teaching are matters of this present life; those whom one fails to transform and teach are enemies from a third lifetime.
If one does not transform and teach them, there is fear that all sentient beings will fall into ruin; yet even transforming and teaching them constitutes an enmity."
"Are you still teaching and transforming others? The monk said, "I am. The Master said, "Do all sentient beings see you?
The student said, "They do not. The Master said, "Why do they not see you? The student said, "Because I am formless (*animitta*).
The Master said, "Do you see me, this old monk, right now? The student said, "The Master is not a sentient being. The Master said, "Then recognize your own fault."
[The Master] immediately attained it.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "The Dragon Girl’s heart was intimate in her offering; all of this is a matter of spontaneity. A questioner asked:
"If it is already spontaneous, why did she offer [the pearl]? The Master said: "If she had not offered it, how would one know it is spontaneous?"
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Of eight hundred men who have become Buddhas, it is difficult to find even one true practitioner.
A monk asked, "In a place where there is neither Buddha nor person, is there still any practice? The Master said, "Setting aside those two, there are hundreds of thousands of millions of others.
The student asked, "When a practitioner comes, where are they? The Master said, "If you think in such a way, you are not [a practitioner]."
[The Master] was practicing meditation. The monk prostrated. The Master said, "There is a great place for you to be situated. A monk asked, "When white clouds do not fall, what then?
The Master said, "This old monk does not know how to ride an elephant. The student said, "Is there no guest and host? The Master said, "I am the host;
you, Dharma brother, are the guest. Where are the white clouds? A monk asked, "When great skill appears as if clumsy, what then?"
"What? The Master said, "You have lost the timber for a ridgepole.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "As for the word 'Buddha,' I do not like to hear it. A monk asked, "Does the Master still act for the sake of others or not?"
The Master said, "To act for others. The student asked, "How does one act for others? The Master said, "Not knowing the profound principle, one's efforts at contemplating stillness are in vain."
The student said, "Since it is 'mysterious,' what is the essential meaning? The Master said, "I do not hold a text. The student said, "This is the mystery;
what is the essential meaning? The Master said, "My answer to you is the essential meaning."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Each person has their own Zen; each person has their own Way. Suppose someone were to ask you, 'What is Zen?

What is the Way? How would you answer him? A monk then asked: "If each person already possesses Zen and the Way, why have there been so many discourses from the ancient masters down to the present day?
The Master replied: "It is because you are wandering ghosts. The student asked: "I do not yet understand how that is so."
The Master then withdrew and remained silent.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Do not pass your time idly; recite the Buddha's name and contemplate the Dharma. A monk then asked: "What is the practitioner’s own recitation?
The Master said: "Who is it that recites? The student said: "It is without companion. The Master rebuked him: "You donkey!"
Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "If it is the first phrase, it serves as the teacher for the patriarchs and Buddhas.
The second phrase serves as the teacher for humans and devas. The third phrase does not even suffice to save oneself. A monk asked, "What is the first phrase?
The Master said, "It serves as the teacher for the patriarchs and Buddhas. The Master added, "Excellent! Start from the beginning. The student asked again. The Master said:

Furthermore, he has sent away both humans and devas. The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "It is not that he did not bring it; it is not that I, the old monk, do not respond. A monk asked: [Why did you say this? The Master said: "If I had said it was because he did not bring it, I would have been wrong. If I had said it was because I did not respond, I would have been wrong. The monk said: [What then is the meaning? The Master said: "I am not one who does not respond. The monk said: [How so? The Master said: "Because I am not one who does not respond. The monk said: [Then what is the response? The Master said: "The response is right here before you. The monk said: [Is there no other way to express it? The Master said: "There is no other way to express it. The monk said: [If there is no other way to express it, then why do you speak of 'not bringing' and 'not responding' now? The Master said: "Because you have not yet seen through your own nature, I speak thus. The monk said: [If I were to see through my own nature, what would be the case? The Master said: "If you were to see through your own nature, you would be like me. The monk said: [What is it like being like you? The Master said: "Like a mirror reflecting all forms without discrimination. The monk said: [If it is like a mirror reflecting all forms without discrimination, then how can there be the distinction between seeing through one's own nature and not seeing through it? The Master said: "The distinction lies in whether or not one recognizes the mirror itself as the source of all reflections. The monk said: [If the mirror is the source of all reflections, then what is the nature of the mirror? The Master said: "The nature of the mirror is such that it neither comes nor goes, neither arises nor ceases. The monk said: [If it neither comes nor goes, neither arises nor ceases, then how can it reflect all forms? The Master said: "Precisely because it neither comes nor goes, neither arises nor ceases, it is able to reflect all forms without obstruction. The monk said: [If it reflects all forms without obstruction, then why do you say that it is not something that can be grasped or described? The Master said: "Because it is beyond words and descriptions, it is called the Great Mirror Wisdom. The monk said: [If it is the Great Mirror Wisdom, then what is its function? The Master said: "Its function is to illuminate the path of all sentient beings, leading them to liberation. The monk said: [If it leads all sentient beings to liberation, then why do some remain in samsara while others attain nirvana? The Master said: "This is due to the karmic conditions of each individual. The Great Mirror Wisdom is impartial and does not discriminate. The monk said: [If it is impartial and does not discriminate, then why do we speak of good and evil, cause and effect? The Master said: "Good and evil, cause and effect, are all manifestations within the Great Mirror Wisdom. They do not exist apart from it. The monk said: [If they do not exist apart from it, then how can one transcend them? The Master said: "Transcendence is simply realizing that there is nothing to transcend. The monk said: [If there is nothing to transcend, then what is the ultimate goal of practice? The Master said: "The ultimate goal of practice is to realize the non-duality of self and others, and to dwell in the state of great equanimity. The monk said: [If one dwells in the state of great equanimity, then what is the nature of that state? The Master said: "The nature of that state is such that it cannot be defined by any conceptual mark. It is the realm of the Buddhas and the patriarchs. The monk said: [If it is the realm of the Buddhas and the patriarchs, then how can ordinary people enter it? The Master said: "Ordinary people can enter it by casting off all deluded thoughts and returning to their original nature. The monk said: [If one returns to one's original nature, then what is the original nature? The Master said: "The original nature is the very mind that asks these questions right now. The monk said: [If it is the very mind that asks these questions right now, then why do I still feel confusion and doubt? The Master said: "Confusion and doubt arise precisely because you do not recognize your own mind. If you recognize it, there is no confusion or doubt. The monk said: [If there is no confusion or doubt, then what is the experience of enlightenment? The Master said: "The experience of enlightenment is like the sun rising in the sky: it illuminates everything, leaving nothing in darkness. The monk said: [If it illuminates everything, leaving nothing in darkness, then what is the darkness that remains? The Master said: "The darkness that remains is the darkness of ignorance. When ignorance is dispelled, there is no darkness left. The monk said: [If there is no darkness left, then what is the light of wisdom? The Master said: "The light of wisdom is the light of the Dharma-nature. It is eternal and unchanging. The monk said: [If it is eternal and unchanging, then why do we speak of birth and death, coming and going? The Master said: "Birth and death, coming and going, are all illusory appearances within the Dharma-nature. They have no reality apart from it. The monk said: [If they have no reality apart from it, then how can one escape the cycle of birth and death? The Master said: "To escape the cycle of birth and death is simply to realize that there is no cycle to escape. The monk said: [If there is no cycle to escape, then what is the meaning of liberation? The Master said: "Liberation is the realization that one has always been free. The monk said: [If one has always been free, then why do we seek liberation? The Master said: "We seek liberation because we have forgotten our original freedom. Once we remember it, there is no seeking left. The monk said: [If there is no seeking left, then what is the practice of a Bodhisattva? The Master said: "The practice of a Bodhisattva is to benefit all sentient beings without attachment, and to cultivate the six paramitas until they reach perfection. The monk said: [If one cultivates the six paramitas until they reach perfection, then what is the fruit of that cultivation? The Master said: "The fruit of that cultivation is the attainment of Buddhahood. But even Buddhahood is ultimately empty and non-existent. The monk said: [If even Buddhahood is empty and non-existent, then what is the ultimate truth? The Master said: "The ultimate truth is beyond words and concepts. It can only be realized through direct experience. The monk said: [If it can only be realized through direct experience, then how can one transmit it to others? The Master said: "Transmission occurs when the teacher and student meet in a state of mutual resonance. It is like two mirrors reflecting each other. The monk said: [If it is like two mirrors reflecting each other, then what is the essence of that reflection? The Master said: "The essence of that reflection is the Great Compassion of the Buddhas. It never ceases to guide all sentient beings. The monk said: [If it never ceases to guide all sentient beings, then why do some receive the teaching and others do not? The Master said: "This depends on the karmic roots of each individual. The Great Compassion is impartial and does not choose. The monk said: [If it is impartial and does not choose, then why do we speak of the distinction between the Mahayana and the Hinayana? The Master said: "The distinction between the Mahayana and the Hinayana is a provisional teaching for those of different capacities. In the ultimate sense, there is only the One Vehicle. The monk said: [If there is only the One Vehicle, then what is the purpose of the various teachings? The Master said: "The purpose of the various teachings is to lead all sentient beings to the One Vehicle. The monk said: [If they lead all sentient beings to the One Vehicle, then what is the final destination of the journey? The Master said: "The final destination of the journey is the realm of the Tathagata. There, all phenomena are merged into the single Dharma-realm. The monk said: [If all phenomena are merged into the single Dharma-realm, then what is the nature of that realm? The Master said: "The nature of that realm is such that it cannot be described. It is the realm of the Buddhas and the patriarchs. The monk said: [If it is the realm of the Buddhas and the patriarchs, then how can ordinary people enter it? The Master said: "Ordinary people can enter it by casting off all deluded thoughts and returning to their original nature. The monk said: [If one returns to one's original nature, then what is the original nature? The Master said: "The original nature is the very mind that asks these questions right now. The monk said: [If it is the very mind that asks these questions right now, then why do I still feel confusion and doubt? The Master said: "Confusion and doubt arise precisely because you do not recognize your own mind. If you
"What will you use to answer? the Master asked. The monk heaved a long sigh. "What will you use this time, Master?
the monk asked. "Will you not let me down? The Master said, "If you had accepted me just now, I would have let you down.
Since you did not accept me, I have not let you down."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Tonight, this old monk shall provide answers. Anyone who can ask a question, come forward! A monk stepped forth and bowed. The Master said:
"I had hoped to throw a brick to draw out a gem, yet I have received nothing but a cinder block.
[The monk] asked: "Does a dog possess Buddha-nature or not? The Master said: "No. The student said: "From the Buddhas above down to the ants below, all possess [Buddha-nature]."
[The monk asked: "Why does the dog lack Buddha-nature? The Master said: "Because it possesses the nature of karmic consciousness.
[The monk] asked: "What is the Dharma-body? The Master said: "The Response-body. [The monk] said: "I am not asking about the Response-body. The Master said:

"You simply take care of the Response-body. [The monk] asked: "When the bright moon is suspended in the sky, what then? The Master said: "What is your name, Reverend? The student said: "My humble self."
The Master said, “When the bright moon is suspended in the sky, where is it? A questioner asked, “What is it like exactly at the time of the second and eighth days of the month?
The Master said, “East, west, east, west. The student asked, “What is ‘east, west, east, west’? The Master said, “It cannot be found.

A questioner asked, “What is it like when the student does not understand anything at all? The Master said, “I do not understand either. The student said, “Does the Master know that there is [something]?”
[The monk] said, “None. The Master said, “I am not a piece of wood. How could I not know? [The monk] said, “It is wonderful that you do not understand.
The Master clapped his hands and laughed. [The monk] asked, “What is a man of the Way? The Master said, “I tell you, he is a Buddha-man.

[The monk] asked, “Whenever there are words and phrases, or the raising of a hand and the moving of a foot, it all falls within the net of the student. Apart from this, please speak for me, Master. The Master said:
The old monk had finished his meal but had not yet drunk tea. Master Ma asked, "Does the Master still practice cultivation?
The Master said, "If this old monk were to practice cultivation, it would be a disaster. [Ma] said, "Since the Master does not practice cultivation, who then is to practice it?
The Master said, "You, Master Ma, are the one who practices cultivation. [Ma] said, "How can I be called one who practices cultivation? The Master said, "If..."
"Without practicing [the Way], how could one hope to be thrust into the position of a human king? One is fed until one is nearly frozen red upon the earth, with no time for release in sight.
Thereupon, the Great Official shed tears and bowed in gratitude.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "It is not that you, O *ācārya*, did not bring it forth; it is not that this old monk does not respond. He further said:
"Do not raise your fists or join your palms, O *ācārya*; this old monk will not respond with the meditation seat or the whisk.
A question was asked: "What is it like when one cannot reach it through thought? The Master said: "Come over here. [The questioner] said: "Coming over here is precisely where one reaches it. As if...
"What is this place that is beyond the reach of thought? The Master raised his hand and said, "What do you call this?
The monk replied, "I call it a hand. The Master asked, "And what do you call mine, O Monk? The Master said, "I could give it a hundred names.
The monk said, "That is beyond your hundred names, Master; what would you call it then? The Master said, "In that very state is where your thoughts cannot reach. The monk bowed.

[The monk] prostrated. The Master said, "I am teaching you to reflect upon it until you can grasp it. [The monk] asked, "What is it? The Master said, "The teachings of Śākyamuni and the teachings of the Patriarchs are your teachers.
[The monk] said, "As for the Patriarchs and the Buddhas, the ancients have already spoken of them.

What is the point where one cannot reflect upon it? The Master again raised his finger and asked, "What do you call this? The monk remained silent for a long while. The Master said, "Why do you not respond?"
He said, "The head has already been struck; what more is there to doubt? A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "This old monk is deaf.
Ask in a loud voice. The monk asked again. The Master said, "You ask about my house style, yet I recognize your own house style."

Question: "When the ten thousand objects arise all at once, how is it? The Master said: "The ten thousand objects arise all at once. [The monk] asked: "One question and one answer constitute 'arising.
What is 'non-arising'? The Master said: "The meditation seat is non-arising.

Just as the monk was about to prostrate, the Master said: "Do you remember the question and answer? [The monk] said: "I remember. The Master said: "Try to recite them. As the monk was about to speak, the Master questioned him: "What is like..."
"What is the Buddha of the present? The Master said, "The one in the hall. [The student] said, "That is the Buddha of appearance.
What is the Buddha? The Master said, "This very mind is it. [The student] said, "This 'very mind' is still a limitation. What is the Buddha? The Master said, "No-mind is it.
The student said, "As for having mind and no-mind, do you permit a student to choose between them or not? The Master said, "Having mind..."
[The Master] said: "Your mind has been entirely selected by you. What more could this old monk say? A student asked:
"I have come from afar to seek a teacher. May I ask what your house style is like? The Master said: "I do not speak of it to others. The student asked: "Why do you not speak of it to others?
The Master said: "That is my house style. The student said: "Since the Master does not speak of it to others, how can one..."
Hai came to take refuge [with the Master]. The Master said, "You are Hai; I am not Hai. The student asked, "I do not understand how matters are within the sea.
The Master said, "The old monk has caught one. He then asked, "Who is it that neither the Buddhas nor the patriarchs can approach?"
The Master said, "It is neither the patriarchs nor the Buddhas. The student asked, "How can it be that one cannot approach it?
The Master said, "I told you it is neither the patriarchs nor the Buddhas, neither sentient beings, nor things. Do you understand? The student asked, "What is it?
The Master said, "If it had a name, it would be the patriarchs, the Buddhas, or sentient beings. The student said, "One must not simply go on like this. The Master...
[Yun] said, “I have not yet given you leave to go. [The Master] asked, “What is the ordinary mind? The Master said, “Foxes, wolves, and jackals are it.
[The Master] asked, “By what skillful means can one hear that which has not been heard? The Master said, “Setting aside for a moment that which has not been heard, what have you ever heard?
[The Master] asked, “The teachings state: ‘A mani jewel that follows colors. What is its original color?”
The Master called the monk’s name. The monk responded, “Yes. The Master said, “Come over here. The monk then crossed over. The Master asked again, “What is your true nature?
The Master said, “For now, follow the colors. A student asked, “Does the person of ordinary mind still receive instruction and transformation?
The Master said, “I do not enter through his gate. The student said, “If that is so, then do not sink that person on the other side.”
[The student] said, "Ma. The Master said, "Very good, the ordinary mind. [The student] asked, "What is the thing that a student must maintain?
The Master said, "It cannot be singled out until the end of the future. [The student] asked, "Who is the person of great cultivation? The Master said, "The administrators of the monastery are.
[The student] asked, "As soon as a student arrives, they do not know anything at all; what about the affairs of the gate? The Master said, "Up!"
"What is your name? The student said, "Huinan. The Master said, "Excellent! You do not even know [your own name]. A question was asked:
"A student wishes to learn, yet he also slanders the Master. How can he avoid slandering you? The Master said, "What is your name? The student said, "Daojiao."
The Master said, "The one who goes to a quiet place is the rice granary. A question was asked: "What is the Great Meaning of the Master? The Master said, "Neither great nor small.
The student said, "Is this not the Great Meaning of the Master? The Master said, "If there were even a hair’s breadth [of it], ten thousand kalpas would not suffice.
A question was asked: "The myriad dharmas are fundamentally at rest, yet people themselves create clamor. Whose words are these? The Master said, "It is spoken by one who has emerged."
“Come, and you die. A questioner asked, “It is not the Buddha, it is not an object, and it is not a sentient being. This is a definitive statement. What is an indeterminate statement?
The Master said, “Above the heavens and below the heavens, I alone am honored. A questioner asked, “What is the Perfect Circle of Vairocana?
The Master said, “Since I was a child and left home to become a monk, my eyes have never seen spots. The student said, “Does the Master still [see them]?”

[The student] said, "There is no such thing as being a person. The Master said, "I wish for you to see the circular form of Vairocana forever. [The student] asked, "When the Buddhas and Patriarchs were alive, they transmitted [the Dharma] from Buddha to Buddha and from Patriarch to Patriarch.
After the Buddhas and Patriarchs have passed away, who transmits it? The Master said, "From antiquity to the present, it has always been within my own sphere.
The student said, "I do not yet understand what it is that is transmitted. The Master said, "Every single one is entirely subject to birth and death. [The student] said, "That cannot be."
[The Master] said, "This has buried even the Patriarchs. The Teacher asked, "What have you transmitted? [The monk] asked, "When both ordinary people and sages are exhausted, what then?
The Teacher said, "I wish you would become a Great Virtue; I am but an old monk who obstructs the Buddhas and Patriarchs. [The monk] asked, "I have heard of Zhaozhou from afar;
why do I not see him upon arriving here? The Teacher said, "It is my own fault. [The monk] asked, "A bright moon is suspended in the sky; I wonder about the room..."

The student said, "If that is so, then the Master does not act for the sake of the present age. The Master said, "If one cannot save oneself from illness, how can one save others from their illnesses?"
The student said, "What can be done about the fact that the student has no place to rely? The Master said, "If you rely, you will step on the ground;
if you do not rely, go freely wherever you wish. A question was asked: "When the mind does not fathom the mind, what then? The Master said, "Fathom whom? The student said, "Fathom oneself.
The Master said, "There are not two. A question was asked: "When the boundaries and surface are not seen, what then? The Master pointed to a pure water jar and said: [It is here.]
"What is it? The student said, "A pure water jar. The Master said, "Very good; you do not see its boundaries. Question:
"What is returning to the root? The Master said, "To intend is already to deviate. Question: "Without departing from words and phrases, how can one attain solitary liberation?
The Master said, "Departing from words and phrases is solitary liberation. The student said, "Just now, no one taught me to come here. The Master said, "For what reason did you arrive?"
The student said, "Why does the Master not select [the right one]? The Master said, "I have already selected it long ago.
A question was asked: "That which is not mind is not yet wisdom. Please, Master, give us a single phrase. The Master said, "I am behind you.

A question was asked: "What is the ultimate reality? The Master said, "The ultimate reality. The student said, "Which one is the ultimate reality? The Master said, "I am the ultimate reality; you are not."

The student did not understand the Master’s words. The student said, “It is not that I do not ask. The Master said, “Ultimately, where does it reside? A student asked, “What is it like when one is not hung with even an inch of silk?
The Master said, “What is there to not hang? The student said, “Not hanging even an inch of silk. The Master said, “Excellent! Not hanging even an inch of silk!
A student asked, “What about a person who is as if their head were on fire and they must extinguish it immediately? The Master said, “Just practice.”
The student said, "Where? The Master said, "Do not occupy another's seat. The student asked, "Who was the master during the empty eon?
The Master said, "I am sitting right there. The student asked, "What Dharma do you teach? The Master said, "I teach what you have asked."
Question: I have heard it said in the past that "emptiness and luminosity illuminate themselves. What is meant by "self-illumination"? The Master said:
"It does not refer to being illuminated by another. The student asked: "What is it like when there is no place for illumination? The Master said: "Your speech has fallen into error.

Question: "What is 'it'? The Master said: "At the moment before a single thought has arisen. Question: "Who is the Dharma King? The Master said: "The Great King in the prefecture is. [The student] said: "..."
"The Master is not so. The Master said, "You intend to rebel. Altogether, there is but one King, yet you do not recognize him.

but can he still be accepted? The Master said, "Let me see how you would teach others. A question was asked: "Among the three bodies [of the Buddha], which..."
"What is this original body? The Master said, "It cannot be lacking even one thing. A student asked, "I do not know who the patriarch is in this land.
The Master said, "Since Bodhidharma came here, all have been [patriarchs]. The student said, "In what position is the Master? The Master said, "I do not fall into a sequence of ranks.
The student said, "Where then are you? The Master said, "In your ears. A student asked, "Without abandoning the source..."
"Do not pursue the secondary. What is the Right Path? The Master said, "A truly fine renunciant. The student said, "I have never been a renunciant from the start.
The Master said, "Take refuge in the Buddha; take refuge in the Dharma. The student said, "I do not know for certain whether there is a 'home' to be renounced or not.

The Master said, "You must simply renounce it. The student said, "Where would you arrange him? The Master said: [Note: The provided text ends abruptly with "The Master said: following the final exchange.]
"Furthermore, sit at home. A student asked, "When one with clear eyes sees all things, does he still see form? The Master said, "Strike it down! The student asked, "How can one strike it down?

[The monk] said, "Is this not it? The Master said, "I have never used this to instruct people.

[The Master] distinguished the phrases. Question: "What is the Master’s very own meaning? The Master said: "Stop, stop; there is no need to speak. My Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive. Question:

The Master said, "Yes. The scholar said, "May I beg for the staff in your hand, Reverend?

"What is it? The old woman said, "There is not a single dharma that can be taken as an object of the mind. The Master said, "Hmph! The old woman said, "Hmph!

I made a cotton robe in Qingzhou that weighs seven *jin*. Question: What is one who has left the home life? The Master said: [Silence].

*The Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters*, Volume Fourteen:
The Continued Record of Chan Master Zhaozhou Zhenji. The Master ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying:
"The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the wooden Buddha does not pass through fire; the clay Buddha does not pass through water."
Water. The True Buddha sits within; bodhi, nirvana, suchness, and buddha-nature are all but clothes clinging to the body—they are also called afflictions.
Do not inquire about them, and there will be no afflictions. Upon the ground of ultimate reality, where would they be placed?
When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault. Simply investigate the principle and sit for twenty or thirty years. If you do not understand, cut me down!
The old monk’s head is gone; it is like a dream, an illusion, or a flower in the sky—exerting oneself to grasp at it is merely labor in vain.

If the mind does not differ [from its true nature], then the myriad dharmas are likewise so. Since they are not obtained from without, what more is there to be constrained? It is like a sheep: why do you further scramble for things and put them in your mouth?
When I saw Master Yaoshan say, "If someone asks you something, simply tell them to shut their dog's mouth," I understood.
The old monk also says: "Shut your dog's mouth! To grasp at 'me' is defilement; not grasping at 'me' is purity.
It is just like a hunting dog, intent only on getting something to eat. Where would you place the Buddha-dharma?

how would you respond? The Master said, “Salt is expensive; rice is cheap. Question: “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Are you the Buddha?”
Question: "What is leaving home? The Master said: "How could you see this old monk? Question: "What is the point where the Buddhas and Patriarchs do not cease?
The Master said: "There is no omission. Question: "I beg the Master to point out the original source. The Master said: "The original source has no illness. [The student] said: "..."

[The monk] asked, "Does a person who dwells in unconditioned tranquility fall into a state of sunken emptiness? The Master said, "They do fall into sunken emptiness. [The monk] said, "I have investigated this thoroughly."

[The monk asked: "In the end, what of it? The Master said: "To become a donkey or a horse. [The monk] asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "It is the bed-legs.

[The monk asked: "What is it like at that time? The Master said: "From where does it arise? [The monk] asked: "What is it like when, on the ground of the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), not even a single speck of dust is admitted?

The Master said: "Everything is entirely contained within it. [The monk] asked: "What is the one phrase? The Master responded with an affirmative "Yes. The monk asked again. The Master said: "I am not deaf. [The monk] asked:

[The Master] said: “Take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha. Do not bite the old monk. A questioner asked:

The Master said: “What do you say, *ācārya*? A questioner asked: “What is the one phrase? The Master said: “Say what? A questioner asked: “How is it? The Master said: “Say what?”
"This is one phrase. The Master said, "Two phrases. A question was asked: "How is it that only the Buddha alone is the true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)? The Master said:
The Demon’s Words. Question: “What is bodhi? The Master said: “This is an icchantika. Question: “What is the mark of a great man?
The Master said: “A fine child. Question: “When all is silent and there is no dependence, what then?
The Master said: “I am behind you, old monk. Question: “What is a monastery (saṅghārāma)? The Master said: “What else is there? [The questioner] said: “How so?”
[The monk] was a person from this monastery. The Master said, "I, the old monk, and you, Dharma brother. [The monk] asked, "When two dragons contend for a pearl, who is the one that obtains it?

"I do not say that I receive the myriad streams. Question: "What is Vairocana? The Master said: "Vairocana. Vairocana. Question: [The questioner asked again.]
"Do all Buddhas have a teacher? The Master said, "They do. [The monk] asked, "Who is the teacher of all Buddhas? The Master said, "Amitābha Buddha. Amitābha Buddha.

the water has no sound as it plunges into the ravine. [The monk] said, "I did not ask about that. The Master said, "It is you who do not recognize your own teacher. [The monk] asked, "All..."

The Master said, "This salt-smuggler! [The monk] said, "And what is it like when one does travel the Great Way? The Master said, "..."
"Bring me back my official pass! A question was asked: "What is the original body? The Master said: "Ever since you recognized this old monk, this very fellow has been none other than that.
[The student] said: "If it is so, then I have passed away from one life to another from the Master. The Master said: "..."
"Not only in this life; even through a thousand or ten thousand lifetimes, you would not recognize this old monk. A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said: "The ultimate truth is indeed not non-existent; it is simply that one cannot observe it. Question: "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said: "Losing the ultimate truth."

Question: "When practice has not yet reached [the goal], and when questioning has not yet reached [the truth], what then? The Master said: "Reaching is non-reaching; a man of the Way regards it as spittle and saliva.
[The student] asked: "What is the matter within that? The Master spat on the ground. Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
"If you do not call it the 'Patriarch's meaning,' you have still not arrived. [The student] said: "As for that which is original..."
"What? The Master said, "The four eyes gaze at one another; there is no second sovereign. Question: "Even without physical form or appearance, is there still understanding?
The Master said, "Do you understand right now? Question: "What is a person who has great shamelessness?
The Master said, "All possess the inconceivable. Question: "I, this student, intend to go to the South to study a little of the Buddha-dharma."

The Master said, "Vast is the universe, and countless are the people. [The student] said, "Please, Master, do not answer with words. The Master said, "It is fitting for this old monk to be thus. A question was asked:
"When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, "The loser suffers no loss; the winner suffers no gain."

[The Master] used [it]. A question was asked: "What is the mark of a great man? The Master said: "What is it? A layman offered him a *kāṣāya* robe and asked: [the same question]. The layman said: "If you do not realize the fruit, who is it that is called a sage? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a sage. The layman said: "If you are not a sentient being, who is it that is called a living being? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a living being. The layman said: "If you are not a living being, who is it that is called a creature? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a creature. The layman said: "If you are not a creature, who is it that is called a being? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a being. The layman said: "If you are not a being, who is it that is called a self? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a self. The layman said: "If you are not a self, who is it that is called a person? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a person. The layman said: "If you are not a person, who is it that is called a master? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a master. The layman said: "If you are not a master, who is it that is called a teacher? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a teacher. The layman said: "If you are not a teacher, who is it that is called a guide? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a guide. The layman said: "If you are not a guide, who is it that is called a leader? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a leader. The layman said: "If you are not a leader, who is it that is called a savior? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a savior. The layman said: "If you are not a savior, who is it that is called a refuge? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a refuge. The layman said: "If you are not a refuge, who is it that is called a protector? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a protector. The layman said: "If you are not a protector, who is it that is called a field of merit? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a field of merit. The layman said: "If you are not a field of merit, who is it that is called a vessel of the Dharma? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a vessel of the Dharma. The layman said: "If you are not a vessel of the Dharma, who is it that is called a recipient of the teaching? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a recipient of the teaching. The layman said: "If you are not a recipient of the teaching, who is it that is called a follower of the path? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a follower of the path. The layman said: "If you are not a follower of the path, who is it that is called a practitioner? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a practitioner. The layman said: "If you are not a practitioner, who is it that is called a seeker? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a seeker. The layman said: "If you are not a seeker, who is it that is called a renunciant? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a renunciant. The layman said: "If you are not a renunciant, who is it that is called a monk? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a monk. The layman said: "If you are not a monk, who is it that is called a bhikṣu? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a bhikṣu. The layman said: "If you are not a bhikṣu, who is it that is called a śramaṇa? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a śramaṇa. The layman said: "If you are not a śramaṇa, who is it that is called a holy one? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a holy one. The layman said: "If you are not a holy one, who is it that is called a noble one? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a noble one. The layman said: "If you are not a noble one, who is it that is called a saint? The Master said: "It is the one who is not a saint. The layman said: "If you are not a saint, who is it that is called a realized one? The Master said:
"Wearing such garments as these, will you not fail the ancients? The Master threw down his whisk and said, "Whether ancient or modern.
A monk asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Stretch out the hands, but do not stretch out the feet.
A monk asked, "How was it before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Full of firewood; full of water. [The monk] asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "Full."
The firewood was soaked with water. A student asked, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "Have you finished eating your congee yet?
He replied, "I have finished. The Master said, "Go wash your bowl. A student asked, "What is the Vairocana Teacher? The Master said, "Has the white camel arrived yet?
He replied, "It has arrived. The Master said, "Lead it away to graze on grass. A student asked, "What is untaught wisdom? The Master said:
The old monk has never instructed you, Dharma-heir. [The student] asked: "What is the one phrase of intimacy? The Master said: "The talk has fallen away. [The student] asked:
"Without using the mouth, is it still permissible to deliberate? The Master said: "It is precisely the time for it. [The student] said:

"I ask the Master to deliberate for me. The Master said: "The old monk has never brought it forth. [The student] asked: "When the Second Patriarch cut off his arm, what was he doing? The Master said: "Powder."
[The Master] broke his bones and shattered his body. [A monk] asked, "To whom do you make offerings? The Master said, "I offer to whoever comes. Question:

"Why did the Bodhisattva Anantagātra not see the crown of the Tathāgata’s head? The Master said, "You are an ācārya. Question: "Day is the light of the sun; night is the light of fire. What is divine light?
The Master said, "The light of the sun and the light of fire. Question: "What is it? The Master said, "The light of the sun and the light of fire."
[The monk] asked at the very point [of inquiry]. The Master said, "Wrong. [The monk] asked, "What is the state beyond questioning?

The Master said, "Discern it within the preceding phrase. [The monk] asked, "What is the mark of a great man? The Master reached toward his face with his hand, crossed his arms, and assumed a solemn expression.
[The monk] asked, "What is the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*)? The Master said, "This is the conditioned (*saṃskṛta*). [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said, “The ox has been lost in the pen. A student asked, “I have come from afar; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, “As soon as you enter the gate, you should spit right in my face. A student asked, “What is the direct, single path? The Master said, “Has the boatman of Huainan arrived yet?
The student said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “It is fortunate that you have come. A student asked, “Does the cypress tree [have Buddha-nature]?”...
"Is there buddha-nature or not? The Master said, "There is. [The student] asked, "When will you become a buddha? The Master said, "Wait for empty space to fall to the ground."
[The monk] asked, "When will empty space fall to the ground? The Master said, "Wait until the cypress tree attains Buddhahood.
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Why do you revile the old monk here in the monastery? [The monk] said, "What fault have I committed?
The Master said, "I cannot allow you to revile me here in the monastery. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said—
[The Master] said, "Hairs grow on his teeth. A question was asked: "When the poor man arrives, what will you give him? The Master said, "He is not poor.

[The questioner] said, "But how can he avoid seeking out the Master? The Master said, "He simply remains in poverty. A question was asked: "Why does the Bodhisattva Anantagātra not see the crown of the Tathāgata’s head?
The Master said, "It is as if separated by a fine silk gauze. A question was asked: "Regarding the nectar of the devas, who is it that..."

[The monk] said, “I may eat. The Master said, “Thank you for bringing it. A question was asked: “What of one who transcends heaven and earth? The Master said, “Wait until there is such a person, and then inform me.
A question was asked: “What is a monastery (saṃghārāma)? The Master said, “The triple gate and the Buddha hall. A question was asked.
"What is non-arising and non-ceasing? The Master said, "Originally it has never arisen; now it likewise does not cease. Question: "What is the Lord of Zhaozhou?

The Master said, "It is the Great King. Question: "At the point of urgency, I pray that the Master will speak. The Master said, "Urination is a minor matter; it must be for the old monk himself to go about it.
Question: "What is the sixteen-foot golden body? The Master said: *Note: The final response regarding the "sixteen-foot golden body" is omitted from the source text.*

[The Master] did not strike the collar [of the robe]. The student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, ask someone else to cut it for you. A question was asked: "What should one do when a student has doubts?
The Master said, "Large is suitable; small is suitable. The student said, "Large doubts. The Master said, "Large is suitable for the northeast corner;
small is suitable behind the Sangha Hall. A question was asked: "Who is the person above the Buddha? The Master descended from his meditation seat and ascended again.
Guanzhan said, "This fellow is so tall and large he could be cut into three stakes. What is there to ask about 'upward' or 'downward'?
A nun asked, "What is the secret, hidden meaning? The Master pinched her with his hand.
She said, "The Master still has this. The Master said, "It is you who have this."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Thirty years ago, when I was in the South at the head of the brazier, there was a 'guestless and hostless' koan.
To this very day, no one has brought it forth. A monk asked: "World-Honored One, you have received such offerings from the Great King."
"What will you offer in return? The Master said, "Recite the Buddha's name. [The monk] said, "Even a poor man knows how to recite the Buddha's name.
The Master said, "Call the attendant and give him one coin. [The monk] asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Though the screen is broken..."
The skeletal frame still remains. [Question: What is the meaning of “non-transmigration”? [Master: You say this wild duck flies from east to west. [Question:
What is the meaning of the [Buddha’s] coming from the West? [Master: From where have you received this news? [Question: Who is the person amidst the dust? [Master:
Bring me some money for tea and salt. [Question: Great... (Note: The final character "大" (dà) appears to be an incomplete fragment.)

Ear Sanzang said for the third time, “I have searched for the National Preceptor but cannot find him. I do not know where the National Preceptor is. The Master said, “He is inside your nostrils, Sanzang.
A monk asked, “What is it like when the blind turtle encounters the hole in the floating wood? The Master said, “It is no mere coincidence.
A monk asked, “What is it like when one has long dwelt in mountain ravines? The Master said, “Why do you not hide away? A monk asked, “If it is like this...”
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Prostrate yourself. As the monk was about to offer his words, the Master called for the novice Wen Yuan.
When Wen Yuan arrived, the Master rebuked him, saying, "Where have you been just now? [The monk] asked, "What is one's own original intent?
The Master said, "I do not need an ox-slaying blade. [The monk] asked, "I have long heard of Zhaozhou’s Stone Bridge; having come here..."
[The Master] saw only a rickety footbridge. The Master said, "Dharma brother, you see only the rickety footbridge; you do not see Zhaozhou’s Stone Bridge. [The monk] asked, "What is the Stone Bridge?
The Master said, "Come over here, come over here. He added, "It carries donkeys and it carries horses.
[The monk] asked, "What is your surname, Preceptor? The Master said, "It is found in Changzhou. [The monk] asked, "How old are you? The Master said, "It is found in Suzhou."
Ascending the hall, he said: "As soon as there is right and wrong, one is distracted and loses one's mind. Is there still any possibility of answering the question?
A monk stepped forward, struck the attendant once, and said, "Why do you not answer the Master? The Master then returned to his quarters.

Later, the attendant requested further instruction, asking, "Was that monk who just now here capable or not? The Master replied, "The seated one sees the standing one; the standing one sees the seated one."
[The Master] was sitting at the bottom [of the hall]. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "The one outside the wall. The monk said, "I am not asking about that.

The Master said, "Which Way are you asking about? The monk said, "The Great Way. The Master said, "The Great Way leads straight to Chang'an. A monk asked, "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then?
The Master said, "Brushing away the dust is not non-existent; seeing the Buddha is not to be attained. A monk asked, "What is the sickness-free? The Master said...
[The Master] said: "The four great elements and the five aggregates. [The student] asked: "What is icchantika? The Master said: "Why do you not ask about bodhi?"
[The Master] asked, "What is bodhi? The Master said, "This very thing is precisely the icchantika. At times, the Master would count his fingers and say, "I, this old monk, call this a fist;
what do you all call it? A monk said, "Why does the Master use an external object to point it out to people?
The Master said, "I am not using an external object to point it out to you. If I were to use an external object to point it out to you, Ācārya, I would be burying you."
Leaving, he said, "What can be done about this? The Master then said, "Take care. A question was asked:

"If one question and one answer both fall into the realm of heavenly demons and external paths, and even if one remains silent, one still violates the net of the Buddha’s teachings—what is the house style of Zhaozhou?"
The Master said, "You do not understand how to ask. [The monk] said, "I request the Master to provide an answer. The Master said, "According to you, you deserve twenty blows of the staff."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "As soon as there is right and wrong, one becomes distracted and loses one's mind. Is there still any possibility of answering the question?
A monk stepped forward, gave a novice a slap, and then departed. The Master immediately returned to his quarters.
On the following day, he asked his attendant, "Where was that monk yesterday? The attendant replied, "He left at once. The Master [nodded].
[The Master] said, "For thirty years I have been riding horses, yet I was knocked off by a donkey. A monk asked, "Do you still receive those who come in such a manner?
The Master said, "I receive them. The monk asked, "Do you still receive those who do not come in such a manner? The Master said, "I receive them."
[The Master] said: "If you come this way, I will receive you as a teacher; if you do not come this way, how will the teacher receive you? The Master said: "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak.
My Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive. The Great King of Zhin asked: "Venerable Master, how many teeth do you still have?"
The Master said, "There is only one tooth. The Great King said, "How can it eat anything? The Master said, "Even though there is only one, it bites down on everything.
A monk asked, "What is the student’s pearl? The Master said, "Ask in a loud voice. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "You do not know how to ask. Why not say, 'I do not ask about high or low; what is the student’s pearl? Why [not ask this]?"
[The Master] asked thus. The monk then asked again. The Master said, "I almost let this fellow pass. Question: "Both extremes are silent; how do you, Master, proclaim the Dharma?
The Master said, "This year there is no wind or waves. Question: "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; what should they discuss?
The Master said, "Today we are hauling timber to erect the Sangha Hall. [The monk] said, "Is it not just this very thing that constitutes receiving students?"
[The monk] said, "There is no person. The Master said, "This old monk does not understand double-sixes, nor does he understand chess.
[The monk] asked, "What is the true human body? The Master said, "Spring, summer, autumn, and winter. [The monk] said, "If it is so, it is difficult for this student to understand.
The Master said, "You ask me about the true human body. [The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "What is your name?"
[The Master] says: "So-and-so. The Teacher says: "Within the Han-yuan Hall; amidst the Jin-gu Garden. [The student] asks: "What is the teacher of the seven Buddhas?"
The Master said, "If you wish to sleep, then sleep; if you wish to rise, then rise. A questioner asked, "The Way is not outside of things, and that which is outside of things is not the Way.
What is the Way outside of things? The Master struck him. The man said, "Master, do not strike me; later on, you may strike the wrong person.
The Master said, "Dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish; it is the patch-robed monks who are difficult to deceive. When the Master saw the Great King enter the hall, he did not rise.
He patted his own knee with his hand and said, “Do you understand? The Great King said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “I have been a monk since childhood and am now old;
when I see people, I lack the strength to descend from my meditation seat. [Someone] asked, “What is loyal speech? The Master said, “Your mother is ugly.
[Someone] asked, “How is it for one who has remained mindful from the past until now? The Master said, “It is impossible to fix the mind constantly.”
"Recall all the Buddhas of the ten directions. Question: "What is loyal speech? The Master said: "Eat an iron staff. Question: "What is the matter that lies beyond the Buddha?
The Master then clapped his hands and laughed loudly. Question: "One lamp lights hundreds of thousands of lamps;
from what place does that original lamp arise? The Master then kicked out a single sandal and said: "If you are a master, then..."
"Do not ask in that way. [The monk] asked: "When one returns to the root and attains the essential meaning, yet follows after illumination and loses the fundamental source—what then?
The Master said: "I do not answer this question. [The monk] said: "I beg the Master to answer the question. The Master said: "It should be so. [The monk] asked: "What is the state beyond thought?
The Master said: "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! [The monk] asked: "Ascending to Tuṣita at night and descending to Jambudvīpa by day—within this, what is..."
“What kind of mani-jewel does not appear? The Master said, “Say something! The monk asked again.
The Master said, “Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on this long ago; until this very day, he has not attained the wondrous. Question: “What is it like in a place beyond thought?
The Master said, “Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Question: “What is the treasure within the robe? The Master said, “What do you dislike about this one question? [The monk] said, “This...”
[The monk] asked, "What is this? "How is it with the Jewel? The Master said, "In that case, you have lost your robe. [The monk] asked, "When there is no inn for ten thousand miles, what then?
The Master said, "Stay overnight at a Chan monastery. [The monk] asked, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not?
The Master said, "Before every door, the road leads to Chang'an. [The monk] asked, "When presented face-to-face, is the Great Meaning fully exhausted or not? The Master...
[The Master] said, "Lower your mouth. [The student] asked, "What about when there is nowhere to collect? The Master said, "I told you to lower your mouth.
[A student] asked, "What is the one phrase of the present moment? The Master said, "I, this old monk, am not as good as you. [A student] asked, "Who is it that comes forth?"
The Master said, "Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. A questioner asked, "How is it when the numinous grass has not yet grown? The Master said, "If you smell it, your skull will split open.

The questioner asked, "And how is it when one does not smell it? The Master said, "It is like a man standing dead. The questioner asked, "Do you permit students to harmonize [with this]? The Master said, "When people come, do not speak of it to them.
A questioner asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "Just as soon as..."
Before he had received the precepts after leaving the household life, he went everywhere asking people about the Dharma. He asked, "What is the holy? The Master said, "Not ordinary.
He asked, "What is the ordinary? The Master said, "Not holy. He asked, "When it is neither ordinary nor holy, what then? The Master said, "A fine Zen monk.
Another asked, "When two mirrors face each other, which one is the clearest? The Master said, "Your eyelids, Reverend, cover Mount Sumeru."
A questioner asked: "A student has recently entered the monastic community; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "Heaven! Heaven! The questioner asked:

"The former phrase has already passed; how is it when the latter phrase is difficult to clarify? The Master said: "To call it such is not permissible. The questioner said: "I ask the Master to explain it for me."

The Master said: "Question! Question! [The student] asked: "What is it like when [the path] is high and steep, difficult to ascend? The Master said: "I, this old monk, do not go to the summit of the high peak.
[The student] asked: "Who is it that does not act as a companion to the myriad dharmas? The Master said: "A non-person. [The student] asked:

"Please grant the Master one phrase regarding the Middle Way of the *Zhongsheng* (Dharma-vehicle). The Master said: "Today I have no money to give to the magistrate. [The student] asked: "As for the student..."

[The student] asked another question. The Master did not answer separately. The Master said, "How strange! [The student] asked, "Outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles, how do you receive people?
The Master said, "Since this world came into being, the sun and moon have never changed. [The student] asked, "When the three locations are not interconnected, how does one transcend consciousness?
The Master said, "Consciousness is something external. [The student] asked, "When all capacities and conditions converge, I do not yet know what the matter therein is. The Master—
[The Master] said, "My eyes are fundamentally upright; I do not speak of what lies within them. A questioner asked, "If one does not stop at the pure ground, what kind of person is that?
The Master said, "You are not yet a person among those within. The questioner asked, "What is it to be a person among those within? The Master said, "Stop! [The questioner] asked.
"What is the source of the myriad dharmas? The Master said, "Beams, rafters, pillars, and columns. The student said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "You do not understand even while joining your hands in the *añjali* gesture. A question was asked: "What is it like when one brings nothing at all? The Master said, "Put it down."
Question: When meeting a man who has attained the Way on the road, one does not respond with speech or silence. I wonder, what then does one use to respond?
The Master said: "A person comes from Chenzhou; he brings no news from Xuzhou. Question: Opening the mouth is conditioned activity (*saṃskṛta*). What is the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*)?
The Master pointed with his hand and said, "This is the unconditioned. [The monk] asked, "This is the conditioned;
what is the unconditioned? The Master said, "The unconditioned. [The monk] said, "This is the conditioned. The Master said, "It is the conditioned."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "As for the single word 'Buddha,' I do not like to hear it. A monk asked: "Does the Master still act for the sake of others?
The Master said: "Buddha. Buddha. A monk asked: "Having exhausted the present moment, what is the very point?
The Master said: "Having exhausted the present moment, do not ask about that. The monk said: "What is the point? The Master said: "I told you not to ask. The monk said: "How so?"

[The student] said, “I have seen it. The Master said, “Great, there is nothing outside; small, there is nothing inside. [The student] asked, “When one is free from the four propositions and transcends the hundred negations, what is it like?
The Master said, “This old monk does not recognize death. [The student] said, “This is a matter concerning the Master’s own domain.

The Master said, “Exactly so. [The student] said, “I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, “When one is free from the four propositions and transcends the hundred negations, with what would you instruct me?”
Question: What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "Within, there is not a single thing; without, there is nothing sought. Question:

What is returning to the root and attaining the essential meaning? The Master said: "To answer you would already be a deviation. Question: What is the doubting mind? The Master said: [To speak of it]—*text breaks off*.

The Master replied, "Your answer is already mistaken. A questioner asked, "Does one who has left the household life ever become a layperson again? The Master said, "One who leaves the household life is simply a Dharma master.

Whether he leaves or does not leave, I, this old monk, do not concern myself with it. The questioner asked, "Why do you not concern yourself with it? The Master said, "If it were otherwise, that would be leaving the household life.
A questioner asked, "What is it like when there is no teacher for a disciple? The Master said, "The nature of untainted wisdom is fundamentally [so]."
"Complete. He further said, "This one is a disciple without a teacher. A question was asked: "When neither the boundaries nor the center are seen, what then?
The Master said: "Why do you ask such a thing? A question was asked: "When it is clear yet not pure, and turbid yet not muddy, what then? The Master said: "Neither pure nor muddy.
[The questioner] said: "What is this? The Master said: "How pitiable! [The questioner] said: "What is 'universal penetration' (tongfang)? The Master...

[The Master] said, "Set aside Vajra-dhyāna. A question was asked: "What is the treasure within the bag? The Master said, "Why do you find fault with it? [The questioner] said, "What if its use is inexhaustible?
The Master said, "Is that which belongs to oneself heavy? He added, "When used, it is heavy; when not used, it is light. A question was asked:
"What is the very intent of the Patriarch? The Master spat. [The questioner] said, "As for the matter therein, it is like..."
[The Master] spat on the ground. [The student] asked: "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said: "Transcending practice. [The student] asked:

"Please point out the place of true rest. The Master said: "Pointing would not be resting. [The student] asked: "How is it when there is no question? The Master said: "It deviates from ordinary speech. [The student] asked:
"When the four mountains press in from all sides, what then? The Master said: "There is no trace of exit. [The student] asked: "Upon reaching this point, you say 'no'—"

"How is it when [the Way] is attained? The Master said, "One cannot speak of it. [The student] asked, "How then does one speak of it? The Master said, "In the place where it cannot be spoken. [The student] asked.
"All words and phrases ultimately do not transcend the summit. What is that which lies outside the summit? The Master called for the novice Wen-yuan.
"Wen-yuan," he called, and the novice responded. The Master said, "It is already late this afternoon. [The monk] asked, "What is the Vairocana Teacher? The Master said:
"Do not speak with harsh words. A question was asked: "The ultimate Way is without difficulty; it is only that one dislikes making discriminations.

How can one avoid making discriminations? The Master said: "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. [The student] said: "This is still discrimination. The Master said: "You low-born fellow!
Where is there any discrimination here? A question was asked: "What is it to be a person outside the triple world? The Master said: "What can you do? I, the old monk, am right here!"
"Within the three realms. Question: "What about one who knows both existence and non-existence? The Master said: "If you ask further, you will be asking me, this old monk, on purpose."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Go toward the south to seek out the monastic groves; do not remain here. A monk then asked: "Master, what place is this? The Master said:
"This place of mine is a forest of firewood. The monk asked: "What is the Vairocana Teacher?"

The Master said, "Nature is the disciple. [The disciple] asked, "What is it like when one returns to the root and attains the essential meaning? The Master said, "Too hurried! [The disciple] said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "From where does 'not understanding' arise? Prime Minister Liu entered the monastery and saw the Master sweeping the ground.
Question: "Great Good Spiritual Friend, why do you sweep away the dust? The Master said: "It comes from without. Question:

"When a sharp sword emerges from its scabbard, what is it like? The Master said: "Black. Question: "At the very moment of asking, how does one distinguish the white? The Master said: "There is no leisure for such effort. Question:
"When one joins the palms before another, what can be done about it? The Master said: "I have seen you joining your palms at all times."
