At the hour of Ren (11 p.m. to Ding (3 a.m.), who would not cherish the bright moon before their door? Within, one only worries about the time of lying down to sleep;
what clothes are there to wear, and what can cover [one]? Layman Liu, Upāsaka Zhao Wu—though their mouths speak of goodness most wonderfully, let the mountain [remain as it is].
The monk’s bag is empty; when questioned, he has no connection to anything and understands nothing at all.
Son of the midnight hour, when have the mind and its objects ever found even a moment’s rest?

When one considers the renunciants throughout the world, how many can there be who serve as abbots like me? A simple earthen bed, a broken reed mat, an old elmwood pillow, and absolutely no bedding. The honored image is not...
When burning frankincense, one perceives only the scent of cow dung within the ashes.
Seeing the construction of a stupa, there is a verse that says:
"Since it is originally perfected in itself, why labor to pile stones? To speak of carving and engraving names is worlds apart from my [view]. If someone should ask about this:
He never pointed or drew lines.
Seeing that the views and understandings of various quarters followed divergent paths, he then composed the verse:
"South of Zhaozhou, north of Shiqiao; within Guanyin Monastery is Maitreya. The Patriarch has left behind a single sandal."
"Up until now, I have not been able to find it.
Because of the fish-drum, there is a verse:
'The four elements have long been the work of creation; its sound is entirely precious because of the emptiness within. Do not blame me for not giving it to the common man.'"
It is said that this is simply because the musical scales of the *gong* and *shang* differ.
Because of the lotus, there is a verse of extraordinary beauty:
"The roots and sprouts bear snow-fresh purity; one knows not from which era it was distinguished in the Western Heaven. Whether the mud is deep or shallow, no one [can fathom it]."
Upon emerging from the water, he finally realized it was a white lotus.
Attached to this is the eulogy for the Master composed by the Prince of Zhao:
"The moon over the emerald stream; a head within the clear mirror. My teacher, my transformation—Zhaozhou of the world."
Lamenting Master Zhaozhou, Two Poems The Master departed from Yungshui, stirring kings and lords;
The light of the Mind-Seal was withdrawn as the whisk was tucked away. Mist and haze shroud the moon over the pine-clad ridges;
Waves submerge the ferryman’s boat upon the blue ocean. As the single lamp is suddenly extinguished, Pāpīyas rejoices; The two eyes of the Way are once more shrouded in darkness.
Companion in Grief. Though you are a traveler beyond the clouds who has attained clarity, tears still flow whenever I gaze upon your vase and desk.
The Buddha-Sun sets in the west and the Patriarchal Seal is shattered; the pearl sinks into the vermilion pond and the moon’s radiance fades.

Shadows spread through the chamber as the incense smoke grows somber; the wind rises in the meditation hall and the pine tones grow faint. With a single sandal, you have recently left behind traces of your transformation; where in the Five Indias will you appear again?
Upon encountering the return [of the text], the disciples who have realized emptiness were moved beyond both grief and joy; yet they remained tearful before their snow-covered curtains.
This was further collated and finalized by the Dharma-transmitting, purple-robed Śramaṇa Chengti, incumbent of Qixian Baojue Chan Monastery on Mount Lu.
Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Fourteen;
Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Fifteen:
The Extensive Record of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen, Part One.

Compiled by the late Master Shoujian, who was granted the purple robe by the Great Master and whose disciples clearly recognized his virtue, this is a collection of the Master’s formal discourses given in response to specific occasions.
After a long silence, he said: "The dynamic of proclaiming the Way is indeed difficult to reconcile or dissect; yet, if even a single word..."

The *qì* (seals/affinities) are already manifold; how much more so when they are explained at great length. What benefit would there be [in such detail]? Nevertheless, within the vehicles of the teachings (*jiao-cheng*), each has its distinct classification:

the Vinaya constitutes the study of precepts (*śīla-śikṣā*), the Sūtras constitute the study of concentration (*samādhi-śikṣā*), and the Śāstras constitute the study of wisdom (*prajñā-śikṣā*). The Three Piṭakas, the Five Vehicles, the Five Periods, and the Eight Teachings each have their respective points of convergence.
However, the Perfect and Sudden One Vehicle (*ekayāna*) is extremely difficult to clarify. If one can realize it directly and immediately—[then it is understood].

This is worlds apart from the realm of the patch-robed monk (*śramaṇa*). If you attempt to present your spiritual mechanism (*jī*) within the words of the monk’s gate, it is merely a vain exertion of thought.
At the threshold of his teaching, there are thousands of variations and myriad distinctions; if you intend to advance forward, your error lies in seeking the path of another’s tongue.
As for the matter that has been handed down from of old—how should one approach it? Can one speak here of "sudden" or "perfect" enlightenment?
"This side" and "that side"—can you attain it? Do not misunderstand. Do not see such a statement and immediately engage in speculative calculation regarding what is neither complete nor sudden.
Here, one must be a person of true caliber before one can succeed.
Do not take the words of your teacher, or words that merely resemble them, or words of mere conjecture, and present them everywhere as your own realization. Do not misunderstand. Just now—

"What matters are there? Examine them by making a definitive resolution before the assembly. At that time, the provincial governor, Lord He, paid his respects and asked, "I, your disciple, request your instruction.
The Master said, "Before one's eyes, there is no grass other than this. An official asked, "Is it not the case that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in the water?

The Master said, "In the clear waves, there is no path through which to penetrate. The official pressed further, "From where did you, Reverend, obtain this? The Master said, "Ask again, and I shall answer once more."
[The monk] asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "At this very moment, what is it like? The Master said, "Layer upon layer, the mountain passes.
An official asked, "Surrounded by a thousand sons, which one is the true heir? The Master said, "The abbot residing below the hall has already received your inquiry.
[Another] asked, "Today you open the feast; with what will you instruct us? The Master said, "Discern deeply the wind that comes. The monk followed up, "Is it not simply this very thing?"
[The monk] said, "Ma! The Master said, "Wrong. [The monk] asked, "Since ancient times, the virtuous ones have transmitted mind by means of mind.

Today, I ask the Master: with what will you provide this teaching? The Master said, "There is questioning and there is answering. [The monk] further said, "If that is so, then the teaching is not in vain. The Master said, "Without questioning, there is no answering.
[The monk] asked, "Generally speaking, every word and phrase is a mistake. What, then, is not a mistake? The Master said, "Right in the wind."
"A single phrase—where does it arise from? The student replied, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said, "Do not err. [The student] asked.
"What is the mechanism of the simultaneous pecking and hatching? The Master said, "An echo. The student asked, "Is there still a response?
The Master said, "Now, proceed slowly. A questioner asked, "What is the matter of the student? The Master said, "Receive this one question with full gravity.

A questioner asked, "What is the single phrase of the separate transmission outside the teachings? The Master said, "Bring it forward and ask before the assembly. The Master added, "Do not say that today you are deceiving me."
Gentlemen, I have no choice but to create a scene of disorder before you.
Should a person of clear vision see this, it would become a laughingstock; now, there is no way to avoid it. Let me ask you all:
what matters have you ever had from the beginning? What have you ever lacked? To tell you that "there is nothing" is already to bury you alive. You must...
Only when you reach this state will you succeed. Do not let your mouth lead you into confusion by questioning your own mind while it remains dark and murky;
there is much more to come tomorrow and the day after.

If your faculties and understanding are hesitant, then for the time being look east and west at the gate of the ancient masters' transformative teachings to see what principle lies therein. Do you wish to understand? It is all because—
It is because you yourself have been steeped in thick delusions for immeasurable kalpas. As soon as you hear someone speak, doubt immediately arises;

you question the Buddha, question the Dharma, question the "upward" path, and question the "downward" path, seeking intellectual understanding. In doing so, you only become further estranged from the truth.
"To conceive a thought is already an error; how much more so to utter words! Is it not the case that there is no conceiving of thoughts?
What else is there? Take care. Question: "What is the 'One Song' of Yunmen? The Master said: "The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. The questioner pressed: "And what about the one who sings it?
The Master said: "For now, proceed slowly. Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "The sun."
Looking at the mountain from within. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Long rain, no sun.
The monk pressed further, "What is 'long rain, no sun'? The Master said, "It is soaking everything through. A monk asked, "What is it that is without a trace? The Master said, "[He] looked."

[The Master] was performing communal labor at Tiantai and traveling the mountains at Nanyue. A questioner asked: "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said: "Nine times nine is eighty-one. A questioner asked:
"What is the student's own self? The Master said: "Traveling the mountains and enjoying the waters. The questioner pressed: "What is the Master’s own self? The Master said:
"Fortunately, the *vina* (chant leader) is not here. A questioner asked: "What is the Teacher of the Doctrine? The Master said: [Silence].
The Master said, "You are being far too impolite. A question was asked: "What is the teaching of one lifetime? The Master said, "I speak to each person accordingly. A question was asked.
"What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said, "Universal. Question: "What is sitting upright and contemplating the true nature of reality (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*)?
The Master said, "Losing money in the river and searching for it in the river. Question: "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "One cannot understand it.
[The student] further asked, "Why can one not understand it? The Master said, "Simply maintain that you cannot understand it. Question: "What is the ordinary state?"
[The Master] said, "In what way do you apply it? The teacher said, "First, where would you go with such entanglements? A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the teachings?
The teacher said, "Which sutra are you looking at? The monk said, "The *Prajñāpāramitā* Sutra. The teacher said, "'The wisdom of all wisdoms is pure'—have you even seen this in a dream yet?"
The monk said, "Setting aside for a moment the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, what is the intent of the teaching?

The Master said, "My heart bears no grudge against others, and my face shows no color of shame; I grant you thirty blows. A monk asked, "How can one repay the four debts of gratitude and the three realms of existence?"
The Master said, "Cradling one's head and wailing to the blue heavens. A question was asked: "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said, "The smell of rice gruel. A question was asked.
"What is samādhi? The Master said, "Come to this old monk and ask; give me back a single phrase.
[The student] asked, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said, "On the water above the mountain to the east. [The student] asked, "I beg the Master to point out a path of entry."
The Master said: "Eating porridge, eating rice.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "I have no choice but to tell you all that there is nothing at all; even this is already a mutual obscuration.
Yet you still wish to step forward, following words and chasing phrases, seeking understanding and interpretation—this leads to a thousandfold divergence."

They make ten thousand distinctions and extensively pose questions and difficulties, winning a victory in every instance; yet their tongues are so slippery that they drift further and further from the Way—when will this ever come to an end?
This very matter, if it were found within words and speech, then how could the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings not contain words?

For what reason, then, is it said that the Way is transmitted separately outside of the teachings? If it were derived from scholarly understanding or intellectual cleverness, then consider the holy ones of the Ten Stages (Daśabhūmi).
People speak of the Dharma like clouds or rain, yet they are still rebuked for their realization of nature as being "like looking through fine gauze.
By this it is known that all those with a mind are worlds apart from the enlightened. Nevertheless, for one who has attained the bottom, how could the fire of the Way ever burn the mouth?
Though speaking of matters all day long, nothing ever hangs upon the lips or teeth; not a single word has ever been uttered.
All day long one wears clothes and eats rice, yet one has never touched a single grain of rice nor hung a single thread of silk.
Even so, this is still merely talk concerning the gate of the teaching hall; one must truly attain such a state before it is realized.

From the perspective of the Zen monk’s school, to present one's spiritual capacity within the words is but a vain exertion of waiting thought. Even if one were to take responsibility for it under a single phrase, it would still be...
The Drowsy One. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the one phrase? The Master said, "Lift it up. The monk asked, "What is silence while speaking?
The Master said, "A clear faculty passing through the palm. The monk pressed further, "What is speaking while silent? The Master said, "Huh!
The monk pressed further, "What is it when there is neither silence nor speech? The Master chased him away with his staff. A monk asked, "What is the Sword of Yunmen?"
The Master said, "Ancestral. [The monk] asked, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said, "Please ask another question.
[The monk] asked, "What is the white ox on the open ground? The Master said, "Confronting the situation, there is no changing the path. [The monk] further asked, "Where do you let it go?"
The Master said: "To raise it again does not transcend the dust. A question was asked: "What is the samādhi of every particle of dust?
The Master said: "Water in the bucket; rice in the bowl. A question was asked: "What is the profound essence of the single suchness? The Master said: "You lack one question. A question was asked:

"What is that which is within the profound? The Master said: "Zhu-tu (a sound). The student pressed further: "How is it so? The Master said: "Withdraw quickly! Withdraw quickly! You are an obstruction."
Someone else asked him. Question: “What is the place beyond deliberation? The Master said: “It is difficult for the conscious mind to fathom. Question:
“What is it like when one ‘borrows light by boring through a wall’? The Master said: “Just so. Question: “What is it like when a single word expresses everything?
The Master said: “Torn asunder. The student pressed further: “How does the Master go about picking it up and handling it? The Master said: “Pick up the dustpan and broom.”

[The Master] said, "Come forward. A questioner asked, "How can one raise the cry so as not to fail the intent of those who have come? The Master said, "What do you say? The questioner pressed further, "Is it still in accord with the intent of those who have come?
The Master said, "Now, proceed slowly. The Master continued, "The Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings—whether explained horizontally or vertically;
even the old monks throughout the world, speaking in every direction—compared to what I am about to speak, which is as fine as the point of a needle, they are all but silence."
The principle is here. To speak in such a manner is already like trying to heal a dead horse with medicine. Nevertheless, how many people have reached this realm?

I do not dare hope that you will have resonance within your words or conceal the blade’s edge within your phrases; yet, in a single blink of an eye, there are a thousand differences—a windless calm where the waves are stilled.
I pray you may partake of this offering. Question: What is the phrase for penetrating the Dharmakāya? The Master said: "Within the Northern Dipper."
[The Master] hid his body. A question was asked: "What is the fundamental principle? The Master said: "No question, no answer. Question:

"What is the meaning of 'the triple world is mind-only' and 'all phenomena are consciousness-only'? The Master said: "Today I do not answer questions. The student pressed: "Why do you not answer? The Master said:
"When will a donkey ever understand? Question: "What is the 'blow-off-hair sword'? The Master said: "Gè (a bone). And again: "Gè."
Yunzi. Question: "What is inner and outer radiance? The Master said: "Where would you ask such a thing? The student said:

"How does one attain clear penetration? The Master said: "Suppose someone were to ask you suddenly; what would you say? The student pressed: "After attaining clear penetration, what then? The Master said:
"Setting aside 'clear' for a moment, give me your 'penetration'. Question: "What is the most urgent phrase? The Master...
[The Master] said, "Eat. A question was asked: "What is the original mind? The Master said, "Clearly manifest when raised up. A question was asked: "What is the aperture of the patch-robed monk?
The Master said, "Letting one move past by a single step. The questioner pressed: "Please, Master, speak. The Master said, "Playing the lute for a cow."
Question: What is the practice of the Mahāyāna? The Master said: "A single cup in hand. Question:

What is the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*)? The Master said: "Entering the Buddha hall from the monks' hall. Question: What is the single phrase that does not touch the lips?
The Master said: "Shut your dog's mouth. Question: What is the ocean-seal samādhi (*sāgaramudrā-samādhi*)? The Master said: "Just pay your respects."
[The student] bows. [The Master] asks, "Wait for me as I go east and west. [The student] asks, "How can one turn and move so as not to fall into stages?
The Master says, "The Southern Dipper has seven; the Northern Dipper has eight."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Brothers, you have all come from various quarters seeking out masters to resolve the matter of birth and death.
In every place you have visited, surely there were no senior elders who offered compassionate and skillful words? Is there any phrase that you have been unable to penetrate?
Come forward and bring it forth; let the old man discuss it with you all. Is there any such thing? Is there any? At that time, a monk stepped forward, intending to speak.
Xin asked next. The Master said, "Depart, depart! The road to the Western Heaven is long, more than a hundred thousand miles," and he immediately descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is the provision for the present age? The Master said, "To speak of it is not difficult; but from where does discernment come?
A monk asked, "What is the eye that does not sleep? The Master said, "It does not recognize. A monk asked, "What is the command that is never transgressed? The Master said, "Which one?"
"Does the master monk see [it] yet? Question: "What is the mark of a great man? The Master then raised his fist. Question:
"What is the point of urgency for a student? The Master said: "Are you afraid that I do not know? Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?"
The Master said, "One Buddha, two Bodhisattvas. A question was asked: "What is the bellowing of the mud ox on the snowy peaks?
The Master said, "Mountains and rivers run. He pressed further: "What is the neighing of the wooden horse of Yunmen? The Master said, "Heaven and earth turn black. A question was asked:

"What is 'the brothers adding ten characters'? The Master said, "I am talking nonsense with you. A question was asked: "What is the Master doing for [the sake of]... The Master said, "I am talking nonsense with you. (repeated)
The Master said, "A person’s word: let the heart not betray others, and let the face show no color of shame. Quickly prostrate three times. Question: "What is the matter of natural spontaneity?
The Master said, "Why do you step forward? Question: "What is the meaning of the teachings? The Master said, "Why do you step forward?"
The Master said, "Your tongue is too talkative; bring me another question. A monk asked, "What is it like to move freely in all directions?
The Master said, "I grant you one point."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To cite a single phrase and instruct you to directly accept it—this is already like spitting filth upon your head.
Even if you were to pluck a single hair and suddenly illuminate the entire world, that too would be like gouging out flesh to create a sore.
Nevertheless, you must truly arrive at this state before it will do. If you have not yet reached it, then for now—"
You may obtain a hollow grasp, but you must instead step back and seek it beneath your own heels; see what kind of principle this is.
There is not so much as a single hair’s breadth here that can provide you with an intellectual understanding or cause you doubt.
Moreover, each of you possesses a matter of your own upon which the great function is manifest before you, requiring no further exertion of even a hair’s breadth of effort.

If you possess this power, you are no different from the Patriarchs and Buddhas. It is simply because your own roots of faith are shallow and your evil karma is thick that you have suddenly sprouted so many horns;
why do you carry your alms-bag across thousands of villages and ten thousand miles to undergo such humiliation?
Furthermore, what is it that you people lack? You great men—whom does this not concern?
If you take sole responsibility for yourself and still do not grasp it, then you must not allow yourselves to be deceived by others or merely follow their instructions.
As soon as you see the old monk open his mouth, you ought to take a millstone and shove it into his mouth; otherwise, you will be like flies on excrement.
They will snatch you away by biting and sucking. Three or five of them gather their heads together to deliberate, thinking, "How grievous it is for our brothers!
Because the ancients, for a time, could not help you, they left behind a word or a half-sentence to provide you with a path of entry.
If you recognize this kind of matter, set it aside and exert some effort yourself; is this not a small measure of intimacy?
This is the place. Give it freely! Give it freely! Time does not wait for man; one cannot guarantee that the next breath will follow the outgoing one.
What other body or mind is there to be used idly elsewhere? You must take this to heart. Be careful. Adieu.
He ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said: "When the eyes encounter things and do not realize the Way, how can one know the path when setting foot upon it?
A monk asked, "What is enlightenment as it meets the eye? The Master said, "Take away the Buddha Hall for me. Another asked, "What is the first phrase?"
The Master said, "Nine times nine is eighty-one. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "Come closer. The monk came forward, and the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "What is the matter of true study? The Master said, "A most auspicious news. The monk pressed further, "Ultimately, whose child is it?
The Master said, "The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. A monk asked, "I have heard the teaching say that all..."
When asked, "How is it when the wisdom of wisdom is purified? the Master spat upon him. The student asked, "And what about the expedient means of the ancients?
The Master said, "Come, come! Cut off your heels and replace your skull. Take away the spoon and chopsticks from within your bowl; take away your nostrils!
The student asked, "How can there be so many such things? The Master said, "You are just bluffing."
Han: [The Master] struck him. [Han] asked: "What is Chan? The Master said: "It is. [Han] further asked: "What is the Way? The Master said: "Attained."
Question: "In what way are all dharmas the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "Old women in the villages of three households fill the streets and overflow the roads.
Do you understand? The student said: "I do not understand. The Master said: "It is not only you who do not understand; there are many others who do not understand either. Question:
"What is it that the students are all clamoring about? The Master said: "The assembly has been standing for a long time."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The entire universe is brought at once and placed upon the lashes of your eyes.
Hearing this being said, I do not dare hope that any of you will come forward and impulsively strike this old monk with a slap.
Rather, proceed slowly and examine it carefully: does it exist or not? What kind of principle is this? Even if you were to attain clarity here, if..."

If you encounter a monk under my gate, I like to strike him until his legs break. If you were a person of true substance, upon hearing where an old master has appeared in the world, you would have spat right in his face to defile his ears and eyes. If you were not such a fellow, as soon as you heard someone mention it, you would immediately take it upon yourself; that would already be falling into the secondary level of functioning. Do you not look at Master Deshan? When he was asked, "What is the Buddha? he struck the man and said, "The one who asks is the Buddha. If you had been there, you would have hit him back and said, "The one who answers is the Buddha. If you had done so, you would have been a true patch-robed monk. But if you had merely said, "I am the Buddha," you would have been a mere ghost of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I am not the Buddha," you would have been a mere corpse of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I am neither the Buddha nor not the Buddha," you would have been a mere carcass of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I do not know," you would have been a mere skeleton of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I don't dare say," you would have been a mere husk of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I don't understand," you would have been a mere shell of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere dregs of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never heard of this old fellow before," you would have been a mere refuse of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never met this old fellow before," you would have been a mere dust of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never known this old fellow before," you would have been a mere shadow of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never recognized this old fellow before," you would have been a mere echo of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere vapor of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never encountered this old fellow before," you would have been a mere trace of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never met this old fellow before," you would have been a mere remnant of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere phantom of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never known this old fellow before," you would have been a mere apparition of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere specter of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere mirage of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never known this old fellow before," you would have been a mere delusion of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere hallucination of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never met this old fellow before," you would have been a mere fantasy of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere dream of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never known this old fellow before," you would have been a mere nightmare of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere sleepwalker of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere sleeper of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never known this old fellow before," you would have been a mere slumberer of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere dreamer of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never met this old fellow before," you would have been a mere dreamer of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere visionary of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never known this old fellow before," you would have been a mere seer of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere observer of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never met this old fellow before," you would have been a mere witness of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere spectator of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never known this old fellow before," you would have been a mere onlooker of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere viewer of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never met this old fellow before," you would have been a mere gazer of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere looker of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never known this old fellow before," you would have been a mere seer of a patch-robed monk. If you had said, "I have never seen this old fellow before," you would have been a mere watcher of a patch-robed monk. If it were not for this, you would all have fallen into the retinue of Māra and destroyed my school. If you truly do not understand—
Furthermore, let us look within the thicket of entanglements. I have often told you:

within every atom of a buddha-field, all the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven, and the six patriarchs of the Tang land—all reside upon the tip of my staff.

They preach the Dharma, manifest supernatural powers, and their voices resonate throughout the ten directions. Do you understand? If you do not, do not try to deceive yourself with empty words. Nevertheless—
"Is it so? Have you yet seen with clear, correct, and true vision?
Even if you have reached such a state, you have not yet dreamed of a monk-sandhī (novice) in a village of three households where one does not meet a single person.
The Master suddenly took up his staff, drew a line on the ground, and said, "All are here. He drew another line and said, "All are here and gone. Take care."
Question: "What was the meaning of the ancients facing the wall? The Master said: "The twenty-seventh day. He also said: "Samādhi. Question:
"If a person comes who understands nothing at all, how do you receive them? The Master said: "The talk has fallen away. The questioner pressed further: "Where did the talk fall away?"
The Master said, "Seven blows for thirteen. A question was asked: "I have heard it said in antiquity: 'If one realizes it, karmic obstacles are originally empty;
if one has not realized it, one must still repay past debts. I wonder, did the Second Patriarch realize it or not? The Master said, "Certainly. A question was asked:
"What is it that the ancient worthies of old transmitted to one another? The Master said, "Quickly, prostrate three times. A question was asked: "What is the single path of Yunmen?"

The Master said, “Intimate. The student asked, “How is it so? The Master said, “Why such inverted speech and topsy-turvy words? A question was asked: “I have heard it said of old that ‘to conceive a thought is already to err.

How can one avoid erring? The Master said, “A great capacity passes through the palm. The student asked, “If someone were to ask again later, what would you say? The Master said, “A long-standing wind is difficult to change.
A question was asked: “Among the three bodies, which body speaks? The Master said, “Intimate. The student asked, “How is it so? The Master said, “Why such inverted speech and topsy-turvy words?”
[The Master] said, "It is necessary. Question: "What is the body of Śākyamuni? The Master said, "A dried-up shit-stick. Question:
"I ask the Master to provide the essential framework for the School of the Lineage (Zongmen). The Master said, "In the south there is Xuefeng; in the north there is Zhaozhou. Question:

"Does one who has attained ultimate penetration see all phenomena as empty? The Master said, "Suru suru. Question: "All day long I am in a state of urgency, yet I cannot find a point of entry. The Master said, "Suru suru."
[The monk] asked, "I beg the Master to point out the path of entry. The Master said, "When the occasion arises, there is the path.
[The monk] asked, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said, "Mahuang from Puzhou; Fuzi from Yizhou.

[The monk] asked, "What is the intent of the teachings? The Master said, "Pick it up! How would you say it? The monk pressed further, "Please, Master, speak for me. The Master said, "Playing the lute for a cow."
Question: "How does one realize the single path of the profound mechanism? The Master said: "Thirty years from now. Question: "What is the meaning of the coffin revealing the two feet?"
"What does this signify? The Master said, "Words. The student asked, "I do not yet understand what you mean, Master. The Master said, "Tighten your straw sandals. A question was asked:
"When it is neither a profound mystery nor a matter of direct perception, what then? The Master said, "Turn it upside down and speak.
A question was asked: "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth, what then? The Master said, "What more would you see in a dream?"
Ascending the hall, he said, "The Bodhisattva Vasubandhu has, for no reason, transformed himself into a single staff.

He then struck the ground once with his walking stick and said, "All the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are all here expounding their entanglements. Thereupon, he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I am dealing with you on equal terms; when meeting a person, recognize the person.
Even though I speak these words so plainly and compassionately, you still do not understand. Having eaten your fill every day, what are you looking for as you come and go up and down?
What is this pack of wild foxes doing here? With his staff, he drove them all away at once. A monk asked: "At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer..."
When someone suddenly asked, "How should one respond? the Master said, "The assembly, step back. The questioner followed up, "Where does the fault lie?
The Master said, "Return to me the payment for ninety days' worth of meals. A questioner asked, "I have recently arrived at this Dharma seat; I do not yet know what your house style is like.
The Master said, "Without passing through even a single question, how would you speak? A questioner asked, "Regarding the lands of the ten directions..."
"Within the earth, there is only the Single Vehicle Dharma. What is this Single Vehicle Dharma? The Master said, "Why do you not ask something else?

The student replied, "I thank the Master for his instruction. The Master then gave a shout. The student asked, "I have heard it said of old: 'A single mote of dust universally contains all motes of dust.'"
"What is 'one speck of dust'? The Master said, "Beg for a tongue, and bring me another question. A monk asked, "If a student does not ask, will you still answer?
The Master said, "You cannot hang your mouth on the wall. A monk asked, "How is it during all ordinary times?
The Master said, "Although the stench of excrement is熏 (overpowering) me, let me ask you: how many steps do you take while walking during the day?"
"One thousand. Eight hundred travel by night. Where in your alms bowl do you put them? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "You are a fellow who speaks empty falsehoods.
A monk asked, "What is the eye of the teachings? The Master said, "Quickly prostrate three times. A monk asked, "I have heard an ancient saying:"
Niutou spoke both horizontally and vertically, yet he did not know there was a "gate-latch" pointing upward.
[The Master asked: "What is the gate-latch pointing upward? The Master said: "The eastern mountain and the western ridge are green. [The monk] asked: "What is the white ox on the open ground?

The Master said: "Take refuge in the Buddha; take refuge in the Dharma; take refuge in the Sangha. [The monk] further asked: "Where is the white ox? The Master rebuked him. [The monk] asked: "When the tree withers..."
"What is it like when the leaves fall? The Master said, "The body is revealed by the golden wind. Question: "What is the true pearl within the cloth bag?
The Master said, "Can it be described? Question: "What is the offspring of the ancestral lineage? The Master said, "There is resonance within the words."

Ascending the hall, he said: "Now, a bodhisattva who studies Prajñā must recognize the illness of sentient beings; if one recognizes the illness of sentient beings, one then recognizes the illness of the bodhisattva who studies Prajñā.
Is there anyone here who can discern this? Come forward and discern it before the assembly. The assembly remained silent. He then said:
"If you cannot discern it, do not hinder my walking east and west."

Ascending the hall, he said: "Today I am discussing tangled vines with you—excrement and ashes, urine and fire, muddied pigs and scabby dogs who do not recognize good from evil, making their living in a pit of filth.

Therefore it is said: 'The entire universe, the Great Earth, the teachings of the Three Vehicles and Twelve Divisions, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and the instructions of all the teachers in the world—all at once rest upon the lashes of your own eyes.'"
"I will take you along. Even if you were to attain sudden enlightenment right here, you would still be a fellow who fails to seize the opportunity.

To have jumped headlong into a pit of excrement for no reason—you could not even pass through my gate as a monk; your legs would be broken. At that time, three monks came forward and prostrated themselves all at once.
The Master said, "I accept this as a formal confession. A monk asked, "How can one swiftly transcend the triple world?"
"Go! The Master said, "How can you quickly transcend the three realms? He stepped forward and said, "It is. The Master said, "If it is, then rest. He asked again.
"How is it when one is busily occupied all day long? The Master said, "When confronting the situation directly, there is no path of resonance.
[The monk] asked further, "How about that? The Master said, "It cannot be spoken. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when everything is swept clean in a single stroke?

The Master said, "What can you do about this old monk? [The monk] replied, "This belongs to the Master’s own side. The Master said, "You are a man who deceives with empty talk. [The monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "..."
[The Master] uttered a single word. The student asked, "After it has been penetrated, what then? The Master said, "A thousand miles, the same wind.
A monk asked, "The ancients said, 'One knows the ultimate matter. What is this ultimate matter? The Master said, "How can you expect it to be in my hands?
The student pressed, "I am asking about the ultimate matter. The Master then struck him with his staff and said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! This is precisely when one must break through!"
He then invited him to ask for further instruction, saying: "People like this everywhere only know how to throw everything into disorder. Come closer; I will question you.

You who are constantly on the long benches discussing 'upward' and 'downward,' transcending Buddhas and patriarchs—do you say that even a water buffalo has the principle of transcending Buddhas and patriarchs?
The monk replied, "Someone has already asked about this just now."
The Master said, "This is what you have learned on the long benches. Do not say 'it exists' when it exists, nor say 'it does not exist' when it does not.
The monk said, "If it exists, why would you further don fur and wear horns? The Master said, "I know that you are merely a class of people who parrot words.
He added, "Come, come! Let me ask you more: You all carry your staffs slung across your shoulders and yet claim—"
I have practiced Chan and studied the Way, seeking a principle that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs. Let me ask you:
in the twelve hours of the day, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; while defecating or urinating;

even down to the insects in the grassy ditches or at the butcher's stall in the marketplace selling mutton—does any such principle exist there that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? Whoever can speak it, come forth!
"Come. If you do not exist, do not obstruct my walking east or west. He then descended from his seat.

When the Master saw a monk enter, he said, "The tiles have crumbled and the ice has melted. The monk asked, "What fault is there in this student? The Master said, "Seven blows for thirteen. [End of] Question.
"What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "On the long benches there is porridge and rice.

A questioner asked, "I have heard it said of old: 'The Way has no crossroads; those who stand upon it are all in peril. What is the Way? The Master said, "Go and look for yourselves during the communal work.
A questioner asked, "What is the single phrase outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles? The Master said, "Your question, Reverend, makes this old monk leap three thousand feet."
[The monk] bowed. He stepped forward and said, "I thank the Master for his instruction. The Master said, "Stop! Stop! Tell me, how do you understand the old monk’s words? The monk had no reply.

The Master said, "Thirty years from now, I shall give you thirty blows of my staff. A monk asked, "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; what should they discuss? The Master said, "Your father inside your own house.
A monk asked, "One phrase from Caoxi is known throughout the land. The Master said, "It is not so. The monk asked, "Why not? The Master said, "Because it is not yet heard by the whole country."
"I do not yet understand: who is it that can hear Yunmen’s single phrase? The Master said, "You, Dharma brother, do not hear it.
He pressed further, saying, "Can a student approach it? The Master said, "Observe it closely and with careful deliberation."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Tathāgata attained enlightenment at the moment the morning star appeared. A monk asked, "What is it like to attain enlightenment when the morning star appears?
The Master said, "Come closer; come closer. As the monk stepped forward, the Master struck him with his staff and drove him away.
He ascended the hall. A monk came forward and bowed, saying, "I request the Master to answer my question. The Master called out to the assembly.
When the assembly looked up, the Master immediately descended from his seat.
He ascended the hall. After a long silence, a monk came forward and bowed. The Master said, "Too late! The monk responded with an "Amen. The Master said, "This lacquer bucket!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "If there is anyone who can answer a question, bring forth a question. A monk came forward, bowed, and said: "I request the Master to examine me. The Master said:
"Casting the line to catch a giant sea monster, you have caught nothing but a shrimp. The monk said: "Master, do not be mistaken. The Master said:
"Three thousand miles in the morning, eight hundred in the evening—what about that? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the original source? The Master picked up his staff and said, "If you were to pick it up, you would go upward.
The monk asked again, "What is the original source? The Master said, "Jambudvīpa in the south; Uttarakuru in the north.
A monk asked, "Why does Samantabhadra ride an elephant? Why does Mañjuśrī ride a lion? The Master said:
"I have no elephant, nor do I have a lion; I shall simply mount the Buddha Hall and ride out through the triple gate. A questioner asked, "What is the intent of the Teachings?
The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. He further remarked, "Even this is precisely the time to discern that it is but a circuitous explanation of the intent of the Teachings."
"If one refers to the essential framework, it is not yet present. A question was asked: "When all-encompassing wisdom penetrates without obstruction, how is it?
The Master said: "Sweeping the floor and splashing water—the official has arrived. A question was asked: "When one recognizes one's nature while following the flow, how is it?

The Master said: "The moon is bright in the eastern hall; the western hall is dark. A question was asked: "What is the matter of the separate transmission outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles? The Master said: "You..."

[The monk] said, “Master. The Master said, “A qilin looks at the Big Dipper in broad daylight. [The monk] asked, “When a student arrives here, why is it that they cannot speak?
The Master said, “Sitting inside a wild fox’s den. [The monk] asked, “Not falling into the categories of past or present—what is its melodic mode?
The Master pulled his staff and immediately descended from his seat. [The monk] asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, “Facing south, one looks at the Big Dipper.”
Question: “What was the intent of the ancients when they slew the snake? The Master struck him. Question:
“What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: “You received the precepts too early, Venerable. Question: “What is the host within the guest? The Master said: “Riding upon a question.”
The student asked, “What is the master among masters? The Master said, “Join your palms. The student asked, “How far apart are guest and host?
The Master said, “Like eyes, like pupils. The student asked, “What matters should they discuss together? The Master said, “Three times nine is twenty-seven.”

A questioner asked: "Since arriving at the Master’s Dharma assembly, I have not understood. I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "Would you dare to cut off your own head? A questioner asked:
"I beg the Master for instruction to cause this student to suddenly cease his confusion and delusion. The Master said: "What is the price of rice in Xiangzhou?
A questioner asked: "When the two Honored Ones meet, what then? The Master said: "It is no mere coincidence."
Ascending the hall, he said, "Śakra Devendra and the Old Man Śākyamuni are quarreling over the Buddha-dharma in the middle courtyard;
it is quite a commotion. He then descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is the true meaning of Caoxi? The Master said, "This old monk loves anger and does not love joy. The monk pressed further.
"Why is this so? The Master said: "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present one's sword; if one is not a poet, one does not offer a poem. Question:
"When the two Honored Ones meet, what do they discuss together? The Master said: "If it is not resolved, then speak. Question:
"When humans and devas meet, what is their intent? The Master said: "Presenting one's faculty before the assembly."
Ascending the hall, he said: "You sons of the patriarchs, you must first clearly grasp the nostrils of a patch-robed monk.
But what are the nostrils of a patch-robed monk? He then said, "Mahāprajñāpāramitā. "Today there is a great communal labor session," and he immediately descended from his seat.
Question: "What is the meaning of [the Master’s] coming from the West? The Master said: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth.

[The student] further asked: "Is there anything further above this? The Master said: "There is. [The student] further asked: "What is the matter further above this? The Master said: "Old Śākyamuni is in the Western Heaven;
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva dwells in this Eastern Land. Question: "What is it like when both parents have passed away? The Master said: "Both."
"Let us set aside the matter of mourning for a moment. Which one is your father and mother? The monk said, "How painful! The Master said, "Truly so! Truly so! Question: "What is the great donor?
The Master said, "He does not discern when facing the occasion. Question: "When someone comes who is utterly shrouded in obscurity, how do you rescue them?
The Master said, "A double case; take this single document as proof. Question: "Regarding the preaching of the teachings..."
"Who is it? The Master said, "Come closer. The monk came forward and asked in a loud voice. The Master struck him. The monk asked, "How old are you, Preceptor?
The Master said, "Seven times nine is sixty-eight. The monk pressed further, "Why is seven times nine sixty-eight?
The Master said, "I have subtracted five years for you."
Ascending the hall, he said: "O sons of the Buddha! Even if you were to say, 'What matter is there?
it would still be like placing a head upon a head, adding frost to snow, blinking from within a coffin, or applying more moxa to a burn scar.
This is a great deal of mess and confusion. What do you intend to do? Each of you should find a place to take birth; do not [be heedless]."
Wandering through provinces and hunting in counties, they do nothing but clutch at idle talk.

Waiting for the old monk’s mouth to move, they immediately ask about Chan and the Way, about the upward and downward paths, and about "how" and "what. They carry away large volumes of texts and speculate within their leather bags;
wherever they go, three or five of them gather around the brazier, their mouths chattering incessantly. Thus it is.
To say this is speech based on public talent; this is speech that strikes out from the immediate situation;
this is speech spoken regarding phenomena; this is speech that embodies the essence. Your father and mother in the house have already finished their meal.
They do nothing but talk of dreams, saying, "I have realized the Buddha-dharma. You should know that traveling on pilgrimage like this—when will you ever find rest?

Furthermore, there is another sort who, as soon as they hear mention of a place of rest, immediately close their eyes within the realm of the five aggregates (the *āyatana*), making their living in the holes of rats, sitting beneath the Black Mountain, and dwelling within the realms of ghosts.
If you had encountered a true master, you would have found a way in right then and there. Do you still dream of such things?
To kill ten thousand people like this—what sin would there be in that? This is called "giving a blow. Failing to meet a true master, you remain at the end nothing but a hollow charlatan.
If you truly have a point of view, bring it forth and let us deliberate together; do not let your time pass in vain. You do not recognize it.
"Good and evil! You chatter and babble together, huddling your heads to spin webs of sophistry. Do not let the old monk see you; if I were to seize you and examine you, you would not measure up.
I would break your waist and say, 'Do not claim I did not tell you: is there any blood beneath your skin? Why do you go everywhere seeking to suffer such humiliation?
These destroyers of the Hu lineage are all nothing but packs of wild foxes, all gathered here to act as such."
[The Master] drove them all away at once with his staff. A monk asked, "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions share one path to the gate of Nirvāṇa.
What is this one path to the gate of Nirvāṇa? The Master said, "I cannot say it. The monk pressed further, "Why can you not say it, Preceptor?
The Master said, "It is because you are the one who raises the question that you may have it. A monk asked, "What is the teaching of the Dharma? The Master said, "Great."
The assembly stood for a long time. [The student] quickly performed three prostrations and stepped forward, saying: "What is 'speaking according to one's inclination'?

The Master said: "In the morning there is congee; at noon there is rice. "What is 'speaking according to what is appropriate'? The Master said: "The three virtues and six flavors are offered to the Buddha and the Sangha.
"What is 'speaking through expedient means'? The Master said: "Your nostrils weigh three and a half catties. "What is..."
The Great Compassionate One speaks. The Master said: "I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. A questioner asked: "I do not ask about the root source of birth and death;
how is the samādhi of the present moment? The Master said: "Your tongue has traveled three thousand miles. The questioner continued: "Today I have met the Master. The Master said:
"I grant you thirty blows of the staff. Another asked: "I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "Shang Da Ren (The Superior Man)."
"Qiu Yi Ji. The student stepped forward and said, "I, this student, do not understand. The Master said, "He transformed three thousand disciples; seventy became scholars.

A monk asked, "Apart from the three virtues and six flavors, is there still any Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "I only fear that you would not ask. The monk stepped forward and said, "Please, Master, speak.
The Master said, "The three virtues and six flavors are bestowed upon the Buddhas and the Sangha."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The eyelashes span across the ten directions; the eyebrows soar upward through heaven and earth and penetrate downward into the Yellow Springs.
Mount Sumeru blocks your throat. Is there anyone who understands this? If you can understand it, drag the Kingdom of Cāmara and battle for the forehead with the Kingdom of Silla!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "In Jiangxi, they speak of ruler and subject, father and son; in Hunan, they say it is not so.
Here in my place, it is not like this. After a long silence, he asked: "Do you see the wall?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Go! Go! Passing the time with one another in dullness—when will it ever end?
He then asked the assembly: "In my speaking thus, is there any fault? A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said: "First, do not ask. The monk stepped forward and said: "Yes. The Master shouted: "You do not even grasp the words! Another asked: "Today we make offerings to the Arhats. As for the Arhats—"
"Will you return? The Master said, "If you do not ask, I will not speak. He pressed further, saying, "I beg the Master to speak.
The Master said, "Joining palms at the triple gate; burning incense in the Buddha hall. [The student] asked, "What is the fundamental matter of a patch-robed monk?"
The Master said, "In the south there is Xuefeng; in the north there is Zhaozhou. The student asked, "I request the Master not to use flowery words.

The Master said, "You must not lose the point of your question. The student replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him. A student asked, "I have heard it said of old: 'If you understand, things are of one family;
if you do not understand, they are as teeth set against teeth. How can one attain this state where things are of one family? The Master said, "Running about in confusion."
"What is it? He ascended the hall and said, "From the very beginning, what exactly has this been? Now, having no choice but to speak, I shall tell you all:
throughout the entire earth, what object exists that can serve as an opponent or a condition for you? Even if there were a needle..."
Feng, you have an obstruction and a barrier between you and me. Pick it up and bring it here! What do you call "Buddha" and "Patriarch"?
What do you call "mountains, rivers, and the great earth," or "the sun, moon, and stars"? What do you take to be the four elements and the five aggregates?
If I speak in this manner, you will call it the talk of an old woman from a village of three households. But should you suddenly encounter one who is of true substance...
When a man of foot-hearing (a true practitioner) hears such words, he seizes him by the feet and drags him down the steps. What fault is there in this?
Nevertheless, on what principle does he act in this way? Do not speak recklessly here merely to satisfy your own tongue;
one must be a man of substance before this can be achieved. Suddenly, if the old man finds the place where you cannot go beneath his own feet, he will strike your legs.
"What fault is there in breaking it? Since it is so, do you now have any question regarding a koan of the *zongcheng* (the essence of the school)?

Wait until this old man has finished answering one turn, then go east or west as you please. A monk was about to ask a question when the Master struck him in the mouth with his staff and immediately descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is it like when a lion yawns? The Master said, "Setting aside the yawning for a moment, try..."
"Listen intently! The monk responded, "Yes. The Master said, "This is the cry of a rat.
He ascended the hall and said, "I have a phrase; I do not dare hope that you will understand it. Is there anyone who can bring it forth?
After a long silence, he said, "I thought the beard was red, but here is another with a red beard. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Having no choice, I shall provisionally act as a physician treating a dead horse.
What am I saying to you? Is it east or west? Is it south or north? Is it existence or non-existence? Is it seeing or hearing? Is it moving upward or moving downward?"
"It is thus; it is not thus. This is called the talk of an old woman in a village of three households.
How many of you have reached such a state? If it corresponds, it corresponds; if it does not correspond, then *svāhā* in a quiet place.
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The old masters of various quarters say, 'One must know that there is a matter beyond sound and form.
Such talk as this deceives the men and women of the world. Sitting alone in the three-bay Dharma Hall, you are merely indulging in deluded thoughts;
you have not even dreamed of my Master’s fundamental tenets. How can you justify the offerings of the faithful? On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month..."

"Every single one of you must repay him before it will do. Even if you were to leap about like mad, it would not avail you. Each of you must exert yourselves! Take care! [The Master] said: "The official seal of the *ācārya* is clear; why seek a further judgment? [The monk] asked: "Was Vimalakīrti’s single silence the same as speaking?
The Master said: "Receive this one question with full attention. [The monk] pressed: "In that case, it was the same as speaking.
The Master said: "What did you just say? [The monk] asked: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: "A flower-planting fence. [The monk] pressed: "Right then—"
"How is it when you understand in this way? The Master said, "A golden-maned lion.
Upon ascending the hall, he heard the bell toll and said, "The world is so vast; why does the sound of the bell wear the seven-strip robe?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "One must not add frost to snow. "Take care," he said, and then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he said:
"Those old bald slaves everywhere sit upon their crooked wooden meditation seats, seeking fame and profit. When asked about the Buddha, they answer regarding the Buddha;

when asked about the Patriarchs, they answer regarding the Patriarchs. Even when voiding excrement or passing urine, it is like an old woman in a village of three households spreading rumors by word of mouth."
He made them all appear similar. What good or evil did he recognize? They were all just like this; even water would be difficult for them to digest.
Entering the hall, he said: "Everyone has their own radiance within; when looking for it, it is not seen, shrouded in dark gloom. He then descended from his seat.
The Master entered the capital and was at the Shouchun Hall. The Sovereign asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "The Emperor has issued an edict;
this monk responds. While the Master was attending a vegetarian feast at Wende Hall, Attendant Ju asked, "Is the fruit on the Ling tree ripe yet?
The Master said, "In what year did you come to believe that the Way is born?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "All of you, why have you come here for no reason? This old monk only knows how to eat and defecate;
what else do I know how to do? You all travel on foot through various regions, practicing Chan and inquiring about the Way. Let me ask you:"
"What is it that you have realized through your travels to all quarters? Try to bring it forth.

He said again, "In the meantime, can you find even a fragment of the old man’s essence within your own house? You have merely found some spittle from behind the old man’s buttocks and chewed it up, taking it to be yourself.
Then you say, 'I understand Zen, I understand the Way. Even if you could recite the entire Tripitaka, what would you do with it?"
The ancients, having no choice in the matter, saw that you were wandering about in confusion;

thus they spoke to you of *bodhi* and *nirvāṇa*, which was merely to bury you or to drive a stake through you to bind you. Seeing again that you did not understand, they told you that there is neither *bodhi* nor *nirvāṇa*.
To know such matters already leaves one with no recourse; yet you still seek further commentaries upon them. This sort of thing—
He utterly exterminates the Hu race. From the beginning until now, it has all been like this. Where has it gone to this day?

When I was traveling as a pilgrim in the past, there were certain people who provided me with commentaries; they did not have ill intentions, yet one day I saw through them—they are nothing but a source of laughter.
It is because I have not died for three or five years that such a person exists to exterminate the Hu race.
"A single axe-blow breaks the leg. Nowadays, there are many who throughout the various quarters claim to have transcended the world through their twisting and manipulating of words.
Why do you not go among them? What are you seeking here with this dry piece of dung? The Master then stepped down from his seat and, using his staff, drove them all away at once.
A monk asked, "What is the single resolution of the myriad dharmas? The Master said, "Do not let the question be lost. A monk asked, "Death..."
[The monk asked: "How is it when one attains life within the midst [of phenomena]? The Master said: "Three thousand miles by day; eight hundred miles by night. [The monk] asked:
"When the great assembly gathers like clouds, what should they discuss? The Master said: "Today, let go and let the command be carried out.

The monk bowed, and the Master struck him. [The monk] asked: "What is the student’s own self? The Master said: "I fear you do not know me. [The monk] asked: "What is penetration? The Master said: "I fear you do not know me."

[The Master] spoke the phrase on the *dharmakāya*. The Master said, "The seas are calm and the rivers are clear. The Daoist asked, "Sight and hearing are without sound and without form; the Old Lord has already explained this.
As for Yunmen’s single phrase, I request the Master to provide instruction. The Master said, "The road to the Western Heaven is far and remote. The Daoist was speechless.
As the Master was about to descend from his seat, the Daoist said, "I request the Master once more to proclaim the essential tenets. The Master said, "Only those who can speak it may come forth."
"Come forward! No one in the assembly responded. The Master said, "If that is so, then you have failed the host. He then descended from his seat.
Later, when the assembly had gathered for the formal discourse, the Master took up his staff and said, "Having no choice, let us understand it right here.
Look! The three gates are upon this pillar. He then descended from his seat.
The Song of the Twelve Hours: Midnight, the hour of *zi*:
The foolish man speaks of what is similar. The Hour of the Ox, *chou*, at cockcrow: The deluded person holds up a tortoise head.
The Hour of the Tiger, *yin*, at dawn: Who is this person at daybreak? The Hour of the Hare, *mao*, as the sun rises: Han Qing bites upon a withered bone.
At the hour of *shishi* (10–11 am), the vividly manifest faculty is mistaken for the True. At *yuzhong* (11 am–noon) and *si* (noon–1 pm), one goes and comes between north and south.
At *rinan* (1–2 pm), one recognizes the direction and suffers on the road. At *riti* (2–3 pm) and *wei* (3–4 pm), in summer one encounters talk of cold air.
At the hour of Bu (Shen): Zhang San and Li Si meet and speak of the Truth. At the hour of Ri-ru (You): How can one constantly maintain the mechanism?
At the hour of Huang-hun (Xu): Seeing the light of time—who would suffer humiliation? At the hour of Ren-ding (Hai): Only then can one clearly see those sinking into the sea of suffering.
Verse:
Yunmen towers high, the white clouds hang low; the current is swift, and the swimming fish dare not rest. Entering the gate, one already knows the understanding brought forth;
why labor further to mention the mud trampled beneath the wheels?
The path of learning is like a physician treating medicine and disease; it is like a child’s play, leaning on a fence and groping along a wall.
Who can fathom the silence of the deep valley? As for understanding the lineage of the masters, who does not know?
The Kāṅ clan’s circular stagnation remains unclarified; the demon’s depths are profoundly empty, struck by the cold ice. When the phoenix’s feathers unfurl, it soars beyond the azure heavens;
as for the eight-pointed spearhead of Jin, on what could it possibly rely?

This faculty is a response; responding to the faculty, one is deluded. Opening up the faculty, the faculty recedes far away, and the faculty takes refuge in the distance. From dusk until midday, who has anything to hang upon?
Because of this very matter, one is separated from the delusions of sentiment.
The sun overflows the eyes; it is most profound and subtle. Who can say that "I" and "you" are not one? Within the phrase, all who pass by resonate;
face-to-face, it is difficult to encounter this foremost pivot.

In my youth, I dwelt among mountain folk where people were few; beneath the pines we met and spoke of the wonders of the Way. A single phrase before the sharp edge of the sword transcends all taming masters;
had I attempted to ask "how," it would have been a violation spanning kalpas.

Gazing at the ancient pines, the lofty clouds are not uniform; for how many years have the wild geese and cranes nested within them? Though they hatch from their eggs at the same time, there is great difference between them:
when their wings spread and they soar toward the Han sky, the azure heavens seem lowered.
The myriad phenomena, vast and manifold, reach to the most subtle; though they are the very person before one, people instead say they are not. Meeting and encountering one another, they laugh aloud;
looking back and pausing the mechanism of thought—who else could it be?

Exhausting the course of conversation, one speaks much; what use is this for discerning the pivot? It is the noble person who values such speech as wondrous, yet the superior practitioner sees that it only obscures true knowledge.
Since when has the Great Way ever been sought? Without cause, one enters the weeds; rolling up and rolling out again, one does not realize they have grown old in vain.
Above, one sees no heaven; below, one sees no earth. With the throat choked shut, where can one breathe? Many laugh at me;
few appreciate me.
The time for practice is lost; the forest of vines lies in ruin. Intent on human concepts, the body remains stagnant and frail.
To act without regard is already a deviation; to attempt deliberation—when will one awaken? Through how many kalpas?
"Tu tu tu! Li wei xi! The Zen student is startled; the eyebrows between his brows droop.
[This is] the "Chougu Song" (Song of Withdrawing the Gaze), following the "Jian Yi" (Mirror-like Laughter).
From the *Extensive Record of Chan Master Kuangzhen of Yunmen*, Volume Sixteen.
The Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Fifteen;
The Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Sixteen;
The Extensive Record of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen.
Compiled by the Disciple Mingshi Dashi, Shoujian, who was conferred the purple robe.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying:

"Throughout the entire world of the ten directions, across the vast expanse of heaven and earth—if one were to strike it with a single stroke of this staff, all its manifold complexities [would vanish]."
It shatters the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings. Since Bodhidharma came from the West, it would be unacceptable to let this pass;
yet if one does not let it pass, it cannot be extinguished by even a single shout.

The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "The twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven, the six patriarchs of the Tang land, and all the old monks of the world—they are all upon the tip of my staff.
Even if you were to understand this with such clarity that it is unmistakable, you would still be only halfway there.
If you do not let go of this, you are all nothing but wild fox spirits. One day the Master said: "In the past, the elder masters did so for the sake of compassion."
There is talk that "falls into the weeds," by which one recognizes a person according to their words. If it is talk that "emerges from the weeds," it is not like this.
If it were like this, there would be redundant or repetitive speech. Have you not seen how Master Yangshan asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from?"?
The monk said, “Mount Lu. Yangshan asked, “Have you ever traveled to Wulao Peak? The monk said, “I have not. Yangshan said, “Dharma brother, you have never traveled the mountains.
The Master said, “These words were all spoken out of compassion; they are talk that descends into the weeds.
The Master sometimes said, “If one says ‘this very mind is Buddha,’ it is merely a provisional means of mistaking a servant for a master. [This concerns] birth and death.”

Nirvana is like cutting off one's head and seeking to remain alive. To speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs, or the intent of the Buddhas and the intent of the Patriarchs, is very much like exchanging your own eyes for wooden prayer beads (*mohani*).
The Master raised an ancient saying: "Awakening to the Way through hearing sound;
clarifying the mind through seeing form. The Master asked: "What is 'awakening to the Way through hearing sound; clarifying the mind through seeing form'? He then said: "Avalokiteśvara."
A bodhisattva came with money to buy a sesame cake (*hūbǐng*). As he reached out his hand, the Master said, "So, it’s just a steamed bun (*mántóu*).
The Master sometimes said, "The lantern is you yourself; you take the bowl and eat the rice. But the rice is not you yourself.
A monk then asked, "What is it like when the rice is oneself? The Master said, "You wild fox spirit! You belong in a village of three households."
Han said, "Come, come. It is not that you say the meal is for yourself. The monk said, "It is.
The Master said, "When will you dream of seeing a fellow from a village of three houses? At another time, the Master said, "True emptiness does not destroy existence;
true emptiness is not different from form. A monk then asked, "What is true emptiness? The Master said, "Do you hear the sound of the bell? The monk said, "This..."
"This is the sound of the bell. The Master said, "When will you ever dream of it? Case: Master Shushan asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk said, "From Lingzhong. Shushan said, "Have you been to Xuefeng? The monk said, "I have been there.
Shushan said, "When I went there previously, things were not yet sufficient. How are they now? The monk said, "Now they are sufficient. Shushan—
[The assembly] said, "The congee is sufficient; the rice is sufficient. The monks remained silent. The Master said, "The congee is sufficient;

the rice is sufficient. Case: Upādhyāya Fu visited Xuefeng. Upon hearing of his arrival, Xuefeng assembled the community. When Fu reached the Dharma Hall and looked around, Xuefeng immediately went down to inspect the administrative affairs.
The next day, Fu went up to pay his respects and said, "Yesterday I offended you, Reverend. Xuefeng said, "I know it was something like that."
The matter was thus concluded. At that time, a monk asked the Master, "What was it that offended the Master? The Master struck him. [The Master] cited a case:
A monk asked Zifu, "When the ancients raised their mallets or held up their fly-whisks, what was their meaning? Zifu said, "The ancients were like this.
The monk said, "But as for raising the mallet and holding up the whisk—what then? Zifu gave a shout and sent him out. The Master said, "The ancients..."
"What kind of eye is this? The monk said, "How about you, Master? The Master said, "Will you understand it in a donkey’s year?
The monk had no reply. The Master called to the monk again, "Come! Come! The monk stepped forward; the Master struck him across the mouth with his whisk. He cited a verse by Sanping:
"This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing. The Master said, "What do you call 'seeing and hearing'? There was no further sound.

"Form can be presented to you," [the Master] said. The Master replied, "What form or sound is there? "If one is realized within this, there is nothing at all," [the Master] said. The Master replied, "What thing is there?
"The essence and its function may be distinguished or not distinguished without hindrance," [the Master] said. The Master replied, "Speech is the essence; the essence is speech.
He then picked up his staff and said, "The staff is the essence; the lantern is the function. Are they distinguished or not? They are not.
The Path of Seeing. "The purity of the knowledge of all modes. Case: Yunmen said, "The illusory, empty body is itself the Dharma-body.
The Master picked up his staff and said, "The entire earth is not the Dharma-body. Case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "I have newly entered this monastery;
I beg the Master for instruction. Zhaozhou said, "Have you finished eating your gruel yet? The monk said, "I have finished eating my gruel."
Yunmen said, "Go wash your bowl. The Master said, "Tell me, was there an instruction or not? If you say there was an instruction, what did he say to him?
If you say there was no instruction, how could that monk have attained enlightenment?
He cited: A monk asked Xuefeng, "I beg the Master for an instruction. Feng said, "What is it? At these words, the monk attained great enlightenment. The Master [said]:...
Xuefeng said to him, "What did you say? The Master sometimes said, "There are countless dead people on level ground;
one who can pass through the thorn-brake forest is a skilled hand. A monk said, "In that case, the first seat in the hall has something superior.
The Master said, "Sorū sorū. [He] raised the topic of "insentient things preaching the Dharma. Suddenly hearing the sound of a bell, he said, "Old Śākyamuni!"

While preaching the Dharma, the Master suddenly picked up his staff and asked a monk, "What is this? The monk said, "A staff. The Master said, "You will dream of it for as long as a donkey's lifespan.
One day the Master said, "In a village of three households, one practices divination; one divines to the east, one divines to the west.
Even if one suddenly hits upon the truth, it is not certain. A monk then asked, "What is it like when one suddenly hits upon the truth? The Master said:
I humbly submit that the Master once said: "When the Great Function manifests, it does not abide by fixed rules.
