A monk asked Zifu, "What was the meaning of the ancients' raising of the mallet and brandishing of the whisk? Fuzi said, "Ha! The Master said, "Adding frost to snow. Case:
A monk asked Zifu, "How is it that 'a single speck of dust enters right concentration'? Fuzi made the gesture of entering meditative absorption. The Master said, "Adding frost to snow."
The monk asked, "How is it that the samādhi of all sense-objects arises? Fokuang said, "Whom are you asking?
The Master said, "This fellow does not even realize his words have fallen into error. He further remarked, "What he said previously was already a tangle; now he says, 'Whom are you asking?'"
Jiuyu ascended the hall and said, "All of you, do not drive stakes into empty space.
At that time, the Venerable Lingxu came forth from the assembly and said, "Empty space itself is the stake. Jiuyu struck him. Lingxu said, "Master, do not strike me in error.
Jiuyu then returned to his quarters. The Master said, "Adding a point to an arrow. A monk asked, "Just now, Master, you gave [him a blow]..."
"What do you say to that? The Master said, "Beating the bell to thank the echo; a frog comes crawling out. He cited a case:
A monk asked Touzi, "What is the meaning of Milyan? Touzi said, "It must be such a person who can attain it.
Zhaozhou said, "Why not give him his rightful fodder? The Master asked a monk, "What is this rightful fodder? The monk hesitated.
The Master then struck him. [Case] An ancient said: "Silent and still, empty of form and shadow. The Master spread his two hands and said:
"Where could mountains, rivers, and the great earth be found? He also said: "All-encompassing wisdom penetrates without obstruction. The Master said:
"My staff has traveled to the Western Heaven and returned to the land of Silla. He then tapped the meditation seat and said: "This is your nostril. [Case] A monk asked:
Jiashan was asked, "What is the Way? Jiashan said, "The great sun floods the eyes; ten thousand miles, not a single speck of cloud.
The Master said, "If one does not call it a single phrase, and does not call it the Dharma-body, what is it? A monk asked, "What is the student’s own self?
The Master said, "I, the old monk, enter the mud and enter the water. The monk said, "I would go to my death, grinding my bones to dust."
The Master shouted, saying, "The waters of the great ocean are upon your head! Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk was speechless.

The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "I know that the Master fears I am not being truthful. At other times the Master said, "Even if one reaches the point where heaven and earth have not a single hair’s breadth of fault, this is still a turning phrase (*zhuǎnjù*).
Only when not seeing a single color is it half-raised. Even when one has reached such a state..."
Furthermore, one must know that there is a time for the total presentation [of the Way]. At times the Master said: "Bubbles and illusions are equally unimpeded;
yet at every place it is not an illusion, and at every place it is not unimpeded. At other times the Master said:

"Whether speaking horizontally or vertically—bodhi, nirvāṇa, true thusness, or buddha-nature—all are merely matters of secondary deliberation. Only when the time comes to brandish the mallet or raise the whisk [does the true teaching manifest]."
This is also a horizontal and vertical teaching; compared to what preceded it, it is still somewhat inferior. A monk asked, "Please speak of the Way above.
The Master said, "The assembly has been standing for a long time; quickly pay three prostrations. He cited: Chongshou asked a monk, "Do you see the lantern?"
The monk was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying: "Knock over the lantern. Case: Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk said, "I am going to pick tea.
The Master said, "Shut your mouth! Case: "The Dharma-body preaches the Dharma; every verdant bamboo is the Dharma-body.
This is not yet the occasion for grasping the essential point or picking it up. Case: "The conditioned has no three periods of time; the unconditioned has three periods of time."

Conditioned phenomena are subject to cessation; how could they possess the three periods of time? Unconditioned phenomena possess the three periods of time, yet this is not the dharma of abiding in quiescence.
Case: To speak of "true study" is but a web of entangling words. When the staff is raised or the whisk held aloft, one is still only halfway toward true study.
Case: There are three kinds of people. One attains awakening through an explanation; another attains awakening through being called by name. The third...
When the three men saw him being raised up, they immediately turned back and left. You say they "immediately turned back and left"—what was their intention?
He further said, "They too deserve thirty blows. Case: Eating with the Dharma-body is already gouging flesh to create a sore;
yet it is thought that there ought to be such talk as this. Case: A monk asked Yunju, "What is it like when all is perfectly still? Yunju said, "It does not flow. The Master said, "Not..."
[The Master] said, "What flowery talk about 'serene stillness'! It is also said: 'These are words that cut through iron. He raised [the topic]: "Medicine and disease treat one another.
The entire earth is medicine; which of these is your own self? The Master said, "When encountered as base, it is immediately noble. The monk said, "I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master clapped his hands once, picked up his staff, and said, "Take this staff! The monk took it.
[The Master] broke it into two pieces. The Master said, "Even if you were such [a person], you would still deserve thirty blows. He cited:
At the end of summer, Cuiyan ascended the hall and said, "For the entire summer, I have been conversing with the assembly of monks. Look, are Cuiyan’s eyebrows still there?
Baofu said, "The thief’s heart is fearful. Changqing said, "They are growing. The Master said, "The barrier. At other times, the Master said:
He said, "I dare not hope for you to have waves that go against the current; moreover, it is difficult to find one who does not follow the flow of the water.
He then related: When Liang sui first visited Magu, as soon as Magu saw him coming, he went off to weed the field. Liang sui went to where Magu was weeding.
Tanggu paid him no mind at all; he returned to his quarters, closed the door, and remained there. For three consecutive days, Liangsui went to knock on the door.
On the third day, as soon as he knocked, Magu asked, "Who is it? Liangsui replied, "Preceptor, do not deceive Liangsui."
"If you do not come to pay respects to the Preceptor, you will surely spend your entire life being deceived by the sutras and treatises.

The Master said, "There is even a wave that goes against the current; now that you have entered, this is the intention of going with the current. It is also called the 'moment of simultaneous release.
He further said, "When Magu asked, 'Who is it? Liang-sui replied, 'Do not deceive me. Liang-sui did not merely recognize Magu's appearance."
He saw the opportune moment. If he had not come to pay his respects to the Master, he would have been deceived by the sutras and śāstras for the rest of his life;

thus he knew there were places where one could be led astray. Thereafter, when Liangsui returned to the capital, the Emperor and the Great Masters and Virtuous Ones of the Left and Right Quarters repeatedly urged him to stay.
During a tea ceremony, Liangsui said: "Where all others know, Liangsui knows it all. Liangsui...
[The Master] said, "Thus he knew where [the truth] resides; the others did not know. The Master asked, "What is it that Liang-sui knows?
He cited the Heart Sutra: "No eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind. The Master said, "Because you possess eyes that see, it is not improper to say 'no.
However, at the moment of seeing, one cannot say 'no. Even so, what is the use of seeing all these things?"
[The Master said: "What fault is there? Nothing at all can be apprehended. What sounds, smells, tastes, touches, or dharmas are there? He cited the verse:

"Lifting up the light, its silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges," and asked a monk, "Is this not the words of the scholar Zhang Zhuo? The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Your talk has fallen into error.
He cited another instance: A monk was taking his leave of Shishuang. Shishuang asked, "Will you go by boat or by land? The monk said, "When I meet a boat, I take the boat; when I meet land..."
Ji-lu said, "In my way, it is somewhat difficult halfway through. The monk was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "Thirty years from now, this story will spread far and wide.
He also said, "The single phrase at the moment of departure will not be forgotten for eternal kalpas. He cited Master Sheng, who said:
"Striking the void produces sound; striking wood makes no noise. The Master struck the air with his staff, saying, "A-ya-ya! Then he struck again.
The head monk struck the wooden board and asked, “Is that making a sound? The monk replied, “It is making a sound. The Master said, “This worldly fellow!
Then he struck the board again and asked, “What do you call ‘making a sound’? He cited this: A monk asked Shishuang, “Is there the meaning of the Patriarchs within the scriptures? Shishuang said:
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarchs within the teachings? Shishuang said, "Do not seek it within the scrolls.
The Master spoke on his behalf: "Do not fail this old monk; why instead sit in a pit of excrement? He cited:
Shishuang said, "One must know there is a phrase transmitted outside the teachings. A monk asked, "What is this phrase transmitted outside the teachings?"
[The Master] said: "It is not a phrase. The Master said: "That which is not a phrase is precisely the phrase. [The Master] cited:
Dongshan said, "You must know that there is a matter above the Buddha. A monk asked, "What is the matter above the Buddha? Dongshan said, "Not a Buddha.

The Master said: "It cannot be named; it cannot be described. That is why he said 'not'. [The Master] cited: Dongshan said, "A man-child who is unstained amidst the dust. The Master said: [He is one who...]
[The Master] said: "Call a staff a staff; call everything 'everything. [A monk] raised this point:
'The Dharma-body is pure, yet all sounds and forms are merely trivial chatter. Without falling into triviality, what is purity?'"
Again, he asked: "What is the Dharma-body? The Master said: "Not contained within the six. He also said: "The thirty-three heavens;
the twenty-eight lunar mansions. Citing an ancient, it was said: "As my body is empty, so all phenomena are empty; the thousand grades and myriad species are all identical."
The Master said: "The body cannot be grasped; how could all dharmas possibly exist? Therefore, the ancients said that insentient things possess Buddha-nature.
They also said that insentient things are not called the Dharma-body preaching the Dharma. At other times the Master said: "When light does not penetrate through, there are two kinds of illnesses.
First, there is the lack of clarity in all places, as if there were an object directly before one's face. Furthermore, even if it penetrates..."
When one attains the emptiness of all dharmas, there is still a faint sense that something exists; this too is because light has not yet fully penetrated through.

Furthermore, the Dharma-body also has two kinds of illnesses: first, upon reaching the Dharma-body, one does not forget the attachment to dharmas (*dharmagrāha*), and one's own views (*svadṛṣṭi*) still persist, such that one remains seated within the precincts of the Dharma-body.
Second, even if you manage to penetrate through the Dharma-body, you must not let it pass by without further scrutiny.
"Examine it closely; what scent is there? That too is an illness. Case: A monk asked the National Teacher, "What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana?
The National Teacher said, "Bring me the pure water pitcher. When the monk took the pitcher and returned, the National Teacher said, "Put it back in its original place.
The monk returned it to its original place and came again to ask, "What is..."
"Vairocana himself. The National Teacher said, "The ancient Buddha passed away long ago. The Master said, "There is no trace. He raised a case:
A monk asked Guankui, "I have long heard of Guankui; having arrived, I see nothing but a hemp-soaking pond.
Guankui said, "You see only the hemp-soaking pond, yet you do not recognize Guankui. The monk asked, "What is Guankui? Guankui said, "A splitting arrow."
"Urgent! The Master said, "Why did you not respond with the primary pivot? Case: When Inspector Wei saw a painting of an ox butting a tree in a screen, he asked a monk, "The ox butts the tree;
the tree butts the ox. The monk had no reply. The Master provided this on his behalf: "I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha."
Case: An old master asked a monk, "Have you heard it said that Xuefeng has the 'ball' koan? Is that so? The monk said, "I have not seen it mentioned. The master said, "I have heard there is one.
The monk said, "It is merely that other monks are speaking in confusion. The master said, "What is the matter that is not spoken in confusion?
[The monk] was speechless. The Master (Linji) spoke on his behalf: "I am a newcomer; I have not yet entered the hall for formal study. Case: The Buddha asked.
“Non-Buddhist, what is the tenet of your doctrine? The Master spoke on behalf of the non-Buddhist, saying:
“Old Monk, I know you! The non-Buddhist said: “My tenet is that nothing whatsoever is accepted. [The Master] spoke on behalf of the Buddha, saying: “Let this one point pass. The Buddha said:
“Is it your tenet that nothing whatsoever is accepted? [The Master] spoke on behalf of the non-Buddhist, saying: “Gautama, do not let him lose his footing.”
He then asked: "To cite Xuefeng, he said: 'The entire earth is you; what do you take to be something else? The Master said:

'Have you not seen it stated in the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: "Sentient beings are inverted; they are deluded about themselves and pursue external objects"? If one can turn these objects, one is identical to the Tathāgata.'"

Case: The Teaching says, "The mark of the cessation of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words. The Master said, "If you see it as being fixed as it is when speaking now, where would there be 'speaking' or 'not speaking'?
Have you not heard it said: 'Going does not arrive at going; coming does not arrive at coming'? Case: "All suchness contains all.
The Master said, "What do you call mountains, rivers, and the great earth? He also said, "These are all..."
The emptiness of phenomena (*dharmasūnyatā-lakṣaṇa*): neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure. The Master sometimes took up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"This staff has transformed into a dragon and swallowed up heaven and earth; where then do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come from? The Master sometimes drew a circle and said:
"Is there anyone who can get out of this? He cited the Teaching, saying: "These phenomena abide in their own positions. The world...
"The intermediate characteristics are eternally present. The Master said, "Where has Old Śākyamuni gone? He cited a case: A monk asked Touzi, "What is this sutra?
Touzi said, "The *Vimalakīrti* and the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*. The monk asked again, "What is it like when a man-child is unstained amidst the dust?
Touzi said, "Unattached. The Master said, "It is not called the Dharma-body; it is not called the Ultimate Truth (Paramārtha). Nor is it...

He preached the Dharma for them and also spoke of ultimate emptiness (*śūnyatā*). During a meal, the Master picked up his spoon and chopsticks and said, "I do not make offerings to the monks from the South;
I only make offerings to the monks from the North. At that time, a monk asked, "Why do you not make offerings to the monks from the South?"
The Master said, "I want to leave him standing there. The monk asked, "Why do you provide offerings only for the northern monks? The Master said, "One arrow, two targets.
A monk took up the point and asked, "As for that previous meaning, what is it? The Master said, "If it is good, then we share in the glory together."
At one time, the Master struck a pillar once with his staff and asked, "Can the teachings of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the scriptures explain this?
He himself replied, "They cannot. Then he said, "Shoo! You wild fox spirit! A monk asked, "What is your own intention, Master?
The Master said, "When Zhang Gong drinks wine, Li Gong gets drunk. He further cited an ancient saying: "There are words that startle people."

A monk asked, "What is the phrase that startles people? The Master said, "Resonance. [The Master] cited National Teacher Huizhong, who said: "To speak of gradualness is to return to the ordinary and accord with the Way;
to speak of suddenness is to leave no trace behind. The Master said, "Raising the mallet, holding up the whisk, and the moment of snapping the fingers."

If you examine it closely, even this is not without traces. At times the Master would take up his staff and say, "Heaven and earth, the great world—all killing and all bringing to life are contained right here.
A monk then asked, "What is killing? The Master said, "Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down."
The monk asked, "What is 'living'? The Master said, "One must serve as the head cook. The monk asked, "How is it when one neither kills nor lives?
The Master then rose and said, "Mahāprajñāpāramitā. At other times the Master said, "When meeting people, one makes use of the path.
He then picked up his staff and said, "This staff is not the path; these words are not the path. He raised [the point]:
"The Dharma-body eats rice. "The illusory, empty body is itself the Dharma-body. The Master said: "Where in the great earth and the heavens could there be anything?
Not a single thing can be apprehended; one eats emptiness with emptiness. If one were to examine this closely, one might think that such talk ought to exist. He cited:
"The manifested transformation body is not the true Buddha, nor is it the speaker of the Dharma. The Master said: "The manifested transformation body..."

[The Master] said: "This is the teaching of the Dharmakāya; it is also called 'manifesting the essence as entirely true. It is like the Dharmakāya eating the Dharmakāya. He also said: "The rice is not the Dharmakāya;
the staff is not the Dharmakāya. At other times, the Master said: "In the Gate of the Patriarchs, there is freedom in the seven directions and the eight quarters;
killing and giving life are applied according to the occasion. A monk then asked: "What is killing? The Master said: "Winter passes and spring comes. The monk [continued].
A monk asked, "When winter departs and spring arrives, what then? The Master said, "Shouldering the staff crosswise, go east, west, south, or north as you please to gather firewood.
Addressing the assembly, he said, "Even if you speak horizontally or vertically at will, you have not yet become a scion of the School. If one were to rely on the true scions of the School..."
Yi: "This is the 'clanging of the scorching bowl. The teachings of the Three Vehicles and the Twelve Divisions of the Canon are a dream; Bodhidharma’s coming from the West is a dream.
If there were an elder abbot opening the hall to preach the Dharma for others, what fault would there be in killing hundreds of thousands of millions of them with a sharp sword?
He further said, "I thought there must be some principle underlying such talk. One day, the Master said:
Brandishing the mallet, holding up the whisk, snapping the fingers, or raising the eyebrows—each question and answer does not, in itself, constitute the Ultimate Vehicle (shangxiang zongcheng).
A monk then asked, "What is the Ultimate Vehicle? The Master said, "From the underworld to Jambudvīpa, everyone can say it."
Suppose one were sitting in the midst of a bustling marketplace at dawn. On the butcher’s stall there is pork; in the cesspool there are worms.
Do they too have talk that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? A monk said, "Some do not accept it. The Master said, "Some do not accept it.
It cannot be that it exists when you are deliberating and does not exist when you are not deliberating. If you examine the substance of that speech itself—"
Regarding the matter at hand: their words were direct, yet they had not yet arrived; their understanding was one-sided and withered. At times the Master said:
"I have always said that all sounds are the Buddha’s voice, all forms are the Buddha’s form, and the entire earth is the Dharmakāya.
Yet you have mistakenly formed a view within the Buddha-dharma. Now, when you see a staff, simply call it a staff; when you see a house, simply call it a house. The Master.
Sometimes he said: "To act yet there is no acting; to employ yet there is no employing. He then picked up his staff and said:
"This is not 'employing yet there is no employing. What do you call this? He cited Danxia, who said:
"The hundred limbs all crumble away, yet one thing remains eternally numinous. The Master said: "The staff must indeed be numinous. What do you call the hundred limbs? Where [is it]?"
[The monk] says: “I have attained it. [The Master] quotes: “All worthies and sages are distinguished by means of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*).
The Master says: “The staff is not the unconditioned dharma; nothing at all is the unconditioned dharma. [The Master] quotes: “Master Zhi said:
‘At the hour of the Ox (1–3 a.m.), a single round light has long been shining. The Master says: “I do not ask you about that behind your head; bring forth the Way from three thousand miles away!”
"Bring forth a single phrase! It is said: Muzhou calling out to a monk, Zhaozhou offering tea—these are the meanings of "entering the water.

Xuefeng rolling the ball, Guizong dragging the rock, the characters on the sutra cover, the National Teacher’s water bowl, the Arhats writing characters, the place where all Buddhas emerge, and "walking on water atop the Eastern Mountain"—all these belong to the time of the Ultimate Teaching.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "When one reaches the point where everything encountered is free of obstruction, and realizes that names, phrases, and all phenomena are empty, then the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are but names—and even these names cannot be apprehended.
This is called the 'Samādhi in which the Ocean of Nature is Fully Equipped,' yet it is still like ripples surging without a wind.
Only when one forgets cognition within awakening does awakening become Buddha-nature. This is called the 'Windless State.'"
"One who serves a person must further know that there is a 'hole' pointing toward the transcendent above.
The Master sometimes said, "There is nowhere that is not the preaching of the Dharma. When the bell is struck and the drum is beaten, it cannot but be so.
If it is thus, then in all places it is neither existent nor non-existent. He also said, "It is not the case that it exists only when being preached; it does not exist when not being preached."
Then it would simply not exist. If one speaks from the perspective of proclaiming the teaching, this is not yet it; however, within the context of guiding others, it is acceptable.
The Master raised his fan and said: "Life and death and nirvana are fused into a single mass. Then he held up the fan and asked: "What is this? Is it not fused into a single mass?"
To attain such [a state] is not yet sharp or penetrating. Even if one were to act in this way, it would still be making a living inside a ghost cave. Case:
A monk asked Nanquan, "When Niu-tou had not yet met the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring flowers in their beaks to offer him? Nanquan said:
"Step by step, one treads upon the Buddha’s stairway. The monk asked, "Having seen him, why did he not offer the flower?
Nanquan said, "Even if he had not come, he would still have been one thread away from Old Wang. The Master said, "Nanquan only knew how to climb higher step by step;
he did not know how to let go from within the void. The monk asked, "What is meant by 'climbing higher step by step'? The Master said, "Xiangji."
[The Master] said, "The world. A monk asked, "How does one let go from within emptiness? The Master said, "Fill the ditches and block the ravines.

At other times, the Master said, "If you ask about the two words 'Buddha-dharma,' they extend to the east, west, south, and north; they traverse freely in all directions. In the morning one reaches the Western Heaven, and by evening one returns to the land of Tang.
Although this is so, hereafter you must not misrepresent them. He cited the verse of the Patriarch [Bodhidharma]: "The mind follows..."
The myriad phenomena revolve; where they revolve, the reality is truly profound. A monk asked, "What is meant by 'where they revolve, the reality is truly profound'?
The Master said, "Eat this clumsy tongue of mine! I shall walk backward three thousand li. He asked again, "What is meant by 'recognizing one's nature while following the stream'?
The Master said, "Steamed buns and *zhui*-cakes. *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* (The Great Perfection of Wisdom). [Case] Xuansha and Supervisor Wei.
During a conversation with Juncha, Jun said, "The speech of the people of Campā is already somewhat difficult to distinguish; how much more so is the Sanskrit of the Five Indias?
Is there anyone who can discern it? Xuansha picked up his alms bowl and said, "If you recognize this, you will have discerned it.
The Master said, "Why did Xuansha use such elaborate words? He also said, "What did he just say? And he also said, "What is there [to it]?"
"How difficult it is to discern! [The Master] raised [the case]: An ancient said, "To summon empty form with an empty name.
The Master said: "This staff is not an empty name; what it summons is not empty form. What would you call this staff that is not an empty name?

This was because Nanquan had addressed the assembly, saying: "Since my youth, I have raised a water buffalo. If I intend to let it loose to the east of the stream, it will inevitably graze upon others' crops."
"The King’s water and grass are intended for grazing on the west bank of the stream; yet, he cannot avoid eating the water and grass belonging to the King.
It would be better to accept them bit by bit wherever one happens to be; then he will not see them at all. Later, another monk related this to the Master.

The Master said, "Nanquan’s Water Buffalo accepts them bit by bit wherever he is. Tell me, do you say he accepts them within the cow, or does he accept them outside the cow? Even if you were to go toward this..."
In the inner meaning, the place of entry is explained with clarity. I ask you further: where is the ox? Later, Changqing said:
"Tell me, does the ancient master benefit people at the beginning, or does he benefit them at the end? He cited: King Wanda said to Xuefeng, "I intend to build a Buddha hall.
What do you say? Xuefeng replied, "Great King, why not build a Hall of the Empty King instead?"
The Great King said, "I request the Master’s model. Feng opened both hands. The Master said, "One stroke makes forty-nine. [The Master] cited the verse by Baozi praising Longya:
"The sun rises over the connected mountains; The moon is full before the door. It is not that there is no body, But it does not wish to be fully revealed.
A monk asked, "I request the Master to reveal it completely. Longya pulled back the curtain and said, "Do you see it? The monk [remained silent].
Yun said, "I do not see it. Ya said, "Bring me your eyes! Later, Baozi heard this mention and said, "Longya only managed to say half of it.
The Master once ordered a monk to raise an instance, saying, "I will tell you. The monk then raised one. The Master said, "It does not hinder me from telling you.
At other times, the Master said, "Everywhere else, people emerge from within the lines of the measuring cord; here, it is not so."
A monk asked, "I do not yet understand; how about you, Master? The Master said, "Thirty coins for a pair of straw sandals. [The Master] cited: "Grasping the truth, it is established;
form and appearance remain as they are. All dharmas do not migrate. The monk then asked, "What is this non-migration?
The Master said, "Do you see the lantern? The monk said, "I see it. The Master said, "Svāhā in a place of stillness."
Addressing the assembly, he said: "All of you come and go every day; it is not that you do not offer your greetings. But when you cross over water, what do you use to cross?
An elder monk who had resided there for a long time replied, "With my feet. The Master was deeply pleased by this.
He then cited the case of a monk taking leave of Dawsui. Dawsui asked, "Where are you going? The monk said, "I am going to Mount Emei to pay homage to Samantabhadra. Dawsui picked up [a staff].
The whisk-bearer said, "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are both right here. The monk drew a circle, threw it behind him, and then opened his two hands.
He followed this by saying, "Attendant, bring a cup of tea for this monk. The Master finished the story.
[The Master] said, "I am not like that. A monk asked, "How about you, Master? The Master said, "In India they cut off heads and arms;
here, go out and deal with it yourself. Case: One day Huangbo made a gesture of pinching with his hand and said, "All the old monks under heaven are right here.
If I were to let down a single thread, you could run wild and do as you please."
"If I do not let you pass, you will not survive even a single squeeze. A monk asked, "What is it like when you allow a single thread of passage?
Baizhang said, "Seven loose, eight across. The monk asked again, "What is it like when you do not let you pass and you do not spare a single squeeze?
Baizhang said, "Pǔ (Universal). Furthermore, a monk asked the Master, "What is 'seven loose, eight across'? The Master said, "Think of how old this old monk is! The monk said, "If..."

"What is 'universal'? The Master said, "The light of heaven shines back. The monk asked, "What is meant by 'the light of heaven shining back'? The Master said, "Few people know of these bones and flesh.
At another time, the Master said, "A single sphere of perfect radiance has long been manifest. Is there anyone who asks about it?
A monk then asked, "What is this single sphere of perfect radiance that has long been manifest? The Master said, "In Western India, they cut off heads."
He cut off his own arm. Again, it is said: "Remove Mount Sumeru; take away the ridgepole of the Buddha Hall.
One day, the Master donned his *kāṣāya* and said, "I am shaking off my Dharma-body. No one responded. The Master said, "Ask me.
A monk then asked, "Master, what is the meaning of 'shaking off the Dharma-body'? The Master said, "I know you well. [The Master] cited Xuefeng’s instruction to the assembly:
It is said: "The venerable elders of all quarters all claim they 'receive things and benefit living beings. But suppose three kinds of sick people were to come—how would you receive them?
For one suffering from blindness, you raise the mallet or brandish the whisk, yet he does not see. For one suffering from deafness, you speak of samādhi, yet he does not hear.
For one suffering from muteness, you try to teach him to speak, yet he cannot speak. How, then, will you receive them? If...
"You cannot receive this person; the Buddha-dharma has no spiritual efficacy. A monk requested instruction from the Master. The Master said, "Prostrate yourself.
As the monk rose from his prostration, the Master struck him with his staff. The monk stepped back, and the Master said, "It is not that you suffer from blindness.
He then called the monk forward again. As the monk approached, the Master said, "It is not that you suffer from deafness," and he held up his staff.

[The Master] said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "It is not that you suffer from dumbness. At these words, the monk attained realization. [The Master] raised an ancient saying:
"As soon as a single word is uttered, the entire earth is fully encompassed. The Master said, "Now tell me, what kind of word is this?"
He said to himself, "When the spring birds cry out upon the western ridge," and then he commanded a monk, "Ask me this.
The monk then asked, "What words are these? The Master said, "Aha! [The Master] cited Mazu Daoshi, who said, "All speech and language belong to the school of Deva;
take this as the primary principle. The Master said, "Excellent words! It is simply that no one asks about them. The monk then asked, "What is Deva?"
The Master said: "Of the ninety-six types [of heterodox paths] in the Western Heaven, you are the lowest type. He cited Master Zhao, who said:
"If all dharmas were not different, one could not lengthen the web-footed duck by shortening the crane, nor level the mountains to fill the valleys;
only then would they be 'without difference. The Master said: "The tall are naturally tall; the short are naturally short. He further said: "This Dharma abides in the station of Dharma."
"The characteristics of the world are eternally abiding. He then picked up his staff and said, "This staff is not the eternally abiding Dharma.

He cited an ancient saying: "In a single thought-moment, all kalpas are subsumed within omniscience. The Master picked up his staff and said, "The heavens, the earth, and the great world are all upon this very head.
If you can penetrate through this, even the staff will not be seen to exist. Even if you attain it in such a way, it is still not 'sticking.'"
[The Master] said: "Convenient. [He] raised [the case]: Subhūti was preaching the Dharma when Śakra rained down flowers. The Venerable One asked, "Did these flowers come from heaven?
Śakra replied, "No. "Did they come from the earth? Śakra replied, "No. "Did they come from humans? Śakra replied, "No. "From where did they come?
Śakra raised his hand. The Venerable One said, "So it is; so it is. The Master said, "Śakra..."
"What is it like when you raise your hand? It is identical to your four elements and five aggregates; it is no different from the Old Śākyamuni. [The Master] raised [the case]:
"When the World-Honored One was first born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, walked seven steps, and looking around in the four directions, said:
'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. The Master said: "If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow of my staff."
"Give it to the dog to eat; this is for the sake of peace throughout the world. Case: Heshan addressed the assembly, saying, "Is there any master warrior present?
Come forward! At that time, a monk stepped forth and asked, "I wonder, is there anyone among them? The Master said:
Case. [The Master] raised it. A monk asked Xuefeng, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Xuefeng sat cross-legged, holding his staff horizontally.

The Master said, "Constant. [The Master] raised another case. Deshan asked the rōhatsu (attendant in charge of arrivals), "How many new arrivals are there? The attendant said, "Eight people. Deshan said, "..."
[The Master] called for the *dianzuo* (steward) and had him pass [the items] by pressing them down all at once. The Master commented: "What more need be said about passing them by pressing them down?
He cited the following: Xuefeng examined a monk, asking, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "If you recognize it, you will know where I am going.
Xuefeng said, "You are a man who understands; why are you wandering about aimlessly? The monk said, "Do not defile me. Xuefeng said, "I am the one who defiles."
"You are defiling me! How did the ancients blow on the cloth-hair? Tell me how it was! A monk said, "The leftover soup and stale rice have already been eaten by someone else.
The Master rephrased the former statement, saying, "As soon as he struck it, it gave off the stench of excrement.
He provided a substitute for the latter statement, saying, "I thought it was a sky-piercing hawk; it turns out to be a shrimp in stagnant water. He cited Shao:
Mount Shan asked the monk, "Are you not that talkative old fellow Yin? The monk replied, "I dare not. Shan said, "How many mouths do you have?
The monk replied, "My whole body is [mouths]. Shan said, "Where do you defecate for the two necessities, great and small? The monk replied, [silently].
Xiang asked, "If there is a mouth at Mount Shao, I will defecate inside that mouth; if there is no mouth at Mount Shao, where shall I defecate?
Because he was speechless, Mount Shao struck him. The Master (Linji) spoke on his behalf, saying, "This fellow has fallen into a trap;
I grant you thirty blows. He spoke on his behalf again, saying, "I took you for a lion's cub. He said yet again, "Mount Shao now..."

[It] dissolves like ice in the sun. Case: A monk arrived at Caoxi. An elder who was guarding the robes and bowl held up the robe and said, "This is what could not be lifted at the head of Mount Dayu. The monk asked, "Why is it in your hands, Elder?"
The assembly remained silent. The Master said, "Each of them fails to understand. Acting on their behalf, he said, "To hear from afar is not as good as arriving in person.
He also said, "I thought this was a lion’s cub. Case: Muzhou asked a monk, "Are you not Qing Huayan? The monk said, "Yes."
“I dare not. The Governor asked, “Did you see the Avataṃsaka Sūtra in your dream? The monk was speechless. The Master said, “There is great disorder before the gate.
He cited an instance where Baoci of Hunan gave this instruction: “I have a phrase that pervades the great earth. A monk then asked, “What is the phrase that pervades the great earth?
Baoci replied, “No gaps or voids. The Master said, “It is improper to speak in such a way. It should be answered differently.”
Yun said, "Why not ask outside the hermitage? Case: Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying, "Last night at the third watch, Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra fought;
I gave each of them twenty blows and banished them to the two Iron Ring Mountains. Zhaozhou stepped forward from the crowd and asked, "Whom did the Master’s blows cause to eat?
Nanquan replied, "What fault has Old Wang committed? Zhaozhou then bowed. The Master spoke on his behalf: [He should have said: "If you had not struck them, they would have struck you."
"I deeply appreciate the Venerable Master’s compassion. I have found peace and security under the care of his robes and bowl. Case:
When Chongshou saw a monk making steamed buns, he asked from across a window, "Do you see me? The monk said, "I do not. Chongshou said:
"Give me back the money for my sesame cakes! The monk was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying: "It would be better for you, Preceptor, to bow to the cake oven.
Case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the summit of Mt. Miaofeng? Zhaozhou said, "I will not answer that question for you. The monk said, "Why do you not answer?
Zhaozhou said, "If I were to answer, I would fall to the ground. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying: "Master Jueyi."
Case: When Changqing saw a monk approaching, he said, "How can you be so discourteous? The Master (Dongshan) spoke on his behalf, saying, "I, this humble one, am at fault.
He also said, "Jiachen and Yisi. Case: Changqing asked a Confucian scholar, "In the Buddhist teachings it is said that sentient beings use [it] daily yet do not know it;
in the Confucian classics it is also said that they use it daily yet do not know it. What is it that they do not know? The scholar said, "I do not know."
"The Great Way. The Master said, "Truly, one does not know it. Case: A monk asked Muzhou, "Is there a snake on Vulture Peak?

Muzhou replied, "This earthworm. The Master provided this alternative: "White bones reaching to the mountains. Case: Changqing held up his staff and said, "If you recognize this, the business of a lifetime of study is finished.
The Master said, "Even if you recognize this, why do you not abide in it? Case: [End of excerpt]
While Yunyan was sweeping the floor, Daowu said, "Why are you being so busy? Yunyan replied, "One must know that there is one who is not busy.
Daowu said, "If that is so, then it is the 'second moon'. Yunyan held up his broom and asked, "Which moon is this? Daowu shook out his sleeves and walked out.
The Master said, "A servant showing courtesy to a maidservant. He then raised the case: Yangshan asked...
A secular official asked, "What office do you hold? The official replied, "I am a *tui-guan* (Investigating Official).
The Master then held up his whisk and said, "Can you investigate this? The official was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "I have long admired the Master.
[Case] A monk arrived at Cuiyan while the Master was away. He went down to see the administrative officials. The official in charge said, "Have you seen the Master yet? The monk replied, "Not yet."
The administrative official pointed to the dog and said, "If you wish to see the Master, simply prostrate to this dog. The monk was speechless.
Later, when Cuiyan returned and heard these words, he said, "How would you have answered to avoid being left speechless like this? The Master spoke on his behalf:
"If you wish to examine the teacher, first examine the disciple. He raised another case: A Dharma master, while lecturing on the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, invited Cuiyan to a vegetarian feast.
Yan said, "I, this mountain monk, have a question. If you, Master of the Seat, can answer it, I shall provide a meal. Yan then picked up a steamed bun and asked, "Does this possess the Dharma-body?
The Master replied, "It possesses the Dharma-body. Yan said, "In that case, you are eating the Dharma-body."
The Master remained silent. The Head Seat spoke on his behalf: "What fault is there? Yank refused to accept it. The Eastern Envoy said, "Yes, yes. The Master spoke on his behalf:
"I offer my special thanks to the Abbot for gracing this empty assembly with your presence. Case: Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying:
"When the world is ten feet wide, the ancient mirror is ten feet wide; when the world is one foot wide, the ancient mirror is one foot wide. Xuansha [commented].
Pointing to the brazier before him, he asked, "How wide is this brazier? Feng replied, "It is as wide as an ancient mirror.
Sha remarked, "This old fellow has not even set foot on the ground yet. Later, Dongshi took up this case to question a monk:
"Is it that because of the ancient mirror the brazier is so large, or because of the brazier the ancient mirror is so large? Xiyuan said, "Even asking such a question is [already too much]."
"Not yet. The Master said, "Rancid rice and a clay tea stove. Case: A monk asked Yunju, "From what do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise?
Yunju said, "They arise from deluded thoughts. The monk said, "Can you give me a bar of gold out of those thoughts?
Yunju then stopped speaking. The monk did not approve. The Master, having heard this, said, "This is already a tangle; it cannot be settled."
[The Master] said, "I am waiting for him to speak. I imagine he will produce a bar of gold; will he get it? He then took up his staff and struck him. He cited:
Wei, the Military Commissioner of Min, would often say to monks, "Once my term of office has ended, I shall go out to Jiangxi and Hunan and pose a question."
Question: "How did [the monk] kill the old masters of Jiangxi and Hunan? The monk said, "General Supervisor, how would you ask? The General said, "No need for hands or feet.
The monk was speechless. The Master provided a substitute response: "The talk has fallen. He also said: "We humbly pray that you may enjoy the offering. Case:
Wang Taifu asked Beiyuan, "The ancients said, 'Universally manifesting the physical body, pervasively practicing the samādhi. For what reason is this called the Buddha-dharma?"
Mao said, "He does not go to Uttarakuru. Yuan said, "It is precisely because he travels everywhere that he does not go there.

The Master said, "Come with a question posed according to the Dharma. He then cited: When Prime Minister Wang entered the Buddha hall, he pointed to a bowl and asked a monk, "What kind of bowl is this?
The monk said, "A Bhaisajyaguru bowl. The Prime Minister said, "I have only heard of the Dragon-subduing bowl. The monk said, "Wait until [one appears]..."
The dragon immediately descended. Wei said, "If you suddenly encounter one who seizes the clouds and captures the waves coming toward you, what then?
The monk said, "He would not even look back. Wei said, "Your words have fallen into error. Xuansha said, "Even with all your supernatural powers, where could you run?"
Baofu said, "I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Baizhang made the gesture of overturning his alms bowl.
The Master said, "When you are reborn in the heavens in a future life, do not let me down. He cited the case where Dizang asked Chongshou, "In the distant future, with what will you benefit others?
Chongshou replied, "There is nothing that does not benefit them. Dizang said, "There is not a single dharma that benefits them. The Master said, "Even if you were to grant it..."
"Mò! You deserve a blow of the staff as well. He further said: "At that time, I simply would have called him to come closer;
later, there would have been no place for him to peck at. Case: Wang Taifu of Quanzhou asked a monk, "Where do you reside, Senior? The monk replied, "Mount Bānyuè (Half-Moon Mountain)."
Fotu said, "If you suddenly encounter the first or last day of the month, what then? The monk was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "I thought it was like this;
there is yet another 'like this. He cited: Longya usually said, "My elder brother Yunju attained the second phrase."
"I have attained the first phrase. Xiyuan said, "As for Longya speaking thus, does he still manage to support [the truth]?
The Master said, "One must first pay homage to Yunju before one can attain it. Xiyuan said, "The bystanders will laugh. [Case] Chongshou asked a monk, "Do you see the lantern?
The monk said, "I see it. Chongshou said, "Two. The Master provided this substitute response: "Three heads and two faces."
It is also said: "Seven or eight.

The Master was unwell and said, "I am going to travel; I shall go to beat the straw sandals. No one replied. The Master said, "You ask, and I will tell you.
The monk then asked, "Where are you going, Preceptor? The Master said, "To the four quarters, above and below, to provide teachings according to the capacity of those encountered.
[The Master’s] response on behalf of the previous statement was: "Preceptor, you ought to drink ginger-and-attachment soup."

Ascending the hall, he said: "A decree! Long rains have not ceased. [The Master] provides the response: "One arrow, two targets. Alternatively, it is said: "When encountering the base, it is noble; when encountering the bright, it is dark.
[The Master] provides the response: "One rises, one falls. One day he said: "Regarding the 'biting the teeth' phrase—how do you speak?

[The Master] provides the response: "Close [the mouth]. Alternatively, it is said: "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, thirty blows for failing to take responsibility. [The Master] provides the response: "I am like..."

"Yes. He asked the assembly, "Are the Kingdom of Silla and the Great Tang Kingdom the same or different? A representative replied, "The Sangha Hall, the Buddha Hall, the kitchen, the storehouse, and the three gates."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The meaning of the teachings cannot be raised up. Where does the fault lie? [In his stead,] he replied:
"It is because for you the frog is alive. Ascending the hall, he said: "Tell me, when the Ancient Buddha and the pillar intersect, what rank of capacity is that? No one answered. The Master said:
"You ask; I shall give you my answer. The monk then asked. The Master said, "A single cord for thirty cash. [The Master] provided this in place of the previous statement:
"Clouds rise on the southern mountain; rain falls on the northern mountain. The monk asked again, "What is this 'a single cord for thirty cash'? The Master said, "Give it to him.
One day, he said, "In discussing and raising this point, what is being realized? [The Master] provided this in his place: "Salt is expensive."

"Rice is cheap. Someone asked, "If one were to set aside the two characters 'Buddha' and 'Dharma,' what would be accomplished? He replied in their stead: "A dead shrimp. Someone else asked, "There is no need to study Buddha-dharma;
the lanterns and pillars are merely deceiving you. How can you act so that they do not deceive you? He replied in their stead:
"To the south of Zhaozhou, to the north of the Stone Bridge. One day he said, "The ancients sat facing the wall and closed their doors."
"Can you still penetrate this point? [The Master] provides the response: "What kind of dried dung-puck is this? He also says: "One. Or he says:
"Carrying firewood back and forth—within the four deportments of walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, can you get out from behind the nose of Old Śākyamuni?
[The Master] provides the response: "The Master, too, is merely filling a post according to one's capacity. The Master sometimes raises his hand and says: "An ancient Buddha."
"Why do you not come here? [The Master] provided this reply: "One must not lower one’s dignity to accommodate the lowly.
Because a monk was preparing a vegetarian feast for Master Baoci, the Master asked the monk: "Tell me, how many bodies does Master Baoci have? [The Master] provided this reply:

"Today’s meal is prepared according to the Dharma. He asked a monk: "While you are carrying firewood back and forth, where is Samantabhadra Bodhisattva? [The Master] provided this reply: "Carrying [it]."
Chái was already a life of hardship.
Entering the hall, when the assembly had gathered, he said: "This is a great calamity; examine it thoroughly. [A disciple] spoke on his behalf, saying:

"There is no need for another person. He asked a monk: "In this world, whose sin is the heaviest? [The monk] spoke on his behalf, saying: "Level and straightforward. One day, he said: "The ancients..."
"The Human Path. A single phrase that hits the mark is a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas. How can one clarify the way to avoid this fault?
[The Master] speaks on their behalf: "Zhaozhou’s Stone Bridge; the Great Statue of Jiazhou. Or he says: "Does empty space have length and shortness, or not?"
A substitute says: "This monk is so fat; this monk is so thin. One day [the Master] said:
"In the views of ordinary people, where does the error lie? The substitute says: "It lies in making a conceptual understanding of it."
Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered and settled, he said: "If there is a principle that cannot be extended, one dies without being mourned.

If there is a principle that can be extended, it is rare to encounter such a remarkable person. Bring forth a question! [The Master] spoke on behalf [of the assembly], saying: "A transgression. At other times, the Master asked a monk: "How is it?
[The monk] spoke on behalf [of the Master], saying: "Eat less. Or he would say: "All of you have been traveling throughout the world on pilgrimage, yet you do not know the meaning of the Patriarchs."
"The incense burner, however, knows there is the meaning of the Patriarch. How do you understand that the incense burner knows there is the meaning of the Patriarch?
[The Master] provided this in his stead: "Nine times nine is eighty-one."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "One instance is not repeated. What is this 'one instance'? He further said:
"If you do not grasp it, first seek a way of entry. All the Buddhas of the micro-dusts are upon your tongues;
the holy teachings of the Tripitaka are beneath your feet. It would be better to awaken to this. Is there anyone who can awaken? Come forward and speak!"
"Look! [The Master] spoke on behalf [of the assembly], saying: "The conditions for raising a child. He further spoke on behalf of the previous words, saying: "Though Chang'an is pleasant...
Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered and settled, he said: "The wind does not come; the tree does not move. Then he descended from his seat. [The Master] spoke on their behalf, saying:
"The tree breaks and the boat sinks. Or he asked: "How do you speak the first phrase? If you cannot speak it, how will you attain the mind?"
[The Master] sighed. A [disciple] offered this in his stead: "Does the Master not desire straw sandals and a staff? One day, he asked: "How did the ancients of old distinguish people?
A [disciple] offered this in his stead: "The city and its lands were established because of you. The Master, while picking tea, said: "Picking tea is hard work."
He set down his staff and asked a question. [The monk] was speechless. He said again, "If you cannot speak, then recite the 'Shang Daren' (The Great Person).
That will not do either; for now, just follow the vermilion. [Dongshan] spoke on his behalf, saying, "Effort is not exerted in vain. To replace the previous remark, he said, "Labor without merit."
Someone said, "Today is the twenty-seventh. Where do you place it? [The Master] spoke on their behalf: "Hanging on the wall.
He asked a monk, "Who can take up the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings? [The Master] spoke on his behalf: "Novices and probationary monks. One day, he said:
"How do you discern the unobstructed Dharma? [The Master] provides the answer: "Household utensils. Or he asks: "Is there one who can hide their body within the phrase?
[The Master] provides the answer: "I understand. One day he says: "In the capital, are there any pillars and beams? [The Master] provides the answer:
"Every household has its Avalokiteśvara. Or he says: "If it does not correspond, for now follow the vermilion; recognize this well. [The Master] provides the answer: "Because of the student."

[The Master] set it down. He addressed the assembly, saying: "A *zhā* [a written note] is difficult. 'Seven times nine is sixty-three. How would you say it? [The Master] spoke on behalf [of the assembly], saying:
"It cannot be that there is no one at all who can go. He also said: "It would have been better to say this later. The Master sometimes said: "Coming and going during the day; during the day..."
Distinguishing People. Suddenly in the middle of the night, he instructed [his attendant] to bring him an object. Before it had even reached him, [the Master asked], "How do you take it?
[The attendant] replied on his behalf: "How many people have you deceived?"

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Look, look! The Buddha Hall has entered into the Sangha Hall! [On behalf of the assembly, he] said: "The drum beats at Luofu, and the dance is performed in Shaoyou.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Look, look! The three thousand great thousandfold world-systems are all shaken at once. Then...
[The Master] descended from his seat. [A disciple] spoke on his behalf: "Drag it out! One day, he asked: "What is the phrase that clarifies both simultaneously?
[The disciple] spoke on his behalf: "One arrow, two targets. Or he asked: "What is the phrase that does not deceive people? [The disciple] spoke on his behalf:
"Do not say that this is a deceptive phrase. One day, he asked: "When mud and water are not distinguished, where does the fault lie? [The disciple] spoke on his behalf: "Was it not yesterday?"
The Yao people prepared a vegetarian feast. Someone asked: "If it is said that 'day and night, coming and going, you recognize me all along,' what is the single phrase for the shadow-body?
He replied on behalf [of the master]: "I, too, see the sun rise from the east. One day, he asked: "When exerting one's full strength, how do you speak? He replied on behalf [of the master]:
"Five steamed buns and three bowls of tea. Someone else asked: "What is the meaning of stretching out one’s arms level? He replied on behalf [of the master]: "A single staff."

Question: [The Master] said, "Substitute for me. [The attendant] immediately pinched a monk standing nearby. One day, [the Master] asked, "Emptiness is not different from form; how would you say it? [The attendant] substituted for him, saying:
The head gardener was very important. Someone asked, "What is the phrase for that which does not cast a shadow? He replied on behalf [of the Master]: "Manifest.
One day, as the assembly had gathered for the hall discourse, the Master sat for a long while in silence and said, "It has rained for a long time without clearing.

He replied on behalf [of the Master]: "A single blow serves two purposes; cover it over and bring it forth. One day he said, "In the teachings it is said: 'Because of slandering this sutra, one incurs such offenses. Take it away!"
When [the Master] was about to leave through the gate, he brought a scripture. A substitute said, "Amoghapāśa.

Or he said, "You have been in the monastic groves for many years," and then, raising his hand, he immediately lowered it and said, "In the future, you must not act like this. The substitute said, "If you act like this, you will surely fail the Master.
One day, he said, "Yesterday there was a phrase; I do not dare hope that you will understand it. Do you still..."
"Is there anyone who can manage this? [The Master] provided the answer on their behalf: "A sudden leap. He added: "How many people have been run to death!
One day, when the assembly had gathered for the lecture hall, he said, "Everyone has come up here; now each of you go your own way, east or west," and then he descended from his seat.
The Master spoke on behalf [of the student], saying: "Not a little. Or he said: "The ancients attained enlightenment through a single word; they saw their nature upon encountering conditions.
When you pick it up, how will you deliberate? He spoke on behalf [of the student], saying: "The drum of Yunju; the bell of Shanglan. One day he said:
"Coming and going in the daylight, moving up and down, question and answer—this is what you must shoulder. When a question is thrust at you from the side, how will you shoulder it?"
Dai said: "It is said that when one rises early, there are still travelers on the road at night. He also said: "One arises, one falls.
And he also said: "Born in Jizhou."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Heaven and earth tilt; sun, moon, and stars all turn black at once. How do you say it? [The Master] provided the answer on their behalf:
"Better not to have had this good thing at all. When the discourse was finished, the Master stood up, struck the meditation seat once with his staff, and said:
Where would you cast all this entanglement that has just come forth? Those who are quick-witted will see it immediately;
those who are not quick-witted will be deceived by my heated words. [The Master] provides a substitute response: "Adding frost to snow."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The sun and moon shine sideways upon three worlds and shine directly upon four worlds;
I have explained this thoroughly for you. Speak a single phrase! [The Master] provided the answer: "Pūrvavideha in the east; Aparagoyānī in the west. Alternatively, he said:
"In the Buddha-dharma, there is no need to speak of it. What thing in the world is most precious? [The Master] provided the answer: "Do not say that this is cheap."
"Bottom. He also said, "A dry piece of excrement. One day he said, "Today is the fifteenth; summer has begun. What about you, Hanshan?
In his stead, he replied: "The Master asks of Hanshan; the student answers for Shigede. Or he said:
"All of you who travel as pilgrims—do you recognize the twenty-eight patriarchs of India? In his stead, he replied: "Those sitting sit; those lying down lie."
It is also said: "Eat little. During a meal, [the Master] pointed to a white ceramic vessel and said, "This one knows the talk that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs.
[The disciple] spoke on his behalf, saying: "Five times nine is forty-five. It is also said: "The Abbot eats the food himself. One day, he said: "You have been traveling to other houses;
