"What is 'possessing the eye within the question'? A substitute says: "Blind."

Addressing the assembly, he said: "If you cite one, you must not cite two. If you cite two, I will allow you to cite three. [The Master] spoke on behalf [of the student], saying: "Open! The Master sometimes said:
"Heavenly realms and hells, boiling cauldrons and burning furnaces—they cover your head! The Buddhas of the three periods of time are all beneath your heels.
Thirty years from now, your nostrils will point toward the heavens. [The Master] spoke on behalf [of the student], saying: "One must no longer act like a wild beast."
This is the understanding of a fox-spirit. One day he said, "Are the five notes and six scales existent or non-existent?
A substitute replied, "One cannot make a living inside a toad's den. The Master sometimes said, "A single phrase encompasses all; the five thousand-plus verses are *sulu sahā*.
A substitute replied, "Beating the drum at the triple gate, burning incense in the Buddha hall. The Master sometimes said, "Nowadays, half..."
"Xia! Strike! Bring forth a phrase regarding the Way! The Master spoke again: "Mitra-gu, mitra-jñā. He asked further:
"What about 'Mitra-gu, mitra-jñā'? On behalf [of the student], he said: "Bu-lin. He spoke again.
*Kai*. One day he said, "In thirty years, you will understand. [The Master] spoke on his behalf: "A drop falls at the right moment. Or [another said]:
"I do not ask about the thunderbolt striking your head; when the dragon passes beneath your feet, bring me a phrase!
[The Master] spoke on his behalf: "Clouds rise in the morning; rain falls at night. The Master asked a monk: "When Deshan struck him with his staff, tell me, does the student still have some merit?"
"None. A substitute says: "Groundlessly. One day he said: "Within the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, is there still arising and ceasing?
A substitute says: "The yakṣa recited half a verse. Or he says: "If one knows the place of departure, in which eon would there be no patriarchs or Buddhas?"
The Master said, "Fā.

He addressed the assembly, saying, "What is the phrase that does not reveal its sharp edge or bone? He provided the response: "People of the present day must clearly state it for you before they can succeed.
The Master then offered this verse: "The phrase that does not reveal its sharp edge or bone— Before a word is spoken, it has already been entrusted. [He] advanced.
He stammers at the mouth; I know you are utterly at a loss. Another says: "Within the lands of the ten directions, there is only the Single Vehicle Dharma (Ekayāna).
You say for yourself: are you within the Single Vehicle Dharma, or outside the Single Vehicle Dharma? [The Master] provides the answer: "Enter. Another says: "It is so."
One day he said: "The knot is half-broken; three. Bring me a phrase from within the nostrils of the needle-case.
[Another] offered in his stead: "Sailing with the wind upon the sea, a boat on the mountain. Or [another] said: "Half-broken and arranged as three. Where are the nostrils of the needle-case?"

"Bring them all forth for me to see. [The Master] provides the response: "Superior, middling, and inferior. Or [the Master] says: "When boundaries are demarcated and lands are divided, how do you speak of it?
[The Master] provides the response: "Mañjuśrī is Mañjuśrī; liberation is liberation. The Master sometimes says:
"A patch-robed monk must obtain the 'vital point' (bābi) in order to recognize all people under heaven. What is the patch-robed monk’s vital point? [The Master] provides the response: [Silence].
Deshan’s Staff. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"If you hear it superficially, you will realize it deeply; if you hear it deeply, you will not realize it. [The Master] provides a substitute response: "Meeting Bodhidharma while lost. Or he says:
"A patch-robed monk must recognize the eyes of the ancients. What are the eyes of the ancients? [The Master] provides a substitute response: "A frog leaps."
One day, [Zhaozhou] said, "Bring me a phrase from every place. He answered on his behalf: "The Son of Heaven in the bustling marketplace;
the old monk at the tips of the hundred grasses. Or he said, "Bring me a phrase from the dark path. He answered on his behalf: "Hiding the head and exposing the tail.
One day, he said, "Taking south for north, and taking north for south—how do you speak? He answered on his behalf: "By whom? Or...
The Master said, "Before the board has been struck, bring me a phrase. [The attendant] replied, "What need is there for such a pretext?
One day, the Master said, "If one regards existence as existence, how can one avoid it? [The attendant] replied, "It is a sickness.

The Master sometimes said, "When you understand that the sickness is not a sickness, what is the eye? [The attendant] replied, "By day one sees the sun; by night one sees the stars. One day, the Master said:
"Why do light and darkness not manage one another? The Master replied, "It is difficult to mock. Another said, "Where does the fault lie that it is so difficult?
The Master replied, "Discernment. One day he said, "Vast and indistinct—within whose sphere of experience does this fall?
The Master replied, "One must not hold the views of a novice monk or a practitioner. Sometimes the Master would pick up his staff.
The Master said, "Do not say that the old monk is deceiving you. Whether noble or base, whether horizontal or vertical—understand them all at once here.
Do not fail me. [The student] offered this in his place: "The hundred birds bend for their young. He also said: "To suppress it, and to give it.
The Master asked, "Do you see? [The student] replied, "I see. The Master asked again, "What do you see? [The student] offered this in his place: "Flowers. The Master cited an ancient precedent.
A person said: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes picking and choosing. 'This is the Sangha Hall,' 'This is the Buddha Hall'—which of these is non-picking and choosing?
[The Master] spoke in his stead: "Why must it be so? The Master sometimes asked: "When you say 'drawing out the whole' or 'drawing out the half,' how do you speak of this?
Furthermore, what is 'drawing out the half'? He spoke in his stead: "Leap out of the dead shrimp! He also said: [the same].
"How is it to draw out the whole? [The Master] provided the response: "Thunder on the side mountain; rain on the main mountain. The Master sometimes said: "You have only brought this upon yourself;
first of all, you must not misquote. He provided the response: "An event does not arise in isolation. One day he said: "If you recognize it and attain it..."

[The Master] said, "Come forth and speak! What is the point of this dialogue? [The disciple] answered on his behalf: "Recognize your offense. Or [the Master] asked: "What is the phrase that is not to be asked again?
[The disciple] answered on his behalf: "This year the spring air is early; last night the sunbird sang. He also said: "Incense is being prepared in the Buddha Hall;
one joins one’s palms before the Main Gate. One day he said: "It has been eleven days since the beginning of summer. Have you attained it yet?"
"Have you entered the gate? How do you say it? [The disciple] answers on his behalf: "Tomorrow at noon.
The Master, while drinking tea, picked up the teacup and said, "What is it like when one swallows it all in a single gulp? [The disciple] answers on his behalf: "The tea has already been drunk."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "The twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven, the six patriarchs of the Land of Tang, and all the old monks of the world—should they all come forth, where would their fault lie?
He further said: "Suppose you have been here for three winters and two summers, and suddenly go abroad.

If someone asks you what the Old Monk Yunmen taught, what would you say to him? [Yunmen] spoke on behalf [of the student], saying: [The text ends here; the response spoken on behalf is traditionally recorded as: "Three pounds of flax. (三斤麻)
He spat in the face of this wild fox spirit. Speaking on behalf of the former statement, he said: "This man is not mad. Or he said:

"An ancient said, 'That which enters through the gate is not the treasure. What, then, is the gate? Speaking on behalf of him, he said: "Even if you could speak it, it would be of no use. Upon hearing the sound of a drum, he said:
"The drum sound bites through the seven-striped robe. He then pointed to a monk and said: "Bring the cat here! [Speaking on behalf of him: [He brought the cat.]
[The Master] said, "Not another person. The Master asked a monk, "I will not question you about the matter of traveling on pilgrimage;
rather, bring me a single phrase regarding the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics. Is there anyone who can speak it? [The monk] replied in his stead, "Tathāgata for two thousand years.
The Master sometimes said, "I am not questioning you about the teachings of the monastic community (saṃgha). This is heaven; this is..."
Deshan pointed to his own body and said, "This is me. He then pointed to a pillar and said, "This is a pillar.
Which one is the Buddha-dharma? [Another] spoke on his behalf: "It is truly difficult. The Master was drinking tea in the Sangha hall.
Picking up the tea tray, he said, "Steamed buns and dumplings are for you to eat as you please. Tell me, what is this? [Another] spoke on his behalf: "Dry."
"Dog shit! He also said, "The tea has been drunk as well. The Master sometimes asked, "Do you recognize Deshan?
Do not say that I am forcing the noble to become base. [The disciple] spoke on his behalf: "I know it was because of you, Master, that I obtained this [position].

When the Master heard the sound of the meal gong, he asked, "Tell me, why was the drum obtained? [The disciple] spoke on his behalf: "It was obtained because of the hide. When the Master heard the meal gong...
[Sheng] asked: "Do you still recognize the 'Old Lady’s Zen'? [The Master] answered on his behalf: "The drum calls us to eat. One day, [Sheng] said:
"An ancient said, 'Skillfulness and clumsiness both possess life and death. What is this life and death? [The Master] answered on his behalf:
"Not enough when matched above; more than enough when matched below."
Ascending the hall, once the assembly had gathered, the Master said, "The assembly, go for your meal. He then asked a monk, "Tell me, when I told them to go, was there any fault in that?
[The monk] replied on his behalf: "It was not the Master who acted so arbitrarily. As the Master was walking about, he...
[The Master] struck a pillar with his staff once and said, "The Son of Heaven of Silla leaps up to the Brahma Heaven. [The attendant] spoke on his behalf: "Groundless.

The Master sometimes said, "The conventional truth does not require speaking; bring me a single phrase of the Buddha-dharma. [The attendant] spoke on his behalf: "The affection between father and son.
One day he said, "For one who has attained thorough clarity, what thing comes in such a manner? [The attendant] spoke on his behalf: "Do not let it [be so]."

"Subduing people. It is also said: "Śākyamuni is Mount Sumeru. Or it is said: "The ancients said, 'Morning after morning one embraces the Buddha and sleeps; when rising, one rises together with him. You tell me, how would a person whose understanding is dim and hazy act? [The Master] provided this in their stead: *Subduing people.* *Śākyamuni is Mount Sumeru.* *How would a person whose understanding is dim and hazy act?* *Subduing people.* It is also said:

"The ancients said, 'Morning after morning one embraces the Buddha and sleeps; when rising, one rises together with him. You tell me, how would a person whose understanding is dim and hazy act? [The Master] provided this in their stead: *Mount Sumeru.* *How would a person whose understanding is dim and hazy act?* *Mount Sumeru.* Or it is said: "The ancients said, 'Morning after morning one embraces the Buddha and sleeps; when rising, one rises together with him. You tell me, how would a person whose understanding is dim and hazy act? [The Master] provided this in their stead: *Mount Sumeru.* *How would a person whose understanding is dim and hazy act?* *Mount Sumeru.*
[The Master] had not yet arrived. He asked a monk, "In the eye there is no form-consciousness; in consciousness there is no form-eye. Since both form and eye are absent, how can one see form?
Set aside the ancients and bring me a single phrase. [The monk] offered in his stead: "Bring me some steamed buns and fried cakes.
Another said: "Adding frost upon snow. Another said: "What is there? The Master sometimes said: "The flagpole."

“Standing upside down on one’s head—what kind of device is this? The representative replied: “Strike! One day he said: “Those who study the Buddha-dharma are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
Bring me a single phrase from the tips of the hundred grasses. The representative replied: “All together (jū). The Master, upon leaving the room, said:
“The ancients said, ‘That which enters through the gate is not the treasure. You tell me, what about that which goes out through the gate? The representative replied: “One.”

When the Master entered the hall during the meal service, he pointed to the alms bowl of the Sacred Monk and asked the monks, "If you eat it all up, you will fall back into the deep pit of liberation.
If you do not eat it all up, you are still not clever. What would you do? [In place of the monks, one might say:
"While the assembly is eating their rice."
Ascending the hall, he said, "To cut it off completely is not permissible. He then added, "If you do not understand, do not say you did not see the old monk thirty years from now.
[The Master] provided a substitute response: "The Master fears that people might bury [the truth]. He further provided a substitute for the previous remark: "Today I have ascended the hall."
The assembly found this convenient and practical. The Master sometimes struck a pillar with his staff once and said, "Why do you not speak of Chan?

He then added, "You have brought disgrace upon the men and women of this house. No one could respond. The Master spoke for them himself, saying, "Carrying the cangue, one passes through the legal proceedings.
To replace the previous statement, he said, "How can one blame others? The Master would also say, "I do not ask about the fish in the lake that has transformed into a dragon."

[The Master asked: "What is the needle-eye fish? [The disciple] answered on his behalf: "A dot. When the Master heard the sound of the mallet striking, he said: "The world of Miaoxi shatters into a hundred fragments;
holding my almsbowl, I go into the city of Hunan to eat porridge. [The disciple] answered on his behalf: "I eat after bathing. One day [the Master] said:
"In what words is there no mundane truth? In what words is there no hell? [The disciple] answered on his behalf: "Sunny weather."
The sun rose; rain fell and thunder arose. Someone said, "Ordinary mind is the Way. [The Master] asked, "Bring me a phrase for your ordinary Way.
He provided the response: "Five steamed buns, three *zhui*. One day he said, "A single phrase distinguishes the heterodox from the orthodox.
Suddenly someone asked, "What is the phrase that distinguishes the heterodox from the orthodox? How would you say it? He provided the response: "India."
This is different from this land. [The Master] said: "Do not say 'not needed' before today, do not say 'not needed' after today;
when it is precisely today, bring me one phrase. He provided the answer on his behalf: "It is exactly so. The Master sometimes said: "When a sickness meets its cause, it is immediately cured."
"What cause did you encounter? Speak it! The representative said: "Still. Or he said: "How far apart are the bowl, the spoon, and the chopsticks from the pillar?
The representative said: "It is best to separate them. He also said: "I usually obtain this opportunity. One day he asked:
"What do you say for a phrase that meets the challenge head-on? The representative said: "Understood. Or he asked: "What is discernment?"
Regarding "A single phrase of the breeze of compassion," he spoke on behalf [of another], saying: "Recognize it well. One day, he said: "How do you express the phrase regarding the deluded body?

He spoke on behalf [of another], saying: "Yesterday the thunder arose; this morning the sunbird cries. The Master sometimes said: "No need for such jumping about; bring forth a phrase! He spoke on behalf [of another], saying:
"A dead toad has no use. One day, he asked: "What is it? He spoke on behalf [of another], saying: "It is like a man who has lost his way."
The School of Deva. [The Master] says: "In the West, the command was strict; in this land, we must still deliberate. [The Master] says: "Tell me, what thing possesses the four virtues?
[The attendant] replies: "A dead cat. [The Master] further says: "Bring me that which does not possess them. One day, [the Master] says: "Thorns are not pruned or selected.
Bring forth a single phrase. [The attendant] replies: "Set it aside. Or [the Master] says: "There is one who sees all."
"What kind of person is this person? He replied, "A tax-paying man from a village of three households. One day he said, "Without occupying any fields, speak a phrase.
He replied, "It all belongs to the Master. Or he said, "Speak a phrase in reverse and let me see it. He replied, "Bodhisattva.
One day he said, "How do you speak a phrase that puts an end to the cycle? He replied, "Knowing the time."
"Good. The Master sometimes said, "The world is in chaos and everyone is running about; with what will you cross the water? He provided the answer: "Just let it dry in the sun.
Sometimes the Master would take up his staff and make a gesture as if shooting an arrow, saying, "The authorities have sent their weapons! Look, look! He provided the answer:
"The Master must not let them pass," and added, "In front of the Sangha Hall. The Master sometimes said, "One night he stretched out his legs and slept until dawn."
"Bring me a phrase of the Way. [The Master] provides the response: "Why do you not get up quickly? Or he says: "What is the phrase that is completely free? He provides the response:
"That too is quite groundless. One day he says: "If one takes existence as existence, where does this person’s fault lie?
He provides the response: "Suffering. Or he says: "Is there anyone who does not recognize the Patriarch? He provides the response: "The Way of benevolence and righteousness."
[The Master] said, "Furthermore, it is said: 'Do not worry. One day he said: 'If you recognize your fault, there is no fault; if you do not recognize your fault, you do not even know the fault.

[To this, the Master] provided the substitute response: 'It is hot. Or he asked: 'On the road to Caoxi, is there still any worldly talk? [To this, the Master] provided the substitute response: 'The two matters occur simultaneously.'"
One day [Yunmen] said: "Set aside the Buddha-dharma and bring me a question. [The Master] provided the response: "One is already too many. Or he said:
"Since you know its place of origin, in which eon would there not have been patriarchs? [The Master] provided the response: "This fellow does not find it convenient this year. Or he said:

"Where not even an inch of grass grows—do not study Chan, do not study the Way. [The Master] provided the response: "What idle talk is this? Or he said: "Is it so? [The Master] provided the response: "It is."
"Is there a phrase that cannot be swallowed? [The Master] answered on his behalf: "A snake. While walking, the Master struck a pillar with his staff once and asked, "Where have you come from?
[The pillar] replied, "I have come from India. He then asked again, "What are you doing here? [The pillar] replied, "..."
While preaching the Buddha-dharma, he suddenly shouted, "You are deceiving me, you man of Tang!
He then struck him once with his staff and walked away. Turning back, he questioned a monk: "Tell me, what was my intention? The monk then asked, "What, then, was your meaning, Master?

[The Master] answered on his behalf: "There is no need for the host to walk. He also said: "A lion bites. He then asked the monk: "As for the one who is facing the situation [the practitioner], what do you say?"
"What phrase can be uttered at once? He answered on his behalf: "To set forth. He also said: "An old man of a hundred years performing songs and dances.
One day he asked: "How do you speak a sudden, piercing phrase? He answered on his behalf: "Because of one matter, one gains one wisdom. Or he asked:
"With what will you distinguish the Great Canon of Teachings? He answered on his behalf: "A dot. One day he asked: "Why is it that the Buddha Hall does not see the monks?"
The Master said, “Halls. A disciple offered a response: “Painful. Or he said, “I do not ask you about the nostrils of the patch-robed monk;

tell me, while washing a clod of earth in the mud, speak one phrase! He responded by merely snapping his fingers. Again he asked, “And as for the nostrils of the patch-robed monk, how would you speak?
He responded, “Gazing at the mountains, gazing at the waters. The Master once asked a monk, “What is the phrase that is not quiescent? The monk did not answer. The Master said:
“You ask me; I shall tell you. The monk then asked, “What is the phrase of non-quiescence? The Master said, “Pu.

[The Master] provided an alternative for the previous statement, saying, “One must not make one’s livelihood within a ghost cave. He was further asked, “What is ‘Pu’? He provided an alternative, saying, “Understand this meaning.
He also said, “The five characters of Mañjuśrī. Or he said, “What is it to enter a region and follow its customs?”

The Bottom Line. [The Master] spoke on behalf [of the student], saying: "A gentleman may be eight. One day he asked: "What is the one phrase that holds up the main pillar? [The Master] spoke on behalf [of the student], saying:
"Xuefeng is to the south; Zhaozhou is to the north. One day he asked: "The spiritual sprout does not move its roots. Where does the fault lie?"
A substitute says: "How many people have you misled? Or he says: "A single sphere of radiant light has been manifest for a long time.
What is this single sphere of radiant light? The substitute says: "Thank you, Preceptor, for your repeated kindness. The Master sometimes asks: "What is the phrase that corresponds to 'luminosity'?
The substitute says: "Exposed. The Master sometimes says: "Neither form nor sound; to realize luminosity within the essence is the first..."
A questioner asked: "What is the pivot? The Master replied: "One must not make one's livelihood within the den of a wild fox. One day he said:
"When the silken net is spread across the heavens to catch dragons, and the silk net is spread to scoop up shrimp and clams, tell me, where do the snails and oysters fall?
The Master provided the response: "One with eyes. Because the Master had taken off his seven-piece robe, he said to a monk: "Tell me, will you not understand the Buddha in a future life?"

"Is this the Dharma? The monk remained silent. [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying, "Venerable Sir, you are fortunately a great man. He spoke again, saying, "I, your disciple, do not dare to speak. He spoke yet again, saying, "Why do you not dare to speak?
He spoke once more, saying, "Because the Venerable Sir is already here. On the night of the New Year, the Master questioned a monk.

"Steamed cakes are the medicinal food for Arhats. Have you brought some *bi-dong* (steamed buns) as well? [The monk] was speechless. [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying: [The Master said: "If you have not yet attained the fruit of Arhatship, how can you eat such medicinal food?"
"Today the east wind rises. The Master sometimes said: "If you do not measure up, then bring forth a single phrase from within the gate of the ancient masters' transformative teachings.
If you cannot bring it forth, then bring forth a single phrase from elsewhere.
How would you say it? He provided a substitute response: "What came before was still acceptable. One day he said: "Far, it illuminates; near, it clarifies. What is this?"
"Born on the Way. A substitute says: "Only upon entering the water does one see the tall man. Another says: "It is not even necessary. The Master sometimes picks up his staff and says:
"Try to understand it right here. Is there benefit? Is there no benefit? If you understand neither, you will have a vague notion of Buddha-nature and a muddled grasp of True Suchness.
A substitute says: "Not enough when compared to what is above; more than sufficient when compared to what is below. One day he said: "Ten thousand..."
"From where does the Dharma arise? A substitute reply: "One cannot even say it is within the mouth of a toad, O Master.

Because he heard the sound of the drum at mealtime, he said: "The ancients said that all sounds are the Buddha’s voice. Shall we call them the Buddha’s voice, or shall we call them the sound of the drum?
A substitute reply: "The Master has already spoken. He also said: "It would not be well for the Master to eat wheat flour. Because he saw...
A monk came to visit. The Master struck the pillar once and said, "You have come here to deceive me. [The disciple] spoke on his behalf: "Just give the pillar a slap. [The Master] said:
"To benefit others, one must remain at ease. One day he said, "The ultimate Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes discrimination. What is non-discrimination?
He added, "The wondrous form-body of the Tathāgata—Luoluo Li. [The disciple] spoke on his behalf: "It does not emerge."
Substituting for the previous statement, he says: "The ancients have already said it. Because at the time of the meal he struck the seat once, he says:
"This one eats. He strikes the rice table once and says: "This one does not eat. Substituting for him, he says: "One blow serves two purposes. Because they were moving rice, he asked a monk:
"Does the person carry the rice, or does the rice carry the person? Substituting for him, he says: "Both are obtained. He further says: "The toil of moving rice is still..."
"This is acceptable. He then asked a monk, "How much rice is there on the great bridge? The monk replied, "Seventy *shí*.

The Master picked up his staff and said, "The seventy *shí* of rice are all at once upon the tip of this staff. If you can carry it here, that will do; if you cannot carry it, I will starve you to death.
[A student] spoke in his stead: "One must not treat this as a minor matter. One day he said, "There is something to be said: the jackal."
[The Master] said, "The jackal's cry. There is nothing to be said. This lion’s roar—my being thus is the jackal's cry. What is the lion’s roar?
[The disciple] replied, "Nine times nine is eighty-one. The Master sometimes said, "These two words are buried; do not speak them.
[The disciple] replied, "I deeply appreciate the Master’s compassion. He also said, "It was established because of me. The Master sometimes said, "When Sudhana entered..."
"This is the gate. How can you speak so as to go out? [The Master] provided the answer: "In the morning I traveled to Mount Luofu. The Master sometimes said:

"You may bite this sesame cake horizontally or vertically as you please, but without leaving this place, bring me a single phrase. [The Master] provided the answer: "Today’s noodles are fresh. One day he said:
"There shall be reward and there shall be punishment; bring me a single phrase. [The Master] provided the answer: "When it is cheap, it is precious. Heaven..."
A clear sun rises. Someone said, "The Master Longqian drowned; from where did he arise? What is the phrase for 'not remaining alive'?
He answered on his behalf: "What difficulty is there in discerning it? One day, he asked, "How do you speak a single phrase that strikes with resonance?

He answered on his behalf: "When a donkey gives birth, it is a mule; when a horse gives birth, it is a hinny. Someone else asked, "How can one attain the Way so that it is beyond deliberation? He answered on his behalf: [Silence].

"Next year there will be new branches again; the spring wind, causing such turmoil, will never cease. One day he said, "If you can discern the intimate and the remote, why are you still driven by the intimate and the remote?
He provided the following substitute response: "Who placed them there? Or he said: "The ancients said..."
If you understand, it is for immediate use on the road; if you do not understand, it is merely the circulation of conventional truth (*saṃvṛti*).

Bring forth a complete and perfect line of the Way. [The Master] spoke in his stead: "For one coin, two pieces; for two coins, three pieces. One day, he said: "Bring forth a single line. [The Master] spoke in his stead:
The upper part of the character *pǐ* (to match) is insufficient. At the end of summer, he questioned a monk: "At the beginning of autumn, at the end of summer, do not touch upon the ordinary;
bring me a phrase. He provided the substitute reply: "The third and the eleventh; the middle ninth and the lower seventh. The Master asked a monk:

"When the whole body is water, who drinks it? He provided the substitute reply: "It has already served as a cause for laughter for you, O Master. One day he said: "If we do not meet for three days, [it will be]..."
"You may look upon it as it was before. How so? [The Master] provided the response: "A thousand.

*Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies*, Scroll Eighteen.
The Extensive Record of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen, Volume II,
compiled and verified by the master’s disciple Mingshi, who was granted the purple robe by the Emperor,
Shoujian.
The Master saw a newly arrived monk and said, "Xuefeng Zen Master said, 'Open up the road; Bodhidharma is coming. I ask you, what will you do?

The monk said, "I strike the Master’s nostrils. The Master said, "The Earth Deity loses his temper and gives a blow to Mount Sumeru, leaping up to the Brahma Heaven and smashing through Indra’s nostrils. Why did you [not do so] back then?"
[The Master] hid himself within his own country. The monk said, "Master, do not deceive people. The Master said, "What would you do if you bumped into this old monk’s nostrils?
[The monk] was speechless. The Master said, "I knew you were merely one who parrots the words of others.
To represent the point where [the monk] was speechless, [the Master] said, "The Master only fears that I am not sincere," and further said, "Luo lu li. He then asked the newly arrived [monk]: "You—"
"Where are you from? The monk said, "A man from Silla. The Master said, "What did you bring across the sea?
The monk said, "A grass bandit has been utterly defeated. The Master said, "Why are you in my hands? The monk said, "Exactly so. The Master said, "A leaping frog!"
[The monk] was speechless. [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying: "I always find this opportunity. He also said: "Let him leap about as he pleases. He asked a newly arrived monk:
"You borrowed two hundred coins from me at Mount Nanyue; why have you not returned them? [The monk] was speechless.

[The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying: "Today I went out small and met with great fortune. He also said: "Today I did not meet with good fortune. He asked a monk: "When both mind and dharmas are forgotten together, what rank is that?"
[The Master] sat. A monk said, "The second seat. The Master asked, "What is the first seat? The monk said, "I do not dare to fall short of the Master's expectations.
The Master did not approve. He spoke on his behalf, saying, "Buying rice in Shaozhou. [The Master] asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, [he replied].
[The Master] picked up some tea leaves. The Master said, "The person picks the tea; the tea picks the person. [The monk] was unable to respond.
[Dongshan] spoke on his behalf, saying, "The Master has already spoken; I cannot speak further. The Master asked a monk, "Are you the one in charge of the construction?

He replied, "Yes. The Master said, "The entire universe is this house. Who is the master of the house? [The monk] was unable to respond. The Master said, "You ask, and I will tell you. The monk asked.
[The Master] asked. [The monk] said, "He has passed away. [To provide a substitute for the previous remark: "How many people have you deceived?

The Master asked a monk, "Are you one who has left home in Hunan? The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Do you recognize the Vajra-purusha beneath the triple gate? The monk said, "It would be impossible to recognize him further.
The Master said, "You have emerged from a wild fox den. [The monk] was speechless. [To provide a substitute: "If he did not emerge," [he would be a true Vajra-purusha].
At the beginning of the dialogue, it was said: "He is merely a clay figure. It was further said: "What use is there in recognizing this clay figure? And again:
"Please consider that I have newly entered the assembly. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from paying respects at the pagoda."
The Master said, "What did the Patriarch say? The monk said, "What did you say, Master? The Master said, "I thought you were a clever fellow.
[The monk] was speechless. [The Master] provided a substitute response: "It is simply because you are within the realm of benevolence and righteousness.

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk held up his patched robe (*kasāya*). The Master said, "I am asking you where you have come from. The monk said, "Why does the Master not..."

[The Master] received the monk’s words and struck him. [Another] provides a substitute for [the Master’s action], saying: "How fortunate! [Another] provides a substitute for the previous remark, saying:

"Has the Master not yet finished? A monk takes his leave of the Master. The Master says: "Where are you going to take your leave? The monk says: "Yes. The Master says: "The river ahead is difficult to cross.
The monk says: "Everything depends on the occasion. The Master says: "Svāhā. [Another] provides a substitute for the previous remark, saying: "One must not depart without propriety when setting out."
[This is] also [the case]. A later commentary says: "Too coarse-minded. It also says: "Lately, the world has not been good.
The Master asked a monk, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The monk said, "The Master ought to know. The Master said, "I indeed know.

The monk said, "But tell me, where did I spend the summer? The Master said, "A rat poking its head out of a hole. [The monk] was speechless. [An alternate response] says: "He hit the mark. [This is] an alternative for the preceding [case].
The saying goes: he then went out. The monk took his leave of the master. The master said, "Do not let it come to ruin. The monk said, "Master, whatever you have to ask, just ask.

The master said, "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated. [The monk] was speechless. [A master] provided a substitute response, saying: "Defeated! He further provided a substitute for the previous words, saying: [the same].
"Not a little. After the communal labor (*pǔqǐng*) of carrying rice was finished, during the sitting period, he said:
"Lately you have been quite incompetent; it is better to quickly cast off this one bushel of rice than to carry it about. A monk asked, "Where would the Master cast it off? The Master said, "Ha!

As the monk prepared to ask again, the Master said, "It is already nailed down. [The Master] provided a substitute [answer], saying: "Indeed so. He further substituted for the previous remark, saying: "Today we were carrying rice."
*困* (Kùn). It is also said: "Still too near. The Master asked a monk, "Do you see the lantern? The monk said, "I cannot see it anymore. The Master said, "A monkey is tied to a pillar.
[Another] provides a substitute [answer]: "I deeply appreciate the Master’s profound intention regarding the Buddha-dharma. [Another] provides a substitute for the previous remark:
"A good thing is not as good as having none at all. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "Chadu. The Master said, "Trampling it to pieces."
“How many straw sandals? [The monk] had no reply. [The Master] provided a substitute answer: “A pity for the straw sandals. He also said:

“It was not in vain that you wore them out. Seeing the rice steward, the Master asked: “Are you the rice steward? “He is,” [the steward] replied. The Master asked: “How many grains of rice are in each kernel? How many kernels are in each grain of rice?
[The steward] had no reply. [The Master] provided a substitute answer: “I have been watching the stars and gazing at the moon. He also said: “Within the gate of merit and benefit.”
"It cannot be helped that this must be done. During a meal, the Master asked a monk, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "From Huainan. He then asked another monk, "Where are you from?

The monk replied, "From Jingzhao. The Master picked up a steamed bun and said, "I have nothing to offer you who are from Huainan, nor do I have anything to offer you who are from Jingzhao. The two monks were speechless. The Master—
He then picked up a steamed cake, turned it over, and said, "I cherish you—what do you say to that? Again, there was no reply.
[The Master] provided the answer on his behalf, saying, "It is not that the Master cherishes them. He provided the answer on behalf of the previous statement, saying, "Offer them equally to all.
He also said, "Keep some to offer to the Master. He asked a monk, "What sutra are you reading? The monk replied, "Someone has already asked about this. The Master said, "Why are you under my feet?"
[The Master] descended. The monk said, "Exactly so. The Master said, "I humbly pray that you may enjoy [the offerings]. On behalf [of the monk], he said, "Heaven! Heaven!
He also said, "I thought there was none in Shaoyou. He asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying? The monk said, "The *Prajñāpradīpa-śāstra* (Treatise on the Lamp of Wisdom).
The Master said, "Who is preaching the Buddha-dharma upon the Vajra Seat in India? The monk said, "The Master ought to know. The Master said, "Have you seen it in a dream?"

[The Master] remained silent. [A monk] spoke on his behalf, saying: "Not only I. He further spoke on behalf of the previous statement, saying: "Leaping out of the dead shrimp. He also said: "I thought there was none in the Western Heaven.
He also said: "Falling. Once, during a meal, he asked a monk: "How many steamed buns have you eaten? The monk said: [He remained silent].
[The Master] ate four mouthfuls. The Master said, "Why is there only a single hair in your nostrils? [The monk] was speechless. The Master said, "You are speaking empty falsehoods.
[The Master] spoke on behalf of the previous [monk], saying: "One must be careful at the beginning, and one must also guard the end.

Once, during a meal, he asked a monk, "If the soup is received within the rice, and the rice is received within the soup, where does the fault lie? If you can speak, there is something else [to be understood]."
[The Master] deliberated; [the monk] had no reply. [The Master] spoke on his behalf: "Fine soup, fine rice. He also said: "One must not say that the Master is in a den of frogs.

Once, when a monk was taking leave, the Master descended from his seat, took the monk’s hand, and said: "How much money does it cost? [The monk] had no reply. The Master said: "Ask me. The monk then asked. The Master said:
"It is not worth even half a coin. [The Master] spoke on his behalf: "What token of parting do you have?"
When he was being sent off on his journey, [the Master] said: "As you are about to depart, because I saw the characters for 'Dragon Treasury' (Lóngzàng), I asked a monk:

'What does the Dragon Treasury produce? He had no reply. The Master said: "You ask, and I will tell you. The monk then asked. The Master said: "It produces a dead shrimp. [The Master] provided an alternative answer:
"The stench of excrement," or alternatively, "Steamed buns and flat cakes. Once, while they were transporting rice, the Master used his staff...
The Master struck a monk once with his staff and said, "This monk will not go to carry rice, is that not so? The monk said, "I have already finished carrying the rice into the granary.
The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment the fact that you have finished carrying the rice into the granary—who is it that eats the rice? The monk then went out.
The Master said, "You liar who speaks empty falsehoods! He then took up another monk and asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by the master?"
The Master said, "The family way has attained liberation from empty falsehood. A substitute said, "Why do you suppress the noble to make them base?
Another said, "Because of one matter, one wisdom grows. A substitute remained silent and said, "For what reason does the Master say this?
While at the front of the Sangha hall, the Master asked a monk, "What material is this bell made of? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "You ask me. The monk then—
Question: The Master said, "A patch-robed monk does it. [The attendant] merely struck the bell once and said, "Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
He further said, "In front of the Sangha Hall. The Master asked a monk in charge of construction, "Where have you come from?
The monk said, "I have come from the mountain cutting wood. The Master said, "Can you cut it so that it fits the frame? The monk said, "If the Master will let me pass, I shall say. The Master—
[The Master] said, "I let you pass. What do you say? The monk then bowed, and the Master struck him. [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying, "I am also like this.
He also said, "It is a pity that such success is not preserved. He also said, "Strike! He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, [blank].
[The Master] said, "Carry firewood here. The master asked, "The rector is beating the drum; he is not carrying firewood. What do you say? [The monk] had no reply.

[The Master] provided a substitute response, saying: "A mistaken understanding. He spoke again, saying: "It is a pity to labor over carrying firewood. He spoke again, saying: "The Master occupies the position of authority, while I am but a student seeking instruction.
He spoke again, saying: "I have just performed a small amount of labor. The master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From below the mountain. The master...
[The Master] asked, "How many people are there? The monk said, "Four. The Master held up his staff and said, "They are all right here. [The monk] was speechless.
[The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is simply a matter of restraining oneself. He added, "How many people have you misled?
He asked another monk, "How many sesame cakes did you eat? He said, "Three. The Master picked up a sesame cake and said, "Which one is this? [The monk] was speechless. The Master said, "..."
“You ask me. A monk then asked. The Master said, “It does not come forth. [Another] provided this in his stead: “He who deceives his enemy perishes.

The Master asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk said, “From Hunan. The Master said, “Where did you spend the summer retreat? The monk said, “In Hunan. The Master said, “Where is Kaifeng Temple?

The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Go to the hall for instruction. [The monk] had no reply. [Another] provided this in his stead: “Yes. [Another] provided this at the beginning: “Yes.”
A saying goes: "The Master asks from afar; the student answers from nearby. It is also said: "Only just now arrived.

During a meal, the Master asked a monk, "Tell me, how much rice is there in this bowl? The monk had no reply. [The Master] provided the answer for him, saying: "Wild! He also said: "Eat until full and then stop.
He also said: "One ladle, two ladles. Seeing a monk during a meal, the Master asked: "Set aside the bowl, spoon, and chopsticks, and then take hold..."
[The Master] said, "Bring me some dumplings. [The monk] had no reply. [Dongshan] spoke on his behalf, saying, "Good soup, good rice," and then added, "Enough.
He asked a monk, "What sutra are you reading? The monk held up the sutra. The Master said, "Showing one's head from within a ghost cave. The monk said, "What do you see, Master?"

The Master said, "The stolen goods are still here; there is no defense. [The Master] spoke on behalf [of the monk], saying, "Within the Way of benevolence and righteousness, it is not fitting to act in this manner. He questioned a monk.
"What sutra are you reading? The monk said, "The Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra. The Master said, "Does the sutra say that the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure?
The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Why then has your eye passed through the pomegranate tree?
The monk said, "Where is the ancients? The Master said, "The ancients knew; it is you who do not know. [The monk] was speechless. [The Master] provided this on his behalf: "There are many people."

[The monk] did not recognize the situation. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the mountain ranges. The Master said, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The monk said, "At Zhaoqing.
The Master said, "What words or phrases were spoken at Zhaoqing? The monk stepped forward and responded with an assent. The Master said, "One is not accomplished;

two is not so. [The monk] was speechless. The Master said, "It is indeed so. [Another teacher] spoke on his behalf: "Simply maintain this. Later, while serving a meal, the Master picked up [a utensil].
As the leftovers were being served, the Master said to a monk, "I intended to give you half, but then I did not. The monk asked, "Why did you not give it?
The Master said, "Because you went out to gather firewood. [Another] spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is not even bad to give food to someone.
He also said, "Thank you for the Master’s offering. He also said, "Master, why do you act so pointlessly? Later, while drinking tea, the Master said:
"What is the flavor of tea? The monk said, "Please, Master, examine it for yourself. The Master said, "A bottomless bowl is an ordinary matter;
a face without a nose makes people laugh to death. [The monk] was speechless. The Master said, "A fellow who eats his fill by following the crowd.

[The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying, "Just maintain this. He also spoke on his behalf, pouring the tea away immediately. He also said, "Wait a moment; let me prepare a bowl of tea first. The Master asked.

The Master asked, "Monk, where did you spend the summer retreat? The monk said, "The Master ought to know. The Master said, "I do indeed know. The monk said, "Then tell me, where did I spend the summer retreat?
The Master said, "It does not require a single note. [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying, "It does not even require that much. He then questioned another monk.
“What sutra are you reading? The monk assented. The Master said, “Why have you lost it?

The monk said, “Where have I lost it? The Master said, “Take yourself out. [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying, “We were traveling together. He also said, “It is not fitting for a great man like the Abbot to do this himself.
He asked a monk, “I do not want a whole round bun; bring me one that is half-broken. The monk assented.
"Yes. The Master said, "This is a complete whole. Bring it here. [The monk] offered a substitute response: "Whether one gives a feast or not, there shall be no obstruction in the future.
He also said, "The merit cultivated by the donor... The Master asked a newly arrived monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk said, "Chenzhou. The Master said, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The monk said, "Fenjin in Jingnan. The Master said, "How much did you receive? The monk...
[The Master] extended both hands. The Master said, "This is rubble. The monk asked, "Does the Master have anything else? The Master said, "A dry piece of dung—bite it as you please.
[The Master] spoke on behalf [of the monk], saying, "If one does not speak of flaws, how can jade be turned?

He asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying? The monk said, "The *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*. The Master said, "Why have you fallen into meaninglessness? The monk asked, "Where have I fallen into meaninglessness?"

The Master said, "Go out, having already received [the teaching]. [Another] spoke on his behalf: "I regret not having struck first. He asked a monk, "Have you ever lectured on the *Śata-dharma-śāstra*?
The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Why do you speak such empty falsehoods? [Another] spoke on his behalf: "An event does not arise in isolation."

Furthermore, it is said: "Attachment. This refers to when, during the chanting of the robes for a deceased monk, he asked a monk: "Now that we are chanting the robes, does the deceased monk still remain here?
[The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying: "To trouble the great assembly; he could not wait and has already struck the final gong and departed. He then asked the monk: [What would you say?]
“Where have you come from? The monk said, “I have come carrying firewood. The Master said, “How much did you carry? Turn it once over night. The monk said, “Twenty turns.
The Master said, “Why have you knocked out your front tooth? The monk was speechless. The Master then struck him and said:
The class of those who merely mimic speech says in response: "I know well, Master, your Dharma-body and mind. He then offers this in place of the previous words:
"Carrying firewood is already a hardship enough. He asks a monk: "What sutra are you reading? The monk instead points to a monk standing nearby and says:
"Master, why do you not answer me directly? The Master says: "Why does the pillar retreat three thousand miles? Sanshan says: "Is it not so?"

[The monk] was doing something else. The Master said, "This is the way of those who merely parrot words. [A disciple] spoke on his behalf, saying, "It would have been better not to recognize his status," and then, speaking on his behalf again, he said, "Take care" and departed.
Furthermore, it is said that there were not just one or two who did so. When the Master was in the Western Capital, he asked a monk, "Where are you from?"
The monk said, “A man from Khotan. The Master asked, “Have you reached the Western Heaven? The monk said, “I have.

The Master picked up his staff and said, “I do not ask you about the mechanism that flashes like lightning; have you reached this very place? The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master laughed heartily.

[If I were] speaking on his behalf, I would say: “I deeply appreciate the Master condescending from his high station to meet me at my low level. And I would further say: “I thought there was none such in this land.”
Furthermore, it is said: Master Xun asked a newly arrived monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Mount Nanyue.
The Master said, "Why did Guanyin go into Lake Dongting? The monk said, "I, a beginner, do not understand. The Master said, "Go to the hall for practice."
A substitute says: "Yes. Another says: "How many people have been deluded and attached? Another says: "The Master asks about Guanyin;
I respond for Maitreya. During a meal, the Master asked a monk: "I do not ask you about carrying firewood at midnight, but what do you use to eat your rice at mealtime?
The monk picked up his bowl, and the Master struck it down with his staff. The monk was speechless. A substitute says: "Lead [him on]."
Again he said, "Two pieces of skin. Again he said, "The spoon, the chopsticks, the alms bowl, the hand towel, and the sitting mat.
While drinking tea, he asked a monk, "Are you the firewood-gatherer? The monk replied, "Yes. The Master said, "I shall recommend another cup of tea for you. [A student] offered this in his stead:
"Having endured all hardships," or "Your efforts have not been in vain," or "Master, please take note of my hardships. He then asked a monk, "You..."
"Is this a garden? The monk said, "Yes. The Master asked, "Why does the radish not take root? No one could answer.

[The Master] spoke on their behalf, saying, "There is too much rainwater," and further said, "It does not know how to bring joy to others. He then asked a monk, "What kind of person are you? The monk said—

The Guest Master asked, "When a guest arrives, with what will you receive and attend to them? The monk said, "According to the family's abundance or scarcity. The Master said, "This is but a clay bowl and bamboo chopsticks. When a guest arrives, with what will you receive and attend to them? The monk said, "Thank you for the Master’s compassion. The Master said:

The Guest Master asked, "When a guest arrives, with what will you receive and attend to them? The monk said, "According to the family's abundance or scarcity. The Master said, "This is but a clay bowl and bamboo chopsticks. When a guest arrives, with what will you receive and attend to them? The monk said, "Thank you for the Master’s compassion. The Master said:

"A shrimp cannot leap out of its basket. [The monk] said, "There is no match for it. The Master said, "Ask me. The monk then asked, "With what will you receive him? The Master struck him. [Commentary:
He should have struck him at the very moment of the initial question. It is also said: "A plate of rice and two bowls of tea. And it is also said: "Greedy for gazing at the moon in the sky.
The Master asked a monk, "Where did you go forth [into the monastic life]? The monk said, "I am a descendant of Zhaozhou. The Master said, "Master..."

"Where is the old man from? [The Master] replied in his stead: "An old monk who eats his rice. Once, the Master saw an inscription on a beam at a water mill that read, "To endure forever as something imperishable.
Later, the beam was broken. The Master asked a monk, "Since it was said to endure forever as something imperishable, why was it pushed away by the water?
No one could answer. [The Master] replied in his stead: "Without one matter, it is difficult to gain one bit of wisdom. He also said: "Yao and Shun."
The Master asked a monk, "How do you express it so as not to be defiled by mud and water?

[The monk] replied, "The drum beats on South Mountain; the dance is performed on North Mountain. Once, during a meal, the Master asked a monk, "Is there any talk here that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs?
The monk said, "There is. The Master said, "Where has it gone? [The monk] was speechless. [The Master] provided the following response: "In the kingdom of Silla."
It is also said: The Master feared that the monk would not speak truthfully, so he spoke on his behalf, saying, "When eating a meal, it is improper to speak in such a manner.
The Master asked the firewood-keeper, "Why did you snap the large beam with your saw? The monk said, "I did not. The Master said, "If you did not, then let it rest.
[The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying, "Both sides," or "On level ground," or "I know that the Master is a head official and undergoes great hardship."
“Suffering. The Master asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk said, “From Mount Nanyue. The Master said, “In this place, I never engage in idle entanglements with people.
Come closer. The monk then stepped forward. The Master said, “Go! [Another] spoke on his behalf, saying, “Please consider that this student has traveled far.
He also said, “Today there is no prize. Because a monk was standing before the Master, [the Master] struck him once with his staff. His...
The monk turned his head. The Master spread out his hands and said, "Bring me the money. The monk had no reply. [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying:

"If you had not turned your head, how would he have known what was to come? He also said: "Just spit right in his face! Once, because the Master entered the kitchen, he asked the vegetable steward, "How many eggplants are in the pot?
The steward had no reply. The Master said, "You ask me, and I will tell you. The monk then asked. The Master said, "It cannot be digested. [The Master] spoke on his behalf.

He said, "One bucket. He then provided a supplementary remark, saying, "Yes. Because they had returned from the communal labor (fúqǐng) at the bottom of the triple-gate, he asked a monk, "When you are exhausted, what face do you show?
The monk said, "The Master ought to know. The Master said, "I simply do not know. The monk then asked, "When one is exhausted, what face does one show?
The Master picked up his staff and said, "When meeting the long, it is long; when meeting the short, it is short. The monk said, [silently].
[The monk] did not understand why the Master spoke in such a way. The Master said, "I also know you are intimate [with me]," but [the monk] had no reply.

[The Master] provided a substitute answer, saying, "How could you know? He further provided a substitute for the previous remark, saying, "Old and young, yellow and white. The Master asked the head cook, "The Buddha is a manifestation of a thousand billion bodies;
when you prepare rice every day, how many Śākyamuni Buddhas are there in each ladleful? [The cook] had no reply. [The Master] provided a substitute answer.
[The Master] said, "One monk, one sheng of rice. He also said, "Today's midday meal is rather meager.

He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From the pagoda at Nanhua. The Master said, "What words or phrases did the Patriarch have? The monk said, "There were some. The Master said, "..."
He must not misquote [the Master]. The monk said, "I request the Master to lead us through the meaning. The Master said, "I say that one is not so, and two are not right.

[The Master] spoke on behalf [of the monk], saying, "The Master is being far too strict in his instructions. He asked the miller, "When a person beats the sieve, the sieve beats the person. There was no response.

[The Master] spoke on behalf [of the miller], saying, "Lately I have been eating a lot of noodles. He also said, "When a guest comes, you must see them; when a thief comes, you must beat him. He questioned a monk.
"Where have you come from? The monk said, "From the Nanhua Pagoda. The Master said, "Do you see the Patriarch? The monk said, "What is the use of seeing him?
The Master said, "And where would you go, and what would you do there? The monk said, "What fault is there in that?
The Master said, "If going is without fault, what fault is there in seeing? [The monk] was speechless. [The Master] spoke on his behalf: "If it were not thus..."
"How can one know compassion? [The Master] asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "I have come for the midday meal. The Master said, "Bring me the offering money."
The monk said, "What is it that you, Master, lack? The Master said, "And what is it that you lack? The monk said, "I lack nothing.
The Master said, "If you lack nothing, why did you go to the meal? The monk was speechless. [The Master] provided this for him: "What harm is there?"

It is also said: "Chen-kuai" (The Block-chasing). The Master asked a monk, "Are you a person from the north? The monk replied, "Yes. The Master gave him a blow with his fist, and the monk was speechless.
The Master said, "Ask me. The monk then asked, "Where are you from, Preceptor? The Master struck him once more. [The monk] had no reply. [This was] to strike in place of the previous question;
furthermore, it was to provide an answer for the latter by saying: "Within the Way of benevolence and righteousness. Later, a monk came to see the Master after having eaten his porridge.
The Master said, "Have you finished eating your porridge yet? The monk said, "I have finished. The Master said, "Did you bite into the pillar?"
The monk said, “I’ve bitten it. The Master said, “Look! You’re being stubborn. [The monk] was speechless. [The Master] spoke on his behalf:

“I know the Master fears that people are not sincere. He spoke again on his behalf: “Stubborn toward whom? Because the Master opened the door, a monk entered immediately. The Master grabbed him by the chest and said, “What business do you have?
The monk said, “What business do I have? The Master gave him a slap. [The monk] was speechless. [The Master] spoke on his behalf: “Step back.”

When [the Master] advanced toward the person, he acted to preserve the etiquette between host and guest; on behalf of [the monk], he seized him by his dwelling place, saying: "Spit right in the face of this wild fox spirit!
He also spoke on his behalf, saying: "Because you, student, have established it. The Master pointed to a pillar and asked a monk from Dongjing, "In your hometown, is there also such a thing as this?
The monk said, "There is. The Master said, "What do you call it? The monk said, "I call it a pillar."
The Master said, "Even an old man from a village of three households understands how to speak like this. No one responded. [The Master] provided a substitute response: "A true practitioner.
When the Master saw a monk approaching, he raised his fist and made a gesture to strike. The monk stepped forward and made a gesture of receiving the blow. The Master gave him a slap.
