"Let it pass through Cai State as it will; those with nostrils shall discern it. Master Longmen struck the gavel and said:
"In this Dharma assembly, you dragons and elephants, you should contemplate the primary principle (*paramārtha*). The Master said:

"If one speaks of the primary principle, the twenty-eight patriarchs of India and the six patriarchs of the Tang land stand in the lee of the wind. The entire Tripitaka is ten thousand miles of white clouds. In Magadha..."
Vimalakīrti remained silent in his room; even when thousands of Buddhas appeared in the world, he was still lost in sleep and his drowsy chatter had not ceased.
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra had to straighten what was crooked. Thus it is said: "Even if you can realize it before words, you are still stuck in the shell and mired in the seal.
Even if you are thoroughly proficient within a single phrase, you cannot avoid wild views wherever you encounter things. If you hold fast to these boundaries, then speak!
"What Dharma hall has weeds a fathom deep? It is such that the paths of ordinary and sage are cut off; birds cannot fly across it, and there is no place for the monks of the world to draw breath.
Is there anyone among you who does not find this unsatisfactory? Come forth and meet me! At that time, a monk asked:
"The *udumbara* flower appears and the gate of expedient means opens. With the court officials present at the assembly, how do you proclaim the teaching? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
The Master said, "Today is fine weather. The student said, "The bright sun is in the sky; the clear breeze circles the earth. The Master said, "How much do you understand?
A question was asked: "What is the realm within humanity? The Master said, "Jeweled pavilions soar into the void as golden bells chime;
wild monkeys cry out from the crags where strange pines hide. The student asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "A straight nose and slanted eyes."

He said: "Is there anyone else who would like to ask a question? When there was no response, he continued: "Today, Shuangquan shall open a single thread of the Way through the gate of the second meaning to meet you all.
Let us work together with mud and water in one stroke, so that Śākyamuni and Maitreya may cause the earth to tremble and rain flowers to fall;
and let Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, and Mahāsthāmaprāpta each occupy their own station, assisting the Buddha to propagate his transformation. All...
Devote yourself to the fundamental task. As for possessing the capacity and competence to bear the burden, even those at Shuangquan could not avoid entering into a single portion [of this].

Together we speak of how the ladle-handle of the eastern house is long and that of the western house is short. Let it be as it may: spring grasses grow lush green, summer light blazes fiercely, autumn leaves fall from the trees, and winter ice becomes thin.
Why is this so? It is simply because I wish for all people to accord with the seasons and preserve themselves. (The words of thanks are not recorded. Thus it was said.
Holding up his staff, he said: "The ancients said, 'When raised, heaven turns and earth revolves;
when set down, the grass bows and the wind blows. But with me it is not so: when raised, there are holes here and there;
when set down, flowers are spread upon brocade. Tell me, is there still a way to benefit others? After a long silence, he said: "Next year there will be new branches again."
"The spring breeze continues to disturb us without ceasing.
The Master was at Baibyun when he received a written document; picking it up, he showed it to the assembly and said, "If you understand it merely in this way, you will bury the ancestral style;
the transgression would not be small. Fortunately, there is an established precedent; I ask the Rector to read it aloud before the assembly. [The Rector] read it.
[He] pasted [the seal] on. He bestowed the Dharma robe, lifted it up, and said: "Since it could not be lifted at the head of Mount Dayu, why is it here?
Tell me, which is it: this one or that one? Then he said: "Carrying his pitcher, he draws the cool water himself;
yet he puts on the kāṣāya to act as host. He then donned it. Pointing to the area before the Dharma seat, he said: "The Elephant King turns back."
"Like a lion’s stride. When I look at you, my eyebrows knit together. Although it is thus, when the matter reaches such a point, it is difficult to decline or yield.
'Where there is a path to ascend, even those of superior stature walk upon it. [Thus speaking,] he ascended the seat. A monk asked, 'Chan is not of thought or intention;
the Way transcends merit and achievement. How do you speak that single phrase for turning the body? The Master said, 'The assembly sees you.'"
The student said, “I knew the Master possessed such a sharp wit. The Master said, “Only you, Dharma-heir, could have done this.

The student said, “Today, however, I have acted with undue haste. The Master said, “Offered up, it does not become a dragon. A student asked, “Having fought long on the battlefield, your fame is established this day.
Without relying on merit or achievement, how would you speak? The Master said, “A long snake may still be tolerable; but how shall one face the crescent moon? The student [remained silent].
The student said, “A golden arrowhead, well-honed and seasoned through a hundred battles; an iron whip of great strength, regretting there is no enemy.
The Master said, “I know you are not made of golden teeth; how could you otherwise draw the bow to shoot Wei-chi? The student said, “Intimacy of the eye is not as good as intimacy of the hand.
The Master said, “The new elder has failed. The student said, “The mouth is the gate of calamity. The Master sighed and said, “The autumn wind blows briskly.”
Jade dew hangs like pearls; the waters are emerald and the mountains are azure. Crickets chirp and cicadas cry; the Gate of Perfect Penetration stands wide open.
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have passed right through the nostrils of you all, yet you yourselves have simply turned away from it face-to-face.
Again he said: "The Buddhas do not appear in the world; for forty-nine years they preached. I wonder what they preached? At Shaolin there was a wondrous secret.
The calamity extends to descendants; even now, they cannot be separated from it. What more need be said of "sublime secrets"?

If a person recognizes the Patriarchs and Buddhas, they transcend at that very spot. Setting aside for a moment whether one has transcended or not—tell me, where are the Patriarchs and Buddhas right now?
If no one can say, this mountain monk will not begrudge his eyebrows to give them to you all.
[The Master] brought it forth and struck the meditation seat once.
Small Assembly Lecture. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Fatness enters through the mouth. He then cited:

Deshan addressed the assembly, saying, "Tonight I will not answer questions; anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows. Many among the assembly have raised this case, yet few have understood it.
Such people are not few. But tell me, where do you see Deshan? If there is anyone among you who disregards life and limb, please come forward and speak.
If there is no such person, I, this mountain monk, shall go forth on behalf of the assembly to meet the old man Deshan.
Wait for Deshan’s way: "Tonight I will not answer questions; those who ask questions shall receive thirty blows. Simply say to him:
"I will ask no questions, nor shall I take these blows. Do you think this accords with that old man Deshan?
To reach such a state, one must be a true man indeed. Furthermore, Fayuan had been traveling as a wandering monk for over ten years, seeking instruction across the seas.
He investigated and met several venerable elders who claimed they had attained realization; yet when he arrived at the assembly of Fushan Yuanjian, he was truly unable to open his mouth.
Later, under Baoyun, he bit into a single iron sour dumpling and found that all flavors were complete within it.
But tell me, how would you express the phrase regarding this "dumpling"? He then said: "The cockscomb flower blooms in its lovely splendor."
Early Autumn. Who can dye the tips of the purple silk? Sometimes stirred by the wind, they lean against one another repeatedly, as if vying incessantly before the steps.

Entering the monastery, he ascends the hall. A monk asks: "Carrying your staff, you lead the assembly; the Patriarch’s command is being put into practice. You have sealed off the borders—Master [what do you do]? (The Master remains silent.)
“What do you think? The Master said, “The autumn wind blows over the Wei River; fallen leaves fill Chang’an.
The student said, “The four sides have no gates, yet the mountain peaks are exquisite; today the master has finally returned home. The Master said, “Where is your path?
The student said, “Why is it that we face each other yet do not recognize one another? The Master said, “I am glad you have arrived. He then raised the story of the Patriarch.
The Way of the Teacher: "I have come to this land to transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings. One flower opens into five petals; the fruition is naturally accomplished.
Master Bodhidharma came with his feet following his faith and spoke with his mouth following his faith. Yet the descendants of later generations mostly fall into calculating deliberation.
Do you wish to understand the place where flowers bloom and fruit ripens? Pear trees of Zhengzhou, jujubes of Qingzhou—among all things, nothing surpasses a good source.
Entering the hall, he raised [the following]: An ancient said, "If there were a person who, giving rise to the true, returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions would all..."

[All else] vanishes and perishes. But at Shuangquan it was not so. Suppose there were a person who, having developed true realization, returned to the source; then the voids of the ten directions would strike and bump against him.
When [Master] Xinghua ascended the hall, a monk asked, "What was it like before the Master left Sifan? The Master said, "He was in the house."
[The Master] sat cross-legged inside. The student asked, "What is it like after leaving? The Master said, "I will run you to death, O *śrāmaṇera*. He then cited a verse by Fayan:

"Mountains and waters are a fine dwelling for you; the city walls and moats are likewise discussed by me. In stillness, I hear the tolling of bells and the sounding of horns; at leisure, I face the gathering white clouds. Great Assembly:
Although Fayan does not grasp at the clouds or snatch at the mist, how can one deny that a pure breeze pervades the earth?
Today, let us try walking hand-in-hand with Fayan. 'In stillness, I hear the tolling of bells and the sounding of horns'—yet it is not merely sound. 'At leisure, I face the gathering white clouds'—"
Massed like clouds. Furthermore, it is not form; since it is neither sound nor form, how can one deliberate upon it? He then said: "Within the cave, no clouds—there is another heaven;
the peach blossoms are like brocade, the willows are like mist. The immortals do not know how to speak of winter or summer;
though the rocks crumble and the pines wither, they do not reckon the years."
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the heavens above there is no Maitreya; beneath the earth there is no Maitreya. Standing at the crossroads, one is called a thief by others.
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The four sides have no gates and the mountain peaks are magnificent; how can the seasons be distinguished within this?

The Master said: "The Lord of Spring must be meticulous; on every patch of ground, sprouts and buds break forth. The student said: "As spring passes and autumn comes, the affairs remain exactly as they were."
The Master said: "As soon as you have rolled the ball, you must immediately squeeze the vajra.
He then cited an ancient saying: "If I were to tell you, my tongue would fall out; if I do not tell you, my mouth would remain mute.
Tell me, is there still a way to benefit others? Si-men once intended to swallow you whole, but he was hindered by his own front teeth.
"Obstructed! I intended to spit it out for you, but because your throat is too narrow, tell me: is there still a way to benefit others?
He then said: "On all four sides, he has always been Liu Xiaohui."
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said: "The new year begins its reign; all things are renewed.

To manifest this throughout the entire great chiliocosm, it all comes down to but a single speck of dust. He then opened his hands and said, "Is this new? Is it old? Let anyone come forward and speak!
If there is no one, I shall for now propagate these worldly conventions. He then crossed his hands and said, "In the first month of spring, the cold still lingers. I humbly pray that..."
To the Head Seat, the Assembly, and all the administrative officers: may you all enjoy ten thousand blessings in your daily lives.
[The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks: "I do not ask about the cold colors of the thousand peaks; as for the matter of raindrops falling upon the cliff-flowers, what is it like? The Master says:
Today it is the same. The student said: "A single phrase transcends beyond the thousand sages; a thousand mountains lock off ten thousand layers of barriers.
The Master asked: "Where does a single drop fall? The student said: "Wrong. The Master said: "Wrong. The student said: "Wrong, wrong."
The Master then struck him and said: "Thousand peaks stand in emerald array; willows by the banks hang with golden tassels.
Woodcutters sing their songs; fishermen ply their oars. Flutes and lutes clamor the earth; birds warble in sweet tones.

Fair women with rosy cheeks and elegant young gentlemen—each and every one of these has, for all of you, manifested the highest vehicle and opened the Eye of the True Dharma. If you can realize it here, you shall attain the Golden Head."
There is no room for you to stand. If you do not understand, even if you eat porridge and rice, I shall allow you to be pierced through from head to toe.
He addressed the assembly before departing on patrol, saying: "Tomorrow, with a single horse and a solitary spear, I shall go forth to battle for the sake of the nation.
On the day I return victorious with my spear lowered, there will be songs and chants all along the road. Great Assembly, what is this one song of celebration? He then said: "Luo."
"Lao-li. La-lao-li. Is there anyone who can harmonize this? After a long silence, he said: "The embroidered mandarin ducks are finished;
you may look at them as you please, but do not hand over the golden needle to others."
A small *chán* (meditation) assembly on the night of the Cold Food Festival. A monk asked: "The masses have long been parched with thirst;
having braved the rain to ascend this mountain, we pray the Master will provide the expedient means for the upward-moving pivot. The Master said: "I cannot help but enter the mountains once more.
The student said: "In that case, one must tread firmly at every step. The Master said: "Returning empty-handed. The student said: "If it were that side, would it still be appropriate?"
The Master said, "Rarely does one encounter a true connoisseur. The student said, "I thank the Master for providing this testimony.

The Master said, "As for the matter of being a true connoisseur—how is it? The monk made a sweeping gesture with his hand. The Master said, "Once again, you have been blown by the wind into a different tune.

The student said, "Often I simply follow along with his words. The Master said, "Who else could it be? Then he continued: "White peaches and red blossoms; mountains green and waters blue; the clouds..."
Blocking the mouth of the cave: the moon is bright in the vast sky. If you can only realize it within this context, Fayen said, "The moon is bright; the secluded chamber is cold.

The stars diverge from their orbits around the North Star," at which point you must be like crumbling tiles and melting ice. National Teacher Shaor said, "At the summit of the Tongxuan Peak, it is not of the human world.
Outside the mind there is no dharma; before one's eyes are green mountains"—this too must be shattered into a hundred fragments. Why?
The entire universe and the great earth do not require even a single squeeze. Nevertheless, though this is so, matters are never one-sided.
For tonight, let us set this matter aside for a moment.
Entering the hall, he raised the following case: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Bodhidharma, "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths? Bodhidharma replied, "Vast emptiness."
However, there was no sage. The Emperor said, "Who is it that stands before me? Huineng replied, "I do not know.
Furthermore, a monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, "Who can attain the essential meaning of Huangmei? The Patriarch said, "One who understands the Buddha-dharma can attain it.
The monk said, "Can you yourself, Master, attain it? The Patriarch said, "I cannot. The monk asked, "Why is it that you cannot? The Patriarch said, "I do not understand the Buddha."
[The Master] said: "How great, how great is the Patriarch! When questioned, he was immediately ignorant and unable to comprehend.
Why, then, have his descendants spread everywhere? He then said: "One person may pass on a falsehood, but ten thousand people pass on a reality."
Small Assembly (Xiaocan). A monk asked, "A donor has traveled a long distance to your chamber; please grant the Master a single phrase to benefit people.
The Master said, "I shall teach all people in the world to become Buddhas. The monk said, "A traveler from within the vast dust has not come to the mountains in vain.
The Master said, "There are still sentient beings remaining in between. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "Now tell me, is this a Buddha or a sentient being?"
The student said, "The eyes on all four sides are difficult to deceive. The Master said, "Where did you see those four sides?
The monk brushed his sleeves and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "A true adept. He then continued: "Those who can speak with their mouths full do not know that there is something;
those who know that there is something cannot speak. Now tell me, where does the fault lie? When a mountain nine fathoms high is about to be completed, do not spare the final basket of earth."
The soil of the basket-mound ascends the hall.
[The Master] raises [the case]: Yunmen gave a teaching, saying, "The ancient Buddha intersecting with the pillar—what rank of capacity is this?
He spoke on his own behalf, saying, "Clouds rise from the southern mountain; rain falls on the northern mountain. The Master said, "How great indeed was the Great Master Yunmen! Yuan...
"Come here, you little coward! [He] said, "The ancient Buddha intersecting with the pillar—this is the fourth function.
After a long silence, he added, "To speak such words is to have a face three inches thick; your utterance is insolent. You should be struck with Linji’s staff."
"Three blows a day—what kind of person can bring himself to strike? Though his transgressions may fill the heavens, he is now universally released by a new amnesty.

On the occasion of the opening of the summer retreat, the Master ascended the hall. A monk asked: "In the Five Regions, the summer retreat is established and the 'wax man' is entrusted with the task; I wonder, how does Shuangquan handle this?"

Addressing the assembly, the Master said: "My feet do not touch the ground. He then continued, "Since there is nothing with which to make offerings to the great assembly during this summer retreat, I shall host a private banquet to attend to you all.
Thereupon, he raised his hand and said: "La-lo-zhao, la-lo-yao, la-lo-song. Do not resent my lack of formality;
I humbly entreat you to take care of yourselves."
Ascending the hall, he said: "During the twenty-one days, he contemplated such matters. Śākyamuni the Old Man breached the city walls at midnight and went straight to the Snowy Mountains;
that was already no small leak. What more was there for him to contemplate? He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: For a long time, Yaoshan had not ascended the hall. The administrative official reported, saying, "The assembly has long been longing for the Master’s instructions.
Yaoshan said, "Beat the drum! Just as the assembly gathered, Yaoshan returned to his quarters. The official said, "The Master promised to preach the Dharma for the assembly;
why did you not utter a single word? Yaoshan replied, "For the sutras there are masters of the sutras; for the treatises there are masters of the treatises."
The Master said, "How can one blame this old monk? The Master continued, "Even so, though you may obstruct others with your own views, how can you deny that the thief has already revealed himself?
Do you all wish to recognize Yaoshan? He idly holds a scripture and leans against a pine tree, smiling as he asks, 'Where have you come from, guest?'"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Dongshan, “What is the eye of a good spiritual friend? Dongshan replied, “A paper wick without oil.
The Master said, “The old fellow Dongshan was not without [the eye]; he simply was too parsimonious.
If someone were to ask Simian, ‘What is the eye of a good spiritual friend? I would simply say to him, ‘Blind. Why? It is because I wish to be commensurate with the question. He then said, “Paper...”
Twisting it without oil is truly marvelous; no one knows that it cannot be grasped. Turning back, I recall the path I came by;
under the moon, I stride home with confident steps.
Ascending the hall, he raised [this topic]: "The teachings say: 'If one says that the Tathāgata has preached any Dharma, that is to slander the Buddha.
Yet from where did this great treasury of the teachings come? If one says there was no preaching, then what of the five thousand and forty-eight volumes—where would they have been disposed?
At this point, one must be a person of true caliber to grasp it. Do you understand? Do not slander the Four Directions!
Ascending the hall, he raised this case: A monk asked Touzi, “What is the Ten-Body Tamer? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there.
If someone were to ask Si-mian, “What is the Ten-Body Tamer? I, the old monk, would likewise descend from my meditation seat and stand there.
"Why do you merely imitate the cat? Wait until I have finished my calculations, and then I shall tell you.
He ascended the hall and said: "I cite the case where Yaoshan asked Shitou: 'I have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.

I have heard that in the South there is the direct pointing to the human mind, whereby one sees one's nature and becomes a Buddha. I truly have not yet clarified this; I beg the Master for instruction. Shitou..."
The Master said: "It is not permitted to say 'it is so. It is not permitted to say 'it is not so. It is not permitted to say 'it is both so and not so.
When I was among the assembly, I heard my brothers discussing that one must not say 'this very mind is Buddha,' nor must one say 'this very mind is not Buddha.
If you speak in such a manner, how dare you call yourself a Chan practitioner? Why? Because you do not yet realize."

The Old Man of Stone was both civil and martial, possessing a complete mastery of both strategy and tactics. If you wish to see his perspective from all four directions, you must also know it for yourselves:
you see only the surging waves, yet you do not see the Palace of the Sea Dragon.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time gaze from afar and pay homage; the six generations of patriarchs cannot open their mouths.
Today, I shall provisionally act as your guide. But tell me, what is this? One, two, three, four, five.
To boast of a cloth drum at the Gate of Thunder is to mock General Li; it is like shooting at a stone tiger in Lan-tian."
Ascending the hall, he said: "True Suchness, ordinary beings, and sages—all are but dream-like words. Buddhas and sentient beings are likewise merely figurative designations.
Then, if someone were to come forward and say, "Old man Panshan," you should simply say to them: "Were it not for the early blossoming of flowers along the purple road..."
"Who can catch the yellow oriole as it descends the willow branches? If you ask further, [I am] the old woman [Nü-ǔ + Kǒu] from all four directions. She says herself:
"Yes! Be alert!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The mid-winter is bitterly cold. I humbly wish that the Head Seat and the entire assembly enjoy ten thousand blessings in your health and daily life.
May both sides share in the same fortune. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a saying to present to you all; first of all, do not misrepresent it. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he said:
"Last night was the end of the year; this morning is the New Year’s Day. It is but an ordinary day, yet people in the world give rise to divergent views.
They fail to understand how to trace back to the root, but instead merely pursue the branches and tendrils. The new and the old are just as they are right now—examine this closely."
Look clearly! If you still try to deliberate upon it, it is like trying to drill a hole with a bellows from the Qin dynasty.
When the elders of the various monasteries entered the mountain, the Master ascended the hall and said: "Linji’s 'shouting upon entering the gate'—what kind of bowl-ringing sound is that?
Deshan’s 'striking upon entering the gate'—to bend the crooked and make it straight. Yunmen’s three phrases and Caodong’s five ranks..."
"Opening one's eyes is dreaming. Why is this so? "The talent of the Guoqing scholar is noble; the child of a wealthy family is pampered.

Upon reaching Longmen, he ascended the hall and said: "To have a tongue is to be clever; to have no mouth is not to be mute. Going out in seven ways and disappearing in eight ways—this is the refined elegance of a gentleman.
He then descended from his seat.
Upon arriving at Haihui, he ascended the hall and said: "The man of Baiyun Mountain within the Baiyun Mountains holds fast to his borders, leaving no seams or gaps.
No seams or gaps—how much is it worth? Is there anyone who knows its price? He then said: "One, two, three, four, five."
Arriving at Xinghua, he ascended the hall and said: "Worldly affairs are as tangled as hemp; the path to the Empty Gate grows ever more remote.
Among those guests beneath the green pines, how many have found their way home? Together we sing the *huqia* flute melody, unfolding the flowers of the five petals.
Fortunate to meet you fellow practitioners, let us ascend together the white ox-cart. Great assembly, the cart is here; where is the ox? [He then recited: "Fragrant grasses across the ford."
He searched for his head but could not find it; at night he returned as before to lodge among the reeds. [The Master] descended from his seat.
Elder Ganlu Zi grabbed the Master and said, "In the jurisdiction of Shuzhou, there has all along been a grass-robber. The Master said, "The Master must also be on guard."
As Ziyi was about to offer a comment, the Master suddenly pushed him aside.
He then ascended the hall and said, "The Patriarch said: 'Leaves fall and return to the root; when they come, they have no mouth. Although the Patriarch spoke thus, he still lacked enlightenment.
Having said this, he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Are the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "When a person is poor, their wisdom is short;
when a horse is thin, its hair is long. He then continued, "The Patriarch could not describe it; the Buddha-eye cannot see it.
With a compassionate heart on all four sides, I shall open a single thread for you. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring air is now cold and now warm; the spring clouds sometimes roll up and sometimes unfurl.
This has drawn forth the Old Man of Shaoyang, who releases a fish from within the eye of a needle. He then said: "Wrong!"
Xie Zhushi ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is it like when the King demands the *siddhārtha*? The Master said, "Seven apertures and eight cavities.
The student asked, "What is the King’s demand for the *siddhārtha*? The Master said, "The imperial carriage has not yet been arrayed, yet the commands have already been issued."
The student asked, "What is *saindhava*? The Master said, "The eyes twitch and the ears heat up. The monk bowed. The Master said, "A dot."
It is said: Mañjuśrī unfurls the sail, Samantabhadra grips the rudder, and Śrīvatsa and Avalokiteśvara join in the chorus.
Thus they win the right to sit in meditation amidst the clamor of the Double Spring. While sitting in meditation is certainly not a matter of doubt, tell me:
how do you sing the "Song of the Downward-Heading Boat"? *Lalalai, lalalai*—the vulgar air has not yet been cleared away!

Ascending the hall, he said: "Tonight is the fifteenth day of the first month; heaven and earth are one single expanse. The gate of Samantabhadra stands wide open, yet though we meet, we do not see each other.
He then asked: "In whom does the fault lie?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Silence! Silence! Silence! Unsurpassed Bodhi is attained from this. What a tragedy! He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he said:
"Just now I thought of a kōan, but I have already forgotten it. It seems my staff remembers it.
He then picked up the staff and said, "Even the staff has forgotten. He then struck the ground once with it.
He said: "In the same pit, there is no different soil.
*Tut!* He ascended the hall and raised this case: Jingqing asked Xuansha, "A student has newly entered the forest; I beg the Master to point out a path of entry for me."
Sha said, "Do you still hear the sound of the Yan River water? Qing said, "I hear it. Sha said, "Enter from here.

The Master said, "If you have truly attained entry, you may proceed as you please in all four directions and eight points of the compass. If it is not yet so, you must by no means depart from this place."
Xie Dian ascended the hall and said: "The small rope and the string of coins; the large rope and the well-rope—these are things urgently needed every day.

The bamboo sieve and the wooden ladle—though these are broken household items, they each have their proper place for use. Yet, whether one goes north, south, east, or west, not a drop of water can be sprinkled upon them."

On the Winter Solstice, he ascended the hall and said: "The youthful Son of Heaven performs his ritual obeisance at the suburban altar this day; the scholars of the forests and springs look on from afar and sing their hymns:
'Ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Thereupon, he descended from the seat.
A Taoist nun entered the mountains to pay her respects and requested that [the Master] ascend the hall. He said: "The Way that can be spoken of is not the eternal Way—truly laughable!
Chang’e spent one night embroidering mandarin ducks; she could take a golden needle and display its ingenuity, yet she failed to join the two old yellow plums."
How clumsy are these descendants! Now each one has their mouth gaping open. When asked about a tortoise, they call it a soft-shelled turtle.
Today, from all four directions, I shall settle this for you. How can this be cleared? Wretched friend, wretched friend! Do not stick out your tongue behind my back.
Next, from the *Tàipíng Yùlù* (Recorded Sayings of Tàipíng), compiled by the student Qingyuàn:

On the day the Master entered the monastery, a monk asked: "Having departed from Shuangquan and come to join the assembly of Chan practitioners, I pray that the Master will grant me a single phrase for entering the gate."
[The Master] raised [the topic]. The Master said, "I shall wait until each and every one has been scrutinized.
The student said, "If that is so, then people will stop going to Mount Qingliang from afar; they need only burn incense here to see the Master. The Master shouted, "You do not even grasp my words!
The student said, "Today I have personally met his face; this truly surpasses hearing his name. The Master said, "You are still prattling on. He asked, "What is 'Peace'?"

[The Master] said: "A multi-storied jeweled pagoda rises, piercing the heavens; ten thousand ancient pines surround the earth, cold. The student asked: "What is it like to be a person within this realm? The Master said:
"Holding a scripture in hand, leaning against a pine tree, he stands there smiling and asks: 'Where have you come from, traveler? The student asked:
"I have already received the Master’s instruction regarding the realm and the person. As for the matter of the supreme vehicle (*zongcheng*), what is it like? The Master said: "You must..."
"I believe the city walls below are near; indeed, the bells and chimes mingle with the pipes and songs.
A student asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Bare-chested and barefoot. The student asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "A general amnesty is not revoked.
The student asked, "What is the Sangha? The Master said, "Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat. He then said, "I am originally without a mind that seeks anything."
Seeking it, this treasure-store has now arrived spontaneously. Worldly treasures can transform poverty into wealth;
this one treasure can transform the ordinary into the holy. But tell me, right now, are you ordinary or holy? It is neither, for the Way of Great Peace is not either.
Why? "The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip; the sweet melon is sweet from stem to end."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Bodhidharma was groundless in facing the wall at Shaolin; the Second Patriarch cut off his arm and suffered a lifetime of indignity.
What kind of 'wood-honey' (nectar) is one seeking atop the Huangbo tree? Today, Taiping’s two eyes are as black as lacquer. As for Li Guang’s divine arrow—by whom was it struck?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the ten directions, the six generations of patriarchs, and all the good spiritual friends of the world—all share this very same tongue.
If you can recognize this tongue, only then will you understand the 'great empty falsehood' that declares: 'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are Buddha;
grasses, trees, thickets, and forests are Buddha. If you have not yet recognized this tongue, you will only achieve the small."
"You have escaped into empty talk to deceive yourself; there are great matters ahead tomorrow and the day after.
When Taiping speaks like this, is there any ground of reality in it? He replied, "There is. "What is the ground of reality? "Return to the hall and go for tea."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, "Little joy and much anger. The monk asked, "What is the host within the guest?
The Master said, "Relaying words and conveying messages. The monk asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said:
Zhong Kui’s Little Sister. A student asked, "What is the Lord among Lords? The Master said, "The moment a single word leaves the mouth, the embroidered mat upon the earth opens.
He then continued: "Lately at Taiping Monastery, monks gather and disperse in great numbers.
They practice the 'grandmother's Zen' and eat coarse rice. The administrators have lost their care, and the master lacks expedient means. Although it has no flavor..."
As for the flavor, swallow it slowly and steadily.
Master Xie Zhuang said while ascending the hall: "One does not stop until two; even where there is no elegance, one must be elegant.
If you wish to accomplish both public and private affairs, look well at the white ox in the open field."
Ascending the hall, he said: "This very thing reaches up to heaven and down to earth; the Wan River serves as its mouth, and Mount Wan serves as its nose.
Taiping steps back three paces to let you all breathe."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What was it like before Oxhead saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "A heavy burden atop the head. The monk asked, "And after he saw him? The Master said, "A blue cloth covering the front.

The monk asked, "Why did the hundred birds bring flowers to offer him before he had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Wealth and honor are what all people desire. The monk asked, "After he saw him..."
Later, why did the hundred birds not bring flowers to offer him? The Master said, "Poverty and low status are what people detest.
He then continued, "The twenty-eight patriarchs of India spoke thus; the Sixth Patriarch of the Tang land also spoke thus."
The old monks of the world all speak thus; only Taiping does not speak thus. Why? Because a few cannot withstand the many.
But tell me, what is the ultimate truth? One must know that even a sublime dance requires the beat of every hand; the three-platform melody must be hurried by everyone together.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Above is heaven; below is earth. North, south, east, and west remain as they were. Śākyamuni Buddha was merely playing with his own spirit;
Bodhidharma’s coming from the West was full of prohibitions and hesitations. Suddenly, if a man were to come forth and say, "Master, speak in a low voice," you should simply say to him:
"I only wish to throw a brick to draw out a jade."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Today, this mountain monk shall transform the mountains, rivers, and the great earth entirely into gold.
Sentient and insentient beings alike shall all be made to attain Buddhahood. Only then will I enter the peace and security of this community.
Why? Because contention is insufficient; yielding is more than enough."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Taiping does not understand Chan; he has been running outside all along. On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, he will end up with nothing but a mouth.
But tell me, which one is Taiping’s mouth? He then said himself: "I do not even recognize these two pieces of skin."
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: When Baoshou was working as a street monk, he saw two people quarreling.
One man struck the other with his fist and said, "How can you be so shameless? It was at this point that Baoshou attained entry.

If anyone here knows the place where it lands, they may be said to have settled both public and private affairs. Great assembly, listen to a verse; it is most wonderful, truly most wonderful. At this—
Knowing his nature and destiny, [Zhaozhou] struck him on the nose and gave him a punch.
At that moment, he struck him correctly. He ascended the hall and said: "A fellow from the turbid waters of the Great Peace; everything has been thoroughly experienced.
Thus for thirty years, there have been those who praised him. But tell me, what did they praise? A fine fellow from the turbid waters."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: "The teachings say: 'Even if the entire world were filled with those like Śāriputra, and they were to exhaust their thoughts to measure it together, they still could not know it.
Ordinarily, members of the monastic community give a high bow to Śākyamuni and do not prostrate to Maitreya. Is this understanding the Buddha’s wisdom? Or is it not?
There is indeed such a thing among the assembly, yet it is merely baring one's tusks and hiding one's claws during a time of Great Peace."
I have a point of view; I shall offer it to you all without sparing my eyebrows. When someone asks a question, I will answer immediately as the words come to me.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'? The Master said, "The autumn wind blows across the Wei River; fallen leaves fill Chang'an.
The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not the person'? The Master said, "Meeting people on the road."

"Half are monks. The student asked, "What is it like when both person and environment are not wrested away? The Master said, "A young woman rows a light boat; her singing voice follows the flowing water.
The student asked, "What is it like when both person and environment are wrested away? The Master said, "The high sky holds the moon while a thousand gates are closed;
the Great Way is empty of people as one walks alone. He then said, "For several days now, there has been continuous heavy rain."
Wherever it reaches, there is injury and harm. A single drop from the Cao Yuan source fills the human world. When a patch-robed monk takes a single sip, his nostrils reach the heavens.
But tell me, since the names are the same, why are the effects of injury and benefit so different?
Who knows that beyond the distant mist and waves, there is another way of thinking?
Ascending the hall, he said: "A single leaf falls, and the world turns autumnal; a single mote of dust rises, and the great earth is gathered in.

That it is gathered is not in doubt, but who is it that lays hands upon it? The immortal cassia in the moon is uprooted by the roots; the pearl-dragon at the bottom of the sea is pulled by its horns."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To take a handful of earth and turn it into gold is still easy; to turn gold back into earth is difficult indeed. To transform the mundane into the sacred is still easy;
to transform the sacred back into the mundane is most difficult. Why? Who would be willing to humble their dignity to conform to the lowly?
But tell me, how do you express that phrase which is neither mundane nor sacred? He then said: "One must not corrupt the sons of others' families."
The Nun.
Ascending the hall, she raised this case: When the Third Patriarch saw the Second Patriarch prostrating, he asked, "I request the Master to repent for my transgressions.

The Second Patriarch said, "Bring forth the transgression, and I will repent it for you. The Third Patriarch said, "I seek the transgression but cannot find it. The Second Patriarch said, "I have repented the transgression for you."
It was finished. He then composed a verse and presented it to the great assembly: "The unperforated flute and felt clappers— The five notes and six scales are all universally present.
People of the time do not recognize Huang Fanchuo; They laugh, saying, 'This fellow has ascended the jeweled throne.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "To hear shallowly and awaken deeply; to hear deeply and not awaken—how regrettable! How regrettable! Offering to the Buddha does not depend on the abundance of incense.
Ascending the hall again, he said: "Opening the eyes is day; closing the eyes is night. When the tongue is completely severed, who can speak of Prajñā? *Jin* (Gold).
The Ascetic of Form (Rūpa-dhūta) did not enter the monastic community.
He ascended the hall and said, citing Fengxue: "If one grain of dust is established, the state flourishes and the country prospers, yet the village elders frown.

If not even a single grain of dust is established, the state perishes and the country falls, yet the village elders sing for joy. It is not so with 'Great Peace' (Taiping). If one grain of dust is established, the Dharma..."
The grass before the hall is a fathom deep; not a single speck of dust is established. Why is it that flowers are spread upon brocade? It is not said: "Nine times nine is eighty-one;
when the poor man has finished his suffering, just as he intends to stretch out his legs to sleep, the mosquitoes, gadflies, and fleas come forth"?
Ascending the hall, [the Master] spoke on account of the snow. He cited a case: A monk asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still transgression?
Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru. The Master said: "Sometimes when I question a monk, he may point a finger, or take a step forward, or let out a shout, or brush his sleeves and depart.
Yet you, Upasaka, have not yet attained it. Why? Because in the Great Peace, one has never yet directed [this toward others]."
"During the third month, a fall of snow came upon you all. Now, suppose a man were to come forth and say, 'Old Monk, do not act so erratically!
It is not falling now either. Then he would extend his hand and say, 'Finished.'"

Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said: "It is in the mud. The student asked: "What is it like after it has emerged?
The Master said: "It is above the water. A monk asked: "What is it like when the prince has not yet ascended the throne?
The Master said: "Whenever he meets someone, he asks for directions. The student asked: "What is it like when he has just ascended the throne? The Master said: "The whole world is at peace."
Píng asked, "What is it like after ascending the nine-fifth throne? The Master said, "Who discusses good or bad?
He then added, "At the very end, one is most earnest; my house is fresh in every place. Within the great chiliocosm, one cannot avoid being among those who truly know.
But tell me, who is that person among them? Where the level marsh ends, there is green mountain; the traveler is even beyond the green mountain."
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Yunmen said, "On level ground there are countless dead people; those who can emerge from the thorn forest are true masters.
At that time, a monk said, "If that is so, then the first seat in the hall has something superior. Yunmen said:
"Sulu sulu. In the Great Peace, it is not so. On level ground, everyone is a man of stature;
those who can sit within a thicket of thorns are true masters. Why? It is said: "Ke! (The barrier).
Ascending the hall, he said: "Take the waters of the four great oceans to make a single inkstone; take Mount Sumeru to make a single writing brush.

If someone could write the five characters 'The Meaning of the Patriarch’s Coming from the West' in the midst of empty space, I, Taiping, would descend from my seat, spread out my sitting cloth, and prostrate myself before him as my teacher.
If it cannot be written, then the Buddha-dharma has no spiritual efficacy. "Is there anyone? Is there anyone? Having spoken thus, he descended.
The assembly disperses as the Master takes his seat. The Master calls out in a loud voice, "Attendant! Attendant! The attendant responds with an affirmative "Yes.
The Master says, "Gather up your sitting mat. He then asks the attendant, "Have you gathered up the sitting mat?
The attendant lifts up the sitting mat. The Master says, "I already knew you would act like this."

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, “How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said, “The great fool is not as good as the small fool. The student asked, “And after he appeared in the world?
The Master said, “The small fool is not as good as the great fool. He then said: “Entering a field of weeds, one does not discriminate; one simply picks up whatever grass comes to hand.
Not recognizing the elder brother’s wife, one finds out she is actually one’s own sister-in-law. Zhengzhou produces geese.”
Pears. In Qingzhou they produce large jujubes. Beneath the "Towel and Single Robe" [koan], every single one bites from the head down.
Entering the hall, he said: "Yesterday I went into the city and saw a stage of puppet plays. Unable to resist, I drew near to watch them.
Some appeared dignified and extraordinary; others appeared ugly and repulsive. They moved, walked, sat, and stood, in colors of blue, green, yellow, and red. One.
At first glance, it was clear. Upon examining it closely, it turned out there was someone behind a blue cloth curtain.
Unable to restrain my curiosity, I asked, "What is your honorable surname, Minister? He replied, "Old monk, let it be; why ask about your surname?
Monks, at that single phrase of his, I was left with no words to answer and no logic to defend myself. Is there anyone [who can respond]?
"Can you, mountain monk, speak for me? Yesterday you missed the mark there; today you have pulled up the roots here.
He ascended the hall and said, "With salt it is called salty; without salt it is called bland. When Taiping hears this, his mouth will be as flat as a eaves-board.
Then he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wondrous function of spiritual powers lacks nothing in the slightest degree. For those who have attained realization, why indulge in such tedious talk?
When the mud is deep, the Buddha is large; when the water rises, the boat floats high."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The single moon universally appears in all waters; the moons in all waters are subsumed within that one moon.
Truly, these words are so! It may be said that it cannot be sculpted nor painted. Last night at the third watch, it was as white as day.
Xie Dian ascended the hall and said: "Though it is easy to transform the raw into the cooked, it is increasingly difficult to harmonize the many mouths.
If one truly knows the flavor of the salty and the bland, hunger and satiety will naturally no longer interfere with one another."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Last night at the third watch, I dreamed that this staff taught me a piece of Chan.
It told me, 'Master, rise early tomorrow morning and ascend the hall to present it to the assembly. Yesterday was like adding flowers upon brocade;
today is treading on solid ground. Just look at today and tomorrow—what need is there to speak of the Patriarch's intent?"
Reflecting on this, I consider the Yellow-Faced Old Man’s claim that he bestowed a prediction at Vulture Peak to have been in vain.

Even if one were to borrow the nostrils of the great earth, mountains, and rivers to breathe out, it would not be as good as letting go of body and mind; then benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom will manifest spontaneously.
For the cremation of the deceased monk, he held up a torch and said: "The four elements—fire and wind—are mutually opposed. At such a time, follow conditions."
At his ease. On the following day, he again held up a torch for a monk and said, "Yesterday it was like this; today it is also like this.
Tell me, which is yesterday? Which is today? What does it matter whether they are right or wrong?
Look—what color is this fire?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the fifteenth day of the first month. I meet with you all: the tender wheat grows new sprouts, every grain shall become flour.
Whether it is offered or not, it relies entirely upon the fanning of the spring breeze."
Next, from the *Zhu Haihui Yulu* (Recorded Sayings of Master Zhu of the Sea Assembly), compiled by Jingchun.
On the day the Master entered the monastery and opened the hall for teaching, after the proclamations had been read, he said: "The official documents have all been read at once. If one is..."
"The eye of the Vajra—why is it necessary to repeat this in verse? Nevertheless, matters are not always one-sided.

Having said this, he ascended the seat. After offering the incense, he struck the mallet and declared to the four directions: "O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary truth."
The Master said: "A golden arrowhead is accustomed to leveling the Patriarch’s Way; an iron whip is often found when there is no enemy to avenge.
Is there any monk who disregards peril and ruin? Come forth and meet me! A monk asked: "At the foot of White Cloud Mountain, the Patriarch’s command is being put into practice."
"What is the Patriarch’s command? The Master said, "One, two, three, four, five. The student said, "If so, then yesterday was Taiping (Great Peace) and today is Haihui (Ocean Assembly).
The Master said, "Raise your voice, monk! A questioner asked, "In the past you went forth to bring rain; today you lead the assembly here.
With court dignitaries present before your seat, I pray you will let out a single roll of thunder. The Master said, "Do you hear it yet? The student said, [silently].
The wind carries auspicious clouds back to the azure cave; the tides of the vast sea assist the surging waves. The Master said, "How many people understand the mind?
The student said, "Hanshan constantly claps his hands; Shide is always diligent. The Master said, "I thought there was no one.
The student said, "One must not suppress the noble to make them common. The Master said, "For now, pay your respects," and then added, "Let us cease this questioning for a moment."
Now, as for the primary meaning (*paramārtha*): if one can grasp it upon hearing the mallet strike from the four directions, not even a thousand sages can approach it;
the words of the Patriarchs cannot reach it, and all the masters of the world fold their hands in submission.

Why is this so? Furthermore, the primary meaning is fundamentally pure and does not admit any defilements; how could it ever be described? Only those on the same path know it. Today, I let this matter pass with one stroke.
One must provide a distinct interpretation and understanding within the gate of transformative teaching.

Thus, one inherits the legacy of the former sages, upholds the ancestral command, serves as a model for later students, and establishes the school’s tradition. Were it not for such a person, how could this be transmitted?
(The words of thanks are not recorded here. He then said: "Since the expressions of gratitude are concluded, they should not be left empty. I have a verse to present to the assembly."
The sun is warm and the breeze gentle as the flowers are in full bloom; seven layers of mountains lock in the drifting white clouds.
Turning my thoughts back to the bustling splendor of the city, I emerge once more through the pine gate for another stroll.
The Master was at Taiping when he received his certificate of ordination. Holding it up to show the assembly, he said, "To understand it in such a way is already to be a dull-witted person.
Why? If one relies on the five thousand and forty-eight fascicles of the scriptures, is that not 'speaking'? If one does not rely on speaking, how can one distinguish the truth?
I ask the Rector to clearly bring it forth. After the reading of the ritual text was finished, he ascended the seat and said, "The Patriarchal Command..."
"You should go forth. The ten directions are cut off; is there anyone among them who would not spare their own life? Come out and meet this old monk!
At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "The sun and moon are easy to see, but good things are difficult to encounter. The Master said, "This makes people full of doubt.
A monk asked, "Your official letter has arrived and you now accept it; I pray you will proclaim the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. The Master said, "Clouds..."
"Dragons follow the clouds; tigers follow the wind. The student said, "Now that humans and devas have already heard the True Dharma, is there anything more sharp and new?
The Master said, "There is. The student said, "What is this sharp and new thing? The Master said, "Even if you miss it, you do not even know it."
Question: "Venerable Baoyun, Zen Master Taiping—within this context, how do you discern the truth?
The Master said: "Try to settle it for me. The student said: "Is it not that while the moon has no coming or going, its reflection appears in a thousand rivers? The Master said: "..."

"Let them do as they please—divining by tortoise-shell or striking tiles. He then said: "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it manifests only in reliance upon conditions. When a bright mirror stands upon its stand, beauty and ugliness appear of their own accord.
Those who have long studied under superior masters know where to return at the very moment of hearing these words. For those of late learning and beginners, you must be most careful and discerning."

Therefore, following the way of the ancients—that the Dharma has no coming or going and is without movement or change—I have spontaneously composed this "Praise of the Mountain" to present to the great assembly:
The light shines upon every eye, ever fresh in every place; Among them, who can distinguish the distant from the near?
Upon the branches of Jetavana, a thousand flowers bloom in splendor; With each fragrance, there is a spring anew.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Prince Siddhārtha. The monk asked, “What about when he leaped over the city walls?
The Master said, “There were already the Four Heavenly Kings present. The monk asked, “What about when he reached the Snow Mountains? The Master said, “...”
"The reed sprouts pierce his knees; the magpie’s nest is atop his head. The student said, "Alas, this is not yet where a student of the Way establishes himself.
The Master shouted, "After prostrating, withdraw! He then said: "Heaven and earth serve as a great furnace, smelting and refining the strong and the weak.
The Great Way has no origin; its rolling up and unfolding depend on the bellows and the key. The paths of the mundane and the sacred are level and plain; each must observe their own strategy."
Xie Shouzuo ascended the hall and said: "By smashing the peach pit, one beholds its kernel;
by pulling out the dragon’s whiskers, one encounters its treasure. Even so, this is not yet the hand of a master.
When the Yellow Emperor lost the Dark Pearl at the Red Water, he sent Zhi to seek it and failed; he sent Li to seek it and failed; he sent Qi Guo to seek it—"
Having failed to find it, he then sent Wangxiang. Even if Wangxiang were to find it, he would still not be a master of the craft.
How does this compare to today, when we employ a single Chamberlain for Ceremonial Affairs together with the great assembly?
Nevertheless, even so, we have only attained half of it.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Yongjia said: 'It cannot be grasped; it cannot be relinquished. Within that which is unobtainable, one simply attains it.
The Patriarch said: 'It is not mind, it is not objects, it is not Buddha. O Great Assembly, tell me: what is this? Then he said:
'When reaching the river, the land of Wu ends; beyond the shore, the mountains of Yue abound.'"
At the opening of the summer retreat, the Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Baiyun? The Master said, "Seven layers of mountains lock in the murmuring waters.

The student asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Coming in thousands, going in tens of thousands. The student asked, "I have already received the Master’s instruction on the person and the realm;
as for the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage, what of it? The Master said, "A flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech. Thereupon—

It is said: This summer I resided at White Clouds. Zen practitioners gathered there by chance. During these three months of the ninety-day retreat, those of high and low station relied upon one another.
Whether the rice gruel and tea were fine or coarse, we endured them as they came; we studied the scriptures according to our inclination and practiced samādhi as we saw fit.
We who have left the household life should simply let our bellies grow large.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Yesterday there was a certain matter that I intended to present to the assembly, but because this old monk forgot it, I could not bring it to mind for quite some time.
After reflecting for a long while, I said: 'I have forgotten it! I have forgotten it! Then I added:
'In the scriptures there is a mantra called the King of Intelligence. If anyone recites it, when they forget...'"
“I remember it,” he said. He then uttered: “Oṃ ālu-le-ji svāhā. He clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying, “I remember it!
I remember it! Seeking the Buddha, one does not find the Buddha; searching for the Patriarch, one does not find the Patriarch. A sweet melon is sweet to the very stem;
a bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat, he said: "A single mote of dust arises, and the great earth is gathered within it;

a single leaf falls, and the world beneath heaven turns autumnal. Where the golden wind stirs, it awakens the cricket’s song by the steps; when the jade dew falls, it draws forth the cicada’s chirp in the woods.

Upon the distant mists of the separate coves, the gulls and egrets fly about in succession; amidst the sheer cliffs and perilous peaks, the monkeys and apes everywhere vie with one another in their cries. Furthermore:

Seeing the fisherman raise his oar, the woodcutter’s song, the sound of a few pipes from the shepherd boy, a single sail upon the water, and the dream of a solitary traveler—these can serve to manifest the ancestral way and establish the patriarchal style;
thus, for these ninety days, there shall be no labor spent in vain.
The hundred eons are present in the functioning of the current moment. When such a discourse is held, the patch-robed monks knit their brows. Have you not heard it said:
"When not even a single speck of dust is established, one finally returns home; if there is the slightest trace remaining, one is no longer a member of the family."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is it like when you see someone but do not acknowledge them? The Master said, "Each keeps to their own boundary.
The monk pressed further, "What is it like when you see someone and do acknowledge them? The Master said, "Look! You have been struck right on the nose!
The student said, "Thank you for your answer, Master. The Master said, "Let go! He then continued, "An ancient said: 'What is the Immovable Honored One? Morning he goes to India; evening..."
Returning to the land of Tang. "Great assembly, is this not movement within non-movement, and non-movement within movement?
This very point is Baiyun’s realization.
Upon returning to the prefectural seat, he ascended the hall and said: "There is no idle labor on the boat; from moment to moment, circumstances differ. Yesterday it was the city walls..."
[The Master] said, "Inside. Today, amidst the white clouds. Now tell me, where is Ajita (the Immovable Honored One)? He then said himself, "His breath is like a bellows;
it makes one feel affectionately drawn."
Upon returning from his travels to convert others, he ascended the hall and said: "At the Baiyun Haihui Monastery, we have sufficient water, firewood, and charcoal;
we only lack sesame and wheat. Everyone has seen this clearly. I went personally to convert the donors, yet I neglected the Arhats.
I hope for your great compassion as you each look upon the face of the Buddha. O Great Assembly, the Buddha-body fills the Dharma-realm—how then shall you act?"
"Look at this! I say there is not even a single thread separating us.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Fortunately, there is nothing at all; one sets out on pilgrimage seeking to study Chan. Yet, one is instead vexed by the appearance of Chan, failing to pass through the Patriarch’s Barrier.
What is the Patriarch’s Barrier? 'Carrying a torch into a cowpen.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a single broom that sweeps away all the snow of the Snowy Mountains. I have a single mouth that has nothing to say when faced with affairs.
I have a pair of eyes that see clearly even for the blind and the deluded. Passing my life as I please, I call a tortoise a turtle.
Living in the world and learning to be human, one must guard against choking while drinking water. This was what Yangshan once said: "Two mouths."

A monk asked, "The imperial canopy hovers over the assembly, and the pure breeze pervades the seat. As I, a student, come forward, I ask the Master to resolve this for me.
The Master said, "After the last rain of the waning year, one gradually welcomes the spring. The student said, "The heavens drape the precious canopy, and the earth spreads..."
“Jinlian has departed,” [the student] said. The Master said, “It is not that much. The student asked, “What is this ‘not that much’?
The Master said, “I do not wish to speak rashly before the assembly of devas and humans. The student said, “The waves of the ocean of awakening increase in vastness;

the sun and moon of the Śākya heaven turn with increasing radiance. The Master said, “That, too, is unnecessary. He then raised the following: Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, “The World-Honored One transmitted—”
Apart from the golden brocade robe, what is this separate transmission? Kāśyapa called out to Ānanda, and Ānanda responded. Kāśyapa said, "Throw down the banner-pole in front of the gate.
Furthermore, Yongjia said, "Erect the Dharma-banner and establish the fundamental principle; clearly, Caoxi is the Buddha’s command. The Master said:
"Kāśyapa taught to throw down the banner-pole, while Yongjia taught to establish the fundamental principle. Now," he asked, "which is it?"
The Way is fundamentally "reversal" (dào). It is "establishment" (lì). To reach this point, one must possess the eye of discernment (*dharmapravicaya-cakṣus*) before it can be attained.
Ultimately, how so? In reversal, there is freedom in all directions; in establishment, two or three become six. On the Seven Peaks Pavilion, we discuss the profound together;
every word and every phrase clears the ears and eyes.
Returning to the new Sangha Hall, he ascended the hall and said: "Today is the first day of the tenth month;
the construction of the new Cloud Hall is complete, and the assembly of noble ones has attained a period of peaceful dwelling. Its elegance and beauty far surpass those of the old days.

While enjoying its use within these walls, may you all cherish one another and strive to preserve the ancestral style of the Buddhas of antiquity, so that the three realms and four debts of gratitude may receive benefit. There is a separate ceremony for celebration and repentance."

I have heard that [the stele] has been erected with the names of those in their full ranks inscribed upon it. I venture to exhort all donors, both far and near, to take note of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.
Suddenly, someone might come forth and say, "Elder, your composition is quite good. To this, he would reply: "Tsk!
Who dares to say it is not good? It was spoken from the mouth of Baiyun!"

The Circuit Intendant entered the monastery and ascended the hall, saying: "The army follows the seal; the general pursues the talisman. The Bodhisattva of Great Power protects and shelters sentient beings:
those who are compliant he entices with kind words; those who are wicked and stubborn he subjects to shackles and clubs.
In the midst of this, there is a man of vast capacity who cannot be detained by the mystical gate of golden chains, nor can he be gathered within the ranks of the holy or the mundane. If...
"How can it be that you do not attain it? The Buddha-dharma lacks spiritual efficacy. Baoyun had a message; try to explain it. An ancient said:
"The realms of boundless lands—self and other are not separated by the tip of a hair. Ten ages of past and present—the beginning and end do not depart from this very thought.
One may contain Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed, or cast the great trichiliocosm beyond the four quarters. One transforms the great earth into gold..."
Gold. Stirring the long river to produce butter and curd—when one arrives here, what should be done? The lands tremble to welcome Śākyamuni;
precious flowers fill the air to escort Avalokiteśvara.
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival, he raised an example: "In the past, there was a scholar who composed a 'Treatise on the Non-existence of Ghosts.
As soon as he finished writing and set down his pen, a ghost manifested its form, slashed its hand, and said to the scholar, 'What can you possibly do about me?
If Baiyun had seen this at the time, he would have immediately formed his hand into the beak of a magpie and said to it, 'Gu-gu-ku!'"
Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient precedent: Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Zhong, "What will you require after a hundred years?

The National Teacher said, "Have a seamless stupa built for this old monk. The Emperor said, "I ask the Master for the model of the stupa. The National Teacher remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you understand?
The Emperor said, "I do not understand. The National Teacher said, "I have a disciple, Tanyuan, who understands this matter; please issue an imperial decree for him."

He was questioned about this. The Master said: "Everyone in the assembly says that the National Teacher remained silent for a long time, yet they do not realize it was like hanging a drum and waiting for the mallet.

If at that time Emperor Suzong had been a masterful ruler, when the National Teacher was ordered to summon Tanzuan, he should have simply said, 'National Teacher, National Teacher—what need is there for more?
Later, Suzong summoned Tanzuan, and Tanzuan presented this verse: 'South of Xiang, north of Tan...'"
"Within it, gold fills the entire land; beneath the shadowless tree, all board the same boat; atop the lapis lazuli palace, there is no one to guide.
The Master (Linji) spoke on behalf of Emperor Suzong, saying: "Idle talk. Xuedou’s verse says: "A seamless stupa—hard to see;
A clear pool does not permit the azure dragon to coil. Tiers stand tall and distinct; shadows gather in circles. For ten thousand ages, it is shown to people. The Master.
It is said: "Xuedou may indeed have his name transmitted for a thousand ages; this old monk simply loves his words: 'The clear pool does not permit the azure dragon to coil.
This connects the beginning and the end all at once. As for the preceding string of remarks, set them aside for a moment.
But tell me, what is it ultimately like? He then said: "The beautiful maiden has already returned to the clouds and mists; the simpleton still remains guarding the void."
The Abbot ascended the hall and raised an example: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? Yunmen said, "A sesame cake.
Baoyun, however, is not like this. If someone were to ask me, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? I would simply point toward—
Yi said: "Donkey dung resembles horse manure. He also said: "Torn straw sandals. And he also said: "The numinous tortoise dragging its tail.
Now tell me, are these the same or different? Try to discern them.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the ultimate matter? The Master said, "Why need one go out of one's way? He then cited a case:

A monk requested further instruction from Langya regarding the passage, "The essence is fundamentally pure; why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Langya replied, "The essence is fundamentally pure;
why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? The monk attained realization. The Master said, "Though gold dust is precious,"
If it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Patriarch left behind a single sandal; for ten thousand kalpas it has been spread among people's ears.
People carry it on their shoulders in vain while walking barefoot; when have they ever trodden upon that which belongs to themselves?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The practitioner has not yet returned to strike the drum; atop this curved wooden seat, one cannot avoid taking what is mistaken and making it right.
*Chan* (Exertion). Ascending the hall again, he said: "Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao; Chen, Si, Wu, Wei; Shen, You, Xu, Hai. It ends and begins again. There is...
Regarding the craving for existence and weariness with it: how can one ultimately resolve this? Simply apply yourself to mature contemplation. Entering the hall, he said:
"Throughout the entire dharma-realm, when has one ever moved a single step? As for the white clouds in the deep mountains, what kind of reward-land are they?
If one is a person of the true Way, they wash their alms bowl twice every day.

The Master ascended the hall to speak on the method of re-skinning the Dharma drum, saying: "Many years of stubborn hide will not ring when struck; With new hide, a mere movement shakes thunder across the heavens.
If you are unimpeded, do not say it follows the current trend; When there is sound, who can claim it does not come from the drum?
Why is this so? "With both eyes one hears nothing; With both ears one sees nothing. Along this single level path, Who is it that lacks expedient means?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The beginning and the end must return to the source; the noble and the humble employ its words. A sharp sword is cast into empty space; a great staff strikes a rat.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: "After the World-Honored One’s parinirvāṇa, the holy disciples gathered at Vipaśyana Rock to compile the Dharma-treasury."

When Ānanda ascended the seat, his physical appearance and demeanor were no different from the Buddha’s. The great assembly consequently gave rise to three doubts: first, they doubted that Ānanda had attained Buddhahood;
second, they doubted that the Buddha had manifested again; and third, they doubted that a Buddha from another realm had come to transform them.

Ānanda proclaimed, “Thus have I heard,” and the doubts of the assembly were all stilled. At that time, had there been a man among the crowd who stepped forward and said, “Great Assembly, rely upon [this]...”
Go ahead and do it; let each person disperse so as to avoid having their intestines and stomachs churned by these full treasuries of volumes in elegant cases.
Even so, it has still not been completely eradicated. Why? If Ananda says, "Thus have I heard," Baiyun also says, "Thus have I heard.
If you say it refers to that time [in the past], you are valuing antiquity and slighting the present. If you say it refers to this very moment, you are valuing the present and slighting antiquity.
Do you understand? The udumbara flower does not bloom; its traces are severed and it has no fragrance. Entering the hall, he said:
"The Great Master Huineng, the Sixth Patriarch, was a great fool. The descendants of later generations have mostly wandered further into delusion and confusion.
Consider this carefully and well: White Cloud does not grant any concession."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "At the top of a hundred-foot pole, how does one make further progress? The Master said, "Only by walking fast will you succeed.
He then cited Yunmen’s saying: "Awakening to the Way through sound; clarifying the mind through form. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva came with money to buy a sesame cake;
as soon as he let go of his hand, it turned out to be a steamed bun. "Yunmen’s words are indeed excellent," [the Master continued], "and truly marvelous..."
"How extraordinary! For now, you have spoken only of the 'granny's Zen. If it were Baiyun, it would not be so.
What is 'awakening to the Way upon hearing sound' and 'clarifying the mind upon seeing form'? He then raised his hand in the gesture of beating a drum and said:
"Bam-ba-ra-tsa."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Four or five hundred shi of wheat, two or three thousand shi of rice—what a fine medicine for ending hunger!
Even Jīvaka could not find its secret.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example, citing Longya: "I have traveled to famous mountains throughout the land on foot; through years of hardship, my feet have become as worn as socks."
Now that I am old and infirm, I cannot walk; in my hand I hold a broken wooden ladle. Baoyun, however, is not like this:
his feet cannot wear straw sandals, nor can his hands grasp a wooden ladle. He sits upright and accepts offerings, so that the donor may always enjoy peace and happiness.
Ascending the hall, he said: "As for the matter of Bodhidharma’s coming from the West, people today vainly attempt to fathom it. The Milky Way stirs up waves;
the moon-orchid does not waft its fragrance. Why is this? It is a settled case."
The Abbot of Anle Monastery ascended the hall to preside over a vegetarian feast and said: "Last night I had a dream.
In the dream, I saw Master Zhen sitting face-to-face with Śakra in the celestial palace. Master Zhen asked Śakra, 'Are there the five signs of decline in the heavens?
Śakra replied, 'These are the words of the Buddha; how could one speak falsely? Thereupon, Śakra in turn asked Master Zhen:"
Hearing that there were those in Jambudvīpa who did not uphold the precepts, he asked, "Is this true? Zhen replied, "This is what the Buddha has taught;
how could one speak falsely? After a long silence, Zhen said, "Though the celestial palaces are pleasant, they are not places for long-term residence.
He then descended through the eighteen layers of hell and saw King Yama in the main hall whispering with Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Zhen then went out the door.
At the head [of the hall], he saw a youth dressed in blue robes who bowed and said, "The Dragon King of the Eastern Sea invites you and the various Arhats for a meal.
Zhen then went to attend the feast. Upon his return, he obtained several *cintāmaṇi* pearls and distributed them all at once among his disciples.
A white cloud was suddenly struck by the radiance of the pearls, and he awoke from a dream. To this day, the milk of the Dharma has been provided for Master Zhen.
The Fasting Ceremony. Baiyun is invited to ascend the seat. Great assembly, tell me: which is it? That which was dreamed last night, or that which was just spoken?
Among you are all those who have long studied with the masters of old, refined in the Way of Chan.
If anyone can discern this, please come forward and reveal a bit of your news. Is there such a person? Is there? If not, Baiyun has another ancient story. The Old Śākyamuni...
The World-Honored One entered parinirvāṇa by the side of the Bahudā River. Only then did Kāśyapa arrive; he circumambulated the golden coffin and wept.

Thereupon, the World-Honored One manifested his two upturned feet for the great assembly. Now tell me: was it at the time of parinirvāṇa that he was so, or was it at the time of manifesting the two feet?
He then said: "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak. My Dharma is subtle and inconceivable. Those with overweening pride, upon hearing it, will surely..."
Lacking reverence and faith, he thanked the supervisor for the collection and ascended the hall, saying: "Regarding the matter of human life and destiny, first of all one must have a ○.
