Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "Without obscuring the immediate function, I ask the Master to speak directly. The Master said: "Gathering it together and letting it go.
He then cited the story of a monk taking leave of Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell. The Master said: "This changes your heart, liver, and five viscera.
"Where there is no Buddha, run past quickly. The Master said: "A wild goose flies by leaving a trace; meeting people three thousand miles away..."
The monk made a mistake in his response. The Master said, "To step out the door is already a mistake. The monk said, "In that case, I shall not go.

The Master said, "Planting millet, yet beans grow. Zhaozhou said, "Plucking the willow blossoms, plucking the willow blossoms. The Master said, "Unaware that day has turned to night; how can one keep people young?"

In a small-scale sermon (xiaocan), he said: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, he did not establish written words; he pointed directly at the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature, one becomes a Buddha.
Suddenly, someone might come forward and say: "Venerable Sir, you usually love to ask people in your room, 'What is your mind?
I do not understand this, so I instead ask the Venerable Sir: 'What is the Master's mind? To which I would simply say to him:"
"Yet you have come here to stroke the tiger's whiskers. With what state of mind would I rashly speak to you?
If he asks again, 'How do you understand the story of the cypress tree? tell him: 'I have a skillful means.
He will ask, 'What kind of skillful means? You must first ask the Head Seat. Again he will ask, 'How do you understand Deshan’s striking [the student] with his staff upon entering the gate?'"
When I heard this, my flesh trembled. When Linji entered the gate, he immediately shouted. How do you understand this? What kind of tattered straw sandals are these?
Even if you were to pass through them all at once, it would still be "seven times nine is sixty-eight."
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival, he said: "The Mid-Autumn moon! The Mid-Autumn moon! From ancient times to the present, all have claimed it is nothing extraordinary.
Whether it is extraordinary or not, its brilliant, clear light pervades the great thousandfold world-system. Let the people of the world prattle on as they please."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "The temporal teachings of a single dispensation are a 'cutting foot' (a radical). I do not know which character it cuts.
The Master said, "Praṅ. The student said, "I asked about only one character; why did you answer with so much? The Master said:
"Seven characters, eight characters. Xue said, "This too is merely taking advantage of the opportunity.

The Master said, "For so long a time, it turns out there has been someone who knows the flavor of this tea and rice," and then he added, "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs: where there is good news, there is no news."

There is no news. The ancient seal-script is distinct and clear. When picked up, the great thousand-fold world-system stands towering and precipitous; when set down, ordinary people and sages share the same source.
Sometimes it stamps upon the faces of everyone, yet each person willingly submits and refuses to take responsibility for it.
This brings misfortune upon Baiyun, who suffers in vain. Tell me, where does the fault lie?
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "This staff was not obtained from Tiantai or Nanyue;
nor does it come from this land or the Western Heaven. Tell me, where was it born? If you know its place of birth, you shall together receive its use.
If you do not know, then [it is useless]. He leaned the staff against the wall and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following verse]: "The Wondrous, Profound, All-Holding, Immovable Honored One, The Śūraṅgama King, rare in the world!

It dissolves my inverted thoughts of billions of kalpas, And without passing through the aeons of the saṃgha, one attains the Dharma-body. "Great assembly, if you take this as a teaching on Chan, you slander the sutra."
If you treat it as a scriptural assembly, you slander Chan; if you treat it as a single lump, you are muddled and confused.
There are those who can leap out of it—they could spend ten thousand taels of gold every day. If you cannot leap out, there is a place for you to settle.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Everyone knows of the moon’s waxing and waning, but who knows that its waning is its waxing?

Busily riding a boat across the water, they do not realize they are crossing the water while riding a boat. Of the thirty-six thousand days of a hundred-year life, one’s youthful complexion is worn away in vain."
Each person should look into a mirror and see what kind of face they have.
Entering the hall, he raised an ancient case: A monk asked Dongshan, "What is the eye of a good spiritual friend? Dongshan replied, "A paper wick with no oil."
If you ask Baiyun, he would reply: "Without oil, the lamp will not be lit. Although this is so, it is still three thousand miles from Dongshan.
Yet, there is something excellent within it. What is that excellence? You might even stumble upon a pillar in the darkness and attain enlightenment—though that too is not certain.
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said: "It was thus before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja; it is thus after King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja.
It is thus for the Buddhas of the three periods. It is thus for the four and seven patriarchs of India and the two and three masters of the Tang land.
It was thus last year and the year before; it will be thus next year, the year after, the year beyond that, and the year after that. Suddenly—"

On the veranda lies a direct path, yet no one is willing to set foot upon it. Though the first month of spring still brings chill, I humbly wish the Head Seat and the Great Assembly all well-being and prosperity.
Su Wu herding sheep by the seashore finds joy day after day; Li Ling gazing toward the Han Terrace has his laughter break forth all morning long.
Where does this fall? Benevolence and righteousness are severed at the threshold of poverty; worldly sentiment leans ever toward the gates of wealth.
[The Master] ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the fundamental matter? The Master said, "Tongues are tied; there are no words. He then continued:
"Every day when you rise, you take up Linji’s staff, blow the Yunmen flute, respond to Zhaozhou’s clapping, and shoulder Yangshan’s spade to drive [the ox]."
The Ox of Mount Gui: Plowing the fields of white clouds for seven or eight years, he has gradually established a household. I further appeal to you all:
each of you extend a hand to assist one another and sing the song of "Joy in Returning to the Fields. With coarse soup and plain rice, let us pass our days in this manner. Why?
Simply because I wish for the silkworms and wheat to ripen this year, so that Rāhula’s son may receive a single coin.

It is said: Once he was bitten by a snake; he feared seeing the broken well-rope. He ascended the hall and said:
"Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? It is a hundred thousand times better than a cat. He descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: Xuefeng asked Deshan, "Regarding all the sages of the past, by what dharma did they instruct people?
Deshan replied, "In my school, there are no words or phrases, nor is there a single dharma given to anyone. From this, Xuefeng attained realization.
Later, a monk asked Xuefeng, "What did you gain from seeing Deshan that you then ceased [seeking further]? Xuefeng said, "I was empty-handed."
He departed and returned empty-handed. Today Baiyun speaks to those who have not yet attained penetration: "Two men came from Dongjing.
When asked where they had come from, they said, 'From Suzhou.
I then asked them how things were in Suzhou, and they replied, 'Everything is as usual. Even so, they could not deceive Baiyun. Why? Simply because—"
Because their voices were distinct, how could it ultimately be so? "The water chestnuts of Suzhou; the lotus roots of Shaobu. He ascended the hall and said:
"For twenty-five years I have sat upon this curved wooden seat. In citing the ancients and citing the present, there has been nothing lacking;
yet I have simply never uttered the first phrase. Is there anyone among you who possesses great compassion? Please try..."
"Come forward and speak! I wish for all people to know this together. Furthermore, throughout my life of traveling as a pilgrim, have you ever had such a thing?
Have you ever had it? Do not say there is none! Suddenly, someone comes forward and asks, "What is the first phrase?
Baiyun cannot help but say to him, "Why do you act so foolishly?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Difficult, difficult—how many kinds? Easy, easy—without a trace. Good, good—it drives one toward old age. Silent, silent—from this one attains it.
Having passed through these four gates, the people of Sizhou see the Great Sage. Enter!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "This Dharma cannot be shown; words and signs are quiescent. These two lines are still somewhat deficient.
What of it when you suddenly encounter the moment when the wild goat hangs from its horns? He pointed directly upward and said, "Heaven, heaven. He remained standing for a long time.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The mouth is the gate of calamity. He then continued, "Today is the festival of the Lantern Festival;
everywhere the lanterns shine with brilliant clarity. Yet one knows not the will of Heaven: auspicious snow has turned instead into bitter snow."
The poor have turned into withered cocoons; the tortoises have been frozen into turtles.
Only the Chan practitioners of the four seas—each one has dust added to their eyes. Why? Not saying. Not saying. Descent from the seat.

The Master of the Transformation requested the Head of the Assembly to ascend the hall and say: "The work of creative transformation within the ancestral gate functions as the vital breath that brings forth heaven and earth;

through spring, summer, autumn, and winter, it decisively turns the inverted minds of sentient beings toward permanence, bliss, selfhood, and purity. Yet, according to the practical application of a patch-robed monk, it is not yet so:
even if one were to transform the great earth into gold and churn the long river into butter and curd, it would still not suffice."
When he said, "The white clouds remain," suddenly a man came forth and said, "To speak in such a manner is merely the talk of one whose greed is insatiable.
He replied, "You have hit it. *Chan*!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example: "The Great Master Bodhidharma said, 'Who can attain my true lineage? Come forth and I shall provide you with proof.
The nun Zongchi said, 'According to my realization, it is like Ānanda seeing the land of Akṣobhya Buddha: one sees it once and never sees it again. Bodhidharma said, 'You have attained my skin.
Daoyu said, 'According to my realization, there is truly not a single dharma to be found.'"
Bodhidharma said, "You have obtained my flesh. The Second Patriarch performed three prostrations and stood in his place. Bodhidharma said, "You have obtained my marrow. The Master said:
"If one had seen those three men speak in such a manner at that time, each of them deserved thirty blows of the staff.
As for Baiyun today, he too deserves twenty-nine blows; I shall leave one blow remaining for all of you."
Among people, if there is one who knows pain and itchiness, they do not辜负 (betray) the former sages and shall likewise behold the white clouds.
If, however, you do not yet know this, even while eating porridge or rice in the hall, you must chew it thoroughly; for I see many who simply swallow it whole.

Ascending the hall, he raised this case: When Śākyamuni Tathāgata went to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to preach the Dharma for his mother, King Udayana missed the Buddha and commanded a craftsman to carve a sandalwood image.
When the World-Honored One descended, the image also came out to welcome him. Everyone, tell me:
was it the one who descended that was the Buddha, or was it the one who came out to welcome him? Furthermore, the teachings of the school say: "The Tathāgata comes from nowhere."
Nor does it go anywhere. Is this not because the Dharma-body has neither coming nor going? Does the Transformation-body have coming and going?
If one can see into this, ten thousand taels of gold will be consumed daily; if it is not yet so, who shall repay the cost of the straw sandals?

Ascending the hall, he said: "To speak of Chan is to be entangled by Chan; not speaking, on the other hand, manifests it directly. If one truly does not speak, that is truly a wondrous skillful means.
It is like wrestling before a horse, or like a flash of lightning and a clap of thunder. To understand it is to attain great wealth and honor;
to fail to understand it is to face it in vain."

On the occasion of the *zhāi* (fasting) ceremony, he ascended the hall and said: “Neither cold nor warm, one delights in spring excursions; Men and women incline their hearts to prepare for the future.
One realizes for oneself that a lifetime is like an illusion or a dream; Only then does one know that a hundred years are like a floating bubble. Where the cuckoo cries, there lies the true message.”
When the peony blooms, the rustic interest is profound. Who can understand this style of the Gate? In a moment, the youth’s hair turns white. Entering the hall, he said:
"That which was used last time is not applicable today; that which is used today will not be applicable next time. To use [it]...
"Not attached. He said, "Not attached. Again he was struck down. From antiquity until now, who has been wrong and who has not?
Suddenly, someone comes forward and says, "White Cloud was not wrong today either. [Baizhang] himself said, "Wrong! Wrong! Then he descended from his seat.
One day, the Master, holding his staff, walked around the abbot’s quarters and asked the monks, "Is there anyone here who is a person born under the Ox sign seeking to have their destiny told?
No one answered. He then said, "Today Sun Bin has opened his shop, yet not a single person comes to visit.
What a pity—this three-foot-long dragon-hair brush is being called nothing more than an ordinary piece of tattered cloth."
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a most extraordinary matter to present to you all. If I wish to speak of it, I am hindered by speaking;
if I do not speak, I am hindered by not speaking. If I wish to point to the mountains, rivers, and the great earth, I am hindered by the mountains, rivers, and the great earth."
For now, let us settle the matter at the head of the teaching. True gold is not traded for brass. When a man’s resolve is such as this, he is joyful and free from a hundred worries.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: A monk asked Caoshan, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Caoshan said, "Caoshan is not as good [as that]."
"How was it after he left the world? The Mountain said, "Not as good as Cao Shan. The Master said, "If one observes from the standpoint of worldly truth, Cao Shan deserves twenty blows of the staff.
If one observes from the standpoint of the ancestral Way, Baiyun deserves twenty blows of the staff.
Nevertheless, there are eyes at the tip of the staff; between these two men, one is entirely in agreement, while the other is entirely in disagreement. If...
If you can examine this thoroughly, I grant that you possess half an eye.
Entering the hall, he said: "All of you, as soon as you see this old monk moving his lips and raising his whisk, you immediately form a conceptual understanding.
Yet when it comes to the gathering of mountain birds or the wagging of a cow's tail, you treat them as trivialities; you fail to realize..."
"I know the sound of the eaves has not ceased from last night's rain; the lightning flashes still connect with the thunder of the coming night.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Śākyamuni has already passed away, and Maitreya has not yet been born. The myriad phenomena of the forest and the heavens are all pushed aside to one side.
Now, tell me, what is your own eternally abiding *dharmakāya*? He then said: "Whether there is merit or no merit, do not let it fill your belly."
Kongqing, acting as the head of offerings and construction, ascended the hall and said: "Today, Baiyun shall temporarily take the world of the Great Song and make it a single chessboard.
First, he places Mount Tai, the Eastern Peak; Mount Heng, the Southern Peak; Mount Hua, the Western Peak; and Mount Heng, the Northern Peak."
Mounts: among them, Mount Song is the Central Peak. It stabilizes the five directions. Next, Mount Wutai, Mount Emei, Mount Zhidi, and Mount Luofu are employed as supporting forces.
On the left flank, the formations fly like a slanting array of geese; on the right side, there are the double barriers of the tiger’s mouth.
Then he raised his hand and said: "Tell me, where does this one move fall? If you know where it falls, you may be considered a match. If...
Not yet so. Baiyun shall attempt to deliver this message: On the nineteen paths of level ground, the struggle for mastery has not yet ceased.
Do not let a single move go wrong; once lost, a son is difficult to reclaim.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the New Year: The primordial beginning inaugurates a new reign; in India and here in this land, all things are renewed.

The *xièzhài* and *qílín* bring blessings in response to the season. These words are truly not false. It is still cold in the first month of spring. Of many various kinds—venerable Head Seat and the Great Assembly, may you all universally employ [these blessings] throughout the heavens.
Furthermore, the various administrative officers who harbor talent and embrace righteousness, as well as the various fundraising masters who are like dragons.

He resembles a tiger. May you enjoy ten thousand blessings in your daily life; you are truly like gold and jade. Throughout the year’s three hundred and sixty days, may you be certain that your porridge and rice are always sufficient.

On the occasion of the *zhāi* (fast-day) ceremony, he ascended the hall and said: "In the second month of spring, all things are fresh and bright; throughout the realms as numerous as dust motes, it is one and the same sky.
The rain has washed away the moss from last winter’s snow; wild fires have driven the smoke from yesterday’s winds. On the perilous ridges, the cry of a monkey is heard for the first time this day."
On the Yangtze River, travelers are often seen aboard their boats; how many times in a human life can one encounter such a sight? It is well to sow fields of merit with a sincere heart.
On the occasion of the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascended the hall. A monk asked: "Today is the fifth day of the fifth month; for now, the drumrolls have ceased. Although there is nothing to do—"

[The assembly] also requested that he burn one incense stick. The Master said, "Swift as the Imperial Decree. [A monk] stepped forward and said, "Let us wait for the little ghosts to perform some trickery.
The Master said, "Zhong Kui is merely trying to frighten you. He then continued: "Today is the Dragon Boat Festival.
Baiyun has a divine talisman that possesses a modicum of efficacy. I dare not conceal it; I shall present it to all of you. First, you must..."
"First, may the Emperor, the Retired Emperor, and the Empress Dowager enjoy ten thousand years of sovereign health.

Second, may the court ministers, civil and military officials of the hundred ranks, and the local magistrates of the prefectures and counties always remain in their positions of emolument. Third, may the myriad people delight in their vocations, and may rain and wind be harmonious.

Just as he was speaking, a spirit messenger arrived and reported to Baiyun: "I have traveled everywhere to all places, yet it was only because my spiritual powers were small [that I failed to reach you]."
"What can one do about this matter? he asked him. "What kind of matter is it? The messenger said, "The nostrils of the Chan practitioners reach the heavens.
Baiyun spoke to him; do not say 'you'—even I cannot deal with him. Although it is so, "A vast marsh hides mountains;
a principle can subdue a leopard. But in the end, how is it? One draws out three; two adds four. The horns of the yellow ox point toward heaven.
Eight legs hanging down past the nose. Hurry! Hurry! Descend from the seat.
[The Master] ascends the hall and says: A nun asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of the profound mystery?
Zhaozhou pinched her wrist once. The nun said, "The Master still has this. Zhaozhou said, "You still have this. The Master said:
"If this nun were a person of true substance, I would simply tell her: 'I cannot let go of the Master either. He ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "The tongues of all people under heaven have been completely cut off by Baiyun;
but as for Baiyun’s own tongue, I wonder who it is that cuts it off? The Master said, "The Elder Wang of East Village. He then said, "In daily life..."
The matter is not different; rely on you to discern it. If you understand it through words, know that you have not struck through to the core.
If you do not understand it through words, your heart will feel as hot as fire. First pass through Zhaozhou’s barrier and cut off Baiyun’s tongue;
thus you shall not fail the kindness of the former sages, and may return to the hall to rest.

Ascending the hall, he said: "If you wish to stride across the world with ease, when you see this old monk beat the drum and ascend the hall at seventy-three or eighty-four [years of age], I shall take my staff and strike you right in the mouth!
Even so, only by removing the mounting platform before the gate and cutting through the five-colored ropes can you finally attain peace and happiness."
Small Assembly (Xiaocan). A monk asked, "Deshan did not answer a word; for a thousand ages he has blocked the essential ford.
Tonight, as Baiyun conducts this small assembly, I wonder how you will provide the teaching? The Master said, "I cannot; I would not be able to succeed to Master Duan."
The student said, “A master of the school naturally possesses [this realization]. The Master said, “What words are these?
The student advanced and said, “Regarding this very thing, for what kind of person is it established? The Master said, “Do you believe it or not? The student said, “How am I to believe it?
The Master said, “Are you asking because you understand, or are you asking because you do not understand? The student said, “I, however...”
[The monk] would not have come to ask this. The Master said, "Yesterday, I answered a monk in exactly the same way.
The monk asked, "Why then do you meet me today with such hostility? The Master said, "It is simply because the price was not right for the goods.

The monk said, "One may indeed suppress the worthy to make them cheap, but what can be done about the various other quarters [of the Buddhist world]? The Master said, "Everyone, look at this one Zen guest!"
The student said, "Letting one move pass. The Master said, "Hmph! Then he raised the following case: "Grand Master Lu Xian asked Nanquan, 'In my home there is a large stone;
I have sat upon it and slept upon it. I wish to carve it into a Buddha—may I do so? Nanquan said, 'You may.
Lu said, 'Is it not also the case that you may not? Nanquan said, 'You may not. Venerable assembly, one who acts as a good spiritual friend must..."
This clarifies the definitive discernment. Why is it that when another speaks, you say they have spoken; and when another cannot speak, you say they have not spoken?
Do you still know Nanquan’s point of descent? Baiyun, without sparing his own eyebrows, shall explain this through for you:
who is it that says "attained"? And who is it that says "not attained"? If you still do not understand, I, the old monk, now—
Tonight, I shall fashion a likeness for you. He then raised his hand and said: "I take the three realms and twenty-eight heavens to form the Buddha’s head;
the golden wheel and the limits of the waters to form the Buddha’s feet; and the four great continents to form the Buddha’s body.
Although this Buddha has been fashioned, where, then, do you all establish yourselves and find your livelihood? O Great Assembly, do you still...
Have you understood yet? This old monk shall now provide a second model:
take Pūrvavideha as one Buddha, Jambudvīpa as one Buddha, Aparagoyānī as one Buddha, and Uttarakuru as one Buddha.
Grasses, trees, thickets, and forests are Buddhas; all wriggling and moving sentient beings are Buddhas. Since it is thus...
"Ma! And what do you call a sentient being? Do you understand yet?
It is better to let Pūrvavideha be Pūrvavideha; let Jambudvīpa be Jambudvīpa; let Aparagoyānī be Aparagoyānī;
let Uttarakuru be Uttarakuru; and let the grasses, trees, and forests be as they are."
Grasses, trees, and forests; wriggling, moving beings endowed with spirit—let them remain as wriggling, moving beings endowed with spirit.
Therefore it is said: "This Dharma abides in its own position; the characteristics of the world are eternally present. Since this is so, what do you call "Buddha"? Do you understand?
Suddenly, a man came forward and said, "Baoyun, cease your idle talk! Everyone, take note of this turn of words.

He then ascended the hall and said: "One who has throughout his life brought everything to completion and resolution is precisely the one most fit to receive a blow of the staff. But tell me, where does the fault lie?
I strike you for having brought everything to completion and resolution!"

Ascending the hall, he said: "The time since the Sage has passed away is remote; people are mostly indolent. When met with adversity they give rise to anger; when met with favor they give rise to attachment.
But tell me, what is it that is neither angry nor attached? A pair of scissors from the Eastern Sea; a leather bag from the Western Regions."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "I have heard the Master say, 'Before the mountain, there is a plot of vacant land.
As for the time before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranāda, I wonder who was the master of it? The Master said: "Go ask the person who wrote the deed.
The student said: "Why does the Master trouble someone else to answer? The Master said: "It is only because you had others ask. The student said: "To the Master..."
Shangping went out. The Master said, "He is very far away. He then continued, "For five days do not behold his countenance;
for two [days] do not hear his sound. Those with merit shall be punished; those without merit shall be rewarded. He picked up Mount Sumeru and weighed it, and it came out at two taels.
Suddenly, someone spoke: "Why is it that a man of knowledge in this region uses a large scale to weigh people and matters? He replied himself:
"In official affairs, even a needle cannot pass; in private dealings, carts and horses are allowed through."
Xie Jiefang ascended the hall and said: "Yesterday, when Jiefang brought a handful of sand to the front of the abbot’s quarters, as soon as he saw this old monk, he flung it straight in my face.
Fortunately, I had seen it coming and shielded myself with my sleeve; thus, nothing was harmed."
This morning I have brought this up for the great assembly; I dare not conceal it. Why? Because I admire his great courage in being able to deploy such a move.
Suppose someone were to ask Baiyun, "Why do you simply stop there? One does not see it said, "In old age, one does not rely on physical strength for capability.
Although this is so, the roles of host and guest remain distinct.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "For so long a time, where have you been coming and going?
He then continued, "Before Bodhidharma came, it was cold in winter and hot in summer; after Bodhidharma came, it was dark at night and bright by day.
If you all could utter a single word of plain reality, you would hear saltiness when eating salt and sourness when tasting vinegar. If you cannot say it," [he said].
At the gate of Kāśyapa’s monastery, he ascended the hall and said:
"If one discusses this matter, it is like a game of dice. Suddenly winning, one feels joy in body and mind;

the family estate flourishes, providing shelter for descendants, all without realizing it. Yet when suddenly losing to another, one naturally falls into confusion and distress. Nevertheless, although there is..."
There are losses and gains; this matter still remains. Today, Baiyun has a branch to grasp if there is one, and a precedent to follow if there is none.
Have you not seen how Grand Master Lu Xun and Nanquan were watching a game of *shuanglu* (double-sixes)? The Grand Master picked up the dice and asked Nanquan, "In such a way, or not in such a way?
If one goes for the colors with total confidence like this, what then? Nanquan said, "Stinking!"
"Eighteen bones. Great assembly, this place is not far from the county seat.

When outsiders hear of it, they will come to arrest those gambling; what then? He said: 'White Cloud has its own way. I recall Longya saying: 'To study the Way, one must first have an awakening, like once competing in a swift dragon boat.

Though it is an old hall and empty ground, one..."* *(Note: The source text appears to be an excerpt from a Zen discourse record (yulu) containing a dialogue and a verse. The final line is incomplete.)*
Only when the exhausted and emaciated have been delivered does one finally rest.
Entering the hall, he said: "Maudgalyāyana leaped across a pit with both feet; Mahākāśyapa danced upon hearing the *zheng* lute;
Pilindavatsa reviled the river deity; Kāḷodāyin buried himself in filth and mire. Each of these matters is recorded in the teachings."
In general, these are said to be habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*). Yet, consider the gate of the Patriarchs: Bodhidharma sat facing the wall for nine years;
Bimiya held up a staff; Heyshan struck the drum; Shigong drew his bow; Xuefeng rolled the ball; the National Teacher used the water bowl;
Guizong dragged the stone; Deshan would strike as soon as someone entered the door; Linji would shout as soon as someone entered the door; and Wuye, as soon as anyone questioned him...

He then said, "Do not engage in false imaginings. Tell me, what is this? Is there among you any monk who has long studied under former masters, who roams freely throughout the world, and who possesses the eye upon the crown of his head?
Come forth and provide testimony for Baiyun; it is also to let your lifelong efforts be fully realized.
Is there such a one? Is there such a one? If there is none, thirty years from now this talk will spread far and wide. And so he spoke.
As for the ultimate nature of the Way: "In the midsummer heat, the fire-clouds retreat to the azure cavern; in the clear autumn, the perilous dewdrops fall upon the golden basin.
On the anniversary of the former Master’s passing, he ascended the hall and said: "Last year, at this very time, there were three matters from the year before."
This year, it being precisely such a time, many of last year’s seven matters have passed. Among these ten matters, there are many that cannot be counted.
Why is this? Having set aside seven and three, one matter remains. What was said last year is what is spoken today;
it is as swift as an arrow and as black as lacquer. The wordless child speaks incessantly; the legless immortal slaps his chest and kicks out. Thus it is.
[The Master] said: "Let us descend from the seat together with the Ritual Director. Rising at the site of the funeral, he said: "Originally it was you who sent me off; today it is I who send you off.
Birth and death are but common occurrences; one is cast down, yet again raised up. Arriving at the burial site, he addressed the assembly once more:
"Today is precisely the eighth day of the third month. You who escort the funeral procession, listen now: Behold the peach blossoms, red upon the roadside, all in full bloom."
This is to remove the blood from the eyes of men. He ascended the hall and said:
"In the middle spring, the weather gradually warms; the peony buds its eggs. The purple swallow huddles its body; the yellow oriole opens its eyes.
Together we enjoy the fragrant spring with three cups or two goblets. Only the white clouds, however, carry a wooden board for their entire lives."
Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Twenty-One;
Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Twenty-Two;
Recorded Sayings of Master Yan of Dongshan at Huangmei.
Compiled by the disciple Weiqing.

When the Master was invited to the Great Assembly (Haikai), he held up the incense and addressed the assembly, saying: "An eighty-year-old elder rolls a brocade ball. He then handed it to the Rector (Weina).

After the proclamation of the formal documents (shu) was completed, he ascended the seat and said: "The flavor of presiding over monasteries in three places is exactly this; this time, it is my karmic enemy."
It is difficult to avoid. The nostrils of White Lotus Peak; the breath issuing from Mount Haikai.
That evening, for the small *sōdan* (informal sermon), he said: "One becomes three; three become seven. A *ju-jung* flower by the sheep-pasture embankment;
a 'Wang Fu' stone by the Ju-ma River. Striking the ruler with a stone; drawing a winnowing basket in red earth. Let the eyes remain fixed on folly. He spoke again:
"Thirty years in the Huai region; now I am an old Huangmei. It is well that he speaks so clearly; let the ducks listen to the thunder.
Entering the monastery, he burns incense at the Patriarch’s Stupa and points with his finger, saying: "At that time, you departed with your whole being in this manner;
do you remember coming back today? He then asks again: "What serves as proof? "This very thing serves as proof," he says, and then prostrates.
At the opening of the hall at Huangmei, Lord Zai presented the memorial. The Master held it up and showed it to the assembly, saying, "Do you see it?

Within it are contained all rare treasures and extraordinary jewels. If you do not see it, I ask the表白 (Baibiao) to bring it forth before the assembly. After the reading of the memorial was finished, he then said:
They then dispersed in this manner; it was already a great deal of work.
If you do not believe me, he then pointed to the Dharma seat and said, "In a short while, I shall scatter sand and earth upon the upper part. He then ascended the seat.

Having offered incense and made a prayer for the Emperor, he again took up incense and said, "This one stick of incense [was offered] during my twenty-seven years at Shu County, while residing in three monasteries. You all..."

He understood it all at once. He was then about to burn the next [text], when [the master] said again, "You must not do so; you must explain it thoroughly. For fifteen years I have been traveling as a pilgrim.
First, I attended upon Master Xian and obtained his fur. Next, I visited various venerable elders throughout the four seas and obtained his skin.
Then I went to the place of Old Yuanjian of Fushan and obtained his bones. Finally, I was with Master Baiyun Wenda and obtained his marrow."

Only when the marrow [of my realization] is fully realized will I dare to accept the responsibility of being a teacher for others. Today, I burn it within this incense burner, letting its fragrance permeate heaven and scorch the earth;
let those with ears discern it. The Fourth Patriarch struck the gavel and said: "O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary truth.
The Master said: "When contemplating the primary truth, the precious sword’s frost-sharp blade flashes like lightning, piercing through the three worlds."
A thousand. The most supreme, peerless, and incomparable; the eye discerns it and the hand can grasp it. Come forth and let us compare and test! A monk asked:
"The old shop opens anew, displaying precious jewels; every time one picks them up, they are fresh. You, Master, now occupy the seat of Lu and Neng;

how exactly do you wipe away the dust from the mirror? The Master said: "In the morning I go to the Western Heaven; in the evening I return to the land of Tang. The monk pressed further: "I have already attained it."
Xuan-yuan discerned the essential point; from this, the numinous light shines upon the sands of the Ganges. The Master said: "What about the first phrase? The monk replied:
"I do not decline the length of the mountain road; I must pass through even treading on the snow. The Master said: "You are still drunk. A monk asked:
"At the assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard it personally. I wonder, at today’s assembly, who is it that hears it?"
The Master said, "It is no different from Vulture Peak. The student asked, "From antiquity to the present, all have been those who know the sound.
The Master said, "And what about that one phrase of 'knowing the sound'? The student said, "Nodding the head, but not sticking out the tongue.
The Master said, "No one passes you by recklessly. The student asked, "What if someone comes along, seizing the clouds and mist? The Master said, "This old monk."
The drum was struck, and he said: "Just now, my fourth-generation master-uncle struck the gavel and said, 'One should contemplate the primary principle (paramārtha).

But how, pray tell, does one contemplate this primary principle? Do you wish to understand? If the Buddhas of the three periods of time did not possess the primary principle, with what would they transform and deliver sentient beings?
[It is through it that] the Seven Patriarchs of the Western Heaven and the Two Ancestors of the Tang Land, as well as all those throughout the world..."
If the old monk had no ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), with what would he establish the school’s tradition?
It is just as if the present Sage Emperor had no ultimate truth, with what would he govern the world?
If the Prefectural Scholar, the County Magistrate Xuan-de, and all the honored officials here had no ultimate truth, with what would they serve as parents to the people? Even down to...
If the donor lacks the primary meaning (paramārtha), with what will they venerate the Triple Gem?
Nevertheless, even so, each must awaken to it for themselves before it can be attained.
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following] case: An ancient said, "To be a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one must drive the oxen of the plowman and seize the food of the hungry man.
Driving the oxen of the plowman causes his crops to flourish; seizing the food of the hungry man ensures that he is forever freed from hunger and emptiness.
Among those in the assembly who hear this being raised, most are like the wind passing by the ear. Since it has been driven...
As for that ox, why does it cause the crops to flourish so abundantly? Since its food has been taken away, why is it that hunger is forever severed?
At this point, one must possess the skillful means to drive the plowman’s ox and seize the hungry man’s food;
then, pressing and prodding it, one drives it until it reaches the corner of the dilemma, whereupon one may address it.
The Way. Blessings are not received twice; calamities do not strike alone. Entering the hall, he said:
"In the second month of spring, the warmth gradually increases. Hehe! Singing and frequently striking the clappers, the black chicken runs into the flock of geese;
the duckling freezes until its beak is flattened. Floating or sinking upon the water, when will it ever become a precious vessel? Subhūti.
Reflect on this carefully and thoroughly. Heaven and earth are not far from here. Again, he said: "King Bimbisāra, entering the hall:
Today is the fifth day of the second month. The attendants have already come to beat the drum; the elder is utterly bewildered within."
Reflecting upon the words of the Buddhas and the Patriarchs: though the snow lies three feet deep across the great earth, birds and beasts eat only mud and soil.
This year will surely be bountiful; naturally there will be five winds and ten rains. Herein lies a point of excellence. But tell me, what is this excellence?
He then makes the sound of thunder and asks, "What is it? Then he says again, "The thunder has sounded."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Now, as for those who are true Zen practitioners, they are like generals who have crossed the frontier.
If you can bring me even half a piece of Yunmen’s *huping* (staple cake), I will give you half of Mount Sumeru. If it is not so, how dare you call yourself a Zen practitioner?"

Ascending the hall, he said: "Now, one who has left the household life must possess the perspective of one who has left the household life. Only by possessing the eye that discerns the Dharma can one truly be considered a renunciant.
What is the eye that discerns the Dharma? It is breaking a lamp-stand. Ultimately, what is it? Carrying a wooden board. Carrying a wooden board."

On the opening day of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "The early summer is gradually growing hot. I humbly wish that the Head Seat and the Great Assembly are in good health and enjoying ten thousand blessings.

It is like peach blossoms amidst bamboo—flowers upon brocade, flowers everywhere on the ground. Do not let your eyes wander among them. This is the annual custom; there is no need for further investigation.
After descending from the seat, there will be formal greetings and tea served while visiting the various quarters."
Ascending the hall, he raised [the case]: Yongjia said, "There is no person, and there is no Buddha. The great trichiliocosm is but a bubble in the sea;
all sages and worthies are like a flash of lightning. "Great assembly, if you do not possess the diamond eye here, you will see nothing but skulls strewn across the wilds.
What then? Though the road to Jian阁 is perilous, those traveling by night are even more numerous."

Ascending the hall, he said: "Standing in the snow and severing one's arm was intended as an instruction for later generations. It is the person who can propagate the Way; it is not the Way that propagates the person.
What kind of words are these? *Jiangchengzi*.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Where people of this age dwell, I do not dwell; where people of this age walk, I do not walk.
In the end, what is it? The horns of an ox are three inches long; the horns of a rabbit are eight feet long. The four oceans flow toward the East Sea; Prajñāpāramitā."
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is a great road outside the gate; yet you are unwilling to open your mouth wide.
On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, you will wander aimlessly about. How pitiful, my brothers!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is no dharma that can be preached; this is called preaching the Dharma. The night moon is severe and cold, the frosty sky is piercingly chill;
the turtles in the pond have been frozen into soft-shelled turtles. To speak even two more phrases would turn one's tongue into iron."

Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Emperor’s Birthday, he said: "On the eighth day of the twelfth month, the anniversary of the birth of His Majesty the Emperor, one must not speak of other matters.
Then, raising his voice, he proclaimed: "Long live the Emperor! Long live the Emperor!"

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Bodhisattva Anantagātra took a bamboo staff to measure the crown of the World-Honored One’s head. When it reached one *zhang* and six *chi*, it was still another *zhang* and six *chi*.
He measured all the way up to the Brahma Heaven, yet he could not see the mark of the World-Honored One’s crown. Thereupon, he cast down his staff, joined his palms, and spoke this verse:
'Empty space has no bounds, And the Buddha’s merit is likewise. Were there anyone who could measure it, Even through kalpas they could not reach its end.'"
"Enough! Great Assembly, let the Bodhisattva Boundless Body cease his verse for now. Do you all understand how to measure yourselves?
If I were to ask the old monk to measure himself, there would simply be no place to begin. Have you not seen the ancient saying: 'A peck-measure fills the Buddha’s seat;
its merit is difficult to measure. A cup burns incense; purple clouds gather and roll. Why is it so? It is because it is something else entirely."

On the first day of spring, he ascended the hall and said: "In this year, there remains only this month. Yet the heavens have not yet sent down a single snowflake. I announce to the dragon deities of the three realms:
let each of you inform one another that silver shall be spread across the heavens and the earth, so as to accord with the timing and the season. Furthermore—
I beseech the great assembly for your compassion. To contemplate Samantabhadra Bodhisattva—how, ultimately, is this done?
Mahāsattva. At the request of Guo Chaofeng Xiangzheng, he ascended the hall. Before the Dharma seat, Chaofeng burned incense and said:
"This single offering of incense, burned within the censer, forms clouds of light that pervade the entire Dharma realm; I offer it to my elder brother, the Abbot."
Chan Master, I humbly pray that from this vast and square seat amidst the clouds, you will part the face of your countenance and release the form of our former teacher for all people to depict.
Why is this so? "We met of old by the cliffs of Baiyun; the matters of yesteryear and today are not the same.
The night is still and the waters cold, yet the fish do not bite; a single incense burner scatters the fragrance of white lotus winds."—The Master.
He then said: "Namo satvata parāya. Thus, thus. How many times have I gazed upon the white clouds above the stream?
The yellow plum blossoms open amidst the snow. Not thus, not thus. The tender willow twigs are like golden threads; they must simply appear in accordance with the season.
Have you not seen how Layman Pang asked Great Master Ma: 'That which does not consort with the myriad dharmas—'"
"Who is this person? Mazu Daoshi said, "I will tell you once you have sucked the waters of the West River dry in a single gulp.
O Great Assembly: To suck the waters of the West River dry in a single gulp is to reach the very bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom deep abyss.
This rickety footbridge is not Zhaozhou’s bridge; how can bright moon and clear wind compare?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring rain falls boundlessly; heaven and earth already possess this knowledge. The Lord of the East issues his true command: plum and willow branches, one by one.
You guests at the Gate of the Patriarchs meet one another in this very moment. To meet is not non-existent, but what matter is there to speak of?
Having said this, he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient case: Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Zhong, “After you have passed away, what will you require?
The National Teacher said, “Have a seamless stupa built for this old monk. The Emperor said, “I request the Master’s pattern for the stupa.
After a long silence, the National Teacher asked, “Do you understand? The Emperor said, “I do not understand. The National Teacher said, “I have a Dharma-heir disciple named Tanyuan who...”
The Emperor was familiar with this matter and requested that he be summoned for questioning. The Master said: "In front are pearls and agates;
behind are agates and pearls. To the east are Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta; to the west are Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.
In the center is a single banner, which, being struck by the wind, cries out, 'Hu-lu hu-lu!'"
Ascending the hall, he looked around to the left and right of the meditation seat, then took up his staff in his hand and said, "It is only one foot longer.
He descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall again, he said, "There is a thing in the world that belongs neither to the ordinary, nor to the sage, nor to the heterodox, nor to the orthodox."

It does not belong to the correct [path]. When all matters arrive at their appointed time, they issue commands spontaneously. One must know this even at the cost of one's life; it would require changing one’s very nature. He ascended the hall and said:
"Carrying water to sell by the riverhead—everyone laughs at this as strange. This滞貨 (stale merchandise) leaves no one guessing; it is as if one owes a debt to another.
At the stroke of midnight last night, the stone man fought to perform a prostration. As for these words, do not speak of them to you..."
"I do not understand; I myself do not understand.
He ascended the hall and said, "The ancients said: 'The boundless realms of all lands are not separated by even a hair's breadth from self and other;
ten eons of past and present do not depart from the single moment of the present thought. The Master said, "It is so, it is so—but it is simply too old-fashioned. Xuefeng then showed [the meaning].
The various paths: take the entire earth and pinch it up until it is the size of a grain of millet; I toss it before you. You lacquer buckets do not understand!
I beat the drum and invite everyone to look. Great assembly, Xuefeng has deceived you all face-to-face by no small measure.
Nevertheless, is there anyone who can walk in step with Xuefeng? Come forth and meet the Fifth Patriarch! Is there anyone?
"Ma. If there were none, he then took up his staff, struck once, and held it aloft, saying:

"Today, Wuzu and Xuefeng ride together upon a celestial raft to traverse the four great oceans, pierce through the skulls of the eight great dragon kings, and pass over hundreds of thousands of Mount Sumerus;
having returned, they sit upon this Dharma seat, and then escort Xuefeng back to Snow Peak Mountain. It is simply that—"
"Once you have taken a single step, will you all still believe it? If you cannot believe it, I shall raise my staff and say:
Have you not seen what our late Master said? 'Place it at the head of your bed; it is urgent that we strike the rat.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ordinary mind and the sacred intent are revealed in their majestic presence; if every thought is without error, that itself is the site of enlightenment (*dōjō*).

Do not speak of today’s affairs when facing the future; Avalokiteśvara acts with sovereign ease, emitting rays of light from his brow. After a long silence, he said: "Do not try to deceive this old monk!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The three-month summer retreat is now complete. As for the matter of the ninety-day restriction of the feet, how is it?

In the Western Heaven, the wax seal has long been tested by sound; in this land, those who speak of the goose’s pearl are many. In these final times, two thousand years distant, the profound intent is submerged as water and milk blend to form a river.
May the Bodhisattvas of the forests and springs together propagate and protect [the Dharma], lest it fall into ruin and be seized by the various demons."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The season is late autumn and the frost is cold; the Milky Way is bright and clear.
A single incense stick burns in the pine-windowed room—this truly befits the fine scenery of our house."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example: A monk asked Touzi, "Is there anything extraordinary within the Great Canon?
Touzi replied, "The Great Canon is produced. The Master said: "When Touzi was questioned by this person, he was completely at a loss and could not provide a relevant response.
If it were Wuzu, it would not be so. Suppose someone were to ask him, 'Is there anything extraordinary within the Great Canon?'"
There is no such thing. The old monk would simply say to him, "He paid his respects and departed; he accepted it with faith and put it into practice.
Even though this is so, he is ten thousand miles away from Touzi and Baiyun. After all, what is the point of seeking the eyes of those from all quarters?
Ascending the hall, he said: "Awakening is the same as non-awakening; returning home, one seeks the old path. One character is one character; one phrase is one phrase.
Since childhood I have not uttered empty words; at two years old I learned to take steps. A lotus grows from still water; it blooms once every year."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Again and again I call for you, yet you do not return home; You greedily go before the gate to play with dust and sand.
Every year, when the third month arrives, The peonies bloom everywhere throughout the city."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The green vines wind their way straight up to the summit of the cold pine; the white clouds, pale and drifting, appear and disappear within the great void.
From the nineteenth until the twenty-third, more than ten thousand people came here for this assembly, making a great clamor.
Now, I see only this old man alone, his mouth flapping. If you say that many people constitute a disturbance, then one..."
People are still; it is truly like ten thousand miles of white clouds. After all, how is it? One person is bustling and noisy;
many people are silent and still. It is better to return to the hall and drink tea.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind turns with the myriad objects; where it turns, it is truly profound. Yunmen said: "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys a sesame cake with money;
when he lets go of his hand, it is actually a steamed bun. If this is so, then one follows the turning of his footsteps. Wuzu had a saying:
"Recognize your nature by following the flow, and you will enjoy eternal happiness without sorrow. This is the cause.
He brought this up as an illustration for the assembly. Suddenly, he did not know where he was; it was uncertain. After a long while, he called to his attendant.
The attendant responded, "Yes? The Master said, "I have been deluded."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The mid-winter cold is severe and pervades the entire world. For the wealthy and noble, it is easy; for the poor, it is difficult.
Only we who dwell among the forests and springs have neither ease nor difficulty. Why is this so? After a long silence, he said: "I shall tell you in a place where there is no one."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an ancient case: Puhua said, "If he comes from the bright side, I strike him on the bright side;

if he comes from the dark side, I strike him on the dark side; if he comes from within space, I strike him within space; if he comes from the four quarters and eight directions, I strike him with a flail.
When Linji heard this, he sent a monk to ask him, "What if he does not come in any of these ways? Puhua replied, "Tomorrow there is a vegetarian feast at Beici Monastery."
If it were the Fifth Patriarch, it would not be so. Suppose someone asked him, "What if none come in such a manner? He would strike them with his voice.
That person would surely say, "The Fifth Patriarch uses blind censure and blind blows. I want you to speak exactly like that. Why?
So that you may freely present this to all quarters.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In responding to circumstances without fixed method, there is only this. Upon the tip of a single hair, the field of the mind is cleared and expanded;
yet from it grow branches and trailing vines—the family of demons. Each point radiates light, illuminating the ancestral heavens."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The wind is gentle and the sun is warm; the tall trees resound with the song of orioles. The peach and plum blossoms are so beautiful they form rows like shimmering brocade;
the fragrant grasses are so lush they spread out like carpets in an array. A petal falls here, another there—fragments of jade drifting down in misty profusion.
The willows dance three times, then five, trailing long filaments as they sway slowly. At such a time, the ancients spoke of the 'solitary bird'—"
Speech is like a reed-pipe; willows hang down long golden threads. Smoke gathers and the mountain valleys fall silent; the wind carries the fragrance of apricot blossoms.

Sitting serenely through the long day, the mind becomes clear and ten thousand anxieties are forgotten. I wish to speak, yet words fail me; let us deliberate well beneath these trees. After a long pause.
[The Master] said, "You should deliberate upon this for a moment.

He ascended the hall and, citing a case, said: A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? Feng said, "Staring with wide-open eyes, one cannot see the bottom.
The monk asked, "And as for those who drink from it? Feng said, "It does not enter through the mouth. When Zhaozhou heard of this, he remarked, "No..."
"It can enter through the nostrils. A monk then asked Zhaozhou, "What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine?

Zhaozhou said, "Bitter. The monk asked, "And what of those who drink from it? Zhaozhou said, "Dead. The Master said: "If someone were to ask Wuzu, 'What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine?
I would simply say to him, 'Water. And if he asked, 'What of those who drink from it? I would merely say, 'Stop right there.'"
Thirsty. Suppose someone were to come forth and ask, "Are the waters of Caoxi one with this, or two? I would immediately say to him: "Branching out and forming tributaries;
spreading freely in every direction. Irrigating the fields where it is low, splashing water upon the vegetables where it is high."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Zhaozhou spoke of 'the cypress tree. Luling followed with 'snow.
In the midst of white rice, there is a White Lotus Peak. To swallow the waters of the West River in a single gulp—*xīmēi luólàlǐ*, *luólàlǐ*.
I am I; you are you. In a deep village, there is a white-marked beast, with gaping jaws and whiskers, a nine-tailed mane."
[The Master] said, "Long ago. He said, "Eh! How terrifying! A small discourse (*xiǎocān*).
He raised [the following case]: When Yàoshān first visited Shítóu, he asked, "I have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
However, I have heard that in the South there is the 'Direct Pointing to the Human Mind, Seeing One's Nature, and Attaining Buddhahood,' which I truly do not yet understand clearly. Shítóu said:
"It cannot be so. It cannot be not so. It cannot be both so and not so. Yaoshan was at a loss.
One day, while sitting, Shitou asked him, "What are you doing here? Yaoshan replied:
Shitou said, "I do not do even a single thing. Touzi said, "If that is so, then you are idly sitting. Shitou said, "Idly sitting is itself doing something.
Touzi said, "You say you do nothing; what is it that you do not do? Shitou said, "Even the thousand sages do not know. Thereupon, Shitou uttered this verse:
"From the beginning we have lived together, yet its name is unknown; Spontaneously following along, we simply go on like this. Since ancient times..."
"Even those of superior virtue do not recognize it; how could the ordinary people of a hurried moment easily understand it? The Master said:

"O Great Assembly, you must pass through the barrier of the Patriarchs and comprehend the path of the birds and the mysterious way before you can understand such talk. Stonehead has given this instruction."
This is comparable to Zhaozhou’s “pine tree in front of the courtyard,” Dongshan’s “three pounds of flax,” and Yunmen’s discourse on “surpassing Buddhas and patriarchs.
Wuzu also has a verse: “Moving spontaneously, its name unknown; Casting a light glance, listen carefully.
Upon the water, green and lush— It turns out to be duckweed.”
The special messenger from Sishen arrived, carrying the letter of Dharma succession. Before the Dharma seat, the Master received the letter and held it up, asking the messenger, "This is Sishen’s;
where is yours, *ācārya*? The messenger said, "It is right before your eyes.
The Master said, "I almost failed to question you on this point. He then ascended the seat and said, "A good thing is difficult to encounter; why do you not come forth?"
"Come, everyone, sing and respond in harmony. At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "Stonehead’s dispatched letter—still the work of a dull-witted fellow.

Xuansha’s blank paper is but a vain claim of 'sharing the same wind. When Sishian brought it here, what auspicious omen was there? The Master said, "When the spring breath arises, there is no hard ground.
The monk pressed further, "If so, then one has burst through a thousand acres of waves and penetrated the Patriarch’s Barrier. The Master said, [as before].
[The Master] said, "Truly there is none. The student advanced and said, "One could say that after the yellow plums have ripened, no one recognizes them;
only you, Old Teacher of Dongshan, are granted permission [to know them]. The Master said, "There is someone else still. The student said, "Teacher, do not harbor any doubt about this either.
The Master said, "Then you fall behind the *śrāmaṇera*. The student said, "As for the case where the four sides have no gates, toward what does the Old Monk turn?"
[The monk] arrived having received this news. The Master said, "Where have you come from? The monk pointed toward the east and said, "This janitor is so dark.
He then pointed toward the west and said, "This guest prefect is so fat.
The Master said, "Do not point east and draw lines west. The monk made a single stroke with his sitting cloth (zuoju) and said, "This one cannot [be avoided]."
[The Master] called out, "East and West! The monk said, "Look at you, running about so recklessly. The Master said, "Monk, keep your voice down; I fear someone might overhear.
The monk said, "You were quite unrestrained yourself just now. The Master struck his own mouth with his hand and said, "It was my own doing.
The Master then said to the assembly, "Elder Sideside has sent a letter. Before the assembly, it must be read aloud."
A great lacquer barrel on four sides. Master Xiang divided it into half-barrels. It was opened beneath White Lotus Peak;
it has perfumed my nostrils. But tell me, why is it so? There is no place for you to breathe out.

The special envoy of the Taiping era arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "Ten thousand miles without a cloud, the Great Clarity is spotless; the sun and moon of the Patriarchs' heaven are naturally clear and bright.
Taiping does not permit the General to see them, yet he permits the General to establish Taiping."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To bring forth this public case (kung-an) is to accomplish every task. To run outward in pursuit is to be a fool—a fool, a fool!
Ascending the hall again, he said: "There is a thing prior to heaven and earth; formless, it is fundamentally silent and vast.
It is the lord of all phenomena, yet it does not wither with the four seasons. When the ancients spoke thus, it was like adding flowers upon brocade—truly extraordinary. You all...
Furthermore, how do you understand this? Today, Bailian follows the capacities of later students and, not sparing even his eyebrows, has also composed a verse for them:
"Existence within existence; non-existence within non-existence; the subtle within the subtle; the coarse within the coarse."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the fifth day of the third month. This old man has nothing further to contribute. The 'Wordless' points the way with majestic dignity;
it is a pity that monks see only their own suffering. After all, how is it? It is like a person learning to shoot."
Ascending the hall, he said: "In this lovely season, the spring warmth is radiant; throughout the dust-mote universes, it is one and the same sky.

Forests and peaks are lush, competing in their verdant splendor; flowers and willows are fragrant, contending for their fresh brilliance. Butterflies play among the peonies with urgent flight; bees wander the peaches and roses, yet linger in vain.
How many times in human life does one encounter such a spring scene? Why not, within it, plant the field of merit?"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Xinghua said, "When I meet people, I do not come forth;
when I come forth, I act for the sake of others. Sansheng said, "When I meet people, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for the sake of others. The Master said:

"Of these two ancient worthies, one possessed vast and profound literary talent, while the other fully displayed martial skill. Yet, if you say Xinghua was the 'literary' one, that is not so; and if you say Sansheng..."
The Sage was neither a warrior nor a scholar; can you discern this here? If you can discern it, I grant that your entire being is life.
If you cannot discern it, you must judge for yourself.
Ascending the hall, he said: "What is Chan? The Jambu tree is on the southern shore of the sea. Near, it is not separate from the square inch of the heart;
far, it is one hundred and eight thousand miles away. Ultimately, what is it? Chan! Chan!"

Ascending the hall, he said: "The fellow with the shoulder pole for sale; the label reads 'three catties of hemp. A滞貨 (stale commodity) of hundreds or thousands of years—where can one find a place to set one's whole body?
Ascending the hall again, he said: "Today is the twentieth day of the eighth month. The two characters 'Buddha-dharma' are difficult to enter. Great and small elders in the deep village..."
"Elder, even the Patriarch Bodhidharma could not reach you.
He ascended the hall and said: "If you have not yet passed through the Patriarch’s barrier, do not ask about the Great Snow Mountain. One step is ten thousand miles;
it is a thousand hardships and ten thousand difficulties."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised this case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not?
Zhaozhou said, “No. The monk said, “All sentient beings possess Buddha-nature; why does the dog alone lack it? Zhaozhou said, “Because it has karmic consciousness remaining.
The Master said, “Great assembly, how do you all usually understand this? As for me, I usually...”
Simply bring up the word "Mu" (無) and let it rest. If you can penetrate this single character, no one in the world will be able to do anything with you.
How will you all penetrate it? Is there anyone who has penetrated it thoroughly? If so, come forward and speak.
I do not want you to say "it exists," nor do I want you to say "it does not exist," nor do I want you to say "it is neither."
"Is there being or non-being? How do you say it? Take care.

Lü Baowen Jiawen entered the mountains. The Master ascended the hall. A monk asked: "When the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kāśyapa smiled, the Governor’s banner graced this Dharma assembly.
We pray that the Master will use skillful means to proclaim its meaning for us. The Master said: "Six ears do not share a secret."
Jin said, "One does not seek it upon the flower; its brilliance is spontaneously perfect and luminous. The Master said, "Excellent. Jin said, "It may be called 'unveiled and without partiality';
in responding and exalting [the truth], there is a standard. The Master said, "Yes. Jin said, "As for 'knowing the mechanism face-to-face,' how would you say it?"
The Master said, "You must not speak of this to others. The student stepped forward and said, "The Master knows only one part, yet does not know the other two.
The Master asked, "What do you mean? The student said, "The Patriarch, however, said that those who know come; returning to serve as salt and vinegar is precisely the right time.
The Master said, "You have spoken it correctly. The student said, "I have already received the good news from the True Man; among men..."
"There is no further doubt regarding the heavens. The Master then said: "I recall that in the past, a monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, 'Who shall obtain the robe and bowl of Huangmei?
The Patriarch replied, 'The person who understands the Buddha-dharma shall obtain them. The monk asked, 'Does the Master yourself obtain them or not?'"
The Patriarch said, "I cannot. The monk asked, "Why is it that you, Master, cannot? The Patriarch said, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma. Again, he cited:
A monk asked Xuefeng, "After you saw Deshan, what principle did you realize that you then retired from the world?
Xuefeng said, "At that time, I went empty-handed and returned empty-handed. The Master said, "Great assembly, these two venerable ones..."
Last night, one was the Patriarch and one was the Chan Master.
When questioned, they both said, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma," and further said, "I go empty-handed and return empty-handed.
Do you all understand why they spoke in such a manner? If you wish to understand their words, you must first pass through the Patriarch’s Barrier. If...
If one does not pass through the Patriarch’s barrier, one must never attempt to gaze upon it with the correct eye.
When Director Tang Si arrived at the monastery, he ascended the hall and said: "I cite the case where Sansheng asked Xuefeng, 'What does the golden fish that has passed through the net eat?
Feng replied, 'Wait until you have emerged from the net, and then I will tell you. Sansheng said, 'The fifteen hundred people..."
"Good friend, you do not even recognize the 'critical phrase' (huatou). Xuefeng said, "I am an old monk burdened by the affairs of abbotship.
Some among the assembly have claimed that because Xuefeng and Sansheng belonged to different lineages, their words did not accord; others have claimed that Sansheng was a master of the Way.
Xuefeng could not grasp its meaning. In such a discourse, what connection is there?
Suddenly, someone asked Wuzu, "What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? The old monk said to him, "A fine question," and then added:
Great assembly, tell me: are Xuefeng and this the same or different? I cannot explain it for you, but listen to this verse:
No clouds within the cave, a world apart; Peach blossoms like brocade, willows like mist. The immortals have no need to debate spring and summer;
When the rocks crumble and the pines wither, a year has passed.
A special messenger from Zifu Monastery arrived bearing a letter of dharma succession. The Master received the letter in the Dharma Hall and, picking it up, asked the messenger, "It has no name;
from where did you obtain this? The messenger hesitated. The Master said, "By whom was it brought?
He then ascended the seat. He raised the case: Shitou asked Changzi, "Where have you come from? Changzi replied, "From Lingnan."
[Shigong] came. Shitou said, "At the head of Mount Dayu, has the completion of this one set of merit been achieved yet?
Xizhong said, "It was accomplished long ago; it only lacks the dotting of the eyes. Shitou said, "Do you wish for the eyes to be dotted?
Xizhong said, "I request them at once. Shitou lowered one foot. Xizhong then prostrated. Shitou said, "What principle have you seen that you [acted thus]?"
[The student] prostrated. Xizhou said, "Like a single speck of snow upon a red-hot furnace. The Master said, "A single speck of snow on a red-hot furnace—do those who know it perceive it or not?
With a fan made of tortoise hair, one fans a mud ox; a single drop of blood."
The verse says:

Before the mountain of "Meeting the Opportunity," there lies a vast expanse of idle land. With palms joined, he earnestly asks the patriarch: "How many times have you sold it, only to have it returned to yourself?"
I have purchased it, out of pity for the pines and bamboos that draw in the pure breeze.
My mountain dwelling has a bed made of wooden beams and mats of thatch; my pillow is a coarse hemp cloth, sunken in the middle. On this desolate autumn day, a traveler has come to seek refuge.
Overnight, he slept until the break of dawn, his hands and feet entwined;

he has brought upon himself the ancient style of living within a mass of white clouds. Under the moonlight of ten thousand li of frosty skies, he is like one among rare people by the woods and waterside.
Having arrived, I finally know that the joy of my Way is inexhaustible.

To dispel my worldly impulses, I drift slowly amidst the white clouds; as a gentle breeze stirs, one realizes the ultimate nature of the creative power of the cosmos—who can fathom its beginning and its end?
Having investigated this, since it cannot be resolved, one needlessly indulges in self-pity and joy.
One hears the deep, lingering sound of the cold horn as it blares from a solitary city; ten li away on the mountain peaks, things gradually grow dim, yet this single kind of sound is boundless.
The mind: there is that which is capable of listening and that which is incapable of listening.
When illness arises and manifests, the skin clings to the bones; when one stirs and rises, not a single thing remains. One cannot take a step in walking, and the voice for speech—
Low. The nostrils remain as before, starkly protruding.
Within the mountains, amidst the four modes of deportment, he walks;
carrying a basket to gather bracken, he expresses his secluded sentiments. After the cowherd has finished singing the "Hu Family" tune, the cuckoo perches on its branch.
The first line:

Dwelling in the mountains, who could be my companion amidst these myriad layers and thousandfold peaks? Even if a true connoisseur were to come specifically seeking me out, the clouds are so deep that there would surely be no place to find me.
Sitting in the mountains, under a moonlit night, the frosty sky is cold as geese pass by. The ashes in the brazier have been stirred through, yet I cannot sleep;
the dawn-calling bird alerts my ears.

Lying in the mountains, a single expanse of pure light reflects me from on high. If only body and mind could find leisure wherever they go, [this] many years’ coarse cloth [robe]— (Note: The final line "多年布" appears to be a fragment, likely the beginning of a phrase such as "多年布衲" [many years' coarse cloth robe], which is left untranslated here as it is incomplete.)
Let this patchwork robe be torn asunder by the teachings.
I praise the late Master Baiyun:
the true moon is in the sky, its reflection contained within all waters. Yet the reality of that true master is neither the moon nor the water—blue, yellow, azure, and green.
A chaotic blur. Looking at it, one sees half-anger and half-joy.
I praise Master Si-zu Yan for his "aged yellow plum" within the osmanthus package;
it does not bloom upon the ground of yin and yang. How could bees and butterflies know its fragrance travels so far?
To dismantle [this state]: it is difficult to trace his path as he goes and returns.
He praises himself for having dim eyes and deaf ears; his gait is faltering and decrepit. Before others, he forces a smile; with palms joined at his chest, he stands there.
I have composed two self-portraits in eulogy to capture the form through form;
yet all is but illusion and delusion. To seek the Real by means of the Real only results in further estrangement from it. This realization constitutes a public case (gong'an).
There is no task that cannot be accomplished. Throughout the three hundred and sixty thousand days of a hundred-year life, turning over and over, it is always this very same fellow.
I am truly I; I praise myself. Only one knows oneself. Face to face, staring at one another, when will there ever be an end?
In the master’s quarters, he would often cite Zhaozhou’s “Does a dog have Buddha-nature? to which Zhaozhou replied, “No.
When a monk asked for an explanation, the master composed this verse for him:
Zhaozhou’s sword with its blade bared, Its cold frost and blazing flames. If you intend to ask further how it is, Your body shall be split in two.
On Teaching Zen, Two Poems To study the Way, one must first find the point of return.
Hearing sounds and seeing forms are inconceivable; The long sky holds its moon night after night in every house.
How many know that its reflection falls upon the clear pool?
The Way of the Patriarchs differs from no other; the path of the world is level. When people walk upon it, there is no need for alarm.
Before the mind can even conceive of reaching the goal, one has already moved forward—just like Xuansha when he questioned Jingqing about the mirror.
Four Verses for Instructional Disciples:
Those who study the Way are few in number who attain it; how long will disputes over right and wrong and matters of length and brevity persist?
If one relies on words to debate superiority and inferiority, it is exactly like the time before one had attained awakening.
All who travel the path reach the Gate of Emptiness; only those who arrive know its flavor is long-lasting.
When the mind-ground produces no idle weeds, the body naturally emits white light from the ūrṇā-kośa.
A single expanse of autumn light faces my thatched cottage; by the fence, the golden chrysanthemums already waft their fragrance.
Before the cicadas have ceased their song, a cool breeze arises—far superior to the traveler returning to his native land.
Spending the whole day discussing the mystery of the primary school; one seeks the traces of fish within a dried-up riverbed.
Even if there were no stages for the patriarchs and Buddhas, one must still pass through the staff of the extraordinary man.
Having seen off the two Chan practitioners, Ji and De, to Chang’an, their two companions joined hearts in their mission;

their righteousness was as indestructible as tempered steel. Such instances have occurred throughout antiquity and the present; my Way is capable of sustaining them. They are as steadfast and profound as a mountain.
The abyss of the ocean is deep; white clouds cannot linger there. Even the Patriarchs and Buddhas could not restrain it. Gazing to the limit, Shaolin stands steeply aloft;
looking on from the side, Mount Hua rises with its jagged peaks. Having received the teaching of Vimalakīrti’s pointing at the finger, let us play a single melody to seek out those who understand.
Lamenting Master Sengyan, the Fourth Patriarch, who fell ill here and entered parinirvāṇa there:
what gain or loss is there for our school? Birth and death are like flowers in the sky; going and coming are like the tracks of birds.
The eastern peak suddenly sinks into the west; its shadow hangs upon the cold walls of the hall. The thirty-three heavens strike the imperial bell;
together we recite the Prajñāpāramitā.
In mourning for Master Qing of Touzi.
Clouds atop the Peak of Tranquil Abiding scatter as water over Caoxi’s stream; The sail of the floating ferry is hoisted high, sailing straight into the great ocean.
Now that the conditions for its transport have ended, a wild wind arose last night: A girl with hair like hanging horns wears a jade flower;
An eighty-year-old old man puts on embroidered shoes.
Lamenting Chan Master Fudu Yuanjian:
Before the cliffs of Mount Fudu stand slender, green cypresses; Their dense trunks rise high, manifesting a noble character. Tonight, their cold shadows fall upon the western lanes;
Who sings the eighteen strains of the Hu-pipa?
In mourning for the Great Master Chongsheng, bitter mist shrouds the courtyard eaves; sorrowful clouds lock the twilight sky. The Master has returned to the realm of true purity;
his shadow hangs by the solitary, full moon. Gone yet not gone, like a dream; coming yet not coming, who is first and who is last? Who is first and who is last? The Jambu tree.
On the border of Hainan, I mourn for the son of Chen Jixian, who has already chosen to relocate his residence.
This is the foremost pivot of the Chan school: the sail is not hoisted upon the mast; the path of non-abiding is vast and level.
