it does not take a person's head from above, nor does it take a person's waist from the middle, nor does it take a person's feet from below—without even a moment’s hesitation."
"If you can bite him to death, you have succeeded. A monk asked, "What is the White Marsh Dog? The Master [Baizhang] made the sound of a dog barking.
The monk said, "That is still just a dung-eating dog. The Master asked, "What is the dog that bites people? The monk grabbed the corner of his robe and brushed it away;
the Master then struck him. The Master [Zhaozhou] said: "Baizhang said, 'If you can bite him to death, then stop. But tell me—"
The monk brushed him away; Zhao struck him. Who won and who lost? Zhao’s response was much like a medicine bag dangling behind a funeral carriage.
There was also a monk who asked, "What is the Dog of Shending? To which he replied, "Who dares lean against the gate or stand by the door?"
The monks prostrated themselves. [The Master] said to them, "Shending was also very dangerous. A monk then requested further instruction on these words.
The Master said, "At that time, I wanted someone who would not spare their own life or limb;
even until now, no one has been able to satisfy my intention. You two, reveal some news! The monks hesitated. The Master said, "Dead!"
Small Assembly Sermon. He raised an example, saying: "Baizhang Huaihai said to the assembly: 'After this old monk has passed away, I shall become a water buffalo on the mountain below.
On its left flank, I will have written: "The monk so-and-so of Mount Gui.
At that very moment, if you call me the monk of Mount Gui, I am still the water buffalo; if you call me the water buffalo, I am still the monk of Mount Gui. Now, what shall one do?'"
After deliberating, the Master then offered this verse: "I do not say it is not Mount Huai, nor do I say it is not the ox. If you recognize them, where would there be any source?
One must clearly understand how they are rent asunder; Once understood, it is like a boat that is unmoored."
[The Master] raised [the topic]. Shimen addressed the assembly, saying: "The home mountain is good; the home mountain is good. Within the home mountain there is rootless grass;
from the pure source, extraordinary grasses vie in fragrance. A single peal of spring thunder shakes the Way of the Golden Immortal.
The Master said: "What is this spring thunder? Can you explain it for the sake of the great assembly? He let out a shout and descended from his seat.
Small Assembly Sermon. It is said: Nanquan ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The *maṇi* jewel, people do not recognize it;
it is intimately held within the *tathāgatagarbha*. I do not ask about the jewel; what is the *garbha*? Nanquan said, "It is that which comes and goes with you. The monk said:
"How is it with that which neither goes nor comes? Quan said, "That too is the casket. The monk asked, "What is the jewel?
Quan called to the monk; the monk responded. Quan said, "You do not understand my meaning. The Master then offered this verse:
He asked about the *maṇi* jewel; where does the *maṇi* reside? When the name is called, there is the responding voice. Do not misrepresent this in any direction.
Small Assembly (Xiaocan). The Master raised a case: A monk asked Fengxue, "What is the first phrase? Fengxue said, "The three essentials open the seal;
the vermilion dot is narrow, allowing no room for deliberation—therein the host and guest are distinguished. The Master followed this with a shout. "What is the second phrase?"
Xue said: "How could a wondrous understanding fail to accommodate the question of Wuzhuo? How could Upāya fail to respond to the 'cutting-off-the-flow' mechanism?
The Master added his own words: "Before the question was even asked, it was already wrong. "What is the third phrase? Xue said: "Just look at the puppets being manipulated on the stage."

"The pulling and the extracting are both within the person. The Master added a comment: "If one attempts to explain it through intellectual penetration, it is inadequate. Therefore, Master Shoushan said:
"If you realize the first phrase, you become a teacher to the Buddhas and patriarchs. If you realize the second phrase, you become a teacher to humans and devas.
If you realize the third phrase, you cannot even save yourself. He further said: "Even saving yourself is not enough."
The Master said: "Shending also had someone ask him: 'What is the first phrase? He replied: 'Heaven! Heaven!
'What is the second phrase? He replied: 'What do you have, you donkey-headed fellow? 'What is the third phrase? He replied: 'Come closer, and I will tell you.
As soon as the man approached, he struck him. If you can understand it in this way, you will not have brought shame upon the Patriarchs."
"Coming from the West—if one were to question this point by point from the very beginning, when would one ever find rest?
The Buddha-dharma is not a principle of smoothing edges or fitting seams. To speak in such a vein requires that one have long been within the wind of another’s gate.
One must truly detest the Buddha for not acting and detest the Dharma for not speaking; only then can one be so meticulous. Be careful."
Small Lecture. The Master raised [the following]: An ancient said, "This day has passed, and life likewise diminishes accordingly;
like a fish in scant water, what joy can there be in this? The Master said: "When the ancients spoke thus, it was neither for the sake of benefit nor for the sake of non-benefit.
Shending, however, does not agree. This day has passed, and life likewise diminishes accordingly; like a fish in scant water, why should there not be joy? But tell me—"
Contrary to the ancients; in accord with the ancients—try to examine this for yourself. Be careful. To cite an ancient:
A monk asked Shoushan, "How is it when not a single hair has yet emerged? Shoushan said, "Meeting a person with pierced ears on the road. [The monk] said, "Once it has emerged..."
[The Master asked: "What is it like after? Sanshan said: "There is no need for further hesitation. Once, a monk asked Shending: "What is it like when not even a single hair has been stirred?
Shending simply said to him: "On top of White Cloud Ridge. [The Master asked: "What is it like after it has been stirred? The Master said: [Shending replied: "Just as before."
The water flows in the mountain stream. The Master then said: "If it were the two previous turns of phrase, there would be something to chew upon;
one could look east and look west. But as for Shending’s words, they are like eating wooden shavings—there is truly no flavor."
"It can only be attained through one's own seeing and one's own awakening. Do you understand? The heavens are high in the southeast; the earth slopes toward the northwest.
Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Huizhong, "After a hundred years, what will you require? The Master said, "Have a seamless stupa made for this old monk.

The Emperor said, "I ask the Master for the design of the stupa. After a long silence, the Master said, "Do you understand? The Emperor said, "I do not understand. The Master [said]: "If you do not understand, then have it made."
[The Master] said, "I have a Dharma-heir disciple named Tan Yuan who understands this matter. Hereafter, simply ask this man.

After the National Teacher passed away, the Emperor issued an imperial decree to question Tan Yuan. Tan Yuan also remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you understand? The Emperor replied, "I do not understand."
Yuan had a verse: "South of Xiang, north of Tan, in between there is gold filling the entire land; beneath the shadowless tree, the boat is joined together;
upon the lapis lazuli hall, there is no one with knowledge. The Master said, "The National Teacher previously acted in such a manner."
They could not understand it clearly. Next, he asked Danyuan. Yuan offered this verse; tell me, is it complete or incomplete?
Although it constitutes a skillful means, one must realize its underlying meaning before it can be attained. Do you understand? Shending will provide four alternative responses for all of you.

To the south of Xiang and to the north of Tan, the Master said: "There is a path for sovereign and subject. "Within it, gold fills the entire land," the Master said: "The pure and wondrous essence is eternal.
"Beneath the shadowless tree, they board the same boat," the Master said: "A thousand sages share the same track.

"In the crystal palace, there is no one with knowledge," the Master said: "The paths of the mundane and the sagely are severed. The Master said: "If you understand it in this way, you will certainly..."
"Not deceiving one another. Shendeng’s commentary like this merely fails the National Teacher.
When King Ma invited Master Yun of Shimen to reside at Jiaoshan, the imperial carriage went out to receive him. The King himself asked, "What is the Great Way that came from the West?

Yun replied, "The Imperial Chariot with its Six Dragons is a marvel of a thousand ages; the Jade Street lines the staff as it emerges from the Golden Gate. The Master said, "In one sense, they are the same..."
"Answering the king and his ministers with such great composure—how vast and expansive is this samādhi! Why is that?

To answer in such a manner not only does one not fail the great purpose of the Westward Journey, but one is also skillfully able to employ 'reciprocal interplay' (huìhù). Within this, though the matters and principles may be as they are, if someone were to ask Shending:"
"What is the Great Way that came from the West? He replied, "Walking. Now tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different?
Long-time practitioners of Chan will find a point of insight within these words of Shendeng; yet even those of immeasurable capacity often fail to grasp them. A monk asked Master Dage:
"A crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt does not fire its trigger for the sake of a small mouse. Suddenly—

"If one encounters a person who possesses the power to kill or give life at will, what then? Guo said, "When King Han first entered the Hongmen banquet, it was only when Xiang Zhuang brandished his sword that the peril became known.
He also said, "Dan Xiong alone could handle the jujube-wood spear; Wei Chi followed behind him singing a foreign song. The Master said, "If someone were to ask this, [one would say]:
'A crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt does not trigger its mechanism for a mere mouse. Suddenly encountering..."
"When someone who has attained the great power of killing and giving life comes, what do you do?
Shending immediately said to him, "A crossbow of a thousand *jin* does not release its trigger for the sake of a field mouse.

Someone once asked Shending, "A crossbow of a thousand *jin* does not release its trigger for the sake of a field mouse," to which he replied, "Alala! Alala! When that monk hesitated, Shending struck him across the back with his staff.
[The Master] struck him. Let me ask you all: what is the principle here? You must know that the "house style" (家风) of each lineage differs; you should investigate this thoroughly.
National Teacher Zhong asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From the South.

The Teacher asked, "What Dharma do the teachers of the South use to instruct people? He said, "The teachers of the South say: one day, when wind and fire disperse and extinguish [the body], it is like..."
"A snake sheds its skin; like a dragon changing its bones, the original true nature remains perfectly intact. Guo said, "Alas! Alas!
In the South, the Buddha-dharma is half-born and half-extinguished. The monk then asked, "I wonder, Master, how is it here?"
Guo said, "In this state of mine, body and mind are as one; there is nothing else outside the body.
The monk asked, "How can you equate this illusory, bubble-like body with the Dharma-body? Guo said, "Why have you entered onto a deviant path?
The monk asked, "In what way have I entered a deviant path? Guo said, "Have you not seen it stated in the teachings: 'If one sees me by means of form'?"
"To seek me through sound and voice—such people walk a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata. The Master said:
"If one judges by this monk’s words, he does not even understand how to deliver a message; he merely brings trouble upon the masters of the South.

Yet, even according to the National Teacher’s own words, they are like a dragon’s head with a snake’s tail. Previously, when it was said that 'body and mind are as one,' where did that go? Try to examine this!"
Take care. A small *seng* (informal discourse). To cite: While Guishan and Yangshan were walking, Guishan asked Yangshan, "What is that up ahead?
Yangshan said, "A withered tree. Guishan then asked an old farmer tilling the field; the farmer also said, "A withered tree. Guishan said, "This field..."
Later, Old Man [Tanhui] also guided a community of five hundred. The Master said: "Does his intention lie with Yun-tian Old Man?
Or does it lie with Yangshan? Or is it that he was not like this at all? All you venerable seniors, even though all dharmas are thus, there is no need to give rise to further affairs.
This is the conversation between father and son; only those on the same path will understand. Be careful. A monk asked an ancient worthy:
From afar he came to seek a teacher, requesting the teacher to receive him. Deyun said: "The golden rings on both legs ring out clearly;
this is the personal trace of the Tathāgata’s precious staff. Do you understand? There is questioning and there is answering, yet it is rare to meet one who truly knows.

He then asked another virtuous elder: "From afar he came to seek a teacher, requesting the teacher to receive him. The elder said: "Earth gushes forth water from no source; a stone man rides upon a boat."
"Boat. The Master said: "Is this statement the same as the one spoken previously, or is it different?
Although it is but a single teaching style (*ménfēng*), you must first understand where these venerable ancestors launched their speech before you can succeed.

What is 'earth-surging water from no source' and 'the stone man piloting the boat of compassion'? Do you understand? The sea is vast and there is no boat, yet coming and going are never obstructed. Be careful! Nan.
Quan said, "At eighteen, I already knew how to make a living. Zhaozhou said, "At eighteen, I already knew how to break up the family and scatter the household.
You tell me: is it better to break up the family and scatter the household, or is it better to know how to make a living? This is for those who are beginners."

Furthermore, to follow up on what was said before: one who has long been a practitioner of the depths must truly "break the house and scatter the home. If there is even one more word, it is ten thousand miles to Yuzhou.
A monk asked Shimen, "What is the master’s family style? Shimen said, "He knows how to tend the rootless tree."
[He] was able to pick out the lamp from the bottom of the sea. Later, that monk entered the room and asked, "I, your student, do not understand the meaning of picking out the lamp;

I pray the Master will provide a skillful means to guide me who am rootless. Yunmen said, "Jia Dao picks out ancient tones with his pen; as for the place where the pen touches down, who can discern it?
He also said, "It is difficult to meet one who knows the sound. When Shending initially asked, "What is 'one who knows the sound'? Yunmen said, "When you encounter..."

"Welcoming straightforward words, he raises his three-year-old son; singing a folk song from Ba, they travel by different paths. He further composed a verse: "Formless and signless is the Great Awesome Power;
To receive all living beings, he extends his hand again and again. The Bird Path does not obstruct the essence of the perfect mirror; The golden sun constantly emerges from the eastern gate.
The Master said: "Shimen speaks thus and composes a verse thus. Do you understand the house style of Shimen?"
After a long silence, he said: "The golden bird constantly emerges from the eastern gate; take care. Master Liangshan Guan’s verse on his realization of the Way says:
"The precious treasure of former times was buried by dust; For what reason does it emerge today from its old store? To study the Way is to delight in the ineffable phrase;
Penetrating the mystery is not a matter of mental conjecture. A single incense stick of fixed radiance illuminates the Dharma-realm; Ten thousand layers of dust-locks [are now opened]."
Suddenly enlightened, transcending the present and differing from the past, it is ultimately difficult to describe. Fortunately, the Western Hu has come here for no other reason.
The Master said, "Venerable elders, when the ancients spoke thus, what was their intent? Let me ask you all: what is the precious treasure of former times?
Try to speak for the assembly; if you can speak it, Shending will reward you with its price. But if you cannot..."
It cannot be attained; it is like excrement and soil.
Having stood for a long time, I shall now give a brief instruction. "The wind does not rustle the branches; the rain does not break the clods of earth"—let us stop there for now.
How can you perform a somersault that reaches the Brahma Heaven? If there is anyone who can, come forward and display your skill. Is there such a one? Do not let the Emperor... [be deceived].
[The Master] said, "Śakra was provoked to anger. Later, when a monk entered the room, that person came out at once, turned to the left once, and returned to the assembly.
The Master asked, "If Śakra had not been provoked to anger, how would you have handled it? The monk said, "Those who recognize kindness are few;
those who betray it are many. The Master said, "You’ve struck right on the nose!"
Question: According to the occasion, how is one a "guest among guests"? The Master said: "Blind. Question: How is one a "host among guests"? The Master said: "It is as if blind. Question:
How is one a "guest among hosts"? The Master said: "I give you thirty blows. Question: How is one a "host"? The Master said: "..."
Zhongzhu. The Master said, "Yes, understood. Question: "What is the phrase for receiving those of initial capacity? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth."
Question: What is the phrase for discerning a monk? The Master said: "Seven blows in response to thirteen. Question:
What is the phrase for the true command being put into action? The Master said: "Not even a blink is permitted. Question: What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth?
The Master said: "How do you intend to understand it? Question: An ancient said, "At Vulture Peak they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon. What is this?
Zhenyue asked, “Master, [what is it like when] the six states have not yet been pacified? The Master said, “Speak. [He] asked, “What about after they have been pacified?
The Master said, “It would cry out until people were killed. [He] asked, “When one searches within and without and finds not a single thing, what is it like?
The Master said, “The moon is like a drawn bow; there is little rain and much wind. [He] asked, “What is it like at an ancient stream with cold spring water? The Master said, “Not.”
"This is the place where patch-robed monks practice. [The monk] asked: "What is the place where patch-robed monks practice? The Master said:
"I do not see the ancient stream or the cold spring. [The monk] asked: "Regarding the saying, 'A torch before every door,' what is its meaning?

The Master said: "The four seasons and the eight festivals. [The monk] asked: "When the question does not turn, how is it? The Master said: "Right now, is it turning or not turning? [The monk] said: "Thank you for your response."
He further pierced through [the point]. The Master said: "The path of awakening throughout one’s entire being is profound. A question was asked:

"As for those who transmigrate through the six realms, what is their ultimate state? The Master said: "They do not wish to become Buddhas. [The questioner] said: "Why do they not wish to become Buddhas? The Master said: "Even Buddhahood is not ultimate.
[The questioner] said: "Please grant me a word. The Master said: "Yesterday I still remember it; today the words have no gate. A question was asked: "Not..."

[The Master] said, "When one bestows a mere inch of blade and immediately ascends to the position of the Nine-Five (the Emperor), what is it like? The Master said, "The seas are calm and the rivers are clear.

[The questioner] asked, "What is it like regarding the affairs of governance and transformation? The Master said, "In ten thousand households there are no door-locks; they drum their bellies in harmony with the Great Peace.

[The questioner] asked, "When meeting a man who has attained the Way on the road, what is it like? The Master said, "He has been thoroughly scrutinized. [The questioner] asked, "When a student intends to enter the sea, what is it like? The Master said, "The sea arises."

Hai. [The student] said, "If that is so, then I am entirely sustained by this power of grace. The Master said, "When the black wind blows and the rākṣasas appear, turning the light back within brings about the wondrous.

[The student] asked, "What is it like when day and night do not cease? The Master said, "Who is it that does not cease? [The student] asked, "What is it like when the halberds are cast down and the armor is laid aside?
The Master said, "Great merit is not rewarded with a banner. [The student] said, "I beg the Master to grant me his original favor. The Master said, "Withdraw."
Question: "What is it like when one is on a single horse with a solitary spear? The Master said: "Shendeng beats the drum. [The monk] asked: "Ultimately, what is the matter? The Master said:
"I suspect you do not possess such skillful means. Question: "I do not ask about Bodhi and Nirvana; as for the matter of wearing horns and being covered in fur, how is that?
The Master said: "That is not a matter within the scope of you, Venerable Sir. [The monk] asked: "What, then, is within the scope of this student?"

[The student] asked about the matter above. The Master said, "I will tell you only when you have reached this stage. [The student] asked, "What is it like at such a time? The Master said, "Step back three paces.
[The student] asked, "When the two kings meet, what is it like? The Master said, "Crawling on knees and moving on elbows.
[The student] said, "In that case, everything returns to a single lord. The Master said, "The world is vast and wide. [The student] asked, "As for 'Solitary in the Crimson Sky'..."
[The student] asked, "How is it when walking? The Master said, "This old monk simply watches until it is seen through. [The student] asked, "What is it like after it has been seen through?
The Master said, "Give me back the head of the phrase! [The student] asked, "An ancient said: 'Those who come before noon can be made by the wooden man to turn his head.'"
Those who come after noon: the wooden man calls, yet they do not turn their heads. At the very hour of noon, is it by calling? Or is it by not calling? The Master said:
"The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. A questioner asked: "I do not ask about before the lighting of the lamp, nor do I ask about after the lighting of the lamp.
What is the moment of the lamp being lit? The Master said: "A single wheel of light, blazing bright; from ancient times to the present, there has been no darkness. A questioner asked:
[Question: "How was it before all dharmas had been heard? [Master: "The wind whistles; the rain falls. [Question: "How is it after they have been heard?
[Master: "It is good to understand the saying. [Question: "How is it when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water? [Master: "A thousand mountains and ten thousand waters."

[The student] asked: "What is it like after emerging from the water? The Master said: "Ten thousand waters and ten thousand mountains. [The student] asked: "What is it like when the ancient sail has not yet been raised? The Master said: "It has already reached the shore.
[The student] asked: "What is it like after reaching the shore? The Master said: "Still a dull-witted fellow. [The student] asked:

"What is it like when the lion has not yet emerged from its den? The Master said: "Roar! [The student] asked: "What is it like after emerging from the den? The Master said: "Silence. [The student] asked: "What about the fish?"

[The monk asked: "How is it before the drum has sounded? The Master said: "Look at the sky; look at the earth. [The monk] asked: "How is it after it has sounded? The Master said: "Holding the bowl, he ascends the hall. [The monk] asked:
"How was it, Reverend, before you had seen the former masters? The Master said: "Walking east, walking west. [The monk] asked: "How is it now? The Master said: "I am just like this."
[The monk] asked, “How is it after [seeing it]? The Master said, “Carrying my staff slung across my shoulder. [The monk] asked, “How was it before Bodhidharma had come?

The Master said, “Western India and this land. [The monk] said, “How is it after he came? The Master said, “This land and Western India. [The monk] asked, “How was it when the precious sword had not yet emerged from its scabbard?
The Master said, “Wolves’ smoke rises in competition. [The monk] said, “How is it after it has emerged? The Master said, “Peace throughout the world.”
"Level. A question was asked: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "Heaven knew; Earth knew. [The monk] asked: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said:
"There was still a slight difference. A question was asked: "How was it before the Venerable had seen the former masters? The Master said: [Silence].
"Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. [The student] asked: "After seeing this, what then? The Master said: "The sun, moon, and stars. [The student] asked:

"When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then? The Master said: "The Buddha is also dust. [The student] asked: "Before the flowers of awakening have blossomed, how does one discern the reality?
The Master said: "Winter is cold and summer is hot. He also said: "In the cold weather, one shivers from the cold. [The student] asked: "Offering with both hands to the Honored Hall..."
"How is it at such a time? The Master said, "What is it? Question: "When a student reaches the Treasure Mountain and returns empty-handed, what then?
The Master said, "The thirtieth day of the twelfth month. Question: "I do not ask about wearing horns and donning fur; but as for the precious sword emerging from its scabbard, how is that?
The Master said, "Your question is quite clear. [The student] said, "In that case, the law is so strict there are no subjects left. The Master said, "You know."

This was the special procedure at that time for one capable of serving as a *ācārya*. A question was asked: "What is it like when the three vehicles fail to draw them out? The Master said, "Excellent. [The questioner] said:
“What is the meaning? The Master said, “You should rejoice in yourself. He asked, “What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, “When hungry, one does not choose the food.
He added, “When meeting someone, do not extend your hand; there are three carts outside the gate. He asked, “What is the mechanism for receiving people?
The Master said, “Come after the meal, and I will tell you. [The student] said, “Why do you not [tell me] right now?”
The monk followed the sound with a shout. The Master said, "Excellent. The monk bowed. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows.
A monk asked, "What is the Master’s phrase for benefiting others? The Master said, "Gathering firewood and selecting vegetables.

The monk said, "Is it not just this very thing? The Master said, "You must be even more discerning. A monk asked, "What is the Master’s phrase for discerning a patch-robed monk? The Master held up his staff.
[The monk] bowed with his fists together and asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this; how is it? The Master said, "You have indeed analyzed it well.

When the Master was among the assembly, a monk asked, "In the future, whose tune will you, Venerable One, sing? The Master said, "Holding a stringless lute in hand, riding a cow while drumming on its hoof.
A monk asked, "What is the livelihood of a man of the Way? The Master said, "Since my youth, I have never entered [the marketplace]."
At the Study Hall. A question was asked: "How is it that you save beings and benefit all life? The Master said: "You have a question; I, this mountain monk, have an answer.
Question: "What is the Master’s profound depth? The Master said: "The wattle gate is not closed; let those who come and go do as they please. [The student] said: "..."
"May I ask if you permit people to approach you closely? The Master said, "For now, understand the previous dialogue. The official pointed to a wooden fish and asked, "What is this?
The Master said, "It awakens how many drowsy people! The official said, "I have not come here for nothing."
The Master said, "Strike the mindless with the mindless. A question was asked: "An ancient said, 'One can graft the rootless tree and light the lamp at the bottom of the sea.
What is the rootless tree? The Master said, "Unknown in daily use. "What is the lamp at the bottom of the sea?
The Master said, "Piercing to the very marrow. Question: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "Ash on the head and dust on the face. "Why is this so?"
[The monk] said, “It is like this. The Master said, “How can you blame me? [The monk] asked, “I do not know for certain:
is there anything further beyond the Dharma-body? The Master said, “There is. [The monk] asked, “What is this matter that lies beyond? The Master said, “The golden crown atop the head of Vairocana.”
Question: "If one has killed one's father or mother, one may repent before the Buddha. But where does one repent for killing a Buddha or a Patriarch?
The Master said: "As the water rises, the boat grows high. Question: "What is the essence of True Suchness (Tathatā)? The Master said: "Suchness is unmoving. Question:
"What is the function of True Suchness? The Master said: "Cut! Question: "When one sees the horn over the wall, one already knows it is an ox. When one sees smoke across the mountain..."
[The monk] said, "I know it is fire. Not seeing its horns over the wall—what is it? The Master said, "Do not ask me that.
[The monk] asked, "One spreads the seven flowers of purity to bathe this stainless person. Since he is already a stainless person, why does he bathe?"
The Master said, "Even purity is not established. A monk asked, "Since the Bodhi tree is fundamentally non-existent, from where could its fruit come? The Master said, "Can you call it 'non-existent'?
A monk asked, "When the Bodhisattva Dhṛtarāṣṭra repaired the road, he was equal to the Buddha; when you, Master, repair the bridge, to whom are you equal?

Ascending the hall again, he raised an example, citing Master Xuedou: "One question and one answer—there is still something left undone.
Even if the entire universe, with its heavens, earth, grasses, trees, and forests, were all transformed into monks who, with one voice and in unison, posed hundreds of thousands of questions..."

[The monk] said, "Difficult! It would not require this old monk to snap his fingers even once for [the answer] to be universally applicable across high and low, without any discrepancy between before and after.

The Master said, "Cuiyan is not like that. Suppose the entire universe and the dust motes within it were all transformed into monks, each posing a different question—one by one—and I were to say to them all: 'Do you many monks have any blood beneath your skin?'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "To exert one's utmost effort for the sake of the assembly brings disaster from within the private door.

He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he said: "The bell is struck and the drum beaten to gather the assembly; as the various seniors come up and go down, the son inherits the father’s vocation."
"How many people has he deceived!

[The Master] ascended the hall and raised the verse by Panshan, saying: "Light does not illuminate the object; the object, moreover, does not exist. When both light and object are forgotten, what is this thing?
The Master then held up his whisk and said: "The radiant light of all the Buddhas of the dust-motes is entirely contained right here."
I have pierced through the hearts, livers, five viscera, spleens, stomachs, and gallbladders of you all. Do not speak of this before fellow monks;
take great care to guard your mouths. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Small Assembly. Addressing the assembly, he said: "A single blow rings out with crystalline clarity; its resonance thunders through the universe.

As soon as those who know the sound incline their ears, Xiang Yu has already crossed to the east of the river. To understand it thus is precisely to mistake the pommel of a donkey’s saddle for one’s father’s chin.
Small Assembly. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Among the monastics there are extraordinary people; among the laypeople there are also extraordinary people.
The Imperial Court’s Minister of the Board of Sacrifices, Yang Yi, composed a verse which says: "The eight-cornered millstone runs through the void; The golden-maned lion transforms into a dog."
"If you wish to hide your body within the Big Dipper, you must join your palms behind the Southern Dipper. The Master said, "Do you understand?
One verse has been broadcast throughout all quarters, sealing the mouths of the patch-robed monks. He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The phrase that exists and the phrase that does not exist are like a vine leaning against a tree. When the tree falls, the vine withers. Just recognize the very point where the root has fallen.

Ascending the hall again, he said: "The mist rolls away and the clouds disperse; the mountains and rivers reveal their sublime beauty. Without harming the meaning of things, the Persian takes off his hat."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Coarse words and subtle speech alike all return to the primary meaning. Every day you elders come up here;
this old monk tells dreams to deceive and intimidate everyone. Even so, the son inherits the father’s trade—how many people has he not deceived to death?
He descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Ten Stages are heart-stirring; those of the Two Vehicles cannot fathom it. With copper heads and iron brows, he struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
Ascending the hall again, he said: "Sitting upright and composed, one measures one's feet to buy boots; looking left and right, not even a single coin is required."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient precedent: "The former Cuiyan said, 'For an entire summer, I have been engaging in idle chatter with you monks, speaking here and there.
Look—do my eyebrows still remain? Baofu said, 'The heart of a thief is always apprehensive. The Master said, "Why is it so?
When one receives an ox from another, one returns a horse to them. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the depths of the great ocean, they stand in formation; from the very beginning, the second has graying hair at his temples.
Why does it not say that the first has graying hair at his temples? Do you wish to understand? Golden stamens and silver filaments form the jade dew;
the eminent monk does not sit upon the Phoenix Terrace. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Vertically exhausting the three periods of time, horizontally pervading the ten directions—when picked up, even Śakra is startled;
when set down, even the Earth Deity trembles with fear. When neither picked up nor set down, what do you call it? He himself replied, "A frog. Then he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If there were a *śrāvaka*, they would not wait for even a single ray of light. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall again, he said:
"The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it; the *mārjāra* (the cat) and the *gaurī* (the white cow) instead know it. He then picked up his whisk and said:
"The *mārjāra* and the *gaurī* are all here, emitting light and shaking the earth. Why is this so? Because..."
The sections differ. [The Master] descends from his seat.
Entering the hall, he says: "When Deshan entered the gate, he would strike with his staff; when Linji entered the gate, he would shout. Here at Cuoyan, it is not so.
At the triple gate, I would give you thirty blows of the staff. Why is this? Because applying both the staff and the shout simultaneously is already..."
"Excessive! Both ancient and modern commentators have praised this to the point of over-elaboration. When neither of the two paths is traversed, upon what basis can one speak?
A Persian from the South Sea presented an elephant tusk.

[He descends from his seat. He ascends the hall and says: "The assembly has gathered and settled. This 'ready-made' public case is also something that cannot be resolved through calculation. [He descends from his seat.]
Ascending the hall, he lifted up the incense casket and said, "The bright side and the dark side meet in harmony. If you can speak [thus], you may roam freely throughout the world.
If you cannot speak [thus], then close it for now. He descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To have no oil in the sand is a pitiable matter; it is like Chuiyan chewing his food to feed an infant.

When you understand the true nature of good and evil at that time, you will realize for the first time that your face was covered in ashes all along. He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
Because Zhang Yichang from Junzhou arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "I have long thought of the scholar Zhang; we have been parted for over ten months.
Today you have come up the mountain with an iron bowl to cook wild ferns. When you return to Junyang, simply speak in this manner."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "It is said that all conditioned phenomena are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. Please, Master, point out the reality.
The Master said, "The two parts are different; the subsequent text is long. Another asked, "If your entire body is eyes, where is your mouth?"
The Master said, "Three leaps. The monk said, "I do not understand; I have come specifically to request your instruction.

The Master said, "When the autumnal lyrics of the verses have ended, the melodic tones of the song arise in spring. The Master then said, "Clouds withdrawn and mist dispelled, the mountains and rivers are white;
the bright sun freezes the waves, yet there are many paths. He then descended from his seat.
The Master cited an ancient precedent: A non-Buddhist asked the Buddha, "I do not ask about words; I do not ask about wordlessness. The World-Honored One remained seated.

The non-Buddhist said, "The World-Honored One, in his great kindness and compassion, has cleared away my clouds of delusion and allowed me to enter. The Master said, "How great was the World-Honored One!"
He was completely hoodwinked by the outsider right before his eyes. As for the outsider saying, "Let me enter," he had never even dreamed of it.
Since he had never dreamed of it, why did he attain awakening? Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, "Aside from the transmission of the golden robe, what else did the Buddha transmit?
Kāśyapa called out, "Ānanda! Ānanda responded, "Yes? Kāśyapa said, "Throw it away."
[The Master] placed it on the banner-pole in front of the gate. The Master said: "A thousand-year-old tree with no shadow; boots that reach nowhere in this age.
An Immortal of the Five Supernatural Powers asked the Buddha: "The Buddha possesses six supernatural powers, while I possess five. What is that one power?
The Buddha called out to the Immortal of the Five Supernatural Powers. The Immortal responded, "Yes? The Buddha said: "That one power—ask me about it. The Master said: "The Five Supernatural Powers."
The immortal asked thus; the Buddha answered thus. Yet, for the time being, one does not understand even a single point of it.
The Patriarch asked the boy, "From where have you come? The boy said, "My mind has not gone anywhere. The Patriarch said, "Where do you dwell? The boy said:
“My mind does not cease,” the boy said. The Patriarch said, “You have no fixedness. The boy said, “All Buddhas are likewise so. The Patriarch said, “You are not the Buddhas.
The boy said, “The Buddhas are also not [the Buddhas]. The Master said: “The Patriarch asked one question and the boy gave one answer;
together they both lacked understanding. How do you all understand it now? King Kasmira, brandishing his sword, questioned the Honored Lion.

The King asked, "Have you attained the emptiness of the aggregates? He replied, "I have already attained the emptiness of the aggregates. The King said, "Have you also transcended birth and death? He replied, "I have already transcended birth and death. The King said, "Since you have transcended birth and death, you must give me your head. He replied, "My body is not mine; how much less so my head? The King struck him off, whereupon white milk rose several feet high, and the King's own arm fell off. The Master said: *** The Master said: "The King asked, 'Have you attained the emptiness of the aggregates? He replied, 'I have already attained the emptiness of the aggregates.
The King said, 'Have you also transcended birth and death? He replied, 'I have already transcended birth and death.

The King said, 'Since you have transcended birth and death, you must give me your head. He replied, 'My body is not mine; how much less so my head? The King struck him off, whereupon white milk rose several feet high, and the King's own arm fell off. The Master said:
At that time, as the Venerable One craned his neck, the King raised his blade. At such a moment, could anyone have come forth and stopped it?
To this day, no one has resolved this public case (*kōan*). How will the monks of today resolve it? Master Fu Daoshi said:

"Night after night, he sleeps embracing the Buddha; Morning after morning, they rise together again. Whether rising or sitting, they are always in each other's company, Like a shadow following a body."
"Similar. If you wish to know where the Buddha has gone, it is right here in this very sound of speech.

Xuefeng said, "The Great Master Fu was quite large, yet he recognized only that which is bright and luminous. The Master said, "Whether one recognizes it or not, next year there will be new branches again;
the wind of spring continues to trouble us without ceasing. Master Baogong sent someone to deliver a message to Dharma Master Sida, saying: "Why..."
"Without coming down from the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings, what is the point of always looking up at the Milky Way?
He thought: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp; where else could there be any sentient beings to be saved? The Master said:
"Dashi saw only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but did not see the squareness of the chisel's base. When Linji saw a monk approaching, he held up his whisk.
The monk bowed, and Jie struck him. The Master said, "This monk’s grievance was not redressed;
he died without being mourned. Now, how would you provide this monk with vindication? Master Si asked Shenhui, "Where have you come from? Shenhui replied, "From Caoxi.
Master Si asked, "What realization did you obtain at Caoxi? Shenhui straightened his body and—
Dongshan stood up. Guishan said, "There is still some rubble left. Dongshan asked, "Does the Master here have any genuine gold to give people?
Guishan said, "Even if there were, where would you put it? The Master said: "Genuine gold and rubble—these are names and phrases wrongly applied."
"What would you call it now? Master Si ordered Shitou to deliver a letter to Master Rang.

Upon his return, he said, "I will give you a hatchet for dwelling in the mountains. As soon as Shitou arrived, he asked, "When one seeks neither the sages nor values one's own spiritual nature, what then?
Rang replied, "Your question is far too lofty. Why not ask about the lower level? Shitou said:
"I would rather suffer in saṃsāra for eternal kalpas than seek liberation through the various sages. He then departed, thinking to himself, "Did my letter reach him?
Tou said, "The letter did not reach him, nor was the message conveyed. "On the day I left, I received permission from the Master for a 'pickaxe.
I request it now. Baso lowered one foot; Tou then prostrated. The Master said, "Master Baso lowered his foot."
Shitou bowed and departed. For the time being, he did not possess Shitou’s adze. But tell me, what did Shitou use later on?
When Wuxie arrived at Shitou’s place, he asked: "If our words accord with one another, I shall stay;
if they do not accord, I shall leave. Shitou remained seated as usual. Wuxie said, "In that case, we do not accord," and he departed. Shitou [said nothing].
[Zhao] called out, “Master Wuye! Wuye turned his head back. Zhao said, “From birth until old age, it has been nothing but this.
Why turn your head? Wuye was suddenly and greatly enlightened; he then snapped his staff in two.

Dongshan said, “At that time, had it not been for our late master Wuye, it would have been very difficult to take up [the burden]. Even so, he was still traveling along the path. The Master said, “Shitou.”
He took his seat. Wuxie then departed. Shitou called after him, saying, "That has already become too much trouble.
A nun came to visit Linji, wishing to open the hall for teaching. Danyuan tested her, saying, "You have five obstacles; you may not open the hall."
The nun said, "How many obstacles does a dragon girl face in becoming a Buddha? Xingkong said, "A dragon girl manifests eighteen transformations; you try to manifest some yourself.
The nun said, "I am no wild fox spirit; what could I possibly transform? Xingkong then struck her several times. The Master said, "Tell me, does the nun possess the eye?
She can only carry a single length of rope for hanging herself. How do you understand this? A monk asked Master Yao:
Mount Shishuang. A student had a doubt and requested the Master to resolve it for him. Shishuang said, "Come up at nightfall; I shall resolve your doubt for you, O *jialuo*.
When evening arrived and he ascended the hall, the assembly had gathered. Shishuang asked, "Is the monk who came today to have his doubts resolved present? The monk immediately stepped forward.
As Shishuang descended from his seat, he seized the monk and said, "Assembly, this monk has a doubt! He gave him a shove and returned to his quarters.
The Master said: "Yaoshan resolving doubts is like adding mud to dirt. Nevertheless, this monk did not fail Yaoshan.
Yaoshan usually did not speak for the sake of the monks; the Hall Master said, 'The monks in the hall have long been longing for the Master’s instruction.
Yaoshan said, 'Strike the bell! Once the assembly had gathered, he returned to his quarters."
The head of the monastery followed up by asking, "The Master promised to speak for the sake of the assembly; why did you not utter a single word?
Yaoshan said, "There are sutra masters for the sutras and treatise masters for the treatises; how can they blame me, this old monk?

The Master [Dongshan] said, "When Yaoshan returned to his quarters, the head of the monastery had initially resented that Yaoshan would not speak for him. This could truly be called 'misleading him three times.'"
At the Army [Monastery], Yaoshan addressed the assembly, saying: "Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it. If you speak of it, horns will grow upon your head.
Daowu immediately went out. Yunyan asked Yaoshan, "Why did Elder Brother Zhi not respond to the Master?"
Shan said, "It was actually Dhyāna Master Zhi who understood. You should go ask him.
Yunyan then went to ask him, saying, "Elder brother, why did you not respond to the Master just now? Wuye said, "Today my head ached; you should ask the Master yourself.
Later, when Yunyan passed away, Wuye said, "Yunyan did not know 'there is' (you). I regret not having directed [him] toward it at the beginning."
[The Master] said, "Even so, he still did not contradict the son of Yaoshan. The Master continued, "Yunyan did not know 'having' (you).
I regret that I did not tell him at the outset. As for Daowu speaking thus—does it still exist or not?
Master Daci said, "In my entire life, I have never been able to answer questions; I only understand how to recognize the illness. At that time, a monk came forward.
Daci returned directly to his quarters. The Master said, "This monk should have come forward. Daci returned to his quarters immediately; there was no principle whatsoever.
Where is the point of recognizing the illness? Now, one must also be thorough. A monk visited Nan’uan of Ruozhou.
As soon as he reached the Master’s presence, the monk said, "It is lost! Nan’uan drew his staff and held it before the monk; the monk had no response.

[The Master] spoke. The Abbot struck him. The Master said, "This monk knows only that light is produced upon his head; he does not know there is a thorn beneath his feet. Guannan saw that the newly arrived monk was making noodles as an offering.
He took the noodles and showed them to him; the monk then departed. That evening, Guannan asked the Head Seat, "Where is the newly arrived monk?

The Head Seat replied, "He left immediately. Guannan said: *Note: This passage illustrates a classic encounter in the Chan tradition where the master uses a mundane act (making noodles) to test or instruct a newcomer, highlighting the gap between intellectual understanding and realized insight.*
"This is it. [Nanquan] said, "He has only attained a single peg. The Master said, "To observe how the Reverend says he has attained a single peg is very much like 'forcing the noble to become lowly.
Why? Because both of them are monastics. Nanquan picked up some bracken and asked Shanshan, "This is excellent for making offerings.
Shanshan said, "Not only this; even the hundred flavors of exquisite delicacies would be the same for him."
[The monk] did not look back. Quan said, "Even so, you must still taste it all. The Master said, "If Shan-shan speaks in this way, can he avoid [the charge]?
If he can avoid it, he has not yet possessed the eye. If he cannot avoid it, he contradicts his previous words.
When Lu-zu saw a monk coming, he would simply face the wall. The Master said, "Why does Lu-zu trouble himself to such an extent? There is no need to face the wall. If...

A monk came and asked, "What have you seen? [Baizhang] said, "It is good to know the proper time. Deng Yinfeng was at Xiangzhou when he demolished the Hall of Dignified Manners and wore only his undergarments.
Taking up the meditation mallet, he said, "If you can speak, I will not strike;
if you cannot speak, I will strike. The assembly remained silent, so Yinfeng struck them. The Master said, "These words contain a point of penetration. But tell me, whom did he penetrate? Linji.
Linji ascended the hall. A monk stepped forward and stood there. Linji gave a shout; the monk bowed, and Linji struck him. The Master said: "Linji was also very correct.
How would you understand this now? A monk asked Dongshan, "If one constantly and diligently wipes away [dust], so as not to let even a speck of dust remain, why did he not receive the robe and bowl?
Dongshan said, "It is because one directly says, 'Originally there is not a single thing.'"
"Nor have I yet obtained his robe and bowl," [the Emperor] said. The Master said, "If you have not obtained his robe and bowl at all, you are a fellow student of the Buddha.
But tell me, whom do you take as your teacher? Emperor Tongguang asked Xinghua, "I have recovered the treasure of the Central Plains, yet there is no one to appraise its value.
Xinghua asked, "What is Your Majesty’s treasure from the Central Plains? The Emperor extended his hand and made a sweeping gesture.
Regarding "Head and Feet," Huazhu said, "This is the treasure of a sovereign; who dares to appraise its value? The Master said, "Huaxia’s utterance was truly 'drunk with realization.
How would you judge it today? As for Lingyun’s verse on awakening through the peach blossoms:
"For thirty years I have sought the sword-wielder; / Several times the leaves have fallen and branches have sprouted. / Since first beholding the peach blossoms, / Until now..."
Now he no longer had any doubts. He then related this to Guishan, who said, "You have entered through conditions; you shall never again fall back or lose it. You must maintain this well.
He then related it to Xuansha, who said, "Precisely so! Utterly precise! I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate.
The Master said: "If someone were to ask Xuansha’s meaning as it is now, what would you say? Tell me, what about this person?"
"Have you penetrated through to the end yet? Linji was ascending the hall when a monk came forward. Linji gave a shout; the monk also shouted. The monk then bowed, and Linji struck him.
The monk was left speechless. The Master said: "Linji was too coarse-minded. It was fortunate that it was this monk."
If one were a patch-robed monk of the present day, how would they manage to breathe out? Dizang asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk said, "From the South. Dizang said, "What teachings do they show their disciples in the South?
The monk said, "There, gold dust is precious, yet it cannot enter the eye. Dizang said, "I say that Mount Sumeru is in your eye. Master [Linji].

The Master said, "Tell me, was Dizang able to avoid this monk’s eye? A monk asked Zhaozhou, "The Tripitaka Master with the Large Ears searched for the National Teacher three times and could not find him.
Where do you think he was? Zhaozhou said, "He was inside the nose of the Tripitaka Master with the Large Ears.
The Master said, "Just so, was the Tripitaka Master able to avoid the National Teacher’s nostrils? The National Teacher.

The National Teacher called to his attendant three times; the attendant responded three times. The National Teacher said, "I thought it was I who had failed you, but who would have known that it was you who had failed me?
The Master said, "The National Teacher and the attendant were both lacking in understanding. How do you understand this now?"
Qinshan asked Deshan, "Tianhuang spoke thus, and Longtan also spoke thus; I wonder how Deshan would speak?
Deshan said, "Try citing what Tianhuang and Longtan said. As Qinshan hesitated, [Deshan struck him].
Deshan struck him. The Master said, "Qinshan looked only to the front and not to the rear. How would you now provide relief for Qinshan?
Shigong was a hunter. While chasing a deer that passed before Mazu’s hermitage, [the deer] went by.
The Master asked, "Do you see my deer? Zhaozhou said, "What kind of person are you? Gong said, "I am a hunter.
The Master asked, "Are you skilled at archery? Gong said, "I am. The Master asked, "With one arrow, how many do you shoot?
Gong said, "One arrow shoots one deer. The Master said, "Then you do not understand archery. Gong said, "Does the Master not understand archery either? The Master said, "I..."
They discussed archery. Guǒ asked, "With one arrow, how many can you shoot? The Patriarch said, "With one arrow, I shoot a whole flock.
Guǒ said, "Since both sides possess life, why must you shoot them? The Patriarch said, "If that is so, why do you not shoot yourself?
Guǒ said, "If you were to command me to shoot myself, I would truly have no place to apply my hand. The Patriarch said, "This fellow’s ignorance and afflictions have suddenly ceased."
Gong then cut his hair with a knife and attended him within the hermitage. The Master said, "Mazu’s single arrow shot a whole flock;
he still had not mastered archery. My arrow, however, shoots all moving beings and sentient creatures without fail.
Even so, this is only half the story; I leave the other half for those who come after. Dachuan Fo visited Yangshan. He stood on tiptoe... [text ends]
One foot said: "Śākyamuni was like this; the twenty-eight patriarchs of India were like this;
the Master [Huángbō] was like this; and I myself am like this. Yǎngshān struck him with four strokes of the rattan cane. The Master said:
"This cannot be considered a reward, nor can it be considered a punishment. How do you understand it now? Xiāngyán addressed the assembly, saying: "It is like a person climbing..."
A tree. Its mouth is in its branches, yet its feet do not tread upon the tree, nor do its hands grasp the branches. Suddenly, someone asks about the meaning of the Westward Transmission;
if one intends to answer him, one loses one's body and life; if one does not answer him, one violates the question asked. The Master said:
The questioner and the respondent both fail to avoid losing their bodies and forfeiting their lives. How do you, monks of today, understand this?

Xuan Sha addressed the assembly, saying: "The venerable elders of all quarters all say they 'receive things and benefit beings. Yet, what would they do if they suddenly encountered three kinds of sick people?"
"How do you receive them? To one suffering from blindness, you raise the mallet and hold up the whisk, yet he still does not see.
To one suffering from deafness, you speak of samādhi, yet he still does not hear. To one suffering from muteness, you instruct him to speak, yet he cannot speak.
Tell me, how do you receive them? If you cannot receive such people, the Buddha-dharma has no efficacy. The Master said: "Had I known earlier that the lamp is fire..."
The rice had been cooking for a long time. Xuefeng ascended the hall;
once the assembly was settled, he drove them all down at once with his staff and said to an attendant, "Today I nearly entered hell like an arrow shot.

The attendant said, "It is fortunate, Master, that you have returned to human form. The Master asked, "Whether great or small, Xuefeng did not reach the village in front, nor did he reach the shop behind. But how about this?"
"Birth on the Path" provides the way out of the body. Longya asked Cuimei, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Cuimei said, "Give me the meditation board. Longya took the board; Cuimei took it and struck him.
Longya said, "I am willing to be struck, but there is still no meaning of the Patriarch. He then asked Linji, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
Ji said, "Hand me that meditation cushion over here. Ya took the cushion; Ji caught it and struck him.

Ya said, "I am willing enough to be struck, yet there was still no meaning of the Patriarch in it. Later, while staying at Longya, a monk asked, "When you, Master, questioned those two venerable seniors about the meaning of the Patriarch, had those two seniors realized it or not? Longya said, "It was indeed realized."
"It is simply that they lacked the meaning of the Patriarchs. The Master said, "It was so at the beginning; but now, is there still blood beneath the skin of these patch-robed monks?
Nanquan, Guizong, and Magu went to pay their respects to the National Teacher.
When they were halfway there, Nanquan drew a circle on the ground and said, "If you can speak, then go. Guizong entered inside and sat down; Magu performed a woman’s prostration.
Quan said, "If that is so, then I shall not go. Zong said, "What kind of mental activity is this?
The Master said, "Had I seen you all at the beginning, I would have struck each of you with a blow of the staff; then perhaps the world would have enjoyed peace.

Master Faden addressed the assembly, saying, "I originally intended to dwell in the mountains to hide my ineptitude and nurture the Way until my time passed. However, I am constrained by the unfinished affairs of my late teacher."
[The Master] examined [the case], brought it forth, and then set it aside. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the unresolved public case of the former master?
The Lamp struck him with a staff and said, "The patriarch failed to resolve it; the calamity reaches his descendants. The monk said, "What fault have I committed?"
Deng said, "The fault lies with me; the calamity falls upon you. The Master said, "Exerting one's utmost strength for the sake of the assembly, yet disaster emerges from one’s private door.
Longya asked Deshan, "When a student has acquired the Mohe sword and intends to take the Master's head, what then? Deshan said, "Where will you strike?
Longya pointed at the ground. Later, having arrived at Dongshan, as soon as he had finished his formal greetings, he raised the previous matter again.
[The story continues: Dongshan pulled out his staff and said, "Give me back Deshan’s head! Ya was speechless, and Dongshan struck him. The Master said:
"If one does not decide when a decision must be made, how will you decide it now? Zen Master Yunju Qi asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From the hall. Yunju said, "How can you deceive yourself? The Master said: "If it were not like this..."
How do you know it is so? Fenggan wished to travel to Mount Wutai and said to Hanshan and Shide, "If you accompany me on this journey to the mountain, you are of my same stream;
if you do not accompany me on this journey to the mountain, you are not of my same stream."
Hanshan said, "Where are you going to roam on Mount Tai? Digan replied, "To pay homage to Mañjuśrī.
Hanshan said, "You are not of my kind. The Master said, "Fenggan was much like Biancai meeting Xiao Yi. Guishan asked Yangshan:
"From where have you come? Yangshan replied, "From the fields. Muzhou asked, "How many people are there in the fields?
Yangshan thrust his spade into the ground and stood with his hands clasped behind his back. Muzhou said, "There are many people on South Mountain mowing thatch.

Yangshan pulled out his spade and walked away. The Master said, "He only managed to get one peg. Do any of you have another way of understanding this? One day, Nanquan [was presiding over] two halls...

[Master Nanquan] was disputing over a cat. He then held it up and said, "If you can speak, I will not kill it. The assembly remained silent. Nanquan then killed it. Later, he recounted this incident to Zhaozhou.
Zhaozhou took his straw sandals, placed them on his head, and walked out. Nanquan said, "Had you been there, you would have saved the cat.
The Master said: "Great as Zhaozhou may have been, he could only save himself. A monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, "What is the essential meaning of Huangmei?"
"Who attains it? The Patriarch said, "Those who understand the Buddha-dharma attain it. The monk asked, "Does the Master attain it? The Patriarch said, "I do not.
The monk asked, "Why does the Master not attain it? The Patriarch said, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma. The Master [Baizhang] said:
If you understand it, there are two heads; if you do not understand it, there are three peaks. How can you speak of the path of transcendence?
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? Zhaozhou said, "No. The monk said, "All sentient beings possess Buddha-nature;
why does the dog have none? Zhaozhou said, "It has the nature of karmic consciousness. The Master said, "To speak..."
Some say there is none; this is like a pair of colors that match perfectly. How would you speak of it now? Yungai asked Shishuang:
"I do not ask about the time when ten thousand doors are all closed; what is it like when ten thousand doors are all open? Shishuang said: "What is the matter within the hall?
Yungai said: "No one can receive him. Shishuang said: "You have spoken well enough, yet you have only spoken eight or nine tenths of it."
[The Master] said, "It is accomplished. He then asked, "Please, Master, speak. Shuang said, "No one recognizes him.
The Master said, "The beginning was not reached; the end was excessive. He cried out! One night, Master Zihu cried out in front of the Sangha hall, "Catch the thief!
The assembly was all startled. A monk emerged from the hall; Zihu grabbed him by the chest and said, "Caught you! Caught you!"
The monk said, "I am not it. Lake said, "It is indeed so; it is simply that you are unwilling to accept it.
The Master said, "Purple Lake buys a hat to fit the head. One day, Zhaozhou lay down in the snow and cried out, "Save me!
Save me! A monk came and lay down beside him; Zhaozhou then got up and left. The Master said, "This monk was within Zhaozhou’s circle. Do you understand?"
"Is there anyone who can get out? While Dōngshān was on a work assignment (*pǔqǐng*), he went on a tour of the quarters and saw a monk who had not come out.
Dōngshān said, "Why did you not come out for the work assignment? The monk replied, "I am unwell.
Dōngshān said, "When you were usually well, when did you ever go? The Master said: "Tell me, when has this monk ever not gone? Páng Jūshī asked the Monk of Dàméi:
"Long have I heard of the Great Plum. I wonder, is the plum ripe yet? The Plum Master said, "Where will you apply your teeth?
The Layman said, "In pieces. The Plum Master said, "Give me back the pit. The Master said, "These two men did not even reach the village."
Later, he did not go to the shop. When Lu Zu saw a monk coming, he would simply face the wall. Nanquan said, "I usually do not wish to say it to the monks:
you must realize it before even being conceived in the womb. Yet, not even one or half of one can attain it.
If Lu Zu acts like this, it will be 'donkey-year' [never] happening. The Master said, "It is not so here at Dayu. Before being conceived in the womb—"
"I obtained it previously; I shall break your waist! When Master Zhongyi saw a monk approaching, he clapped his mouth and made a "he-he" sound.
Yangshan approached; Zhongyi clapped his mouth again. Yangshan went from east to west; Zhongyi clapped his mouth again.
Yangshan went from west to east; Zhongyi clapped his mouth again. Yangshan stood directly facing him. Zhongyi asked, "From where did you obtain this? Yangshan said, "From..."
Guishan received it. Guishan then asked Xiangyi, "From whom did you receive it? Xiangyi said, "I received it from Zhangjing.

The Master said, "Look at these two old monks; they are utterly deluded, deceiving one another face-to-face. Layuan said, "One who is sorrowful should not speak of their sorrow to another who is sorrowful.
When Bodhidharma was about to pass away, he said to the Second Patriarch, "You have received something from my side..."

"What? The Second Patriarch prostrated himself and stood in his place. Bodhidharma said, "You have attained my marrow. The Master [Zhaozhou] said: "The Second Patriarch was merely smeared by Bodhidharma;
he claimed to have attained the marrow, yet he had not even dreamed of the skin. For what reason did he succeed to the position of the Patriarch? Bimiyan (Guishan) constantly carried a forked staff.
Whenever he saw a monk approach, he would say: "If you can speak, you die under this fork. If you cannot speak, you die under this fork."
Yexia died. Later, Dachen Buddha arrived; he leaped into Biyuan’s embrace. Biyuan then patted Dachen on the back three times.
Dachen rose up, shook his hand, and said, "You have deceived me from three thousand miles away! The Master said, "Is there still a place where he was deceived?
Not only did he deceive that Dachen Buddha, but today Dayu deceives all of you as well."
The above was said by Yaoshan: "The sound of thunder is vast and great, yet there are no raindrops at all. Yangshan had a monk come to take his leave.
Yangshan made a single stroke with his hand; the monk did not depart. Yangshan made another stroke, and the monk then left.

The Master said: "Why did he not leave before? Why did he leave after? Do you wish to understand? I shall specifically provide a commentary to break through this mystery. As for the first [stroke]..."

A single stroke and a subsequent stroke both become two strokes. When the Buddha was in the world, there was a woman who circumambulated the World-Honored One three times and then entered meditative absorption (*samādhi*).
The World-Honored One commanded Mañjuśrī to bring this woman out of her absorption.
Mañjuśrī exerted all his supernatural powers, yet he could not bring her out of her absorption. The World-Honored One said, "Forty-two Ganges-sands of worlds below..."
In that land, there was the Bodhisattva Vimalakīrti, who was able to bring this woman out of her samādhi. At that time, Vimalakīrti went before the woman and snapped his fingers three times;
the woman then emerged from her samādhi. The Master said: "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas; why was he unable to bring the woman out of her samādhi?
What kind of spiritual power did Vimalakīrti possess that he was able to do so? Do you wish to understand?"
The monks went to stay overnight in a temple; the bandits entered a house of ill repute. Mañjuśrī asked Asaṅga, "Where have you recently come from? Asaṅga replied, "From the South.
Mañjuśrī asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained in the South? Asaṅga said, "In the age of the final dharma, the bhikṣus rarely observe the precepts and rules.
Mañjuśrī asked, "How many followers are there? Asaṅga replied, "Either three hundred or five hundred. Asaṅga then asked in return:
"How is the Buddha-dharma maintained here? Zhaozhou said, "Dragons and snakes are mixed; ordinary people and sages dwell together. Cezhuo asked, "How many followers are there?
Zhaozhou said, "The three threes before and the three threes after. The Master [Dongshan] said, "Wenshu spoke of the 'three threes before.'"
"The latter three are three. How do you understand this? Do you wish to understand? "A thousand-year-old shadowless tree; a bottomless boot of the present age.
An ancient said, "I have a single phrase; I will tell it to you when an ox gives birth to a calf. The Master said, "I am not like that.
Even when an ox gives birth to a calf, I will not tell it to you. Why is this so? If I were to tell it to you..."

"Where else could there be another Wang Laoshi? Hearing that Zhaozhou was coming, Daowu put on his leopard-skin trousers and, holding his *jiaoliao* staff, stood at the triple gate with one foot raised.
As soon as Zhaozhou arrived, Daowu gave a shout of "A-ho! Zhaozhou said, "Be careful in your service," and Daowu shouted "A-ho!
again. The Master said: "If anyone can see where these two men have landed, I will not..."
"This obstructs the possession of the eye. If you do not know where it falls, you have not yet possessed the eye.

He then struck the meditation seat once and said, "If you still do not understand, I shall give you three hundred blows! Deshan held a small assembly for a general instruction, saying, "Tonight I will not answer questions.
Anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows. A monk came forward and bowed; Deshan immediately struck him. The monk said, "I have a question..."
The monk had not yet asked why the Master was striking him. Deshan said, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "I am a man from Silla.
Deshan said, "Before you have even stepped onto the boat's railing, you deserve thirty blows! The Master [Yunmen] said, "People all say that Deshan’s use of the teaching tools is excellent.
But if it were like this, would they have ever seen it in a dream? Dayu said, 'Deshan..."
When Shanshi was pushed by this monk, it was as if mountains crumbled and ice melted away. Nevertheless, even today, it is difficult to find a single venerable elder.
When the Bodhisattva Puyan entered meditative absorption and surveyed the trichiliocosm, he could not find the Bodhisattva Puxian.
"I wonder where Puxian is," he thought. The Buddha said, "You need only..."
While arising from a single thought within the samādhi of stillness, one will certainly see Samantabhadra in the sky riding a six-tusked white elephant.
The Master said: "O people, how do you understand this? Puyan toppled the World-Honored One;
the World-Honored One toppled Puyan. Now tell me, where is Samantabhadra?"

The brilliance of the sword’s verse radiates like the sun’s flowing light; has it ever caused the assembly to doubt? Its hair-splitting edge spans the universe, yet when one intends to grasp it, it is already put to use.
As soon as a thought arises, the root is gone; to raise one's eyes is already too late. To meet the opportunity, one must attain the subtle; where else can one find the Muni?
