Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters, Volume Twenty-six:
Essential Teachings of Master Ju of Mount Fahua in Shu Province.

The Master entered the monastery and ascended the hall to address the assembly, saying: "Now, the primary truth (paramārtha-satya) cannot be expressed by intellectual discernment nor measured by the mind’s contrivances;
it is the separate transmission outside the teachings, where no words or letters are established. Having arrived at this point, what further is there to say?
You must directly cut off Vairocana and harbor neither ordinary nor holy beings. Can you do so? If you have not yet attained this, I, this mountain monk, shall [speak] again."
Having spoken these verses, he departed. He did not seal [the teaching] with the Vairocana mudrā; how could he propagate the mind of the ancient Buddha? A bright moon illuminates the secluded valley;
cold waves assist the night mortar. Do you all understand this thoroughly? Each of you should hope to pose a question. Question: "In the past at Vulture Peak, the Buddha shared half his seat;
what is your intention in ascending [this seat] today? The Master said: "Are you able to take this upon yourself? Question: "What is it?"

Regarding the realm of the *Lotus Sūtra*, the Master said: "The latter does not encompass the former. "How is it to be the person within the realm? The Master said: "Look after three days. A monk asked:
"I pray that the Master will directly point out the matter of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. The Master said: "With ears cut off, lying in the street. The monk said: [Silence].
Those who saw him all knit their brows. The Master said, "This is not your realm. A monk asked, "Without falling into the present moment, please, Master, speak.
The Master said, "Falling. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Reed sprouts piercing the knees.
The monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Seven strides and eight bounds. The monk asked, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "Tightly wrapping the head. The monk said, "..."
"What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A broad-faced *caṇḍāla*. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Red lips and white teeth. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Slanting down, scratching the head.
[The monk] asked, "Before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring flowers in their beaks? The Master said, "The fruit has ripened."
"Monkeys and apes are heavy. The monk asked, "After seeing [the flowers], why do they not carry them in their mouths? The Master said, "In the sparse forest, even birds cannot pass.
He asked, "What is it like when snow covers the thousand mountains? The Master said, "The woodcutter loses the ancient path; the fisherman locks his solitary boat."
Question: "One may come within the white clouds; you shall teach you the song of the purple *zhī* fungi. What is the song of the purple *zhī*? The Master said: "It is not in the Wu dialect;
you must use the Han language. Question: "For several days I have not heard the Master’s instructions. What is the meaning of this morning’s ascent to the seat? The Master said:
"One year’s spring ends, and another year’s spring begins. The Master then said: "In studying the Way, one must possess the power of discernment (*pratisaṃvid*)."
The Dharma-eye must not be coarse or superficial. If one attains the clarity and precision of the True Eye, there will be no obstruction whatsoever.
An ancient master said: "Within a single phrase, the Three Mysteries must be complete; within each Mystery, the Three Essentials must be complete.
What was the intent behind the ancients speaking thus? The Goose King selects the milk; he is by nature not of the same kind as the duck.

Ascending the hall, he said: "To say 'this very mind is Buddha' is like using yellow leaves to stop a child's crying. To say 'neither mind nor Buddha' is like administering a remedy according to the diagnosis of the illness.
Tell me, at this point, what do you do?"

Ascending the hall, he said: "If you intend to grasp it, you will immediately encounter a target and draw an arrow upon yourself; if you do not intend to grasp it, you are already three thousand miles away.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The white-browed one does not extend his hand; the road to Chang'an is level and smooth. Return to the hall and drink tea."

Ascending the hall, he said: "Śākyamuni did not appear in the world; Bodhidharma did not come from the West. The Buddha-dharma pervades the world, yet the mouth that speaks of the profound remains closed.
Ascending the hall again, he said: "If one opens the mouth, it becomes redundant speech; if one does not open the mouth, it becomes superfluous speech. Then he said:
The Imperial Edict of the Golden Wheel King: The customs of the thatched-roof shop are unique.
Entering the hall, he said: "Bodhi transcends words and speech; from the beginning, no one has ever attained it. Nevertheless, even so, one cannot avoid verbal transgression."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way. Now tell me, what is it? It is like marking the boat to seek a lost sword, or sticking glue to the bridge-pins to tune the strings."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings are merely a prescription for medicine. But tell me, what illness does it treat?
He then said: "The mouth born of parents."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The bell tolls and the drum resounds; the crows caw and the magpies chirp. For all of you, they have finished preaching Prajñā and expounding Nirvāṇa.
Do you all believe this? Guanyin and Shizhi manifest great supernatural powers right before you.
If you cannot believe it, they will depart for other lands to save suffering beings and benefit living creatures."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods have their mouths hung upon the wall. How can the old monks throughout the land find a way to apply their hands?
When you all go to various places, how will you bring this up? For me to speak thus is merely the result of long-standing habituation;
it is like the lips of one who has been chewing for a long time. He gave a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients had one unresolved karmic cause. I shall present it to the assembly; take note of it clearly.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Virtuous ones, according to the regulations of the monastic community, you must come up once each morning and evening to meet me."
That is not possible. If one speaks in terms of the affairs of the Buddha-dharma, from the beginningless kalpas of dust-like eons, it has never been obscured.
Nevertheless, even so, a rotten seed will not sprout.
He ascended the hall and said: "Does the assembly understand? A single drop of lion’s milk can destroy eight bushels of donkey’s milk. I remember this.
A monk asked an old master, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "Neither a mound nor a tree. Does the assembly understand?
If you do not, I shall provide further annotations. "Neither a mound nor a tree" means [to be] hemmed in by thorny branches.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'If I were to exclusively expound the Dharma of the Patriarchal Lineage, the weeds in the Dharma Hall would grow a fathom deep.
Yet, I cannot simply lock the gates of the Sangha Hall for you, O *dārala* (disciples).
Nevertheless, even so, it is like a tortoise performing acrobatics on dry land amidst the dust."
Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient precedent, saying: "An ancient said: 'When a single speck of dust arises, the whole earth is gathered within it.

The Master said: "When a single leaf falls, the world is autumn. Ascending the hall, he raised another precedent, saying: "Nanquan said: 'To utter the word "suchness" (tathatā) is already a transformation.
These days, monks must walk among the heterodox classes before they can succeed. Now tell me, what is walking among the heterodox classes? He then said: "A stone ox."
Long reclining in the mist of three springs; when the wooden horse neighs, it is the spring after autumn.
Entering the hall, he raised [this case]: A monk asked Caoshan, "What is the one that does not age? Caoshan said, "A withered tree. The monk asked, "What is the one that ages?
Caoshan said, "Not being supported. A monk reported this to Jiufeng, who said, "Three times six..."
"Meaning! Do you all, venerable elders, understand? To love another’s young wife, one must be a white-haired old man.
He ascended the hall and said: "If we speak of the gradual, it returns to the ordinary and accords with the Way. If we discuss the sudden, it leaves no trace.
Even if one were to discuss the sudden and return to the ordinary, this too would be merely forcing it to be so."
Opening the furnace, he addressed the assembly, saying: "One, two, three, four, five—let you arrange them however you wish.
As for the pillar and the lantern, when have they ever become Buddhas or patriarchs? Those who do not begrudge their eyebrows will speak of them directly. A monk asked, "I wonder what you would say?
The Master said, "Beyond the purity of one's self and the lightness of one's gear, there is only the alms-bowl, the water jar, and the coarse robe. The monk said, "Precisely at this moment..."
"How is it at such a time? The Master said, "At night, the solitary moon is cold; in the morning, a single cloud is high. The monk hesitated. The Master asked, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master then presented a verse to him, saying: "Thirty-five or fifty—what need is there to mention them further?
Squareness and roundness, change and function—these are removed from Buddhas and Patriarchs. Before he has manifested his name, I cannot take hold of him. The monk then asked:
"What is the guest within the guest? The Master said: "Though his mouth has no strength to open, he feels ashamed when he exhales.
The monk asked: "What is the host within the guest? The Master said: "A single staff of fresh bamboo; three articles of old hempen robe. The monk said: [No response.]
"What is the guest within the host? The Master said: "How many people look upon these towering peaks? Who can hear this in its stark clarity? The monk said:
"What is the Lord among Lords? The Master said: "Ten-thousand-fathom peaks open wide for all to behold; a thousand peaks reveal their faces. A monk asked:

"What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said: "Spring brings forth and summer nurtures; autumn harvests and winter stores. The monk said: [further inquiry]...
"What is 'seizing the object but not seizing the person'? The Master said, "When the authority is in one's hand for a day, wait and see when the command is carried out.
The monk asked, "What is 'seizing both the person and the object'? The Master said, "The Son of Heaven is noble within the realm; the General is mighty beyond the passes.
The monk asked, "What is 'neither seizing the person nor seizing the object'? The Master said, "A single expanse of heaven and earth; the sun and moon."
[The Master] spoke clearly on both points. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The hand is not as good as the foot. The monk asked, "What is the家风 (family style) of all Buddhas?
The Master said, "The weeding of the wasteland never ends; it is then contested by others. A monk asked, "From antiquity to the present, nothing has been obtained from another.
What did the Sixth Patriarch at Huangmei transmit? The Master said, "Deshan’s staff. The monk asked, "What was transmitted after that?"
"How is it? The Master said, "What need is there for Linji’s shout? Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Purple clouds constantly support his feet;
black mists surround his body as he walks. Question: "The Dharma-body has no form. How is it established? The Master said, "An incense burner in an ancient temple. Question:
"How was it before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A newly tanned drumhead thuds and thunders."

The monk said, "What is it like after seeing? The Master replied, "An old drumhead is too loose; though struck, it does not ring. A monk asked, "The matter of birth and death is great; I pray that you will save me.
The Master said, "I lost my boat in the middle of Lake Dongting. A monk asked, "What is the original source? The Master said, "The mountains are high and the peaks are steep.
A monk asked, "When words do not meet the occasion, I pray that you will provide a teaching. The Master said, "Mountains hide and the sea receives all. A monk asked, "For a long time..."
[Question: "When one dwells in mountain ravines and possesses not a single thing, what then? The Master said: "The feet are thin, yet the straw sandals are wide. [Question:

"Without transgressing anything, I request the Master to provide the essential framework. The Master said: "A deaf person listening from afar. [Question: "I know for myself that I shall become a Buddha; I do not yet know who can bear witness to this.
The Master said: "Master Zhi’s scissors. [Question: "What is the one phrase of intimacy? The Master said: [Silence] (or: "The Master's staff").
[The Master] said, "The Sixth Patriarch was a man from Xinzhou. A monk asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "Before one's parents were born.
The monk asked, "What is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said, "Meeting [you] today.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Three cats, one ferocious. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body? The Master said—
[The Master] said: "Nothing surpasses this. A monk asked: "When the root-source is unmoving, how does one engage with sentient beings?
The Master said: "A fierce tiger is not equal to a clever cat. A monk asked: "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?

The Master said: "Seeking pearls in red water; Sun Bin striking tiles. As a monk entered the room, the Master uttered a phrase: "Re-arranging the fishing rod across the sea, the hook has not yet been cast..."
[The monk] said, "He must love fish and swallow them. The monk said, "A withered tree from many years ago has today sprouted anew.
The Master spoke on his behalf: "Within the Red Silk Tune there is no golden chime; beyond the Green Banner Song there is a civil official.

The monk said, "Lowering the green silk and baiting it again, he will surely catch a great golden fish. As the monk entered the room and spread his sitting mat, just as he was about to withdraw it, the Master said, "One unfolding."
[The Master] gathered them all in at once; every dharma was complete. He intended to ask further about the origin [of this], so he asked:

"Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master then struck him. A monk asked: "Since you are a *kalyāṇamitra* (a spiritual friend), for what reason do you practice both nurturing life and killing life?
The Master said: "That which lives lives of itself; that which dies dies of itself. Before the rain falls, the earthworms stir; it is simply to let the little snakes know. [The monk] asked again.

The Master sang: "Whose tune is this? Whom does the ancestral wind succeed? The Master said: "The head of the treasury is white; the head of the sea is black. The monk said: "The dharma-heir of Fenyang;
the descendant of Linji! The Master said: "Do not confuse the needle and the awl. A question was asked:

"When the Dharma Flower Sutra’s special envoy extended his three requests, what was the matter of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "The roads are dry under a clear sky. A question was asked: "Virtue..."

[The Master] brandishes a staff. [A monk asks: "What is the meaning of Linji’s shout? The Master says: "Cut his tongue into three pieces. The monk says: "It will be proclaimed throughout the four seas.
The Master says: "How bitter and painful! A monk asks: "What is the guest within the guest? The Master says:
"Darkly crossing through the spring dawn. The monk asks: "What is the host within the guest? The Master says: "Do not vainly spy upon the gateways. The monk says: [silence].
“What is the guest within the host? The Master said: “Dignity lost, drifting and drowning. The monk asked: “What is the host within the host?
The Master said: “Light cold, the stars are sparse. A monk asked: “What is ‘taking away the person but not taking away the environment’? The Master said:
“White chrysanthemums have just bloomed under the warmth of the double sun; the young gentleman of a hundred years does not encounter spring. The monk asked: “What is ‘taking away the environment’?”

"Not taking from others. The Master said: "Throughout the great earth, all news is cut off; carefree and solitary, one simply accords with the Real. Question: "What is meant by 'both person and environment being taken away'?
The Master said: "The weeds overgrow and people change their countenance; both ordinary and sage are equally lost. Question: "What is meant by 'neither person nor environment being taken away'?
The Master said: "The clear breeze accompanies the bright moon; the wild old man smiles as they draw near. A monk asked: "I have received [your teaching]..."
An ancient saying goes: "Mount Sumeru is the mallet, and empty space is the drum; would you permit a student to strike it? The Master said, "There is no place for you to apply your hand.
The monk said, "I do not even ask for the mallet. The Master said, "I cannot strike you," and then he offered this verse:
"Yanguan has the drum, distinguishing high and low; Nanquan and Beishan then set them in order. To turn one's back, one must come forth."
The drum of the Tang lands beats; when the head is struck, the northern tribes do not advance. Entering the barbarian lands, one must swiftly grind the sword at one’s waist;
exiting the passes, one must rely on one’s own talent. Cherish this, O Master, lest you shatter it yourself. I am in Jiangdong, while you are in the West. A monk asked:
The student, not yet having encountered the Great Function, requested, "Please, Master, give me one shout. The Master said, "What kind of function is that? The monk said, "The Great Function.
The Master said, "If it is the Great Function, how could it receive a shout? The monk then shouted. The Master said, "A single pool of green water;
waves crashing in two places. The monk offered this verse: "Highly holding the Patriarchal Seal, he stilled the wild functions; Whether sitting or lying down, one must surely reflect upon this."
"I know. Yet I have been completely shattered by my enlightened teacher. Seeking Buddhas and Patriarchs outside is hardly remarkable.
Question: "I recall your words, 'Not bringing a single thing. What is it that you put down? What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "You are the *li-yin* (the cause of realization)."
"What have you put down? The monk said, "The Buddha-dharma is not so extensive. The Master said, "It lacks my blow across the back. What will you do about that?
The monk said, "So there was never such variety after all; now you are merely making a show. The Master showed him a verse, saying:
"Your staff flies high, and I shall simply rest. In this life, there is neither joy nor sorrow. When the clouds part, wait as you please."

The wind blows them away; let remain the moon over the green pool in the midst of autumn. A monk asked, "Regarding Zhaozhou’s ‘East Gate, West Gate, South Gate, North Gate,’ what is the underlying meaning?

Do not come; you must also examine this with great care. Take heed. [The Master] ascends the hall and says:
"I cannot recall it all. Heavenly flowers fill my robe. Even if one had a thousand words, they would not equal a single moment of silence. He descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "In the past, Great Master Xuansha addressed the assembly, saying: 'Everywhere it is commonly said that one should receive and benefit sentient beings.
But suppose you suddenly encounter three kinds of sick people—how would you receive them? If a blind person comes, you raise your mallet or brandish your whisk, yet they still do not see.
If a deaf person comes, you speak to them, yet they still do not hear. If a mute person comes, you try to make them speak.'"
[The opponent] said, "Furthermore, it cannot be attained. If one cannot attain it by meeting these three people, then the Buddha-dharma has no spiritual efficacy.
The Master said, "Excellent, brothers! Do you know where the true mark is manifested? This mountain monk will not spare his eyebrows to explain it for you all.
As for you all, who normally possess two eyes—when have you ever truly seen with them? You possess two ears—when have you..."
"I have heard it said that one possesses a tongue; yet when has it ever spoken?
Since there is no speaking, no hearing, and no seeing, from where could form, sound, fragrance, taste, or touch come? Even so, how many people can actually reach such a state?"

Thus it is said: "A wooden puppet; a stone daughter. In the three months of winter, the yang energy is at its peak; in the sixth month, frost descends. There are words that do not depend on the tongue;
there are wordless phrases that are most essential. If you understand my final phrase, few in this world will know it.
At midday meals and morning congee, there is nothing else to do but discuss the wonders of the Way over a cup of tea and incense before the brazier. He descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Hall of Universal Radiance is within the human realm; where ordinary beings and sages intermingle, there is no coming or going.
If you can personally behold it within a single speck of dust, the light from a single pore will reveal the Compassionate Countenance."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "In the past, when the Great Wisdom Chan Master Baizhang was attending Mazu for his second interview, he stood in attendance.

Mazu raised his whisk. Baizhang said, 'Is it used right here? Is it apart from this? Mazu hung up the whisk and asked, 'When you open your mouth to teach others in the future, with what will you provide for them?
Baizhang took up the whisk and held it upright. Mazu said, 'Is it used right here? Is it apart from this?'"
Baizhang hung his whisk back in its original place. The Patriarch then gave a shout, which left Baizhang deaf for three days straight.

"Great assembly," [the Master said], "what need is there to speak of being deaf for three days? It was enough to cause the drum to be beaten at Longmen for the morning assembly, where the entire congregation gathered like clouds.
The monks' hall swallowed the Buddha Hall whole; the pillar hung upside down from the lantern; heaven was high and earth deep; the moon was bright and the wind [blew]."
Clear skies; rain falls in season and winds are harmonious; rivers are clear and seas are calm. When hungry, we eat bitter herbs together with you;
when thirsty, we drink cold spring water with you. Even if flowers were to fall from the heavens, how could they compare to returning to the hall for tea? [Descends from the seat.]
Ascending the hall: On the road to Mount Tiantai, travelers are exceedingly rare; before the Hall of the Broken Oven, there is no ground upon which to express gratitude.
Snow buries the courtyard cypresses; ice locks the Yanxi Brook. Though we are here at the head of the furnace in the South, we do not enter the pickle-jar of another’s house.
Look! On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, it is as if it were still cold in the first month of spring.
Each of you must exert yourselves and press forward; take care not to give way to self-defeat. Descend from your seats.
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Just now, this mountain monk was in the dormitory hall; there was no mountain monk in the Dharma Hall.
When I went down to the Dharma Hall, there was a mountain monk in the Dharma Hall, and no mountain monk in the dormitory hall. If he were present, then there would be dharmas outside the mind;
if he were absent, then the mind-dharma would not be all-pervasive. You venerable seniors are beneath your robes and bowls; as soon as you hear the drum being struck,"
He ascended the Dharma Hall. When an elder was added to the Dharma Hall, the robes and bowl of that elder were subtracted from below.
To add is to fall into increase; to subtract is to fall into extinction. Because of extinction, one falls into annihilationism; because of increase, one falls into eternalism.

How can a wandering monk escape existence and non-existence? How can he escape eternalism and annihilationism? This doubt regarding birth and death is extremely difficult to penetrate and transcend. This is the clarity of the Tathāgata.
Purify your mind. You must exercise decisive discernment; do not be casual. Time flows on, shifting as swiftly as a flying arrow.
Such is this floating world—how brief is human life? Both of us have left the household life; the three realms are but a transient inn.

With bamboo doors and thatched huts, who is their master? We dwell together in austerity, we reside together in stillness. Why is this so? What is new here? What is there to grieve for? What need is there for anxiety or worry? Below...
The Seat. The practitioner has shaved his head and ascended the hall. The pillar has been ordained for many years; the lantern has long since shaved its head.
The Buddha Hall strictly maintains the prohibitive precepts; the triple gate has recently attained rest. The Great Matter is fundamentally equal—unattached and cool.
The full moon has passed over all the grasses, trees, and forests, as if the warmth of spring were blooming everywhere.

[The Master] descends from the seat. On the first day of the month, he ascends the hall and says: "All things are renewed; I speak of my native land. Lifting my eyes, they are still my original father and mother.
Last year’s flowers bloomed with fragrance far-reaching; Beyond the mundane world, mountains and rivers, sun and moon endure long. A monk asked: "In the past, Venerable Bhadra..."
[The student] asked Master Fozhao, "I do not know whether [the ancients] were the same as today or different.

The Master said, "Ancient and modern. [The student] further said, "The man who planted the pine trees has grown old; it is difficult to pass on the bowl. Old Lu went to Lingnan with such great effort.

The Master said, "Try to cite something from the ancients and see. [The student] said, "The kitchen, the storehouse, the three gates, the bell tower, and the Buddha hall. The Master said, "If that is so, then..."
“Is it possible? The student asked, “If one suddenly encounters a person with seven hands and eight feet, what then?
The Master said, “Cut off his heels and bring me a phrase. The student said, “Yesterday someone came from Shuzhou. The Master said, “...”
This, too, is a case of the indolent. Again, it is cited: A monk asked Baizhang, “What is the extraordinary matter? Baizhang said, “Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak.
The monk bowed, and Baizhang struck him. The Master said, “He struck him wrongly. A monk asked Deshan, “What is the extraordinary matter?
Deshan said, “In my school there are no words or phrases, nor is there a single dharma given to anyone. The Master said:
It is still somewhat lacking. A monk asked Luoshan, "What is the extraordinary matter? Luoshan said, "What are you saying? The Master said, "How can this be considered a principle?
O Great Assembly, the ancients baited their hooks with meat, their intent being to catch fish; nowadays, people wash their feet and then board the boat—how many such individuals could there be?
If someone were to ask Longmen, 'What is the extraordinary matter? [he would say: "What are you saying?"* *Note: The final response is implied by the Master's commentary on Luoshan’s style.*
The mountain monk said to him, "It is not far from here to Lake Tai. What is so extraordinary about speaking in such a way?
He then said to him again, "The crab apple tree is but a few paces away. "Assembly, do you understand? If you do not understand it as something ordinary, you must view it as something ordinary.
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Within the body there are birth, old age, sickness, and death; within thought there are arising, abiding, changing, and ceasing;
within the lands there are formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness. These twelve matters are truly extraordinary. Ordinary people do not recognize them, and thus they drift along with them."
When the Tathāgata appears in the world, he points directly to the wondrous mind of nirvāṇa—permanence, bliss, self, and purity.

It is like a single grain of elixir that, when applied to iron, transforms it into gold; a single word of ultimate truth turns an ordinary person into a sage. These twelve kinds [of teachings] are in fact but a single Dharma.

"The one presently sitting in meditative concentration and listening to the Dharma with such clarity—is it not he? Do you believe this? He then said: "The vermilion cassia in the moon is uniquely forbidden from cold;
the frosty plum in the snow alone releases its fragrance. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When awakened, this matter is fundamentally easy; after becoming deluded, this gate is truly very difficult.
At every place, green willows are fit to tie a horse; at every household door, one passes through to Chang'an."
Ascending the hall: On the third day of the third month, and the second day of the second month, we speak of the Great Meaning without destroying conventional designations.

Sentient beings toil in pursuit of fleeting time; thus, O practitioners of the Way, you waste it in vain. On the twenty-ninth of the second month and the first of the third month, there is the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
Even if one is widely learned and masters the past and present, throughout kalpas, how could it ever be different from this very day? This very day—
"What is the matter? After a long silence, he said, "Why wait until today?
He ascended the hall and said, "The sages of the past, seeing that people delighted in worldly toil and did not seek liberation, gave rise to a heart of compassion and told them:
'You who follow after sounds and pursue forms are called madmen. Great assembly, what fine words! How shameful!"
"I am ashamed that the Sages speak thus. Nevertheless, even so, they have already opened the sack;
it cannot be folded back up. Today at Longmen, I shall pour it out completely. Should anyone obtain this, their seeking will cease forever.
He then took up his staff, struck once, and said, "Is this not sound? How do you usually follow it? He then raised the staff again.
The Staff said: "Is this not form? How do you usually pursue it? Do you understand? If you can pursue it as it truly is, there is no bondage;
such a one is a person who has realized the essence of the monastic community. [I have] stood for long."
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony: The wondrous form-body of the Tathāgata is truly impossible to conceal.
Not draped in the garments of original nature, how could he wear the trousers of mother-born flesh? When descending from the Aśoka tree, he took seven steps toward the north, south, east, and west.

Having taken these seven steps, he has brought all sentient beings across while having no one left to deliver. This morning, on the eighth day of the fourth month, our Buddha, the Tathāgata, was born.
On this day, the refined monasteries throughout the world boil water to bathe the Buddha. The Buddha, in turn, bathes with all these people.
Now tell me, what is the Buddha? Do you wish to know? The name of the Buddha is Tathāgata; he is eternally present and never extinguished.
If there is someone who perceives him, I, this mountain monk, shall say no more. If no one perceives him, I shall repeat my verse: "Yesterday the Tathāgata bestowed the Dharma..."
Rain. This morning, the Dharma rain washes the Tathāgata. It is clearly of one single flavor, without distinction; beyond the clouds, the green mountains bloom flower by flower.
Desiring to repay the profound kindness of the Tathāgata, I have bathed him anew within the hall. [Descend from the seat.]
Ascending the Hall for the Summer Retreat: At Longmen, the summer retreat is superior to all other places; the great earth, mountains, and rivers serve to proclaim it.
If you can penetrate through this during these ninety days, there will be no more Buddha-dharma left to deliberate upon.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The eternal void of ten thousand ages; the wind and moon of a single day. When the ancients gave such a report, it was truly a magnificent expression.
How could the wind and moon of a single day obscure the eternal void of ten thousand ages?

How could the eternal void of ten thousand ages fail to clarify the wind and moon of a single day? This is the vast and profound Dharma, the school of sovereign freedom. If you can understand this..."
Where else could there be even a single thread of remaining dharma? [He stood for a long time.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Not having seen you for three days, do not look upon me as I was before. This mountain monk is no longer the person he used to be."

Heaven is heaven; earth is earth; mountains are mountains; waters are waters; the monastic community is the monastic community; the laity are the laity—they are distinct. They were not as they are now.
Someone asked, "I do not yet understand how it was before this. The mountain monk replied, "In my past, heaven was heaven."
The earth is earth; the mountains are mountains; the waters are water; the monastics are monastics; the laity are laity.
Thus, deluded sentiments obstruct and conceal, veiling the source of the mind. Now, let us distinguish them. Suppose someone were to come forth and say, "I, too, am like the Master:
heaven is heaven, earth is earth, mountains are mountains, waters are water, monastics are monastics, and laity are laity. Would this be so?
"Can it be attained? No. It is simply that you have not yet arrived. Is there anyone who can discern this? If you can discern it, then your eyes of the high seat are perfectly clear and bright.
If you cannot discern it, then the strings and flutes resound through the heavens like music on a boat; the brocades and silks shine upon the water like people by the shore. Be careful."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Is the Way far? It is true in every encounter. What is the Way? The Master said, "Eight feet five inches above the head.
The monk pressed further, "I do not yet understand how this principle is so. The Master said, "Seven or eight inches square. The monk pressed further.
"Is this upward path something that a student may still understand? The Master said, "Regardless of whether it is upward or downward, I do allow you to understand it.
The student further asked, "If that is so, then it is born right where it is and extinguished wherever it is.
The Master said, "How many people misunderstand it in such a way! The student said, "A master of the school naturally possesses [this realization]," and then prostrated. The Master said, "..."
"I have never traveled together with the Elder. The Master spoke again: "Within intimacy, it is simply intimacy; within essentiality, it is simply essentiality.
Do you understand? All of you have set your wills upon exploring the profound and intend to seek liberation.
Here in my mountain monastery, I shall by no means cite the present or the past, nor adopt the right and reject the wrong, to confuse you all."
If you do not come forward, this mountain monk has nothing to say. If you do come forward, I cannot help but cut a piece from your own body and give it to you.
Do you know the sensation of pain? If you suddenly perceive it, you may be said to have attained intimacy.
If you do not know its origin, you will simply wonder where that piece came from. How can you be so...?
How fragrant! How foul-smelling! How raw! How ripe! Do you understand this?
It does not depart from its own place, yet it is ever serene; seek it and you will find it cannot be seen. Take care.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Once one fully realizes the One, all matters are complete. Śākyamuni and Maitreya rejoice in this day. If only the mind is at peace, then wherever one is is peaceful.
There is no calamity, no difficulty, and no distinction between past and present. If you wish to know the source of the Buddha-dharma, take note of the first day of the fifth month.
He descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth: Today is the Double Fifth.
In the world, people nail peach-wood talismans and write them upon their doorframes so that ten thousand evils may not spy upon their households and a hundred ghosts may not enter their gates.

Furthermore, worldly people employ needles for moxibustion and gather medicinal herbs while climbing mountains, so that ten thousand ailments may not afflict their bodies and pestilence may not enter their persons. Thereupon, he let out a cry: "Alas!"
"A-ye, a-ye. A-ye, a-ye. All the people of the great earth have burned through my skin and flesh, causing this mountain monk to endure infinite suffering and pain.
Long ago, a high official of the state of Chu, whose loyal words were not heeded, was drowned in the Xiang River. Later generations mourned him;

they placed rice inside bamboo tubes, tied them with five-colored silk threads, and offered them as sacrifices. This custom has been passed down to this day without interruption. Thereupon, he vomited.
He let out several sighs and said, "The people of the world have eaten rice dumplings and caused this old monk’s belly to burst with distension.
Great assembly, others perform moxibustion; others eat food. Why then does the Elder of Longmen suffer both pain and satiety?

This is because he has not yet forgotten emotional attachments and discursive thoughts. Such matters arise from what is seen and heard, and within this gate, they become mere frivolous discourse. Have you not seen?"
A former sage once said: "The ox in Huaizhou eats the grain; the horse in Yizhou has a bloated belly.
The world seeks a physician, yet he applies moxibustion to the left shoulder of a pig. Why is this? Because running far away is not as good as crawling nearby. [He] stood for a long time.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Entering the Dragon Gate, every matter is extraordinary; hearing sounds and seeing forms is inconceivable. Why are the mountains green and the waters blue?
It is entirely because all people exert their power."
Ascending the hall, he struck his staff on the ground and said, "Can you grasp it? Do not say that even today there is still some margin left;
you must grasp it at a place where there is nothing to be sought, overturning the ravines and toppling the mountains, only then will you have grasped it.

For me to speak thus is truly to be beyond reproach for my lack of discernment. Nevertheless, even if you were to grasp it, I would further question you: from the beginning, what was it that was killed?"
"The sins of theft, sexual misconduct, and falsehood; the sins of drinking alcohol and eating meat—to whom should these be returned? Again, he struck the ground with his staff and said:
"The Vajra makes the ugly; the Buddha receives the fragrant oil."
Ascending the hall on the anniversary of Dongshan’s passing: At the end of his life, our former teacher delivered his final word, extracting the thorn from beneath people’s skin.
It is like ice in the midday sun of the sixth month; as it melts away, it is the same everywhere.
Later generations merely followed the echoes, each transmitting their own version, adding one or two, then two or three. Among them, who is the one without ears? See clearly and depart.
He does not come and die. My late teacher, the Old Monk, served whom I for a long time; I received much from his bitter-mouthed exhortations.
How could my sincere devotion to him be forgotten? I have prepared this modest offering. Everyone, tell me: has the late teacher returned or not?
If you say he has returned, more than ten years have passed since his passing—how can you perceive the principle of his return? If you say...
"He does not come. Furthermore, what is the use of preparing a vegetarian feast? To say he comes is a mistake; to say he does not come is also a mistake.
How can one avoid being mistaken? Do you know how? Three whole iron meatballs.
A pair of seamless wooden buns. [The Master] stands for a long time.
He ascends the hall and addresses the assembly: "Suppose someone calls out, 'Venerable One! and the Venerable One responds.
Even if he were not to respond, he must still acknowledge it within his mind. These days, students say that the one who responds is right, and the one who acknowledges it is right. If..."
To understand it in such a way is to be one who enters hell; let that be for now. But tell me: who is it right before you calling your name?
Is there someone calling, or is there no one calling? Can you yet reach a definitive judgment on this?
If there is someone calling, then when mountain spirits and ghosts call you, or when celestial demons and heretics call you, how will you distinguish them?
[The Master] said: "If it is said that no one calls you, yet you are neither deaf nor foolish, how could there be no one calling you?
This is the matter of the headway of birth and death throughout the twelve periods of the day. Do any of you understand this? When someone calls, delusion arises; when no one calls, one is ensnared.
If you can act accordingly, birth and death are severed—ten thousand taels of gold would never exchange for such a thing. [He then descended from his seat.]
Seated.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: When the Rishi Vimala took Sudhana by the hand, he suddenly beheld as many Buddhas of the past as there are motes of dust;
yet upon letting go of his hand, everything was exactly as it was before. Here, the Elder Longmen led the great assembly. At this very spot...
The summer retreat was entered and concluded exactly as before. At the old site where Sudhana once stayed, the myriad Buddhas of the atoms are contained and have their place of return;
at the old site where the great assembly once stayed, the ninety days of the three-month period are gathered up without a trace.

Do you understand? Within a single hair-tip lies an ocean of lands; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Without departing from the conditions of seeing and hearing, one transcends and ascends to the tenth stage.
The four modes of birth and the six realms of existence are the very nature of the mind; the three miserable paths and the eight difficulties are the universal manifestation of the form-body.
Abiding within the Flower Treasury Ocean and dwelling within the inconceivable—such is the essential meaning, and it is indeed our own constant lot.
Do you still believe this? Entering the hall:
Today is the twentieth of the seventh month; it has already been five days since the summer retreat ended.
You Zen monks all say, "I understand. But tell me: is today the twentieth of the seventh month, or is it not the twentieth of the seventh month?
If this question were posed, how would one respond within the Buddha-dharma? Some teachers say: "Why do you not ask about the fundamental matter?
This is the sun and moon of the world. [The Master asks: "Venerable assembly, what is the sun and moon of the world?
Furthermore, could there be any dharma that does not manage [the world]? There are also teachers who say: "Without moving a single star of the world..."
Disciples, I have already clarified that such matters are to be grasped in this very way. Today is the twentieth day of the seventh month.
Great assembly, where is there even a single atom of movement? One who has attained peace and happiness will never engage in such worldly dealings. I ask you, monks:
Is today the twentieth day of the seventh month, or is it not the twentieth day of the seventh month? Is there anyone who can clearly understand this?
"Ma! An ancient said: 'Worldly matters cannot be fully understood; the Buddha-dharma lies far beyond.
If you cannot discern this point here, you will be stifled and obstructed everywhere. Do you understand? It is difficult to place a hand within a great mass of fire;
it is easy to settle one's body upon the ground of cool clarity. [He stood for a long time.]
Ascending the hall, he raised a precedent: A monk asked Yunju, "What is it like to be one who walks the Path?
He replied, "Like the hand of a dead man. "How is it when those walking the Path meet one another? He replied, "Like the eyes of a dead man. "Great assembly, what is this 'hand of a dead man'?
The Master took up his staff and said, "Without grasping it—how is this the 'eye of a dead man'? The Master snapped his fingers.
He opened his eyes and said, "It does not illuminate. You all should understand this well. It was just like when we sent off the deceased monk the other day;
I said, 'A team of dead men is escorting a living man. Is there anyone who can understand such talk? What is meant by 'a team of dead men'?
The Master said, "Moving the body without moving a step. "What is meant by 'a living man'? The Master said—
It is said: "When ten thousand functions do not reach it, you younger brothers of later generations, at the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, why do you not let out a single roar?
Stand like a cliff rising a thousand fathoms, and let me know that you are a true person. Realize the 'dead word' within the living; realize the 'living word' within the dead.
If you do not do so, you will find no life though you seek it, and find no death though you seek it. Eat.
Even if it is difficult, you must let out a roar.
[The Master] descends from his seat. Ascending the hall, a monk asks: "When the Way lies in being too weary to open one's mouth, and the poem is finished by nodding one's head—how is this?
The Master nods several times. The monk says: "Today I have met [you]. The Master says: "Do not open your mouth recklessly. The Master speaks again: "All of you..."
Every day you speak of thousands and tens of thousands of things; it is not that you do not arrive at them. Why, then, do you fail to understand? It is simply because your faith is insufficient.
If you could truly believe, you would arrive without traveling. The affairs of the worlds of the ten directions would be understood all at once, without waiting for deliberation.
You people speak of thousands and tens of thousands every day; it is not that you do not speak of them. Why...
Therefore, it remains unclear; this is also due to a lack of sufficient faith. If one were able to have such faith, then there would truly be nothing to say.
The Dharma taught by the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time can be understood all at once, without waiting for deliberation.
O Great Assembly, have you yet reached such a state? In this school of mine, we speak only of realization and awakening, not of intellectual understanding.

Explanation: If one is a person bound by birth and death, one must seek direct realization (*pratyakṣa*). If one is a person of human ego engaged in the study of the Way, one feels ashamed at not understanding;
thus, one must seek intellectual comprehension, searching everywhere for similar phrases and mutually validating them.
They have exterminated the Hu race. Since then, the Hu have brought disorder and corrupted the men and women of our families. Within my gate, none of this exists. Do you understand?
Even a deaf man sings the Hu jia flute; he simply cannot hear for himself whether it is good or bad, high or low.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The people of this world all say that traveling the road is difficult. But let us examine the original, authentic gold as it enters the fire.
Through repeated smelting, the essence of the gold becomes pure; with a single blow, it is fashioned into a jade balustrade."
The Master of Transformations is invited to ascend the hall: A single pole, a single hat, and a single raincoat; At the head of a rapid current, he lowers his fishing line.
It is easy to catch the scaled dragon upon the hook; He returns under the bright moon to the depths of the reeds. Case: An ancient asked three venerable elders.
Two dragons contend for a pearl. Who is the one that obtains it? One says, "To obtain it is to lose it. Another says, "The old monk merely watches.
Another says, "Who is it that does not obtain it? The Master said: "To obtain it is to lose it; why make such a fuss?
'The old monk merely watches'—watching what business would that accomplish? As for the final phrase, 'Who is it that does not obtain it? if a person can understand this..."
It is attained. Once you have attained the words and phrases of the Patriarchs and the entire Great Canon, doubts will naturally vanish.

Can you still clarify this? Who is it that has not attained it? It is neither grasping nor abandoning. When it is carried by horse and borne by donkey, that is precisely the moment of returning home. [The Master] descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he struck the Dragon Gate drum and called forth the iron *jūzen*. "I invite you to bite through it once; how could this mountain monk ever deceive you?
My late teacher attained its power long ago, and its flavor remains undiminished today. If you cannot bear it, then it is truly a fine iron *jūzen*."

Ascending the hall, he raised [the following]: "The Master of Changsha said, 'If I were to constantly promote and exalt the teachings and the lineage, the grass before the Dharma Hall would grow a fathom deep.
Truly, these are his words! The Master of Xuansha said, 'It is because of your inverted perceptions that there is coming and going.
Truly, these are his words! Longmen has often seen you all acting in this way; therefore—"
I told you before that it is not so; you must realize it is not so for it to be attained.
Since all people do not realize it is not so, this is why Longmen tells you it is so; you must realize it is so for it to be attained.
Since all people speak of it being so or not so, this is why Longmen says it is neither so nor not so; you must realize it is neither so...
"It is not that it is not thus; only then is it attained. You all are neither thus nor not thus.
This is why Longmen said: 'It is thus, yet not thus. You must be both thus and not thus before you can attain it.
"Assembly, when emotion ceases and wisdom manifests, and when the illness is gone and the medicine removed—is this not a free and unencumbered monk? Longmen usually has one more [point]."
As for this sentence, how does it apply to each person? Have you not seen the monk who asked Master Mazu:

"Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations, I pray the Master will directly point out the meaning of the Westward Transmission. The Master said, "I have no heart-mind today; go ask Zhizang.
The monk asked Zhizang, and Zhizang said, "I have a headache today; go ask my brother Hai. The monk [then went to ask Hai].
He went again to ask Hai. Hai said, "When I reached this point, I did not understand. The monk reported this to Master Ma.
The Master said, "Zangtou’s head is white; Hai’s head is black. "Great assembly, he spoke of white and described black;
the principle is quite clear. Do you all see Master Ma? To stand for so long is truly groundless."
Ascending the hall, he said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like gazing at the full moon on a mid-autumn night;
pure and free from the veil of clouds, all people see it, and throughout Jambudvīpa there is nowhere it does not illuminate. Yet each of you dwells in a different land and a separate well."

Each has their own parents, home, and mountains. Tell me, do these still exist within that state? As for the mountains, rivers, valleys, and remote, uninhabited places—do these still exist within that state?
Furthermore, how could there be no people coming from elsewhere? Each person says they have seen this moon;
yet this full moon does not come from this direction, nor does it go to that direction. If it were to come from this direction, then it would not exist in that place.
Furthermore, if that [moon] has already departed from that direction, why is it seen here? The same applies to the four intermediate directions, above, and below.
Thus it is said: "A thousand vessels are set out side by side; all the thousand vessels are round. A single stream flows through the river; a single moon shines solitary and clear.
Long ago, someone pointed at the moon and asked Master Nanquan, "When shall I attain such a state? Nanquan replied, "Wang Laoshi..."
Ten years ago, I also came in this very same way. Monks, I tell you that in this matter there is no place for your conjecture, nor is there any place for your conceptualization.
Now, all you practitioners of Zen say, "I have understood it. But where is it that the light does not reach?
For now, let me ask you about that which the light does reach: from which realm did you, Venerable One, come in your previous life?
"After this body has perished, where will one be reborn? Will one become a deva, a human, a denizen of hell, a hungry ghost, or an animal?
If one does not know this clearly, what is the use of such empty talk?
One day, while the Great Master Mazu was gazing at the moon, two or three disciples were attending him. The Master said, "At this very moment, how is it?"
Xitang said, "Excellent offerings! Baizhang said, "Excellent cultivation! Nanquan shook out his sleeves and departed.
The Master said, "The Sutras return to the Tripitaka; Zen returns to the sea. Only Puyuan alone transcends the mundane world.
Observing how they debated in this manner, it was truly extraordinary. When the Master posed this question, all the great beings were moved to silence.
To patch a nose cut off and hope to restore one to a whole person; to fill a ravine and shift a peak so as to achieve level ground—does this accord with Master De’s single question?
Do you understand it thoroughly? After a long silence, he said: "Fortunately, there is no place of partial illumination; yet, there is still a time of non-illumination."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "The Patriarch said: 'Do not love the holy and hate the ordinary. If you understand the dharma of the ordinary person, it is itself the dharma of the sage.
If you recognize the dharma of the sage, it is itself the dharma of the ordinary person. Everyone knows that the ordinary and the holy are non-dual;
why then do ordinary people drift in samsara while the various sages are liberated? It is also said: 'Do not discard delusion to pursue enlightenment. Now, what is enlightenment?"
That which was formerly delusion is now awakening; that which is now awakening was formerly delusion. Everyone knows that delusion and awakening are non-dual.
Why is it that the deluded remain as obstructed as before, while the awakened remain as lucid as ever?

Can you all discern this clearly? Once the distinction between ordinary and sage, awakening and delusion, has been thoroughly penetrated, one will see the person of original nature with transparent clarity. I ask you: what is this?
"Great assembly, what is the person of original nature? Usually, when teachers and monks speak, where do they not see this person of original nature?
Is Mr. Donkey-Lips the Great Sage of Sizhou? It is also said that he has no face; where could one encounter him?
When distant water cannot save from a near fire, apart from these two paths, what is the person of original nature? After a long silence.
The Master said: "Even if one were to attain awakening upon hearing [the teaching], how could that compare to attaining it for oneself directly?
He descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "In the past, the Venerable Wuzhuo traveled to Mount Wutai to pay homage to Mañjuśrī.

Upon reaching the foot of the mountain, he stayed overnight at a temple. There he encountered an elderly monk who was waiting for him. The monk asked Wuzhuo, 'Virtuous One, from where have you come? Wuzhuo...
He replied, "I come from the South. The old monk asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma in the South these days?
Wuzhuo said, "In this age of the Dharma's decline, few bhikṣus observe the precepts. The monk asked, "How many followers do you have? Wuzhuo said, "Sometimes three hundred, sometimes five hundred.
Wuzhuo then asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained here, Master? The monk replied, "Ordinary people and sages dwell together; dragons and snakes are intermingled."
Zhaozhou said, "How many people are in the assembly? The monk replied, "Three times three before, three times three after.
Zhaozhou did not understand and, having a youth bring a crystal cup of tea to serve to him, he then asked, "Is there such a thing as this in the South?"
Zhaozhou said, "There is none. The monk asked, "If there is none, with what will you drink your tea? Zhaozhou again failed to understand. The Master then ordered a youth to escort him out the gate.
Zhaozhou observed that the temple had no name plaque and asked the youth, "Why does this temple have no name plaque?
The youth pointed behind him toward the *vajrapāṇi* (kongo). Zhaozhou looked back; suddenly the youth was gone, and he found himself alone in a forest.
[The Master] said: "O Great Assembly! Wuzhu traveled far to Mount Wutai to pay homage to Mañjuśrī. Yet, when he actually beheld him, he did not recognize him.
How truly bitter! Therefore, Master Mingzhao composed a verse: 'The sacred monastery pervades the entire realm of sand; Mañjuśrī fills my eyes as we engage in conversation.
Yet, beneath these words, I failed to open the Buddha-eye; Turning my head, I see only the lush green mountains.'"
At Mount Yan, Master Xuedou also composed a verse which says: "The thousand peaks wind and turn, their color like indigo;
Who would say that Mañjuśrī is here in dialogue? How laughable are the many followers at Qingliang Mountain— Three times three before, and three times three after. Great assembly!
These two verses span from antiquity to the present; they are indeed beautiful, yet for all their beauty, one still does not see Mañjuśrī.
I, this mountain monk, shall now compose a verse for you all, saying: Beyond the green mountains, white clouds fly; By the green waters, the stream leads guests home.
Do not wonder why I urge you repeatedly to drink as we sit; Since we parted, I have rarely seen you. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he rested his staff upon his shoulder and said to the assembly, "It is truly laughable! It is truly laughable! He then laughed heartily, "Heh-heh.
"Yesterday, two people were discussing a certain matter with this mountain monk. Upon hearing it, I laughed so much all night long that my intestines and stomach ached.
Again he laughed heartily, "Heh-heh. "Does the great assembly wish to know? One of them said, 'Today is...'"
The third day of the month. According to the official calendar, it was written as the third; however, the people in the village said it was the fourth, following the local village calendar.
When they asked the old monk, "Is it the third? the mountain monk replied, "It is the third. They asked, "Is that the official calendar?
The mountain monk said, "It is the official calendar. They asked, "What the villagers call the fourth—is that the local village calendar? The mountain monk said, "The third."
"Fourth is the village calendar. That man nodded his head. Again, another person said, 'Today is the fourth; it is written on the official calendar.
But the people in the village say it is the third. This refers to the village calendar. What do you say to this, Elder?
The mountain monk replied to him, "It is the fourth. The third is the village calendar. That person nodded his head.
The two men met and recounted their respective experiences in detail. One said, "The elder told me it was the third.
The other said, "The elder told me it was the fourth. The two then came to see the mountain monk and asked, "Today is the third;
today is the fourth. Upon hearing this, the mountain monk laughed until he nearly died. The two men said, "Elder, please do not muddy the waters."
"Turbid. Speak clearly and well. The mountain monk says to you: "It is you yourself who are not clear. Where is the turbidity?"
"Great assembly, do you understand this meaning? Seeing that they do not comprehend it, I can do nothing about it.

A Zen monk among the assembly said, "Venerable sir, why is it that after beating the drum to assemble the crowd, you do not speak even a word of the Buddha-dharma or the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, but instead occupy yourself with mundane, idle matters?
This is merely the worldly view of common people. When I, the mountain monk, heard this—
[The Master] finished speaking and asked him, "What idle days are there in this world? Furthermore, what is 'emotional view' (*qingjian*)?
Bring it here and show me. He originally did not understand. Seeing that he did not understand, [the Master] further composed a verse to present to him. The verse says:
What is called "intimate" is also intimate; there is neither falsehood nor truth. The ignorant and worldly call it "self," while heterodox followers call it "god.

As for this so-called "self," when has it ever been a self? As for what is called "god," how could it ever be a god? A person must be truly discerning. Then, picking up his staff and descending from the meditation seat, he said:
"The sixteen-foot body of purple-gold—before the seat, he further addressed the assembly, saying: 'I do not wish to trouble you.'"
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "When the Great Function manifests and no rules or regulations are maintained, what then? The Master said, "Who would believe you? The monk then gave a shout.
The Master said, "Try taking another step forward and see. The monk said, "Fortunately, I have one bow and three arrows;

when the opportunity arises, I intend to shoot those who are not level. The Master said, "In youth, he once broke through the ranks of dragons and snakes; now in his decline, he is like a mere child."
The monk sang a verse. The Master shouted again. The Master said, "So, you are nothing but a wild fox spirit. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "When has your great function ever been manifest? The Master spoke again: "In ancient times there was one person, Master Nanquan.
Do you all recognize him? If you can recognize him, your entire life will not have been spent in vain. Do not let it be that you see Master Nanquan but fail to..."
"Consciousness. Do you recognize it? Once, a layman asked, "In my home there is a piece of stone.
It has been used for sitting and for lying down. Now I wish to carve it into a Buddha; I do not know if this is permissible. Nanquan said, "It is permissible.

"Is it not permissible? [the layman asked]. "It is not permissible," [Nanquan replied]. "Is there anyone who can clearly understand this principle? Nanquan said, "Yes. Longmen said: [The text ends here.]
"What a fine Buddha! Nanquan could not say it; Longmen said, "A fine piece of stone. Do you see it?
He said, "Within the house of a disciple. How can one speak of a 'house'? Where is the house? O virtuous ones, you have come directly from within the house.
What is there within the house? Holding this single piece of stone—vast, firm, and enduring—it was once at Vulture Peak.
Offering to the Buddha: When Śakra, Lord of Devas, casually raised his hand, what did emerge from within his heart? "Peace and happiness, as well as long life. [The master] descends from the seat.

Ascending the Hall for the Imperial Birthday: "The Emperor takes the world as his home and the myriad people as his children. Father and child are of one body; this is Heaven."

The next section concerns the family. When the king loves the people and the people revere the king, and when this mutual love and reverence are established, the Way of the King knows no bounds beyond them.

Therefore, the Buddha said: "It is as if the people have obtained a king," and also: "It is as if the people are the king. Furthermore, there is no people outside the king, and there is no king outside the people.
If the king were outside the people, the people would not receive his bounty; if the people were outside the king, the Way of the King would not be expansive. How could this be?

It is said: "The people. Those who lack knowledge are called the people. How is it that one is called a "King"? One who possesses sagehood and spirit is called a King. The present Emperor, the Sovereign, is supremely divine and supremely sagely;
he is the parent of the people. On the occasion of the festival of the Heavenly Descent, the sun, moon, and stars formed a "linked pearl" and "joined jade" configuration.
The Yangtze, Yellow, Huai, and Ji Rivers stir up the turbid and elevate the clear; Heaven and Earth manifest their creative power;
plants, trees, insects, and fish present auspicious omens and display wonders—all of which are brought about by the response to the Emperor’s supreme virtue.

I humbly pray that his longevity may rival the Southern Mountains and his age equal that of the Northern Peak, enduring for ten thousand years forever, without end or limit. Thereupon, he descended from his meditation seat, performed a dance, and said: "Do you understand? The Mountain."
The monks danced, raising clouds of dust, crying: "Ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Ten thousand ten thousand years! He descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "Perfect, luminous awareness does not depend on mental conceptions.
To strive desperately to express it is to fall into pits and ravines. After all, how is it? He then leaned his staff against the wall and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: Once there was a scholar who saw the Chan Master Changsha reading the *Sutra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas*.
He asked, "I have heard the names of so many Buddhas, but I do not know in which lands they dwell.
Changsha said, "After Cui Hao inscribed his poem on Yellow Crane Tower, did you, scholar, ever compose one yourself? The scholar replied, "I have not. Changsha said, "Then compose one for nothing."
The section is excellent. The scholar was at a loss. Great assembly, why did Changsha speak in such a manner when the scholar asked where the Buddha resides?
Why was the scholar unable to utter a single word before Changsha, whereas he usually composed verses on the wind and the moon?
If it were the Yellow Crane Tower, what difficulty would there be in posing a question? Listen as this mountain monk composes a verse for it.

He broke [the silence] and said: "His countenance is most wondrous; his radiance illuminates the ten directions. I have previously made offerings to him, and now I come once more to behold him in person.
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall: At dawn, at the hour of Yin [3–5 AM], within the state of madness lies the person of the Way.

Great assembly, throughout the twelve periods of the day and night—whether turning or walking, bowing or rising, coming or going, speaking of right or wrong, distinguishing south from north, engaging in activities, opening the sitting mat and unfolding the bowl, or eating gruel and rice—all of these are states of madness.
But tell me, which among these is the person of the Way? After a long silence:
He said: "The azure void has sentient beings who look on in longing; the jade terrace has no path by which to seek them out. He descended from his seat.

Upon ascending the hall for the formal discourse, the Master said: "Just now, while I was dreaming in my private quarters, I heard the Dharma drum. I then descended the steps of the hall and dreamed that everyone came up to me.
As they approached to pay their respects, I ascended the Dharma seat. After the attendant had finished burning incense, it is now exactly as it is."
A person within a dream recounts the events of that dream; do you all still see them as a dream? If you can truly see this, you are an awakened person.
Failing to recognize the realm of dreams, you remain utterly submerged. Is there any dharma at all that serves as an opponent for you?
As the ancients said: "There is no dharma before the eyes; the intent lies before the eyes. It is not a dharma of the present moment."
"It is not something reached by the ears or eyes; is this not truly extraordinary? Did you see it in a dream? Śākyamuni Tathāgata said:
"It is like a person who has awakened; even if their mind were sharp and clear, for what reason or cause would they seek to grasp objects from within a dream?
He then picked up his whisk, struck the meditation seat, and asked: "What is this? Do you hear it? He then held the whisk upright and asked: "Do you see it?"
After a long silence, he said, "Among all the spiritual friends in the human realm and the heavens, who can compare to Mengde at Longmen? He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "The ancients said: 'The Buddhas do not appear in the world; for forty-nine years they have preached.

Jin said, "The Patriarch did not come from the West; Shaolin possesses a wondrous secret.
The Master said, "Those who recognize kindness are few; those who betray it are many.

Jin said, "If that is so, then one person may transmit what is false, yet ten thousand people will transmit it as true. The Master said, "How can that which is false be transmitted? Jin said, [and remained silent].
"Let the vast ocean change as it may, / In the end, I shall not deliver [the message] for you. The Master said, "Pay your respects. The Master spoke again:

"From the time he returned to the West with his single shoe until his robes were rolled up and he journeyed south, we have heard nothing but rumors that have drifted down through the human world. From antiquity to the present day,"

Passing it along with mutual respect and acceptance—this is much like one person transmitting an emptiness that ten thousand people transmit as reality. This mountain monk, having suffered many illnesses, has become well-versed in the nature of medicines;
being old, he has grown wise. It is not that I am being critical or exploitative of the ancients, but rather to prevent us from mutually obscuring one another.
You all must have, from the past, encountered points of realization and, through what you saw and knew, received teachings from others within the words of their instruction.
While it is true that there is no lack of coming and going and playful activity within the midst of time, the ultimate reality of the Great Matter can by no means be attained through these.

Only when sentiment is lost and principle is discarded, when calculations are exhausted and paths are at an end, and when there is no place for the mind to be applied—this is precisely where one exerts effort.
This mountain monk usually says only, “Go drink tea”; today I also say, “Go drink tea. Do you understand?
Exhausting the five flavors of Chan from all directions—how does this compare to the mountain monk’s “Go drink tea”?

When you wish to think and yet do not think, and the moment [of realization] is trodden upon, ten thousand miles of cloudless sky are ever revealed.
Ever revealed! Its wondrous function is as vast as the sands of the Ganges, not merely for a morning or an evening. All you practitioners of Chan...
My lord, it would be well to cease hostilities and end war, forever laying down the weapons of conflict. To dwell by water and lean against mountains, one accomplishes great matters.

Have you not seen the ancient masters say: "If one does not practice dhyāna and śamatha, when one arrives here, one will be utterly bewildered"? For a long time...
He stood up and ascended the hall, saying: "Coming and going, going and coming—at the very moment of coming and going, one departs from perception and cognition.

Going. At the moment of coming and going, birth and death are manifest. The arising of the preceding thought is "coming"; the ceasing of the succeeding thought is "going.

Hills and mountains are utterly free from a speck of dust. Spiritual powers and wondrous functions are employed even in carrying water and hauling firewood.
Shitou remained silent and granted his permission. Later, he traveled to Jiangxi to visit Master Ma. [Shitou said: "I do not obscure the person who is originally so;
I ask the Master to cast his eyes high. The Master looked directly down. Shitou said, "Of all the stringless lutes, only you, Master, can play them with such subtlety.
The Master looked directly up. [The Master said: "Great Assembly, had it not been for Master Ma, he would have been thrown into utter confusion by that single question."
Shattered! Everyone, what do you call the "original person"?
If there were no original person, how could one see forms with the eyes, hear sounds with the ears, and engage in all manner of activities and movements? Do you all still see this original person?
Nowadays, everyone says that the original person is formless and signless; they have never put on clothes or eaten food, and they are neither born nor die. Is it like this?
This assembly has attained it; how can one strive to unite with the person who is primordial? Do you wish to know? All of you are precisely that primordial person.
As for this single segment of birth and death, afflictions, and ignorance—how shall they be dispelled? Listen to a verse: "Today’s path we travel together with you;
As we look upon the primordial person together, We share the same name, the same surname, and the same physical form— Death does not exist."
Without birth and without the dust of form—how can it ultimately be? One must by all means refrain from calling this the "original person.
