He replied, "Three pounds of flax. "Great assembly, there is such a matter; for what reason does no one know it? Seeing that people did not understand, Dongshan then—"
The self-eulogy says: A bull’s head is painted with the seven treasures, its forehead dotted with gold. In the clear spring of the second or third month, all farmers take this as their model.
During the Cold Food Festival, a fine new coin is worth three or four hundred iron coins. O virtuous ones!
This single cycle of causes and conditions—whether coarse words or subtle speech—all returns to the primary meaning (*paramārtha*). It is further said: To apply it according to the occasion. One.
This is by no means ordinary. To understand and interpret it in such a way is to bury the ancients.
Do you wish to see the Old Man Dongshan? A wild goose takes flight for a thousand li; a hawk piercing the clouds soars level with heaven. A phoenix is no common creature;
as an auspicious omen, it appears only at its own appointed time. [I have stood long.]
When the Master arrived at Zhencheng, he was invited to ascend the hall. Zhencheng cited the words of Shishuang: "The entire world has never been hidden.
The Master said: "The entire world is not hidden; its whole substance is revealed. If there is even a hair’s breadth of seeing, the matter is still mistaken.

Who among those in the assembly is a guest from Xiantuo? Without stirring a single speck of dust, one arrives home. One who has truly arrived home forgets the words upon grasping the meaning, yet remains solitary and alert."

Those outside [the teaching] give rise to interpretations according to their own sentiments; once such interpretations arise, names and forms flourish. When both speech and thought are forgotten, the ten directions are all permeated.
Have you not seen how the Head of the Hall just now gave a universal address to the assembly? Why, then, would I, a mountain dweller, attempt to further promote it?
It is simply because the wondrous intent is profound and subtle, and people find it difficult to penetrate. Why is this? Once one knows that it is but a few inches away...

In the midst of this, why do you say, "I did not behold the Master’s countenance"? Since it is said that he pervades the boundaries of the world and fills all of space, how can you further say that he was never hidden or concealed?
Do you see where the flaw lies? If you can see this, then you will see Old Man Shishuang and Great Master Xuefeng;
you will also know this mountain monk of Longmen and Elder Zhencheng, as well as this entire assembly of Chan practitioners.
Harmony. Generally, there are places where one is divided. Before this mountain monk had left our own monastery and arrived here at Zhensheng, there was not a single person from Longmen among us.
Now that this mountain monk has left our own monastery, crossed the wilderness, and come to Zhensheng, everyone here has met one another;
thus, there is now one person from Longmen among us. If there were even one person from Longmen...

"Old age brings increase regarding the Dharma. If there were not even one person such as the Elder Longmen, the Dharma would decrease. Because it decreases, one falls into nihilism; because it increases, one falls into eternalism.

Having fallen into nihilism and eternalism, how can this be called right view? It is just like when you, Venerable Sirs, had not yet left the household life—there was not even one person called 'Venerable.
Once you had left the household life, there was one person called 'Venerable. How do you all account for this?"
"Having reached a definitive resolution, one attains peace and happiness in the mind-ground. Can you still deliberate further? There is an entrance here; what else remains to be done?
If [the student] has not yet attained clarity, [the Master] remains silent for a long while and says, "You do not know how to be a guest. He then stands for a long time.
Ascending the hall, he said: Sitting alone, one finally believes that the West has brought forth Bodhidharma. Walking alone, there is no need for red lotuses to sprout beneath one's feet.
Speaking alone, to whom are these words clearly addressed? Who would grant them assent? Investigating alone, every land and every speck of dust reveals the guiding compass.
Meeting and questioning one another to exhaust the ultimate point—do not say that this mountain monk is merely acting out of foolishness.
Ascending the hall on the anniversary of Master Duan’s passing: "The man of old has already mounted the white clouds and departed;
here, only the green waters remain to flow. Once the green waters have gone, they never return; the white clouds drift empty and vast for a thousand years.
According to the old sayings of Hunan, the aged Yangqi lost his golden-haired lion cub; he can be found nowhere south of the Yangtze or north of it. Today at Longmen—
The wind blows with the current; the wind blows with the current. La-la-li. The water is swift and the wind high as the fishing line descends from the weir.
Entering the hall: A bird flies through the void; a person dwells within the mind. When a person dies, the mind remains just as it was; what concern is the void when the bird has vanished?
Human life passes like a fleeting bird; this mind is truly what one can rely upon. Simply realize this mind for yourself; there is no need to ask further.
Coming and going. Therefore, Subhūti asked the World-Honored One: "How does one abide? The World-Honored One replied: "One abides in this way:
causing those born from eggs, born from wombs, born from moisture, and born by transformation; those with form and those without form;

those with perception and those without perception—all to enter *nirvāṇa* without remainder and bring them to extinction. Yet, in reality, there is not a single sentient being who is truly extinguished. Thus it returns.
Do you understand? Within the three realms and all phenomena, there is not even a hair’s breadth of the characteristics of arising and ceasing, or movement and stillness.

It is solely because of delusion regarding this that one is inevitably confused and takes them to be within the physical body. Thus, that which is solid and obstructive is called "form" (*rūpa*); that which experiences is called "feeling" (*vedanā*); that which conceives is called "perception" (*saṃjñā*);
that which flows and changes is called "volitional formations" (*saṃskāra*); and that which discriminates is called "consciousness" (*vijñāna*). All of these are established by one's own mind. For...
Failing to realize that these are called the five aggregates (skandhas), one consequently establishes the duality of matter and mind.

Not seeing the Way, one does not clearly perceive that the five aggregates are all empty, and thus cannot transcend all suffering and calamity. Is this present body of the five aggregates existent? Or is it non-existent?
If one can see and realize it in this way, there will truly be no such things as birth and death. If this is not yet the case, how could there be no coming and going? There indeed are.

First, there are no causes or conditions for birth and death. He brought this up to the assembly, saying: "In the past, when I went with Dàowú to offer condolences, I patted the coffin and asked Dàowú, 'Is he alive?
Is he dead? Dàowú said, 'I will not say he is alive; I will not say he is dead. Jiàn Yuán did not understand.
Later, he heard a monk reciting the Lotus Sūtra: 'Those who should be saved by means of the body of a bhikṣu... [The text continues: "...immediately..."
He manifested in the form of a bhikṣu and preached the Dharma for him. [Zhanran] suddenly attained realization and subsequently went to Shishuang.

Carrying a spade, he walked up and down the Dharma Hall, going from east to west and from west to east. Shishuang asked, "What are you doing? Zhanran replied, "I am searching for the remains of the former master.
Shishuang said, "The vast waves are immense, and white billows reach the heavens. What 'remains of the former master' are you looking for?"
"Bone. Jianyuan said, "The sacred bone of the former master still remains. Great assembly, can you see it? Holding up his staff, he said, 'This is the staff;
which one is the sacred bone? This is the sacred bone; which one is the staff?
He then struck once and said, 'In Chang'an, every night there is the moon in every house; its reflection falls upon the cold pond.'"

One who knows this ascends the hall and says: "If we discuss this matter, it is like a person buying a field. The four boundaries and limits are all clearly defined and the contract is finalized at once;
there remains only the tree in the center that still belongs to me. O Great Assembly, since these four..."
This is the very clear conclusion regarding the "fruit. Why is it that the tree in the middle still belongs to him?
Have you not heard it said: "A field of a thousand years has eight hundred owners"? If you can recognize the tree in the middle, then let them plow and hoe as they please;
let them sow seeds as they please; let them bloom as they please; and let them bear fruit as they please. If there were no "middle," [there would be no such thing].
Jian Shuzi was disputing over what is called "permanent abiding" (changzhu). After a long silence, he asked, "How is it? He replied, "Where it is high, it is level;
where it is low, it is level."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Dragon Gate has nothing particularly marvelous; it is merely called the 'Direct Transmission of the Mind Essence.

Not only is there no fish in shallow water, but even when one probes and searches, there is not a single opening or hole to be found. At the two meal times, they unfold their bowls and spread their mats; day after day, they defecate and urinate.
In every matter, they are just like everyone else—look closely, and it is quite laughable. Since everything is just like everyone else’s, for what reason..."
"What is called a 'good spiritual friend' (kalyāṇamitra)? After a long silence, he said, "Even I cannot fathom this. He then ascended the hall and said:
"Monastic communities (saṃghārāma) are now numerous throughout the world. Yet, if you seek even one person who understands the 'Dharma-preaching of the insentient,' there is none;
let alone understanding it, it is difficult even to find one person who can bring up this story. Why is this? One must have personally heard it from the source."

Only when you have come to understand the Dharma can it be pointed out to you. If you have not personally heard it, even if it were pointed out, it would only increase your worldly afflictions (*kleśa*) and provide no nourishment for your life of wisdom (*prajñājīvita*).
Great assembly, as the gathering is small, pointing it out is especially difficult.

Although the monastic communities (*saṃghārāma*) are daily decaying, if you wish to clarify this principle, you must observe it by leaving behind all conceptual thoughts. If even one person attains understanding, the entire assembly [will benefit].
"Peace of mind through totality. Since it is a single person who attains understanding, why do the entire assembly attain peace of mind?
If it were not so, how could it be called the gateway to liberation?
Ascending the hall, he raised [this case]: Master Zhigong said, "I see that people in the world each cling to their own particular divergent views;

they only know how to seek cakes by the side of the griddle, yet they do not understand how to return to the source and observe the flour. The cake has always been flour; its various transformations depend on human effort. Do you all understand?
The house cat and the white ox recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*; the kitten and the puppy meet one another constantly."

All you meditation practitioners, whether you have attained realization or not: if you say that the self-nature is fundamentally perfect and luminous, it is much like groping in the air to catch a flash of lightning.
Do you understand? It is like seeking Chang’an from atop the Hanyuan Palace, or wishing to be reborn in the Inner Courtyard within the palace of Maitreya.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "A thousand-fathom line hangs straight down; when a single wave stirs, ten thousand waves follow.
What is this 'single wave'? The Master said: "How do you usually swallow and spit it out? The monk asked: "What are the 'many waves'? The Master said:
"What difficulty is there in putting on clothes and eating food? The monk asked: "Please, Master, speak the phrase at the tip of the hook. The Master said: "You..."
[The Master] himself took [the fish]. The monk said, "The bold one who casts his line upon the river—on his pole, there is often a scaled dragon.

The Master said, "There is no connection. The Master spoke again: "O virtuous ones, there is nothing superior to this moment. There is always this 'so-it-is' (rnam pa de lta bu), yet there is also a time when it is not so-it-is.
Those who study Chan say there is no time when it is not so-it-is; to speak of 'so-it-is' is already [a conceptualization]."
It is not like that. When it is "like that," it is called attaining mindfulness; when it is "not like that," it is called losing mindfulness. Now I ask you all:
do you always lose mindfulness, or is there also a time when you do not lose mindfulness?

For those who study Chan, they always speak of the time of attaining mindfulness, yet to speak of "attaining mindfulness" is already to have lost mindfulness. If you wish to know how it is "like that," simply understand this.
When you do not grasp [it] in such a way, you must clearly understand mindfulness. Simply recognize the moment of lost mindfulness;

therefore, the former masters said, "In this way, in this way," and also said, "Not in this way, not in this way. O eminent elders, why do you seek such strange things? For this reason, Śākyamuni Tathāgata further said:
"Whether mindfulness is attained or lost, there is nothing that is not liberation; whether dharmas are established or destroyed, they are both called Nirvāṇa."
The hells and the celestial palaces are all pure lands. Do you yet know this one segment of reality?
If you know it, you will forever transcend the afflictions of beginning and end; throughout the twelve periods of the day, you will naturally abide in peace and ease, free from concerns.

Descending from his seat, he ascended the hall and said: "Within the Dragon Gate, without moving, one practices the kōan of the ancient Buddhas. Having personally encountered their true countenance, how could one fail to speak of one's own appearance?
The minds of ordinary beings and sages are equal; the paths high and low are level and plain. When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, the temple steward..."
[He] lost his beard and eyebrows. For what reason? [The master] descended from his seat.
He ascended the hall and raised the case: "When the Great Master Huineng was at the head of Mount Dayu, he said to Upādhyāya Shiming: 'Do not think of good...'"
Do not think of evil. At this very moment, which one is the original face of Elder Ming?
Ming then attained great enlightenment. "Assembly, do you understand this saying? At this very moment, throughout all kalpas, he has never been deluded."
Step by step, one transcends the triple world;
returning home, doubts are suddenly severed. Ascending the hall, he raised this case: A monk asked National Teacher Zhong, "What is the original body of Vairocana?
The Master said, "Hand me the pure pitcher. When the monk handed him the pure pitcher, the Master said, "Take it back and place it where it was before. The monk then returned it.
At his former dwelling, he came again to ask, "What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana? The Master said, "The ancient Buddhas have long since passed away.

This Dharma-gate cannot be understood through mere intellectual comprehension unless one has realized it through entry; if you let the monkey of the mind run wild, you will only end up with conceptual understanding.
Ordinarily, everyone says, "From where does it come? It is not Vairocana," yet they do not even recognize this. He asked again.
Is this not because he passed away long ago? Furthermore, it is said that the National Teacher was in his own state of *samādhi*.
If you ask about Vairocana again and again, he himself is an ancient Buddha who passed away long ago. Again, it is asked: "What is the original body, Vairocana?
After a long silence, one should understand well; if you do not know thoroughly, you will fall into the weeds. I shall tell you: hand it over to me!
"Bring the pure pitcher. Interpreting it in such a manner merely lets loose the monkey-mind; one does not see the National Teacher when he says, "I have attained it in my heart.
To take *eranda* as a sandalwood tree is to lose the essential meaning; to regard nectar as a garden of thorns (*kaṇṭaka*) is likewise so.
Do you understand? Beneath the gate of the Great Sun, every day is autumn; before the Hall of the Bright Moon, every moment is summer. O Great Assembly! It is like this.
"What is this Vairocana? "Returning to the hall to drink tea. [He] descended from his seat. Ascending the hall:
Once, Master Zhaozhou visited a hermitage keeper and asked, "Is there? Is there? The hermitage keeper held up his fist. Zhaozhou said, "The water is too shallow;
it is no place for a boat to moor," and he swept his sleeves and departed. He then visited another hermitage.
The Master asked, "Is there one? Is there one? The abbot of the hermitage held up his fist. Zhaozhou said, "He can grant and he can take away; he can kill and he can bring to life.
He then paid three prostrations and departed. The Master said: "The abbot of the hermitage raised his fist in the same way.
Why did Zhaozhou accept one and not accept the other? Tell me, where does the gain and loss lie? Zhaozhou.

Rising by oneself and falling by oneself; how many masters have you scrutinized and broken through? The Hermitage Master sits blocking the vital ford; how many winters and summers have passed? Do you wish to recognize Zhaozhou?
(He strikes the right corner of the meditation seat and says: "Recognize Zhaozhou! Do you wish to recognize the two hermitage masters?
(He strikes the left corner of the meditation seat and says: "Recognize the hermitage master! Is there anyone who can examine this for gain or loss?

[The Master] stepped down from his seat. After a long silence, he said: "It is easy to open one's mouth from beginning to end, but difficult to preserve a heart that remains steadfast through the winter's cold.

He then descended from the seat. Layman Wu invited him to ascend the hall [for another sermon]. "The body is the Buddha-body; you must believe that the six sense-faculties are pure. Conduct is called Buddha-conduct."
Thus we know that the three karmas are perfectly luminous: when the body is pure, defilement has no place to arise; when conduct is luminous, darkness has no place to emerge.

The arising of defilement stems from delusion regarding purity; one fails to perceive or realize that purity itself becomes defilement. The departure of darkness must necessarily result from attaining luminosity.

That clarity is identical to darkness is difficult to believe and difficult to understand; thus, while the various sages constantly bestow their protective empowerment, sentient beings abandon themselves to neglect.

If one were to simply change one's thoughts at the very beginning of what can be done, and transform one’s emotions toward the end of error, one would personally open the key of wisdom and look upward to knock upon the gate of compassion.

With the wisdom-eye that perceives the minds of others, [the Buddhas] know all clearly; even grave offenses and karmic grudges from past lives may all be repented. This is the compassion of the Bodhisattvas.
May my vows pervade the Sahā world; when sentient beings cast themselves in sorrowful supplication, may there be no one who does not receive a silent response.

Thus we know that light and darkness share the same substance, and defilement and purity originate from the same source. Ordinary beings have the opportunity to attain Buddhahood, and Great Beings have the mandate to deliver living beings.

If it were not thus, the myriad virtues would arise in vain. Layman Gongda and Dao-ren the monk thoroughly understood the nature of bubbles and illusions, and fully realized the transience of all things.
We have come together into the mountains to investigate and clarify this matter. This morning, we invited the mountain monk to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma.
I recall that in the past, when Pei Xiu visited Master Hualin, he asked, "Does the Master have any attendants?
Huilin replied, "There are one or two. Pei Xiu asked, "Where are they? Huilin then called out, "Dakong! Bukong! At that moment, two tigers emerged from [the thicket].

From behind the hermitage, two tigers roared and emerged. Xiu was startled and terrified upon seeing them. Lin said to the two tigers, "There is a guest; depart for now. The two tigers roared and left.
Xiu asked, "What practice did you master, Master, that you have brought about such a response? Lin remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you understand?
Xiu replied, "I do not understand. Lin said, "This mountain monk constantly recites the name of Avalokiteśvara; the assembly understands."

Do you understand this meaning? Constantly recite the name of Avalokiteśvara; his power subdues even fierce beasts. When the eye of the Way is clear and penetrating, how can the myriad conditions exist?
How excellent is the Great Being! He extends his hand at all times. Keep this in mind and let it dwell there; thus one shall attain peace, joy, and long life. [Descend from the seat.]
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Yongjia attained enlightenment in a single night and then declared: 'How many times born, how many times dead? Birth and death drift on, without end.
Since I have suddenly realized there is no birth, what anxiety or joy can there be regarding honor or disgrace? "Great assembly, to speak of the existence of birth and death is a verbal expedient;
to speak of the non-existence of birth and death is likewise a verbal expedient. Once one has entered the realm of verbal expedients, then..."
These are matters of practice; furthermore, while practice is coarse and easily manifest, principle is subtle and difficult to reveal. Thus, the words are near while the intent is far-reaching.
How can one clarify such a far-reaching intent through words that are so near? Is this not indeed difficult? The former sages taught:

"Attain the intent and forget the words; set aside the facts to contemplate the principle. Later generations, failing to understand this, seek principle outside of facts and search for intent beyond words.

It is like grasping and rubbing the void with one’s hand; one merely exhausts oneself in vain, for in the end there is no benefit. Do you wish to know where power is exerted and where the mind is applied?

You must find the non-substantial within the substantial and the wordless within the verbal; only through such awakening and entry will you be intimate with it. It cannot be attained through intellectual understanding alone.
If it is thus, its manifestations and concealments, its activities and applications, are a divine function difficult to fathom. Have you not seen how a monk asked Shoushan: "If..."
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Shoushan said, "At the edge of King Chu’s city, the Ru River flows eastward.
Upon saying this, someone attained awakening and returned to the hall.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The light of the five colors is produced by a visual impairment (*taimira*). Simply remove the impairment; do not remove the dust.
If you say that the original eye has ever been impaired, you are like one who dies of thirst by the river."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "Before the kalpa-fire and before the Ābhāsvara Heaven, there is a separate realm;
watching the hunt from the imperial tower is not like clearing a field of reeds. The monk then held up his sitting cloth and said, "I wonder what this is called? The Master said:
"Right View mows the thatch-field. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "You still act as the host. The Master spoke again, "It would have been better to say a single phrase;
had someone been able to understand it, there would have been some merit. But if no one can understand it, my words would become false.
After due reflection, it is better to stop for now. Let us all go together into the hall to drink tea at our own leisure."
He is free and at ease. He need not fear that at some other time or on another day he will be exposed by others. Why? Because the General already possesses a glorious reputation;
even if he does not receive a fief as a marquis, it is still of no consequence. Go drink tea. [The Master] descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case. He said: "Master Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying: 'Wang Lao-shi is going to sell himself.
Is there anyone who will buy him? At that time, a monk said: 'I will buy him. The Master said: "What a fine Zen guest! Nanquan said:
"'Not at a high price, not at a low price'—how will you buy him? The monk had no reply. The Master said: "Ha! It makes one laugh to death!"
Several venerable elders have provided commentaries on this monk’s words. Zhaozhou said, "Next year, I shall make a cloth robe for you, Master.
One person said, "What kind of logic is that? Another said, "The Master belongs to me. Later, Xuedou said, "There is no room for the Master elsewhere.
Venerable assembly, these many elders vied with one another to purchase [the karmic merit], did they not?
I must transport my own household goods. Master Wang, our transaction has not yet been finalized; I dare not dispose of them recklessly.
Such wares as these are rarely seen in all antiquity or today. Today at Longmen, I am also selling myself. Thus, there are those that are precious and those that are base.
The base are not worth a single coin, while the precious are beyond comparison with gold and jade. Will you buy?
It belongs to you; even if you do not purchase it, it still belongs to you. If you recognize this Dragon Gate, the Dragon Gate will become your companion.

Whether in the presence of others or in solitude, whenever you give rise to a thought or stir a movement of mind, it knows you entirely. It will cause you to proceed toward the good and cause you to cease from the evil.
Even if you pass through the three miserable realms and traverse the eight difficulties, it will not abandon you for a single step, but will always be with you.
Act as a companion on the Way. If you do not recognize Longmen, Longmen will become your adversary;
he will cause you to leave the household life, send you forth on pilgrimage, direct you to seek out teachers, and dispatch you to investigate the truth.

He will then lead you to a state of non-understanding, leaving you in a state of bewilderment, causing you to search for intellectual comprehension, and leading you to craftily construct rationalizations. Thus, he causes the Pure and Wondrous Land to...

It creates mountains, rivers, and the earth; it takes constant delight in the Dharma-body while producing ignorance and afflictions, resulting in a lack of mastery and the constant arising of regression.
It never lets go for even a single step and constantly acts as your adversary. O Great Assembly! You have been at this Dragon Gate for a long time.
To recognize it is to be a fellow traveler; not to recognize it is to be an adversary. Is there anyone here who can clearly understand this?
"How is this? He then picked up his staff, tapped it once, and said: "First, a companion; second, an enemy. Pervading both the favorable and the adverse, as vast as the sands of the Ganges.
The eye is empty; the cataract is the flower. Having reached the Dragon Gate, the Way is boundless. He then set down the staff and said:
"Stop showing off your cleverness. Return to the hall."
Ascending the hall: "In the twelfth month, the fan’s merit is exhausted; a vast, cool breeze stirs through the vast void.
It does not merely serve to dispel the sweltering heat of the sixth month, but for a moment provides you with relief from your vexations and fever. Descending the seat.
When the Fifth Patriarch arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "The Great Master of Caoxi transmitted the robe and returned to Lingnan.
Later, Reverend Rang received the Dharma and bestowed it upon Great Master Ma. Great Master Ma received Baizhang; Baizhang received Huangbo."
Huangbo attained Linji; Linji attained Xinghua; Xinghua attained Nanyuan; Nanyuan attained Fengxue;
Fengxue attained Shoushan; Shoushan attained Fenyang; Fenyang attained Master Ciming.
Master Ciming received one person, the Venerable Yangqi. Now, let us look at the matter he attained. This old fellow—
It is said: "In my place here, it is like climbing a pole in a bustling marketplace; everyone sees it. How could you deceive their eyes?
Later, the old man Yangqi succeeded only Master Duan. This elder once resided on this mountain and composed a verse which says:
"When the pearl at the bottom of the sea stirs, The moon in the clouds appears again. On a cool night without a wild wind,"
The pure light is entirely one. Later, Master Wenduan received the Dharma from our late teacher alone. Our late teacher had said:
"Just by biting through a single iron pastry, one comes to possess all hundred flavors.
This is why this old man has spent his life with a stubborn mouth, fond of speaking blunt words. Since the time our late teacher entrusted me with his charge, the Great Dharma has been transmitted.
"Bring it here. Finally, on Mount Dongshan, it was all at once entrusted to the present Abbot of the Fifth Patriarch’s Hall.

On this day, we have the good fortune to stand before this vast assembly of humans and devas; I pray that you will not withhold your compassionate grace, but once again proclaim and manifest it, so that the ancestral school may have a firm foundation.
My Way becomes ever more clear; there is no one who does not share in this great fortune. Ascending the hall:
"Phenomena as bubbles and illusions are equally unimpeded; how is it that you do not awaken? The pupils in your eyes are like blowing a whistle—realization of the Dharma lies right within it.
It is neither of this age nor of antiquity; six dice roll out, and the bowl is full of red. "O Great Assembly! People of this time..."
"Why sit on the ground watching Yangzhou? The bowl with its handle is a newly fashioned style. Riding an ox while mounted on an ox—this makes people laugh to death.
He ascended the hall and said: "When you people had not yet reached Longmen Mountain, you thought Longmen was in the world. Now that you have arrived at Longmen..."
Mastery of mind. The pines and cedars rustle, the waters murmur. Do you all recognize Longmen Mountain?
If you do not recognize it, you cannot avoid its mountains being green and its waters being blue. How much of the light and time of a hundred years can there truly be?

Before you have turned the light back to reach the source, everything becomes a dream and an illusion. [The Master] then took up his staff and said: "Sentient beings of the six realms create offenses and karma."
"The Buddhas of the three periods of time who have attained Buddhahood and become patriarchs are all upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff. Do you people see them?
(He strikes once. He says, "They are shattered into a hundred fragments. Then he extends his hand and says, "Bring me even so much as a hair's breadth of them!"
He struck the floor once more and said, "Holding the talisman of nocturnal illumination in hand, how many know when day breaks? He then descended from his seat.

Entering the hall, he said: "The *xièzhài* (unicorn) is ridiculed for being kept in the same pen as sheep; yet when incense and rotten herbs are placed together, it is the incense that must remain fragrant.
O worthy ones, those who have attained the Way never distinguish themselves from others, yet they are praised by all the sages of the past—truly there is something extraordinary."
Among humans, it is like two people who share the same womb, the same parents, the same house, and the same teacher;
even in matters of food, drink, and speech, they are entirely without difference. One day, they enter the examination hall together for the same subject, yet one passes while the other fails.
The one who passes becomes forever distinct from the common masses, whereas the one who fails...

These two are originally ordinary people; from the beginning, there has been no change in their fundamental nature. Yet, there is a difference between nobility and meanness, high and low, just as there is between attaining and not attaining—initially there is no difference at all.
However, one person attains it and their rank becomes equal to the sages, while the other person remains deluded and thus becomes an ordinary worldling (*pṛthagjana*).
Although the persons themselves are not distinct, the distance between delusion and awakening is vast. How can the great assembly not be struck with awe?
How truly terrifying! As Master Xianglin said: "Twenty years ago, I saw those of my own generation who all attained the Way.
Day and night I pondered, 'What did they attain that allowed them to depart in such a manner?
For twenty years I constantly observed them, and later I too became like this. You should look at these former worthies."
These words of bitter admonition are indeed worthy of trust. How can you persist in clinging to a stump, wasting your days and months in vain?
You should each take this to heart; henceforth you must depart. There is no need for you to stand here any longer. Descend from your seats.
Ascending the hall: At the Dragon Gate on the fifteenth day of the third month, the great drum beats its call at every stroke.

It calls forth all at once, yet this only gives rise to confusion and disorder. Great assembly, since it has called them all forth at once, why does it specifically give rise to confusion and disorder?
This is a fine opportunity; how will you all resolve it? If you do not know how to resolve it, you will become even more confused. If you know how to resolve it, it is different.
After a long silence, he said: "This single segment of causes and conditions has no one to sever it; I leave it for all quarters to examine and sever together. He ascended the hall and said:
"I have obtained my original name and ordination certificate, and have traversed the mountains and rivers of my own land. Having heard that there is an Elder at Longmen,"
"I have come here to study the Way and practice Zen. How can such a clear-headed person as this stand right here and nod off to sleep?

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Students nowadays do not investigate the Buddha’s words; they only investigate the words of the patriarchs. They do not realize that the words of the patriarchs are themselves the words of the Buddha.

If you wish to see it clearly, Do not seek it within the six sense objects. If you can see it right now, You will know the source of the myriad phenomena. If you do not see it right now, How can you avoid being deluded? He then descended from the seat.
"What is this radiance? [Dongshan] answered on his behalf: "The triple gate, the Buddha hall, the kitchen, the storehouse, and the monks' hall.

This state of confused turmoil is taken as the nature of the mind. Once deluded, this becomes the mind, and one is inevitably bewildered by form."

Within the body, one does not know that the physical form, extending outward to the mountains, rivers, empty space, and the great earth, are all objects manifested within the wondrously bright, true essence of the wondrous mind.

Even having words is not correct, let alone being without words. Do not dream! From morning until night, you treat the Buddha-dharma as one side and the patriarchs as another.
Speech is one extreme; having speech is one extreme; being without speech is one extreme; conceptualization is one extreme; being without conceptualization is one extreme.
If it is thus, it can truly be said that when looking, nothing is seen—only a dark, murky void. [I have] stood for a long time.
