Xing. The Master said, "Tomorrow is the twenty-seventh. Question: "What is the fundamental matter of a patch-robed monk?
The Master said, "A camel crossing the Han River. Question: "What is the one phrase that is intimate and direct? The Master said, "Bodhidharma had no front teeth."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Study must be genuine study; insight must be genuine insight. If you have not yet seen clearly, you must discipline yourself to seek and inquire extensively of those who have gone before.
There is no room for even the slightest pretense. For now, seek an entrance at Dongshan’s place.
All dust-motes and lands, all realms, all Buddha-realms, all realms of sentient beings—throughout the entirety of the ten directions."
All things and categories are simultaneously brought into the palm of one’s hand; they reside within the eye, yet possess no marks of coming or going.

They do not obstruct seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing. When one lifts a single foot, heaven and earth tremble all at once; when one takes a single step, the waters of the ocean all surge with billowing waves.
When one lifts a foot, Mount Sumeru shatters into a hundred fragments; with a single spittle, the void—
Empty space falls flat upon the ground. Do you all know for yourselves whether this is being utilized every day?
Dongshan, having no other recourse, has applied the treatment for a dead horse; before these brothers of superior capacity, it has become nothing but a source of laughter.
What could one possibly say in the presence of those of such superior capacity? One must push, one must press, let out a shout, and strike with the staff.
"A single blow—can you attain it? Pointing to heaven, pointing to earth—can you attain it? Five-character and seven-character verses—can you attain it? Fine wind, fine rain—can you attain it?
To sing and proclaim in such a manner is to stir up the entire earth so that it cannot turn; it is to take a broom, sweep everything into a single heap, and burn it with fire.
Tie it with bamboo strips, cast it into the river, and let it flow away. But how will you go? Take care! Question:
"What is the realm of Dongshan? The Master said: "A villager. Oil Gourd. Question: "When one’s own body and hands commit offenses..."
[Question: "How is it when one is beset by verbal entanglements? The Master said: "Look at this solid cast iron. [Question: "What is it like after one has realized this? The Master said:
"Seeking food by following the smoke, one mistakenly enters the house of a tanner. [Question: "By what means can you provide instruction so that students may penetrate through the golden dust?
The Master said: "The hooves of the Son of Heaven’s horse ring out. [Question: "If the mind is free from affairs, the myriad dharmas do not..."
"How is it at the moment of birth? The Master said, "The wind-bells have a melody truly worth listening to; yet even as one listens, the tune remains unformed.
[The student] asked, "At such a time as this, where are Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra? The Master said, "The elder is eighty-one; the tree does not grow.
[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "One is not formed; two are not so. [The student] asked.
"What is the original eye of the student? The Master said, "A whirlwind does not turn to the left. Question: "Vimalakīrti held up the four worlds with his palm;
I wonder where Vimalakīrti’s body is located? The Master said, "It is behind you, O teacher. [The questioner] said, "..."
"Why is it that you remain behind the student? The Master said, "Give me back the head of the phrase. Question: "Dharmas have no fetters; why is it that entering them is so difficult?
The Master said, "A Persian reading Sanskrit texts. Question: "If one goes directly like this, one still traverses the path.

Please grant us a word regarding the place where effort is saved. The Master said, "The leather belt does not fit the girth. Question: "How is it? The Master said, "Give me back the head of the phrase."
"This is the source of the Great Way. The Master said, "The heavens are wide, but the earth is narrow. A question was asked: "All Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra.
I wonder, from what place does this sutra emerge? The Master said, "Not a single character is to be marked with a dot."

[The student] asked: "How is it that not a single word is touched by a dot? The Master said: "The blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head. [The student] asked: "What is the phrase that transcends birth and death?
The Master said: "Sweeping the floor and filling the vase. [The student] asked: "I do not ask about the long serpent or the crescent moon;
what of the lone horse and single spear? The Master said: "The thread is large, but the nostrils are small. [The student] asked: "When the mouth is about to speak..."
Yet his words failed him; his mind sought to grasp the object, but his reflections were lost. This is still a matter belonging to the realm of birth and death.

What, then, is the matter that transcends it? The Master said, "Ānanda did not carry the Buddhist scriptures. The questioner asked, "If one only obtains the root, there is no need to worry about the branches. What is this root?"
The Master said, "His hands are slender and his feet are large. [The monk] asked, "What is the 'end'? The Master said, "It cannot be measured.
He ascended the hall and said, "In this place of Dongshan, the usual practice within the abbot’s quarters is not like that of other places. When someone comes up here—"
One goes down. With a chirping and buzzing sound, he speaks of the Chan Way and the Buddha-dharma in private;
yet all of it is spoken from his full mouth before you brothers—spoken from his full mouth, brought forth from his full mouth, selected from his full mouth, and sifted from his full mouth.
There is no place for you to shield or conceal yourself on the left or right; he has turned it all out at once. How, O Virtuous Ones, will you thoroughly comprehend this? You—
Try to speak before the assembly. It is like the ant that can settle anywhere, yet cannot settle upon a flame.
They have been led astray by those old bald monks from all quarters with their sweet lips and eloquent tongues, who say, "This is Chan;
this is the Way; this is Bodhi and Nirvana; this is True Suchness and Liberation. Thus they are deceived.
A twelve-foot nail and an eight-foot wedge; the wedge is right in the eye, yet one neither knows nor perceives it.
Upon suddenly arriving here at Dongshan, one does not know what kind of talk this is. Do you understand?
Even if you were to understand True Suchness (*tathatā*), Nirvāṇa, Bodhi, and Liberation without the slightest discrepancy, you would still be bound by a rope at your heels, unable to escape.
If you are a sharp and discerning monk, take one bite and cut it off completely, becoming a free and easy monk—would that not be delightful?
If you cannot cut it after three or two bites, you will continue as before to enter the ranks of the dull-witted;
when will there ever be a time for you to emerge? Dongshan, having no choice, exerts his strength for you from the sidelines. Take care! Question: What is...?
The Master said, "A phrase for receiving people. The Teacher said, "When the cock crows and it is not yet dawn, the neighbor walks at midnight.
[The student] asked, "How does one comprehend this? The Teacher said, "Go freely east or west. [The student] asked, "What if one seeks instruction in just this way?

The Teacher said, "A scale of a thousand catties cannot be stopped. [The student] said, "The path of birds does not exist. The Teacher said, "You have miscalculated the fixed point on the scale. [The student] asked.
The speaker and the listener—both are like an illusion. When there is neither speaking nor listening, how can it be? The Master said: "A horse cannot overtake it. [The student] said:
"If that is so, then I shall believe, accept, and practice it. The Master said: "Give me back the head of the matter! [The student] asked:
"How can one discuss the principle so as not to obscure the Master’s school? The Master said: "Heaven is dark blue and earth is yellow. [The student] asked: "What is 'unchanging and unmoving'?"
"Realm. The Master said, "The thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. Question: "What is the realm of the one true reality?

The Master said, "A patch-robed monk’s worn-out straw sandals. Question: "Setting aside existence and non-existence, please give us the definitive point, Master. The Master said, "A three-legged cauldron without handles. Question:
"When both [existence and non-existence] have vanished, what then? The Master said, "Holding the needle while losing the thread. Question: "Without passing through..."
[The Master] spoke a verse from ancient times: "I beg the Master to employ the universal sound. The Master said: "A scholar riding a donkey. [The student] said:
"If that is so, then I, this disciple, shall listen attentively. The Master said: "Holding a handkerchief in his hand. [The student] asked: "I do not ask about the present mind;

what is the original mind? The Master said: "Long waist and short legs. [The student] asked: "Regarding the source of the Immovable Wisdom, how does one engage with sentient beings? The Master said: "Great."
"Pitiful that Bodhisattvas lack hands and eyes. A questioner asked: "Before one’s face are three shifting phenomena; behind one are ten thousand forms. What of this? The Master said:
"Nata does not recognize his father. The questioner asked: "How is it that Nata does not recognize his father? The Master said: "The pupil in the eye builds a breath-ball. A questioner asked:
"I do not ask about the earth being encompassed and heaven being universal; but as for responding to the occasion without missing the mark—how is that? The Master [said]:...
[The Master] said, "I announce this three times to the great assembly. A question was asked: "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said:
"The Sixth Patriarch loves to eat *huáluó* (mixed) rice. A question was asked: "Before a word has been spoken, the Buddhas of the ten directions already know [the time].

What of it? The Master said: "'Do not come,' O bhikṣus; [I shall speak of] the desire and the purity. A question was asked: "The matter of birth and death is great; we pray that the Master will save us. The Master said: "The three families."
The villagers lost their fire. [Student] asks: It has been said of old that "the lands speak and sentient beings speak; the three periods of time are spoken of simultaneously.
This is certainly not non-existent. I wonder, for whom is this spoken? The Master says: "Those with three heads and two faces. [Student] says:
Is it that it is indeed not non-existent, yet is it also non-existent? The Master says: "A shrimp leaping cannot get out of the measure. [Student] asks: What is it to not rely on a teacher?

[The student] asked about the matter of reaching the ultimate limit. The Master said, "Observe the celestial phenomena at night. [The student] asked, "By taking whom as his teacher did Śākyamuni attain unsurpassed bodhi?
The Master said, "Among the three thousand offenses, none is greater than filial impiety. [The student] asked, "If one knows there is [the truth], one does not establish it."
Even false existence does not arise. At such a time as this, how can one speak of it? The Master said: "Six ears do not share a secret. Question:
"What is the source of the Great Way? The Master said: "Barefoot, one boards the boat. Question: "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished?
The Master said: "Three rounds of *karmavācanā* (formal ritual acts). [The questioner] said: "After the *karmavācanā*, what then? The Master said: "Why [do you ask]?"
[The student] does not observe the five precepts. Question: "Even this is still not it. How then is it so? The Master said:

"By nature, I do not drink wine. Question: "From antiquity until now, it has not been obtained from another person. What did the Sixth Patriarch hear at Huangmei during the night? The Master said: [He heard the sound of the wind in the pines.]
Zhigong held up his staff and asked, "When it comes to using it, how is it? The Master said, "What would you do with that ruler?
A monk asked, "What is 'a hair swallows the vast ocean'? The Master said, "The lips of the Sixth Patriarch are large.

A monk asked, "Who is the person who understands the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Two paths of binding. A monk asked, "Regarding the principle that 'the lush green bamboos are all True Suchness'—"

"How is it? The Master said, "In the morning one roams among mountains and waters; in the evening one dwells in a thatched hut. A question was asked: "When one has attained self-acceptance, ordinary people still have their own perceptions and views.
But when one does not see oneself, what then? The Master said, "Look at this cast-iron lock fastened with raw iron. A question was asked: "As soon as one extends a single question..."
“I regret that I did not think of this sooner. I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, “Both will find it convenient. A monk asked, “What is the fundamental matter of the student?
The Master said, “A three-legged shrimp has no back legs. A monk asked, “When there is no sign before one’s eyes, how does one manifest the True School?
The Master said, “An eighty-year-old old woman holds a fan in her hand. A monk asked, “What is the mirror of no-mind? The Master said—
[The Master] said: "The water is three feet deep. [The student] asked: "Does it still reflect the mind of the student? The Master said: "It is seen through to the very marrow. A question was asked:
"When a single speck of dust is raised, the entire earth is fully contained within it. What is this 'single speck of dust'? The Master said: "A Persian entering a temple. A question was asked:
"I see only the long hair of a tortoise, but I do not see the horns of a hare growing. I beg the Master to manifest the horns of a hare. The Master said: "The pupils in the eyes."
[The Master] was building a balloon of qi. A questioner asked: "When the silk is exhausted, the loom stops; this is the meaning of the provisional practice of all Buddhas.

Regarding the matter that transcends this, I ask the Master to speak directly. The Master said: "Do not lose your affection for the many. A questioner asked: "In all quarters it is said 'this very mind is Buddha.
I wonder, how is it here with you, Master? The Master said: "Seven or eight pieces of a bottomless bowl. A questioner asked: "What is it to transcend Vairocana?"
Regarding Śākyamuni’s discourse, the Master said:

"When Kāśyapa looked at the Buddha, as he ascended the hall, the Dharma drum had just been struck and the entire earth was fully encompassed. All you virtuous ones, do you know whether you are coming and going within the sound of that drum?
Speak before the assembly! If you cannot say, you have been thoroughly deceived by Dongshan. He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "‘This very mind is Buddha’—this breaks the two doubts of attachment. ‘Neither mind nor Buddha’—this is like staying overnight in a thatched hut, yet still remaining outside the gate.
As for the one path above, not transmitted by the thousand sages, how can these entangling words be the matter within the domain of a patch-robed monk?
After a long silence, he said: "Even if you could produce it, it would be nothing more than a worn-out straw sandal. He descended from the seat. A monk asked: "Heavenly Hall..."
[The monk] asked: "What kind of people dwell in hell? The Master said: "Dongshan. [The monk] asked:

"What is the Dharma-body? The Master said: "Walking on water wearing boots. [The monk] said: "Is that not so? The Master said: "A tortoise on the water with its head glowing red. [The monk] asked: "..."
"Activity, cessation, effort, and extinction—these are still the maladies of *dhyāna*. How can one avoid them? The Master said: "A Brahmin monk does not bare his shoulder. Question:
"Before there is a question and before there is an answer, how does one deliberate? The Master said: "He cannot hold the alms bowl; he breaks the bowl."

Question: "The golden crow emerges from the sea, its brilliance illuminating heaven and earth; how does this compare to the matter of this very moment? The Master said: "Kunlun crosses the sea boasting of his treasures;
at the gate of the Persian, he displays his abundant beard."
Ascending the hall: "The realms of boundless lands—self and other are not separated by even the tip of a hair.
When the sound of the fish-drum vibrates at Dongshan, at Yanqing, Baima, Vulture Peak, and Guyin, the monks and masters all enter the Sangha hall in ranks to eat their meals.
How many of you, virtuous ones, can recognize them? Speak before the assembly! If you can speak here, then there will be something truly excellent."
"There is no traveling on foot. If you do not attain the Way, there will come a day when Old Yama demands payment for your straw sandals.

He then descended from his seat. A monk asked, "One who transcends Buddhas and Patriarchs is hard to find. I beg the Master for a single phrase to reveal the source. The Master said, "Cutting a robe, one mistakes the collar for the lapel.
A monk asked, "In an ancient temple, pure and secluded, how does one discern the host? The Master said, "Reproach. The monk said, "By what skillful means can you obtain it?"
Beholding his compassion, the student burned incense, knelt on his right knee, and asked: "To ensure that the Buddha-seed is not severed, I pray for a word from the Master. The Master said:
He was struck by the planet Venus. Question: "When the entire earth is covered in gold, how is it used? The Master said:
"The constellations fill the heavens; it rains during the day."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Virtuous ones, you carry your alms-bags and staffs to travel through thousands of villages and ten thousands of miles, solely because you do not understand birth and death, and you seek to penetrate the Dharma and awaken to the Way.
Wherever you go, there must surely be venerable elders and good spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) whom you may visit.

If they can untangle your entanglements and remove your fetters for you, such that your eye of the Way becomes clear and you are able to discern right from wrong, and they are fit to be your masters, then immediately—"
Break the staff and hang up the alms-bag; strive for that ultimate penetration, and do not worry that it will not be accomplished.

If you open your mouth and move your tongue to speak of "upward" and "downward," "this side" and "that side," "mysterious realization" and "wondrous realization," or of "exit" and "entry," "ruler and minister" and "father and son," or "clarifying the essence" and "clarifying the function"—all of this is to slander Prajñā and bury the ancestral wind; it shows you do not recognize what is good.

You wicked bed-wetting brat! You have brought misfortune upon future generations with no end in sight. I shall pull you down from your rope-cot, strike your spine with a staff, and drive you out through the triple gates.
I will send you back to wander as a pilgrim to serve as a superior condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) for you. Only then will you be able to breathe freely within the Gate of the Patriarchs;
furthermore, you must join your palms and stand with feet together there, responding with a cry of assent, and gather up the wild fox drool and spittle for yourself until you are truly convinced.
He spoke again: "I have had the Master select [the truth] for me and explain it to me, so that I might find a place of peace and ease.

But have you truly awakened? Have you truly attained clarity? To call this 'sickness' while failing to meet a skilled physician, or to mistakenly take another's toxic medicine—recognizing the bridge of a donkey’s saddle as one's father’s chin—what connection has that with your own fundamental matter?"
"I know that your lifelong wandering as a pilgrim has done nothing but wear out your straw sandals; from beginning to end, you have achieved nothing but being a wretched fellow.
Begone! Question: "To discipline oneself in order to seek the Truth is the great error of a practitioner. To be able to discern the heterodox from the orthodox—"
[The student] said, “I am still at odds with the essence of the Way; I do not yet understand how to practice and realize it. The Master said, “Six dice all come up red at once.
[The student] asked, “It is not within, it is not without, and it is not in between. I wonder, where does it reside? The Master said, “A loose-fitting robe does not cover the body.

[The student] asked, “What is the student’s own self? The Master said, “One’s own kinfolk do not grant one any advantage. [The student] asked, “What of the ten thousand [things]? The Master said, “... (text fragment)

"When conditions have all ceased and the six gates are simultaneously at peace—how is it then? The Master said, "The sky is clear, yet you refuse to go. [The student] asked, "If one goes in this very manner, how is it then?
The Master said, "One must wait for the rain to soak one's head. [The student] asked, "When people from throughout the entire world come, how do you instruct them?
The Master said, "Your tongue is stuck to the roof of your mouth. [The student] asked, "I request the Master to pull out the wedge. The Master said, "Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down."
Question: When the mind and its objects are not yet clear, what is it like? The Master said: "The tongue protrudes to the crown of the head. Question:

The Great Canon of the Teachings is but a field of right and wrong; I, the student, earnestly request the Master to speak. The Master said: "Having hands, one does not snap the fingers. Question: What was the meaning of the Emperor of Heaven striking the head cook?
The Master said: "Having drunk wine, one does not thank the host. Question: What is the student? The Master said: "Having hands, one does not snap the fingers."

[The student] asked about the ultimate matter. The Master said, "Speak. [The student] said, "I do not yet understand what you are saying. The Master said, "Stirring a stake in the mud. [The student] asked.
"How does one proceed so as to immediately attain the ultimate principle without error? The Master said, "Lowering the hook upon the water.

[The student] said, "If that is so, then it is a mistake to labor in vain along the path. The Master said, "To know for oneself is to be half-way there. [The student] asked, "It is said, 'If you only obtain the root, do not worry about the branches.
What is the root of this student? The Master said, "A straw sandal with no sole. [The student] asked, "What is the dust-age [of samsara] that never ends? The Master said, "A single blade of grass."

[The monk asked about] a matter that is obscure. The Master said, "One who has stripped off his clothes does not cross the water. [The monk] asked, "When adding one and subtracting one, where does the principle return?
The Master said, "A leap year occurs once every three years. [The monk] asked, "A true practitioner of the Way does not see the faults of the world.
I wonder, what faults are there in the world? The Master said, "Two people wear crimson robes; one wears black. [The monk] asked, "In a place where smoke and clouds do not reach, call it..."
"What are you doing? The Master said, "The burning of paper money was not done at the proper time. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then one must carve an image of the Buddha into the ground.
The Master said, "One does not notice the stench of one’s own excrement. [The monk] asked, "Among the three bodies (trikāya), which body preaches the Dharma?

The Master said, "The words of the father come from the father’s own mouth. [The monk] asked, "What is the mouth that preaches? The Master said, "Give me back the head of the story. [The monk] asked, "As for [the state of] suchness..."
"What is the phrase for brushing away the dust to see the Buddha? The Master said, "A red banner is unfurled atop Mount Chu.

Question: "Mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way. Is there still a fault here or not? The Master said, "Know the size of the immortal. Question: "Regarding the root-source of birth and death, I beg the Master to point out a path of entry.
The Master said, "The head is split and the forehead is torn. [The student] said, "I do not understand. I beg [for further instruction]."

The Master gave an indication. He said, "Above heaven and below heaven. A question was asked: "I have heard it said of old: 'Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil;
the Sovereign attains the One and brings order to the world. But when a monk attains the One, what then? The Master said, "Five times nine is forty-five;
the great sun enters the door. A question was asked: "Are the Buddha-dharma and the Way of Chan the same or different?"
The Master said, "He combs his hair but does not wash his face. A questioner asked, "When the bright moon is suspended in the sky, how does it reflect and illuminate?
The Master said, "Its measure is insufficient. A questioner asked, "Having long sifted through sand and gravel, I have yet to see the true gold.

I pray the Master will point the way. The Master said, "Entering the water, my feet remain dry. The questioner said, "If that is so, then this student has gained its use. The Master said, "Alas, your soles are still damp. The questioner said, "Indeed."
"A single word can cause the loss of a nation. The Master said, "I do not know whether it is so or not; if it were so, it would be truly marvelous.
A questioner asked, "Everywhere else is within the confines of the measuring line. I wonder, how is it here in your monastery, Reverend? The Master said, "An oar and an arrow strike Mount Sumeru.

A questioner asked, "Leaning on a fence and feeling one's way along a wall is something everyone knows. As for the True Dharma Eye of all Buddhas, I ask the Master to point it out directly. The Master— [remained silent].

[The Master] said, "In a dream, it strikes the third watch. A question was asked: "When one is self-reflectively aware while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down throughout the twelve hours of the day, how is it?

The Master said, "Watch someone else eating their meal. [The questioner] said, "But what can be done about the fact that the shadows of the trees do not slant? The Master said, "The words of a parent come from the mouth of the parent. A question was asked:
"If there is even one dharma, Vairocana falls into the state of an ordinary person; if there are no ten thousand dharmas, Samantabhadra loses [his ground]."
[The student] asked, "As for that realm, I do not yet understand how it is. The Master said, "The pupil in the eye builds a ball of qi.
[The student] asked, "The myriad phenomena of the forest and all things are all sealed by a single dharma. What is this one dharma? The Master said, "What would you do with your eyes?
[The student] said, "Do you permit a student to make use of them? The Master said, "How regrettable! [The student] asked, "Gold and brass..."

[The student] said, “It is manifest before you; I request the Master to explain. The Master said, “A two-legged toad swallows the moon. [The student] asked, “What is it like when there is no testimony for the ultimate word?

The Master said, “When one has a toothache, they cauterize the left ear. [The student] said, “Sweetness and bitterness are commonly spoken of. The Master said, “You do not truly understand what you have heard.”
Calling a bell a jar. A question was asked: "What is it like to be one who obtains the pearl from the black dragon’s belly without having traversed the vast ocean?

The Master said: "Four hands and eight arms. A question was asked: "I have long been ignorant of the jewel in my robe; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "A magnet does not attract a needle. A question was asked.
"Curved like the moon, with three stars spread wide. It does not exist in the Western lands; what is the situation here? The Master said, "East, south, west, north. Question:
"How can one accord with the Way throughout the twelve hours of the day? The Master said, "Picking up the east and feeling for the west. Question:

"Regarding the ancestral vehicle of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, I ask the Master to grant us an instruction. The Master said, "An old crow’s thread has snapped. Question: "In a single thought-moment..."
[The student] asked: "It has not yet arisen; why then do you not see yourself? The Master said: "One draws lines on the ground to create a prison. [The student] asked:
"When this single phrase is exhausted throughout the Dharma-realm until the end of the future, what then? The Master said: "With money, one’s way is open for a thousand li;
without money, one is deaf behind the wall."
Ascending the hall, he said: "A single grain of cinnabar turns iron into gold; a single word of ultimate principle transforms the ordinary into the holy.
The worldly dharmas are likewise so. Dongshan asks you venerable ones: what is the principle that transforms the ordinary into the holy?
Try to speak it before this assembly. Although it does not emerge from the head, it has already been spoken within the belly. How so?"
This is the principle of transforming the ordinary into the sacred. But tell me, what is it that is transformed? Do not nod off! How so?
Is it a shout or a blow with a staff? Such an understanding is merely like beating a wooden gong at every street corner and alleyway.
Those practitioners who recite the *hṛdaya* mantra using a wood-apple (*kataka*) rosary have their views and understanding already established.

But what should you, you monks, do? You must possess the eye of wisdom to be able to distinguish the heterodox from the orthodox; do not simply pass your time in this manner. Venerable ones, time does not wait for man;
you must exert yourselves with all your might. Wake up from your sleep and see for yourself what the principle is! Long ago...
Stand up. Take care. Question: Does a person who does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion still have the matter beyond?
The Master said: "A Daoist wears a crown on his head. Question: What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Truly and accurately so. Question:
What are the Three Jewels? The Master said: "One cannot reach a consensus. Question: What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: "Soy sauce."
A maggot in a jar. [The student] asked: "What is it like when one arrow hits the mark? The Master said: "It passes by. [The student] asked: "Where does it pass by?
The Master said: "It sticks."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Now, as for those who call themselves Chan masters, they must have clarity regarding their own fundamental matter and possess the eye that discerns the Dharma.

Eulogy on the Universal Access to Reality According to Objects (with Preface):
Nothing is more supreme than the Way; nothing is more vast than the Dharma. There is no expression that does not manifest the Way.
There is no phenomenon that does not emerge from the Dharma. Now, the sentient beings are vast and boundless; when one exhausts their origins and ends, to what do they return?
Everywhere they are in a state of frantic haste; relying upon birth and death, on what can they rely? Dongshan has composed this verse in brief to lift up the great principles.
The Name Penetrates Reality According to Objects. The verse says:
When it is present before one's eyes, what is easy and what is difficult? How can one point it out? To manifest that the Dharma is wordless, objects possess their own objects.

To speak is to have words; yet, luminous clarity is unimpeded, and perfect understanding is boundless. To see this is to realize the Way; there is no need for repetition. Every single thing is myself;

the essence of all the sands of the Ganges is complete. Phenomenon after phenomenon is devoid of inherent existence; where words are used, there is nothing that can be said. It is seen with the eyes and heard with the ears.

It penetrates downward to the Yellow Springs; it is nothing other than this. The ancient sages all transmitted it; one who attains it may preserve it, and one who sees it remains at ease.
The idle talk of today arises from groundlessness. There is yet another word—look well, look well!

Verse on Clarifying the Way: The Great Way is level and easy; it is vast and boundless. It is clearly transparent and utterly still—how peaceful! Its wondrous function contains all within it, manifesting as square or round according to things.

This is the Dharma of one’s own fundamental mind, yet sentient beings are deluded regarding its source. There is no separate Way apart from the Way; there is no separate mystery apart from the mystery.

As previously stated, those who lack faith must rely on objective conditions (*ālambana*). To realize that the mind of consciousness (*vijñāna*) is itself the Buddha is peace. What does the mind take as its object of consciousness? And what is the consciousness apart from the mind?
When both mind and consciousness have vanished, the seeing of the Way (*darśanamārga*) is foremost. From antiquity to the present, the essence remains as it is.
Ordinary and sage beings share this together; the sands of all worlds stem from the same source. Sages of past and present have awakened to this and transmitted it.

My son, three monkeys tossing coins at night; the oxen’s verse on tending a single ox:
moving in and out without a pen or corral, let it loose among the fragrant grasses, and its coat-color can finally be revealed.
Leaving at dawn, no one pursues him; returning at dusk, no one calls for him. His strength is irresistible; he has horns but lacks a nose-ring.
If not employed, he follows his own will; if employed, he turns according to the person. There is no wasteland under heaven; it is all transformed by this ox.
If someone seeks him out, he runs away to the ends of the earth; yet when brought before you like one of us, we ask: "Do you see him or not?
Following the ox, there is a dog in every household;
it startles small men and is difficult to perceive. All day long it follows the ox, yet it never understands how to respond when called by a person.
Seeing a guest, he makes no sound; seeing others, he is uniquely adept at kindness. When you intend to deliberate as he approaches the gate, you have already lost to him.
Pay close attention to this Chan Master; you must watch with full alertness. No matter how quick-witted you may be, you will remain unaware that you have become a dead man.

The Verse on the Ten Minds: The mind is spring. It rains universally upon mountains, rivers, and the great earth. Whether astringent, sour, salty, bland, sweet, or bitter—all receive this spring.
Merit nurtures and assists;
the mind is like water, conforming to the shape of its vessel—whether square or round, broad or narrow. Sometimes it follows people directly, becoming turbid or foul;
yet in all such instances, it fully embodies the Dharma of the Dharma King.
The mind is fire; it heats the fruits of sentient beings' afflictions until every branch and leaf flourishes everywhere, and a single lotus flower of the mind blossoms.
The mind is a scale; ten thousand households and a thousand gates share it together, yet its rise and fall depend on the slightest weight. Thus, one should accord with oneself.
Know that the mind is the measuring ruler;
it shows the world how to live uprightly. Do not allow the finger to push against the scale, lest one fall into the three miserable realms of hell from which it is difficult to escape.
The mind is a measure; it exhausts all that lies beyond the horizon within the mouth of right and wrong. Mountains piled high and peaks heaped up reside within the thoughts of the mind;
after death, one must personally undergo the resulting retribution.
The mind is a lamp, illuminating the darkness of the human world. When the mind instructs one to walk uprightly yet one cannot do so, one must resort to deception.
To conceal the causes for rebirth in hell is to treat the mind as a mirror;
yet while it reflects the right and wrong of the human world so clearly, one may speak with someone face-to-face as if with perfect honesty,
only to act as dark as lacquer behind their back.

The mind is the Way. Ordinary beings and sages dwell together as the moon shines brightly; one realizes Bodhi right in the midst of clamor, which accords with the true and correct Way of the Tathāgata.
The mind is the teacher; it threads through the six thieves without a moment’s separation, calling them forth at all times before one's eyes. As soon as they emerge—
Even the Gate cannot withstand him.

The Master said, "The verification is right before your eyes. The questioner continued, "In that case, the mind does not betray the person, and the face shows no shame. The Master said, "..."
"Why have you betrayed me? The monk said, "The Master must also understand my words. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows of the staff.
A question was asked: "In the teachings it is said that, for example, in a mani-jewel palace, three corners are always hidden and one corner is always manifest.
What is this ever-manifest corner? The Master said, "Dangerous!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "It has rained well for several days. Now tell me, from where does the rain come? If you say it descends from heaven, which one is heaven?
If you say it emerges from the earth, what do you call earth? If you still do not understand, therefore the ancients said:
'The path before heaven and earth—let people not forcibly shift it. To produce intellectual interpretations within this is to have eyes upon one's forehead.'"

Furthermore, he places a awl [in the midst]. He also says: "The self and others are within the blazing sun; compassion is within the clouds and mist; the provisional robe is within the frost and snow;
and one hides the body within the hailstones. Can you still hide your body? If you cannot hide it, you will instead have your skull shattered by the hailstones."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Vast and boundless is the universe, and countless are the people within it.
How many among these men are true heroes? Now tell me, are 'men' and 'heroes' the same or different? Thus the ancients said: 'The Buddha-dharma is not so vast;
what is difficult to find therein? Now tell me, what is difficult to find? It is simply difficult to find one who does not understand the Buddha-dharma."
"Is there anyone among you who does not understand the Buddha-dharma? If there is, reveal your message for me to see.
Thus, it was from among the seven hundred followers at Huangmei that the attendant transmitted the robe and received the Dharma. Tell me, did that attendant understand the Buddha-dharma?
Therefore, we know that when the tally sticks filled the stone chamber, the young boy realized the Way; how could this have anything to do with a talkative patch-robed monk?"
Regarding the affairs of the Sangha, he ascended the hall and said: "Xuefeng rolls the ball; Luohan writes characters; Guizong slays the snake; Dawsui burns the slash-and-burn fields.
Tell me, what matter does this clarify? Is there anyone who can clarify it? Try saying something. If you cannot clarify it..."
To cut a snake, one must be one who cuts snakes; to burn a slash-field, one must be one who burns slash-fields.

When the dust of emotion stirs and deluded views arise, if there is no sinew in the eyes, one will be poor for a lifetime. Question: "What is the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū? The Master said: "A word does not echo twice. Question:
"What is sitting in the place of enlightenment for ten kalpas? The Master said: "Calamity does not come alone."
[The student] asked, "What is it that does not manifest as Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Though gold dust is precious...

[The student] asked, "Why is it that one cannot attain the Way of Buddhahood? The Master said, "It cannot be placed within the eye. [The student] asked, "What is it like when it rains for a long time and does not clear?
The Master said, "The radish does not take root. [The student] asked, "Since it has been raining for a long time, why does it not grow?"

[The student] asks about the "Root. The Master says: "Feel free to cry out to the Emperor of Heaven. [The student] asks: "What is the treasure of Mount Xing? The Master says: "How many monastic robes do you have?
[The student] further asks: "I request the Master’s instruction. The Master says: "Feel free to wander about at will. [The student] asks: "What is the phrase that does not change?
The Master says: "It changes. [The student] further asks: "Ultimately, how is it so? The Master says: "The webbed feet of the duck are long; the legs of the crane are short."
[The Master] entered the hall and said: "If you desire to seek much, you fear it will hinder the Way. As for you venerable seniors, have you yet accomplished your work on the Way?
If you have not yet accomplished it, then a thousand kinds of clever explanations will not benefit your mind, nor will ten thousand varieties of deliberation."
What is the principle here? Thus an ancient said: "If you have no mind, I shall also rest.

If you do not wish to go while the weather is clear and dry, you must wait for the rain to soak your head. Question: "What is the essence of *prajñā*? The Master said: "A clam containing the bright moon.
He further asked: "What is the function of *prajñā*? The Master said: "A rabbit carrying a fetus. Question: "The three springs have already passed; the nine summers..."
Again, a student approached. "I have not yet attained clarity; I beg the Master for a direct pointing. The Master said, "I would strike your head until it shatters into seven pieces.

The monk said, "I know that the Master is earnest toward deluded disciples, but what can be done since this student has not yet understood? The Master said, "It is not the fault of the sun or the moon.
[The monk] asked, "The scriptures contain skillful means for the sake of students' understanding. This student has come before you; I beg the Master for a direct pointing. The Master said, "See!"
The case is settled. [The student] stepped forward and asked, "I do not yet understand; where does the student's fault lie? The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows.
A monk asked, "Before the world existed, was there still Buddha-dharma or not? The Master said, "It was never lacking for even a moment."
"Only one moment remains before death. A question was asked: "I do not ask about raising the mallet or brandishing the whisk, nor about raising an eyebrow or blinking an eye.

Regarding the single path that transcends all, I beg the Master to proclaim it. The Master said: "Why are you carrying a cangue and presenting a legal indictment? He stepped forward and said: "If it is so, then I thank the Master for his expedient means. The Master said:
"The punishment shall not be doubled for an offense already committed. A question was asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind and style does he succeed?"
[The student] asks: "Who? The Master says: "Layer upon layer of mountain passes. [The student] further asks: "What is the purpose of this assembly today? The Master says: "Playing the lute for an ox.
[The student] asks: "The true source has no trace or sign; how can one speak of the ancestral founder? The Master says: "A person is made clear within the phrase."
Jin said, "In that case, clouds arise from the southern mountain and rain falls on the northern mountain. The Master said, "Willow catkins encounter the warm wind.
A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "A monkey tied to a dew-pillar."
Ascending the hall, he said: "A thousand people crowding the gate is not as good as one person pulling the bolt. A monk then asked, "What is 'a thousand people crowding the gate'?
The Master said, "Waiting by the stump for a rabbit. The monk pressed further, "What is 'one person pulling the bolt'? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"You are not that hand or foot. Question: "What is Chan? The Master said: "The most bitter is yellow myrobalan.
He pressed further: "What is the Way? The Master said: "That which is sweet is licorice."

Ascending the hall, he said: "As soon as the drum has ceased—rarely does one encounter a true master. A monk came forward and bowed. The Master said, "The drum is beaten for the three armies. The monk said, "The long serpent and the crescent moon have already been unfurled;

a lone horse and single spear need not vainly claim merit. The Master said: *Note: This is a dialogue from a Chan (Zen) discourse. The "long serpent" and "crescent moon" are metaphors for the vast expanse of the Dharma or the enlightened mind. The "lone horse and single spear" symbolize the solitary practitioner. The Master’s response implies that the monk has already displayed his full capability.*
[The ice] melts away and [the wall] crumbles to pieces. The monk said, “Yes. The Master said, “Suru suru. Question:
In the Hall of the Empty King, who serves as the attendant? The Master said: “Ratnaśikhin Buddha.”
Ascending the hall, he said: "Nanquan said: 'Since my youth, I have raised a water buffalo. If I intend to let it loose to the east of the stream, it cannot avoid eating the king's water and grass;
if I intend to let it loose to the west of the stream, it cannot avoid eating the king's water and grass.'"
It is better to take a little bit wherever you are; he never sees it at all. Thus, Master Yunmen said: "Countless dead people lie upon the level ground;
to pass through the thorn-brake is to be a skilled hand. This applies even if you were to cut off both the mundane and the sagely.
"Exhausting both existence and non-existence is merely like a rat entering a rice jar; one still does not know that there is a 'transcendental aperture' above.
A monk then asked, "What is this transcendental aperture? The Master struck him and said, "I have already taken a lump of excrement and smeared it across your mouth;
why do you come further to bite my hand? As the monk hesitated, the Master drove him away.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Divine methods and secret arts are not transmitted from father to son. This mountain monk has a medicinal prescription:
black beans are good for making sauce. He then descended from his seat. A monk asked: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: "Dust fills the eyes."

Question: "What is the emptiness of form? The Master said: "Selling chives in the leek garden. Question: "It is said that 'an emanation is not the true Buddha, nor is it the one who preaches the Dharma.
I wonder, then, who is it that speaks? The Master said: "The pillar has missing lips. Question: "What is the bottomless alms bowl?
The Master said: "Hang it on the wall. The student followed up: "I wonder, then, what will be used for the morning and evening gruel?"
The Master said: "A ceramic bowl and bamboo chopsticks. Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Embracing one's own stolen goods while crying out for injustice.

Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Mountain clouds and wild pheasants. Question: "What is it like before the lighting of the lamp? The Master said:
"In the empty kalpa, there were no idle people. The monk asked: "What is it like when the lamp is actually lit? The Master said: "A spark enters the ox."

[The Master] struck him with his staff. The student asked, "What is it like after the time of Dīpaṃkara? The Master said, "A patch-robed monk runs all over the world. A question was asked: "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "It is still just a piece of copper.

The student asked further, "How is it after it has been polished? The Master said: *Note: The original text ends abruptly with "The Master said," implying a response that was likely a continuation of the previous theme (e.g., "It is still just a piece of copper" or a similar non-dualistic statement).*
"Set it aside for now. A student asked, "I have a question; I wonder if you will answer it, Master? The Master said, "A crane in the southland; a fox in the northland.
The student pressed further, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Look within three months. A student asked, "At what time did Sudhana enter the pavilion?
The Master said, "At the very end, with earnest persistence. The student pressed further, "Ultimately, how is one brought to collapse?"
The Master said, "It would be better to retreat three steps. The monk said, "In that case, the ancients were not ahead, and the people of today are not behind.
The Master said, "The King of Qin struck the *qín*. A monk asked, "All day long you are anxious and distressed, solely because of the remaining snow in the courtyard.
How can this snow be made to melt away? The Master said, "Spring will arrive before long. The monk stepped forward and said, "In that case, when the red sun rises..."
[The student] said, "It has been washed away entirely. The Master said, "Adding frost upon snow. [The student] asked, "What is it like when one builds a carriage while the door is closed?
The Master said, "Has it even been completed yet? [The student] further asked, "What is it like when the tracks meet upon going out the door?

The Master said, "Under the workshop of Lu Ban. [The student] asked, "I have received the teaching that says: 'When one person awakens to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions all vanishes.'"
"If it is already empty space, how can it be extinguished? The Master said, "One who returns to the source should know this.
He continued, "In that case, where a single bubble arises, all waves arise together. The Master said, "Look closely at what was said before."

Because General Li had petitioned for the Master’s purple robes, when he ascended the hall on that day, a monk asked: "The imperial grace has descended from afar, and you have newly donned the purple vestments.
I wonder, Master, how will you now repay it? The Master said: "My head wears the sky; my feet tread the earth. The monk pressed further: "..."
"If that is so, then one knows how to repay kindness. The Master said, "You too are like a mouse eating salt. A questioner asked, "The silken decree illuminating the sun descends from heaven;
the Imperial Grace is supreme. How will you, Master, repay it? The Master said, "How wonderful that the weather is cool!"
The student said, "In that case, the clouds and dragons meet, and the sun and moon shine once more. The Master said, "Idle words.
The Master then said, "Let us stop this questioning for a moment. On this day, there is imperial grace; tell me, from where does it descend?

This old monk’s original vow was to cover this illusory body with tattered robes and to patch the wounds of hunger with coarse food. Unexpectedly, the Commander heard of this and bestowed upon me the honor of a purple robe."
This would immediately contradict your original intention; not wearing it would again be a failure to honor the Heavenly Mind. Whether you say it is worn or not worn, let that be as it may.

But tell me, what robe did the Patriarch wear? If you understand thoroughly, I grant that the Venerable One wears a robe all day long without ever having attached a single thread to it, and eats a meal all day long without ever having bitten a single grain of rice. If you do not understand thoroughly, look at this old monk!
"Today I shall go forth robed in my dharma-cloak. Thereupon, he donned his robes. The Master addressed the assembly, saying:
"The Wisdom Gate (Zhimen) remembers a statement made while I was still in my mother’s womb. Today I shall present it to the great assembly.
You all must not attempt to analyze it through intellectual reasoning. Is there anyone here who can provide such an analysis?"
"If you cannot resolve this through deliberation, do not err in your presentation after thirty years. Or it is said: "Ascending to heaven does not require a ladder;
the entire earth has no path to walk upon. At such a moment as this, where can one find a place to settle the body and establish one's life? Or it is said:
"A thousand people lining up at the gate are not equal to one person pulling open the bolt. Is there anyone here who can pull it open? Try saying so before the assembly.
If you cannot say it, then stay outside the gate for now. Someone said, "Days pass and months go by; the wounds and sores only grow more numerous."
"What can you cure? If you cannot cure it, how will you deal with this ulcer? Another said:
"I do not ask about thirty years ago, nor do I require you to bring forth anything from thirty years hence. Regarding the very present moment, can you speak of it?
If you cannot speak of it, then one point is not penetrated and both sides fail in their merit. Another said: "Jing..."
"I do not ask you about the thorny forest. How do you speak the single phrase of 'leaving home'? Another said: "I do not ask you about the thunderclap upon one's head.
When the clouds part and the rain disperses, bring forth a single phrase. Another said: "Traveling on foot throughout the world."
Someone said, "I am practicing Chan. The master asked, "What is the meaning of Chan? Another replied, "During the day, as I come and go, I have no doubts at all.
The master said, "Then bring me a single phrase in the dead of night. Another replied, "I do not ask you about slinging my staff over my shoulder;
rather, speak a single phrase from within the nostrils of a needle. Another replied, "The alms bowl has no bottom; what can it possibly accomplish?"
One might say: "A mad elephant has no hook; with what shall it be restrained? If it cannot be restrained, do not let it trample upon the crops of others. Another might say:
"When the heavens send down seasonal rain, why does the withered tree not produce flowers? Another might say:
"Heaven, earth, the sun, and the moon—all return to exhaustion when their time comes. What is the phrase that transcends this? Or one might say: "To leave the body behind—"
"I do not ask you about 'phrases. Bring me a phrase from a village of three households. Another said:
"A monk must first penetrate through the 'name-body' and 'phrase-body' before he can possess the single eye of a monk.
Is there anyone who can say it? Another said: "Can you say the phrase that cannot be uttered even with a full mouth? Another said: "Look up at the sky."
"Why do you not recognize the moon? Someone said: "Bending one's head to pick up the sesame seeds.

"Why do you not see the ground? Someone said: "Early autumn, late summer; wandering the mountains and playing with the waters—let that be as it may. Suddenly I ask you this: speak quickly! Someone said:
"I do not ask you for the single phrase upon leaving the gate. When ten thousand miles of sky are cloudless, speak a single phrase! Someone said: "Perilous!"
"On a steep path, I shall not question you; on a level field, bring me a single phrase. Another said:
"I shall not question you regarding the yellow scrolls and red volumes; as for the matter of the patch-robed monk, what do you say? Another said:
"Even when ordinary and sagely sentiments are exhausted, that is still not the fundamental business of a patch-robed monk. So, what is the fundamental business of a patch-robed monk?"
Matter. Try to penetrate this; wait until you have finished speaking. If you cannot say it, do not say that Longju has buried you.
Regarding the Song of the Essential Principles: "In Kunming Lake one loses the sword; in Qujiang Lake one finds the saw. *Chacha* chacha, just pass the time.
At that time, amidst a vast and chaotic expanse as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, the coarse and austere [monks] drag their robes along the path.
A sharp and capable monk opens a single road. A lion does not seize the cub of a qilin; how could a fierce beast deign to look beneath its bed?

Mucilinda enters the water and departs; this time, do not spew forth clouds and mist. The swift falcon and the agile hawk soar and strike toward the heavens; the dull bird merely huddles at the base of the fence.

He does not go. The Buddha and the Patriarchs say: "Cease further raising this matter. Even if one were beyond the extraordinary, it would still not be permitted; a settled case already involves many complications.
How much less can one venture into another's gate? The night crow—whom has it been snatched away? At dawn, wearing snow upon its head, it meets with pointed accusation.
The wild bee does not cling to its old nest; a fierce general will never die at home.
The "Ba-ni" (the core essence) of the Chan Patriarchs—do not boast of non-duality. When Vimalakīrti remained silent, Mañjuśrī lost the advantage.
As for the core essence of the patch-robed monks: on high plateaus and dry land, lotuses do not grow; how could their fragrance be tolerated?
The Zen Master’s nostrils; the lion’s play. When the water rises, the boat floats high; he exerts himself with great effort. To the assembly he asks:
What thing is sought with bitter toil yet not obtained? What thing comes of its own accord without being sought? What thing cannot be broken by a hammer of iron?
Broken. What thing closes at night and opens by day? If a person does not grasp the meaning of this mountain monk’s words, the precious palace of lapis lazuli will grow with green moss.
Two verses based on this matter.
Turning left and turning right again, one’s body is clad in the Mahāyāna. Letting go, one reaches the deep spring;
regardless of depth or shallowness, look for the lunar disc within the fierce flames of the furnace. You must quickly fix your eyes; do not be negligent.
If you have not yet lowered the hand of weary birth, how can you escape this body of blazing light?
One day, the World-Honored One ascended the seat. The great assembly gathered like clouds. Mañjuśrī rose from his place and struck the gavel, saying:
"Contemplate clearly the Dharma of the Dharma-King; the Dharma of the Dharma-King is thus. Thereupon, the World-Honored One descended from the seat.
Mañjuśrī struck the gavel to inform the assembly: "The decree of the Dharma King must be thus.
If there were any *srotaāpanna* guests within this assembly, they would not have waited for the radiance of the hair-tuft between his brows."
A Verse on "Do Not Engage in False Conceptions" by Fenzhou:
Mazu brought forth one Fenzhou; false conceptions resound like thunder across the nine provinces.
If you lack the eyes of a patch-robed monk for investigating Chan, you will mostly be searching for bubbles upon the sea.
Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying: "On South Mountain there is a tortoise-nosed snake.
You all must look at it carefully;

the matter of the tortoise-nose is difficult to grasp. Those who try to realize it through direct confrontation are deluded; as they raise their heads, they mistakenly enter the weeds where the partridges cry upon the ridges."
Xuefeng’s Verse on the Ball:
"Who can discern the pivot of Xianggu’s ball-rolling? Of the fifteen hundred, how many truly know? Raising one's eyebrows, it spans a thousand miles;
One must be a lion cub of our school."
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the 'blowing-hair sword'? Yunmen said, "The Patriarch. Verse:
The precious blowing-hair sword was asked of Yunmen; When a visitor meets the opportunity, how could it remain? Meeting a swordsman on the road—what then?
The person in the steamer carries his head and flees south.
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the house style of the Master? Yunmen said, "If a scholar comes, report it;
every monastery has its own house style. However, this is not the same as the matter at hand with Yunmen. If there is a scholar outside the gate..."
Even one as accomplished as Yan Hui would not have understood this.
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Yunmen said, "Looking at the mountains in broad daylight. (Verse)
To look at the mountains while the sun is out is but common; to deliberate upon the meaning of the Patriarchs who came from the West is in vain. A golden-maned lion is rarely encountered;
for the most part, foxes are called wolves.
Yunmen draws back his gaze;
Yunmen draws back his gaze, laughs, and says "Heh! Heh! If you hesitate, you will meet his gaze and his "Heh!
Even if Zhang Liang possessed many stratagems, in the end, they would be difficult to employ here.
A monk asked Dawsui, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder whether this very thing is also destroyed?
Dawsui said, "It is destroyed. The monk said, "If that is so, then it must follow along with it."
"Follow as they say; follow them away.
In the verse, one must strictly avoid following others or failing to understand them. Great Following has spread these words to the ends of the earth:
"Within the true pure nature, the moment a single thought arises, there are already a thousand differences and ten thousand divergences."
Master Dàsuī saw a turtle on the land. A monk asked, "All sentient beings have skin over their bones;
why is this sentient being's bones wrapped in skin?
Dàsuī took off a shoe, covered the turtle with it, and departed.
Like a turtle withdrawing its six limbs, the name has already been revealed; do not go before others to play with your eyes.
A single leather shoe covers it all, yet even until now, you have still not awakened.
A monk asked Dongshan, "What is the Buddha? Dongshan said, "Three catties of hemp;
the hemp skin is three catties—there is no need for a scale. How could the scale-head consent to sit upon a fly? As soon as a single thought arises, the tendons and bones are exposed;
it is a vain labor to seek further for the zero-point of the balance."
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? Yunmen said, "I do not understand. The monk asked, "Why do you not understand?
Yunmen said, "Simply maintain this 'not understanding. You ask about the practice of a śramaṇa;
the practice of a śramaṇa is supreme. If one were to teach people how to understand it, their karmic nature would be difficult to escape."
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "I have long heard of the Stone Bridge at Zhaozhou; having arrived here, I see only the 'leopard' (a play on words for 'robber').
The Master said, "You see only the leopard; you do not see the Stone Bridge. The monk asked, "What is the Stone Bridge?
Zhaozhou replied, "It carries donkeys across; it carries horses across."
Zhaozhou’s Stone Bridge originally has no stars; the current is swift, so even the swimming fish find it hard to rest.
Upon the bridge, one sees only the tracks of donkeys and horses—who would dare to walk upon the imperial highway?
Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Please speak on that which transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
Nanquan immediately returned to his quarters. Zhaozhou said, "This old fellow usually talks incessantly, yet he could not manage even a single question."
Transcending the four propositions and severing the hundred negations—only one who is intimately acquainted with him can recognize him. Leaping down from the meditation seat, he simply departs;
let the hawk pursue its flight through the heavens.
Emperor Tongguang ordered the various Chan masters to sit in their respective ranks and said, "I have acquired the treasures of the Central Plains, yet there is no one to appraise them.
Xinghua asked, "What are Your Majesty’s treasures from the Central Plains?
The Emperor extended both hands, spreading out the ends of his head-wrap (*fukutō*). Xinghua said, "The King's..."
"Treasure! Who dares to offer a price?
A king’s treasure is truly difficult to appraise. Xinghua manifested his form and spoke these words, offering a stroke of strategy:
he spread out both hands, revealing the ends of his official cap, as the imperial edict hung suspended from the Phoenix Tower.
While at Nanquan’s vegetarian feast, Nanquan himself carried a tray of raw offerings before the Head Seat and said, "The offering is presented.
Shanshan, who was serving as Head Seat at the time, replied, "Non-arising. Nanquan said, "Even non-arising is still not it," and he passed by.
Shanshan then called out, "Venerable Elder! Venerable Elder! Nanquan turned his head and asked, "What is it? Shanshan—
It is said: Do not say that this is "not yet. The verse says:
The ancients patrolled the hall and personally plowed the raw land; crossing waters and rowing boats is no easy task of cultivation.
Do not say that "no-birth" (anutpāda) is still "not yet"—if even a single hair’s breadth is not resolved, confusion will run rampant.
A monk asked Changqing, "When there is a question and an answer, the roles of guest and host are clearly defined. But when there is neither question nor answer, what then?

Changqing said, "Everyone who meets them says they have retired from office; yet among those beneath the forest trees, one has never been seen. Verse: Everyone who meets them says they have retired from office, But among those beneath the forest trees, one has never been seen.
Everyone says my mind has found rest; yet when questioned, where is there ever a place for it? Words and heart at odds, you deceive yourself;
in the swift river of karma, you drift along as you please.
A monk asked Changqing, "When many hands sift through gold, who is the one who obtains it? Changqing said, "Those with skill obtain it.
The monk asked, "Does this student obtain it as well? Changqing said, "It is still very far off."
The verse says:
Among the multitude of hands sifting for gold, who is the one who finds it? How could a single speck of dust act as an obstruction? The vast waves stretch far and wide, yet the gold remains distant;
with nothing accomplished, they return empty-handed.
Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhimen Zu, Volume Thirty-nine:

To benefit sentient beings through the essential pivot of spiritual capacity, one cannot establish words without compassion and wisdom; to expound the tracks and boundaries of the Way, one cannot do so without accommodating those of middle and inferior capacities.

To reach the ultimate limit: were it not for the vast awakening that stirs all beings and the transcendent, solitary resonance, how could the flames continue through a thousand lamps and the fragrance ascend through five branches?
The Master was a direct descendant of Shaoyang and a successor of Xianglin. He opened up the profound realm of heaven and humanity, and shook the grand statutes of past and present.

He established the gate of transformative edification and loftily spread its influence across the seas. Having arranged these teachings so they emerge in mutual succession, he brought them to their full flow.

As I descend to mingle with these gathered scholars, I venture to offer my humble observations on the ranks of the assembly. Having undertaken this revision, I have sought only to value brevity and concision.

Alas! The descendants of our ancestral lineage are as widely dispersed as the stars. Some confine themselves to the interpretations of a single region or a single master, thereby defiling the wisdom of those who came before.
Others impose a mixture of partial Chan and partial Vinaya upon their juniors, giving rise to heterodox views through the medium of pen and tongue; this is truly madness.
Narrow-minded in their verbal acumen, they criticize Yuanming for employing the "three phrases" in receiving disciples and point to Jinghui’s mention of the "three clusters" [of precepts].
Since these are neither based on factual reality nor widely accepted as authentic, they merely spread delusions through hearsay, seeking fame and profit;

they are truly a great pestilence within the monastic community. How can such things be tolerated? To suppress a school of thought, one must first enter its inner sanctum; if one has not yet discerned its depths...
This is different. It is merely to bring harm upon oneself. As the *Lüyu* states: "The gentleman does not speak unless it concerns the Odes and the Books;
he does not move unless it concerns Rites and Music. Therefore, the sages of old kept their mouths shut with three seals to admonish their own hearts.

How much more so for us, who when conceiving a single thought or establishing a single matter, ought to strive for broad salvation rather than indulging in destructive talk that consumes the gold and gnaws the bones; do we not truly fear this?
Be cautious, lest you whet the axe that fells your own body; let this serve as a mirror for reflection. May those who understand me, upon reading these writings, cease their slander;
and may those who peruse this collection savor its Way. Then, the chilling breeze of wisdom shall reach everywhere, far and wide.
Written on the fifth day of the month of Rūbīṇa in the year of Xīnwèi by the disciple Míng, abbot of Zàishèng Temple on Mount Xuědòu in Míngzhōu.

Volume Forty of the *Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies*:
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yue of Yunfeng during his First Residence at Cuoyan.
Compiled by the Disciple Qi Xiao.
While the Master was at Tong’an, he accepted an invitation from Cuiyan to ascend the seat. A monk asked: “Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master said:
“The new elder does not answer questions. The monk pressed further: “In that case, you are the true heir of Dayu. [The Master replied: “Fen... [text fragmentary]”
Yangqin said, "I grant you twenty blows. The Master then said, "Today this mountain monk has been caught out on level ground.
Do you all know where the failure lies? An official will not tolerate even a needle, yet in private one may pass through with a carriage and horses.
He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
The following night, during a small *sǎn* (informal discourse), a monk asked: "In the past at Vulture Peak, the half-seat was shared; what is the meaning of the two masters today? The Master said:
"The heavens are high—who can crane their necks to look up? The monk pressed further: "If that is so, then Vulture Peak of the past is today’s Cuiyan.
The Master said: "The earth is vast—few are those who understand. The student gave a shout, and the Master struck him. Another monk asked: "I come to you, Master, bearing my raw jade."
"I request the Master to polish me. The Master said, "I do not polish. The monk asked, "Why do you not polish?
The Master said, "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. A monk asked, "The Buddha did not return to his native land to teach;
why does the Master return to his hometown to serve as abbot? The Master said, "I let this one point pass. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him and said, "Is there no other master here?"
Zen practitioners, you who are monks of the fundamental portion—why not come forth to provide mutual verification? Is there anyone?
It would be truly excellent even if one were like a chisel in a cloth bag, never poking its head out. Generally speaking, to uphold the lineage of the school, one must first be such a person.

If you do not yet possess eyes that can pass through a rushing torrent or a blade, or eyes as swift as a spark or a flash of lightning, do not trouble yourself to bring it forth. At the critical moment...
Ji dashi was immediately placed in the seat of succession by Deshan. Deshan said, "Today I am exhausted. Ji said, "Old man, why are you talking in your sleep?
Deshan reached for his staff; Ji then overturned the meditation platform. The Master said: "How extraordinary, all you practitioners!
Observe these two masters: one pressing, one nudging, briefly revealing their style. It is much like climbing a high mountain hand-in-hand."
"Nevertheless, even so, one cannot avoid being laughed at by bystanders. Now tell me, who is the bystander?
With a shout, he struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Leaving Tong’an, the assembly requested that he ascend the hall. A monk asked, “Now departing from Fengling and about to arrive at Longsha, what is the Venerable One of Immovability?
The Master said, “The sky is cold and the rain is falling. The monk pressed further, “I have come here specifically to pose this question;
how do you not point it out for me? The Master said, “Tie your straw sandals tight. He then continued, “This mountain monk’s Way is shameful and his virtue is meager.”
I am utterly incompetent; how could I have expected that this mission would travel so far, with the monastic community requesting me like clouds gathering?

This is surely due to the profound fraternal affection of the Abbot, the Head of the Hall, and the vast manifestation of his Way. I shall only strive with the resolve of one treading on thin ice, never daring to forget my sincerity in repaying his kindness.
Furthermore, Cuiyan Yixing has arrived as a special envoy, accompanied by more than forty attendants; within just a few days, there has been considerable commotion.

I am deeply moved and filled with gratitude; these feelings gather within my breast. Furthermore, as you, Master Xing, have followed this man of high virtue, you have both cultivated the beauty of human character and strengthened your resolve.
As you traverse this long journey on foot, I hope that each of you will take care of yourselves.

However, the eminent person who has left the household life takes the benefit of others as their own responsibility; their movement is like drifting clouds, and their stillness is like the spirit of the valley.

How could they harbor thoughts of self and other, or allow their emotions to be bound by activity and tranquility? Since they have no mind regarding self and other, they likewise have no attachment to coming and going.
Thus, while the manifold phenomena arise from elsewhere, what concern are they to me? Such being the case, I hope that all those above [will understand].
The man held his golden mendicant’s staff high and rolled up his cloud-like robe lightly; the next day he set out. Wherever he went, he was not successful.
Later, when the Master was presiding over the hall at Shanglan and had finished reading the formal proclamation, he pointed to the Dharma seat and said, "Is there anyone here who cannot be deceived?
If there is, come forward! He then pushed over the meditation seat, shouted, and dispersed the assembly. Yet, even so, he was not yet a true master.
"Furthermore, half has been saved. Is there anyone else? After a long silence, he said: "Since no one has come forward, I, this mountain monk, today will not spare my eyebrows;
I cannot help but point to a deer as a horse and turn the sun into the moon. Do not blame me for this thirty years from now. He then ascended the seat.
Having finished the invocation for the Emperor, he again held up the incense and said: "O Assembly, this single offering..."
Fragrance! Heaven cannot cover it; earth cannot support it. The Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, the teachers of the world—none have dared to look upon it with a direct eye.
Where, then, do you all seek to grope for it? Yet, while the official gate admits not even a needle, the private path allows for carts and horses.
On behalf of the late Master Chirwan Ji, he sat in the full lotus posture. The Rector struck the gavel and said:
"O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary truth. The Master said: "When the ancestors failed to resolve it, the calamity reached their descendants.
When matters have come to such a pass, how can one allow for further exoneration? What is called the work of leaving the world to benefit sentient beings is termed the Gate of the Primary Truth."
"There is only speech; there is no real meaning at all. If you people understand this thoroughly, my work as a monk in this world is finished.
If it is not yet so, ask whatever doubts you have. A monk asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings: 'If there are those who hear the Dharma, there is not one who does not become a Buddha.
Today, the ceremonial canopy is spread before the assembly; what is the Dharma? The Master said, "The sword has already passed far beyond."
"You are merely marking the boat where it sank. Jin said, "On Mount Dayu, you once exerted your strength; today in Yuzhang, you truly proclaim it.
The Master said, "Looking at the water from the edge of a cliff—this is but a groundless cause for sorrow. A monk asked, "Whose song do you sing, Master? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed?
The Master said, "Those who recognize the Dharma are afraid. Jin said, "Once a word has left the mouth, even four horses cannot overtake it. The Master... [remained silent].

[The Master] said, "I let this one move pass. The monk clapped his hands. The Master said, "Go out yourself and take this upon you. A monk asked, "The morning canopy has already been unfurled; I prostrate three times in request.
I beg the Master for a single phrase that reveals its fresh point. The Master said, "Repeated words are not worth eating.

The monk stepped forward and said, "If so, then the clouds disperse and every house has the moon; spring comes and flowers bloom everywhere. The Master said, "Gazing upward with bared forehead, I look toward the rising sun. A monk asked, "Master..."
[The monk] said, "There is a strategy that pierces the heavens; the student has a plan to enter the earth. When the two armies clash, what then?
The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, beat the drum of retreat. The monk hesitated. The Master then gave a shout. The student said, "Everyone they meet says they have retired from office;
yet not one person is ever seen beneath the forest trees. The Master said, "Drag him out! He then said, "Cease your questioning for now."

The true treatise of the Buddha-dharma is not to be sought through competitive debate. To strike out and brandish sharp rhetoric in order to crush those of other schools—is this truly the way of the Patriarchs?
Therefore, the entire Great Canon cannot explain itself; even the Buddhas of the ten directions [cannot do so].
It cannot be proclaimed; it radiates brilliance through the present and the past. Transcending all views and knowledge, it completely fills the ten voids—how could it have any fixed location?

It is only because emotions arise that wisdom is obstructed, and because conceptualizations shift that the essence becomes distinct. Thus, though one acts all day long, one does not realize it oneself.

For this reason, the former sages exerted themselves, turning their heads back toward the realm of dust and toil, skillfully opening up expedient means. Since these expedient means exist, they can still be realized and verified.

"Ma! If you can realize this, you will be able to benefit beings according to their capacities and manifest transformations without fixed direction—appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unrolling, among humans and in the heavens.
Even so, you must not do this under the gate of a monk. Why? Because it would break his mouth wide open with laughter!
