The Master said, "A fabricated monk! Then he continued: "In years past, I once visited here; today I come again.

Not only has human fellowship increased in joy, but the forests and springs have grown even more beautiful. Now tell me, how do you express the single phrase that does not harm the meaning of things?"
[The Master] remained silent for a long while, then said: "The heavens are high in the southeast; the earth slopes toward the northwest. He descended from his seat.

[On another occasion,] he ascended the hall. A monk asked: "The Master has ascended the precious throne to proclaim the essence of our school. As a student who has come before you, I request that you grant us your instruction."
The Master said, "Chu Shi does not deserve jade. The student advanced and said, "Friends fill the world, but how many can truly know one's heart?
The Master said, "Rotten wood cannot be carved. He then added, "This is the Lion’s Throne within the Flower Treasury Pavilion of the Universal Radiance Hall."
Humans and devas are gathered here; ordinary beings and sages dwell together. Today, as we must comply with human sentiment, how can I reveal the truth?

If I were to proclaim the teaching in a manner that deviates from the fundamental principle, the great earth would surely fall into desolation. To level the high by following the low will inevitably invite derision and wonder.
"Tell me, how do you speak that single phrase which does not fall into the gate of transformation? After a long silence, he said, "Take care of your eyebrows!
He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall for a formal discourse, he said: "The Buddhas appearing in the world cause people to fall into a level plain; the Patriarchs coming from the West merely catch echoes in the void. One Great...

The teachings of the Tibetan tradition deceive the common folk; even a clear-eyed monk cannot save himself. When you people arrive here, on what basis will you discuss and understand? After a long silence, he said:
"Exerting one's utmost effort for the sake of the assembly, yet disaster emerges from one's private door. He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Ascending the hall: "The precious sword has already been lost; the empty boat is carved in vain. Buying hats and measuring heads—south of the Yangtze and north of the Yangtze.
[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "No one picks up what they find on the road. The monk pressed further, "Who is it that walks upon the Way?
The Master said, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated. The monk bowed. The Master let out a long sigh and said, "Linji’s vanguard lets one move pass;
Deshan’s subsequent command remains to one side. Let us now manifest the single phrase that is entirely without partiality."
"How would you say? After a long silence, he said, "Today, Cuiyan has lost. He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat. He then ascended the hall and said:
"The Wheel of Dharma was turned three times throughout the great thousandfold world; that wheel is fundamentally and eternally pure. Thus it was with Vipaśyin Buddha..."
He emits light from the eyebrows and eyelashes of you all, shaking the earth and turning the Great Dharma Wheel. Look, look!
Seeing that you all do not understand, he returns to enter parinirvāṇa upon the tip of the Cuoyan whisk. (He strikes the meditation seat.)

Descending from his seat, the Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Your fame resounds through the universe; we have known you for a long time. May we briefly catch a glimpse of the tradition of Cuoyan?
The Master said, "A slippery stone does not strike the frozen bottom. The monk gave a shout. The Master said, "What are you doing? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.

[The Master] struck him. Question: "What is it like before one has even stepped onto the Red Gate? The Master said: "A shove. He pressed further: "What is it like after one has stepped on it? The Master said: [A shove].
[The Master] tears [the robe]. The student advances and says, "If that is so, then all under heaven shall submit to the Han.

The Master lets out a long sigh and says, "A thousand people crowding the gate are not equal to one person treading the pass. When one person treads the pass, a thousand or ten thousand people can reach the land of doubtless peace and bliss.
Is this not joyful? Is there anyone here now who can tread the pass? After a long silence, he says, "I see."
"If one does not act for the sake of the Dharma, what bravery is there? He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Upon ascending the hall, he took up his staff and said, "The golden-scaled dragon does not appear; laboring in vain, gather in your fishing line and return.
He threw down the staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Buddhas of the past have already passed away; the Buddhas of the future have not yet been born.
Right now, at this very day, the Buddha-dharma rests entirely with Cuiyan. To let go is to benefit sentient beings according to their capacities;

to hold fast is for things to crumble like ice melting. Now tell me, is holding fast better, or is letting go better? After a long silence, he said: "Tsk! You wild fox spirit! With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat.
The assembly descends from their seats. [The Master] ascends the hall. "The skull is constantly dry within the world; the nostrils touch upon the family style.
Suddenly raising his staff, he says, "The old man Xuansha has already pierced through it. Do you understand? He speaks again: "No one offers a price; I shall strike for three hundred."
He struck the meditation seat, descended from it, and ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "What is it like when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard? The Master said, "It is inside the scabbard.

The monk pressed further, "And what is it like after it has emerged from the scabbard? The Master said, "Three in the capital, four in Bian. A monk asked, "What is the Master’s house style? The Master said:
"Large wood wrapped in large hide. The student asked, "If a guest were to arrive suddenly, what would you use to receive them? The Master said, "Small wood bound with small hide.
A questioner asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Unfurling the mooring ropes and setting sail.
A questioner asked, "What is the great purport of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Heaven is long-lasting; earth is enduring. The student added, "In that case, the 'large month' has thirty days."
[The day was] the twenty-ninth, a month with fewer days. The Master said, "Why has Old Śākyamuni lost his nostrils?
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "You hollow talker, you deceiver! He spoke again, "The true does not conceal the false;
the crooked does not hide the straight. It can be verified in the present; it truly cannot deceive the eyes of others. But tell me, what are your eyes? Can you verify them?"
"Is it so? If you can verify this, then Cuiyan will crumble like falling rocks and melt away like ice. If you cannot verify it, I entrust it to Master Deshan.
Having said this, he descended from his seat.
On the eighth day of the fourth month, he ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "An inch-long nail driven into wood.

The monk pressed further, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas. He then continued, "The scriptures state that the eighth day of the fourth month is the day the Buddha was born.
He emitted a great radiance that illuminated the ten directions, and golden lotuses sprang up from the earth, naturally supporting him."
With his two feet, he walked seven paces each toward the east and west, as well as the north and south; he pointed his fingers at heaven and earth and let out a lion’s roar, declaring:
"In the directions above, below, and the four intermediate points, there is no one who can surpass me. Later, Master Yunmen took up this story and said:
[Yunmen] said, "If I, this old monk, had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to the dogs, just to ensure peace in the world.
The Master [Xuedou] said, "How extraordinary, O Zen practitioners! Although Yunmen possessed a strategy for settling the chaos, he lacked the way to emerge from it himself.
If you can discern this, I grant you the single eye atop your head. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, Cuiyan said today, "I will not spare my eyebrows as I speak to you all:

the entire Great Canon of the Teachings, the coming of the Western Patriarch, and the horizontal and vertical explanations of the old monks throughout the land—none of these are matters within the domain of a true monk."
Furthermore, what is the matter within the scope of a patch-robed monk? [The Master] suddenly picked up his staff and said, "This whole crew of lacquer buckets!
He then descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Carrying pole and wooden staff wherever you go, perform your play upon meeting the stage. Although this is so, one hand does not clap alone. The assembly—
"Among you here, is there not a true master of Chan, a monk of the fundamental lineage? What prevents you from coming forward to join us in this mutual chanting and response?
Is there anyone? At that time, a monk came forward and bowed. The Master said, "Vague and indistinct, like a melody just beginning to be heard, it is then blown by the wind into another tune.
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What was the meaning of the Buddha holding up a flower at Vulture Peak? The Master said, "Once a word has been uttered, even four horses cannot overtake it.
The monk pressed further, "What was the meaning of Kāśyapa’s smile? The Master said, "The mouth is the gateway to calamity.
A monk asked, "What was the meaning of the National Teacher calling his attendant three times? The Master said, "He was old and virtuous," and added, "There is no need for attachment."
"Sage. "Sage" is merely an empty name; one need not loathe the ordinary. The ordinary is falsely established.

If you reach the point where both sagehood and ordinariness are exhausted in sentiment, this is called "the true permanence being manifest in its essence. Therefore, the ancients said: "Simply exhaust false conditions, and you are the Buddha of Suchness. Can you all believe this?
If you can believe it, even if you dwell in a thatched hut, stay outside the gate for thirty years.
"The back nostrils reach toward heaven; do not mistakenly resent others. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The public allows no needle, yet the private permits carriages and horses. Today, disregarding my own life, I shall offer an ancient story for the sake of the assembly.
After a long silence, he said: "Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind upon this long ago, yet until this very day, he has not attained it."
"Excellent. He then descended from his seat and ascended the hall, saying:
"All of you coming up here in this manner is much like thrusting your head into a vat of glue;
going down in this manner is likewise stumbling on level ground. Even if you neither come nor go, I shall strike you three thousand times in the morning and eight hundred times in the evening."
"One hundred. He then descended from his seat.
To ascend the hall and cut things in two with a single stroke is not yet to be called a true master. To level the high by means of the low is certainly not the work of a true adept.
When Cuiyan reached this point, his mouth was like a coffin-lid. How will you all deliberate upon this? After a long silence, he said: "If you wish..."
"You shall not incur the karma of the Avīci Hell; do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata. Having said this, he descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, he looked at the wind and set the sail—a practice shared by all quarters. "Cutting through nails and severing iron"—Cuiyan does not agree with this. How would you express the single phrase:
"Light swallows the ten thousand phenomena"? After a long silence, he said: "A fellow with a dragon's head and a snake's tail! He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Before one realizes that objects are mind-only, various kinds of discrimination arise. Once one has realized that objects are mind-only, discrimination no longer arises.
Knowing that all dharmas are mind-only, one then abandons the appearances of external dust. O virtuous practitioners of dhyāna:

consider, for instance, the great earth, mountains, and rivers, light and darkness, form and emptiness—all these phenomena manifest before you. How can you speak of a principle of 'abandoning' in this regard? At this point—
"Having attained clarity, you are still in the midst of the journey; you must know that there is yet another aperture above. He then descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he said:
"The three realms offer no peace; they are like a burning house. How do you express the single phrase for leaving the body? After a long silence, he spoke.
He said: "Clouds atop the ridge have no leisure; water flowing down the ravine is in great haste. He descended from his seat. Then he ascended the hall and said:
"If you see that all forms are non-form, then the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are entirely without fault. All you venerable seniors!"
Throughout the day you wear clothes and eat rice, yet you have never bitten through a single grain of rice, nor have you ever attached a single thread of silk.
Even so, you could transform the great earth into gold and churn the long river into butter and curd.

Nevertheless, while it is true that wearing clothes and eating rice are not non-existent, you have not even dreamed of the stench of sweat found within the gate of the patch-robed monks. Descent from the seat.
At the conclusion of the summer retreat, the Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "In the West, they use a wax man as a test; what do you use here, Master? The Master said, "An iron ball.
The monk pressed further, "Does this leave the student with no place to apply effort? The Master said, "You are merely those who parrot the words.
A monk asked, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said, "Right in the middle of the crossroads. The monk pressed further, "Is there not [another way]?"
"Expedient means. The Master said, "A thousand layers and a hundred turns. He spoke again: "The sun and moon flow on; time passes in an instant.

It is only now that the summer retreat begins, and soon it shall be the time for the *pravāraṇā* ceremony. This summer, I am glad that the members of the great assembly have each remained in good health.
Yet those who have left the household life are vast and unimpeded; at the end of the summer, in early autumn, some go east and some go west, departing from this grove."
Lin entered a grove of trees when someone suddenly asked the Elder, "How does Master Cuiyan guide people this summer?
Being thus questioned, how could he respond? Do not say, "Nine times nine is eighty-one.
Do not say, "Once the snow has melted, spring will naturally arrive. Do not say, "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. Do not say, "It is fitting..."
[The Master] took hold of the dog’s mouth. This was not merely letting out a shout; he gave a slap with his palm, struck the dog’s face with his sitting mat, and then swept his sleeves and departed.
"O Zen adepts, such a manifestation is a profound courtesy toward Cuiyan. Since it is not otherwise, how else might one reveal it? Try to speak before this assembly.
Is there anyone who can say it? The assembly remained silent. The Master said, "If you were to come to any [other teacher]..."
[He said: "Just so. Do not say that I have come from Cuiyan. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, a monk asked:
"The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return? The Master said: "The Yellow River has nine bends. The monk pressed further: "Where does that return?"
"If that is so, then there is no interruption between the present and antiquity. The Master said: "Pitifully, the wild goose fills the sands;
its cries echo in anticipation of spring. Question: "What is the first phrase? The Master said: "His hands hang down past his knees. Question: "What is the second phrase?
The Master said: "Ten thousand *li* away at Yizhou. Question: "What is the third phrase? The Master said: "A dung basket and a broom."
Question: "Is there Buddha-dharma on the peaks and cliffs of a mountain? The Master said: "There is. The questioner asked: "What is the Buddha-dharma of the mountain peaks and cliffs?
The Master said: "A monkey climbing a tree upside down. He added: "The old Confucian says: 'When the benevolent see it, they call it benevolence;
when the wise see it, they call it wisdom. The common people use it daily without knowing it. For this reason..."
"The Way of the noble person is rare indeed. Master Zhao also said: "In heaven, he is as heaven; among men, he is as man.

As for the one who can be both heaven and man—how could this be something achieved by heaven or man? O practitioners of meditation, you should know that when the sages established their models, the underlying principle was necessarily the same.
How do you all understand this thoroughly? After a long silence, he said: "Go through the Sangha Hall."
Entering the Buddha Hall, he hides his body within the Big Dipper. Joining his palms at the main gate, he says, "A-he-he! What is this?
He strikes the meditation seat and descends from it.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "The student’s mind and eyes have not yet been opened; I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, "The stone pillar at the crossroads.
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Are you not a man from Hongzhou?
[Another] asked, "How was it before Bodhidharma had come? The Master said, "The waves are broad in the desert sands. [The monk] stepped forward and said, "After he came..."
"What then? The Master said, "Mount Xiongeri is high. A questioner asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Military orders are urgent."
The student said, "What connection is there? The Master said, "Traveling five hundred li a day. He spoke again, "Clouds follow dragons; wind follows tigers.
Water flows to the damp; fire seeks the dry. But tell me, upon what does a patch-robed monk rely? He then held up his whisk.

It is all here. To tear it apart is up to me; to gather it together is also up to me. After a long pause, he let out a shout and said, "The royal decree is somewhat strict. He descended from his seat.
On the day of Cold Food Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "Venerable elders, do you understand? From the winter solstice to the Cold Food Festival is one hundred and five days;
every household adds fresh earth to their graves. Yet when we reflect upon Shide and Hanshan, they were utterly unrefined in their wandering north, south, east, and west.
Nanquan does not beat the drum of Yanguan. He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: At dawn, when day breaks, all affairs are settled. In the continent of Uttarakuru, there is long-grained rice porridge. [The Master] descends from his seat.
Because he had entered the city, the assembly requested him to ascend the hall. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Yuzhang?

The Master said, "The colors of the trees distantly divide the residence of the Immortal Commandant; the light of the lake coldly drenches the pavilion of the former sage. [The monk] further asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master—
The Master said: "In the morning look to the southeast; in the evening look to the northwest. A question was asked: "What is that which is nameless yet flies forever?
The Master said: "The stars in the heavens. He further asked: "What is that which is rootless yet remains eternally firm? The Master said: "The trees beneath the earth."
A lay disciple asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Wearing clothes and eating food according to one's station.
The disciple further asked, "In that case, I shall step back three paces and join my palms at my chest. The Master said, "It is better to have no cup added after one is already drunk.
He then continued, "If words do not meet the occasion, those who rely on the words perish; even if you could speak until the heavens sent down rain in four directions..."

Flowers. The earth shook in six ways; these are all instances of receiving blows under the gate of the patch-robed monks. Yet, affairs are not unidirectional, and principles emerge through many gates.
To accord flexibly with capacities and conditions—how could there be no skillful means? Thus, the ancients said: "Recognize the Emperor in the midst of the bustling marketplace;
realize the old monk at the tips of the hundred grasses. Kāśyapa Buddha is right beneath the feet of you all.
He emitted light that shook the earth and turned the Great Dharma Wheel. Then, raising his whisk, he said, "Look! Look!
Seeing that you all do not understand, I shall now enter the Fire-Light Samādhi upon the tip of this whisk of Cuiyan.
He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he had already descended into the royal palace; before emerging from his mother’s womb, he had finished delivering all sentient beings.
When the ancients spoke thus, they saw only the sharpness of the chisel-tip, but did not see the squareness of the chisel-head. Descending from the seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "I have heard it said in the teachings: 'This one thing alone is real; the other two are not true.
What is this one thing? The Master said: "The nostrils point downward with their large openings. The monk pressed further:
"In that case, there is congee in the morning and rice at the midday meal. The Master said: "Take care of your eyebrows! A monk asked: "What is the seamless stupa?"
The Master said: "The four corners touch the ground. "How is it with the one within the stupa? The Master said:

"The fragrant wind blows away the withered flowers; it rains down those that are fresh and beautiful. Question: "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said: "Skin over bone. Question:
"How was it before Ox-head saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "The person inside the hermitage does not know what is outside the hermitage. "After he saw him, it was like..."

"What? the Master asked. [The student] said, "The water flows down the mountain torrent, free to go this way or that. [The student] asked, "Regarding Danxia burning the wooden Buddha—what was his intention?
The Master said, "Horizontal three, vertical four. [The student] followed up, "Why did the temple administrator’s eyebrows and beard fall off?
The Master said, "Seven openings, eight thoroughfares. He then added, "From the Deer Park at the beginning until the Bahudvārika River at the end, throughout forty-nine years..."
To speak of it all at once, it is but a dream. Have you all ever seen such a dream? Therefore it is said:
"If the eye does not sleep, all dreams are naturally eliminated. But what is this eye that does not sleep? Can you verify it?

If you can verify it, then the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and all the patriarchs of the world will be shattered into a hundred fragments within the eyes of this venerable one. If...
Unable to verify it, today Cuiyan has attained life from within death.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Way is the eternal Way; the Dharma is the eternal Dharma. You all must not, under any circumstances, waste your physical and mental energies."
They rush about seeking words and phrases. Thus it is said: "If there is even the slightest trace, it is but dust; as soon as you give rise to a thought, you are disturbed by demonic realms.
Now tell me, how would you express that single phrase which does not involve such triviality? He suddenly picked up his staff and said, "I let this one pass," and then descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Looking at this hollow basket where a wedge has been driven in—rare indeed is one who can penetrate it directly. How would you express a single word of praise or censure?
After a long silence, he said: "Without the spring breeze, the flowers do not bloom; yet once they have bloomed, they are blown down by the wind.
He struck the ground once with his staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The student understands how to ask about the contentious phrase; I request the Master not to answer with a mechanism that startles people.
The Master said: "Long hair and an ugly monastic face. The monk pressed on: "If so, then day after day there is incense smoke, and night after night there are lamps.
The Master said: "Palms joined behind the head. A monk asked: "I have received the teaching that says: 'But when the one moon is true, within it there is naturally neither this moon nor that moon.'"
"What is the true moon? The Master said, "A blind donkey chasing the great crowd. The student asked, "If that is so, I should have known about today's affairs;
I regret not being more careful in the beginning. The Master said, "From head to tail," and then he took up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"I call this a 'cane' (*zhùzhàngzi*). What do you all call it?
If you call it a 'cane,' the shrimp cannot leap out of the measure. If you do not call it a 'cane,' you will fall flat on the level ground.
After a long silence, he said, "Today, Cuoyan has lost the advantage," and throwing down the cane, he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; where there is no Buddha, one must pass swiftly by.
Where, then, will you all go on pilgrimage, carrying your shoulder-poles and staffs? After a long silence, he said: "In Pūrvavideha he holds his bowl;
in Aparagoyānī he eats his meal. He then descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Even if the mind were to penetrate through immeasurable time, throughout kalpas, how could it ever have been different from today?
But tell me, what is the matter of today like? After a long silence, he said: "A tortoise drills through a wall. He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the expanse of the universe, there is a single treasure, hidden within the mountain of form.
All you venerable Chan practitioners: above your heads is the sky; beneath your feet is the earth; in your mouths are tongues; upon your faces are noses. Where, then, is this treasure?
After a long silence, he let out a shout and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are without obstruction; sound, fragrance, taste, touch, and phenomena are always in samādhi.
This is what the patch-robed monks understand: mountains are mountains, waters are waters; when hungry, one eats; when weary, one sleeps.
Suddenly, Mount Sumeru leaps into the nostrils, and the makara fish pierces through the eyes. How do you deliberate upon this? Liang.
[The Master] said, "Go to the hall. He ascended the hall and said:

"In the Northland of Uttarakuru it is the middle of the night; here in Jambudvīpa it is midday. If one has not yet awakened from the cycle of saṃsāra, how could one ever have smelled the *campaka* flower?
Venerable elders, do you understand? Those with wisdom do not depend on advanced age; those without wisdom toil in vain for a hundred years."
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: The movement of the sun’s shadow shifts; it is the longest day of the year at the southern limit. Everyone knows this—why labor over it so specifically?
When the sun sets and the third watch arrives, he rides his donkey into the marketplace. *Chan*.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If you do not understand the Way upon encountering it with your eyes, you are still somewhat off the mark.
If you do not know the path when you set foot upon it, you have made a mistaken use of names and words. You venerable ones, you have eyes to see forms and ears to hear sounds;
you have noses to smell fragrances and tongues to discern flavors. For what reason, then, do you fail to understand? (Pausing for a long while...)"

It is said: Emperor Wu sought the immortals but did not attain immortality; Wang Qiao sat upright and ascended to heaven. [The Master] struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
Entering the hall, he said: "To emerge from within the gate is easy; to exit through the body is difficult. Let us set aside for now the matter of practicing spring ordinances in winter."
"A single phrase for traversing the journey—how do you speak it? After a long silence, he said, "The whole family boards the fishing boat," and then descended from his seat.
He ascended the hall again and said: "The practice of Samantabhadra and the wisdom of Mañjuśrī: on the peaks of Potalaka a pure breeze arises, and blind donkeys pass by in a herd."
Silla. "The tongues of the Jiaolao extend three thousand li. He ascended the hall and said:
"To contemplate form as emptiness is to achieve great wisdom and not abide in birth-and-death; to contemplate emptiness as form is to achieve great compassion and not abide in nirvana.
All you practitioners of meditation, do you understand? One gallops a horse on the continent of Pūrvavideha in the east; [one reaches] Aparagoyānī in the west..."
Yanini struck the sounding block. "Look! Look! he said. Then, not knowing what else to do, Elder Vimalakīrti let out a shout, struck the meditation seat, and descended from it.
Entering the hall, he said: "Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil; the Sovereign attains the One and brings order to the world."
A patch-robed monk who attains "one" meets a nail on dry land. (With his whisk, he strikes the meditation seat. He descends from the seat.
Entering the hall, he moves his countenance to reveal the ancient road; he does not fall into the trap of silent mechanisms.
The Master said: "The ancients let go like this. Can you leap out? Even if you could leap out, your nostrils are still in the hands of Cuiyan."
[The Master] turned his robe inside out. He said, "Tell me, where is the nostrils of Cuiyan? [Pausing for a long time,] he said, 'Receiving a bull from one person, returning a horse to another.
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Without resorting to triviality, I ask the Master to speak quickly. The Master said, "Mount Sumeru. The monk hesitated; the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "What is the first essential? The Master said, "A snake passing through a rat hole.
"What is the second essential? The Master said, "A monkey climbing a tree. "What is the third essential? The Master said, "Village straw sandals."
Question: What is the essence of *prajñā*? The Master said: “An arrow piercing a willow leaf. [The student] further asked:
What is the function of *prajñā*? The Master said: “Li Guang ambushing the barbarians. Question: What is the pure *dharmakāya*?

The Master said: “A purple branch on a reed tree. [The student] asked: Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said: “There is. [The student] further asked: What is the matter that lies beyond?
The Master said, "Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun. He then looked to his left and right and said, "Why do you act so foolishly? Thereupon he descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall, he addressed the seekers of the Way: "What words are these? Do not let your precious time be spent in vain; it is like adding frost to snow. Having spoken, he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "How distant is the Way? It is true in every encounter. How distant are the sages? They are spiritual the moment one embodies them.
Thus, in the Sahā world, the Buddha’s work is carried out through sound; in the Gandhavyūha world, the Buddha’s work is carried out through fragrant food."
Here at Cuoyan, within the very process of inhalation and exhalation, we offer worship and service to the past and future Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
not a single one is passed over. The Buddhas of the past, present, and future, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, are the attendants of Cuoyan.
"There is not one that does not reach it. If there were even one thing that did not reach it, you would receive thirty blows of the staff. Venerable Elders, do you understand?
'To offer this body and mind to every dust-mote world—this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness. [He strikes the meditation seat and descends from his position.]

On the first day of the year, the Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, “The great assembly has gathered like clouds; what should they discuss? The Master said, “The flowers must bloom throughout the night.
The monk pressed further, “In that case, it is like grass bowing down as the wind blows. The Master said, “Ten thousand miles away, gazing toward the cloud-gate. The monk pressed further.
Entering the water, he saw a tall man. The Master said, "Quickly, pay three prostrations. He spoke again: "The thirty-six cycles have ended;
this morning, they rise once more. In a single kṣaṇa, they do not know one another; how could all dharmas ever be thus? High and low observe their rites; joy and sorrow dwell together.
Vast indeed is the gate of *dhāraṇī*, yet people cannot open it. The jade hare and golden crow hide their heads while exposing their tails."
[He] strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and descends from the seat.
[This is] the "Ascending the Hall" (shàngtáng). Deshan would strike as soon as he entered the gate; Linji would shout as soon as he entered the gate.
Look at these two old fellows—what a complete failure! Nevertheless, things do not arise in isolation; for them to arise, there must be a cause. That Cuoyan did not apply the expedient was because...
"This is what it means to exhaust oneself for the sake of the multitude. All of you have fallen flat on your faces on level ground. On whom does the fault lie?
After a long silence, he said, "To hesitate when one ought to act decisively leads, conversely, to being thrown into chaos. He then suddenly seized his staff and drove them all away at once.
Ascending the hall: In Mahādeva’s “closing the room,” it was already too late for the beginning; in Vimalakīrti’s “refusing to speak,” the handle of the story remains to this day.

This one path that transcends all—where even the thousand sages cannot transmit it—is what kind of feverish delusion? One must, within the gate of the patch-robed monks, stand as steep as a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
This is like drawing the bow after the thief has fled. You all harbor resentment in your hearts and are stifled by words in your mouths;
is there still blood beneath your skin? You are all burying one another right here. When will this ever come to an end? (With his staff, he drives them away.)
Ascending the hall: "Rest now, and rest immediately. If you seek the moment of realization, there is no such moment.
If you attempt to understand this matter through words or speculate upon it with the faculty of thought, you are worlds apart from the truth.

Great men, even if you were to cut through everything with a single stroke, you would still not be in accord—let alone being summoned by others into the abbot’s quarters to be smeared with ointment and pointed at. (He raised his whisk.)

Regarding the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, the *Treatises of Zhaolun*, the sense organs and their objects, form and dharmas, the upward and downward paths, existence and non-existence, gain and loss—should one fail to resolve these at some future time or day, one will not find one's proper place at the moment of death.
Furthermore, there is a certain class of contemporary "patriarchs" who have been chasing fame and pursuing reputation for twenty or thirty years;
they merely instruct people to avoid falling into their verbal traps, claiming this is "penetrating sound and form. Yet, when questioned about the East, they answer with the West.
The West regards this as a phrase beyond the ordinary; thus they pass down such deluded interpretations to one another.
From this point on, the teachings and the sect will be muddled and destroyed, deceiving and confusing future generations. How bitter! How bitter! Such a blade does not exist in the royal treasury.

If you all continue to practice pilgrimage in this manner, you will be like those who wait by a tree stump under the clear breeze and moonlight—the cool rabbit grows ever more distant while the wild grass turns green. [Descend from your seats.]
Ascending the hall, he said: "All of you coming up here in this manner are much like abandoning a tree of sweet peaches to seek out mountains to pick sour pears.
Generally speaking, those who travel on pilgrimage must maintain some degree of mindfulness throughout the twelve periods of the day;
how can you simply follow along in the crowd like this, living in vain and dying in confusion? Observe how the former sages could not tolerate it in a hundred ways."
"What? I declare to you: I now guarantee this matter for you; it shall never be in vain. Do you all believe me?
Even if you were to believe here with total conviction, it would still be like hearing a story without seeing the truth—mistaking a bell for a jar.
[He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.]
Upon ascending the seat at Chengtian Monastery on Mount Nanyue, a monk asked, "What is it like when the two masters meet? The Master said, "The stone bridge leads to the great road.
The monk pressed further, "In that case, the same wind blows from a thousand miles away. The Master said, "A single character hangs from both ends.
The monk said, "The assembly bears witness; I, this student, prostrate in gratitude. The Master said, "You have utterly frustrated me. Another asked, "Since you have ascended the precious throne..."

Elder Brother Chengtian has already been deceiving you all from the start. Now that Cuiyan has just arrived, we must not add frost upon snow.

Nevertheless, once a word has left the mouth, it is as difficult to recall as it is for four horses to overtake it. Since matters have come to this, we cannot help but smear ourselves with ashes and dust;
for what was unresolved by our ancestors brings calamity upon their descendants. Thirty years hence, the nostrils will be far apart.
"O Celestial One, do not mistakenly find fault with people; it is well. [The Master] descends from his seat.

Next, in the *Recorded Sayings of Zhuzhu Falun*, during the inaugural ascending of the seat at the monastery: A monk asks, "The Dharma seat has long been vacant; now the Lion’s Roar sounds. We beg the Master for the skillful means to thunder forth."
[The Master] made a sound. The Master said, "Listen well. The monk stepped forward and said, "If it is so, then as soon as the single sound is split, the great assembly receives your grace.
The Master said, "When the clouds part, there is no need to hide the nine-tailed fox; I grant you your remaining years, but return quickly to the grave. The monk then prostrated.
The Master then said: "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it is born only by relying on conditions. The Way does not travel in vain; it responds immediately upon meeting with circumstances.

Thus, for those who understand the universal principle, every action reveals the point of return. For those who wander and explore, what prevents them from advancing further? Is there anyone here? After a long silence, he continued:
He said: "The fishing rod is worn out, so plant bamboo anew; do not calculate the labor, but rest when you have attained it.

He ascended the hall and said: "A single path is as straight as a bowstring; it stands before the doors of every household. If there are those who strive together to advance, in the end, all must discuss the priority.
He gave a shout, struck the meditation seat, and descended from the hall.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "To contemplate form as emptiness is to realize great wisdom; therefore, one does not dwell in birth-and-death. To contemplate emptiness as form is to realize great compassion;
therefore, one does not realize nirvana. He then suddenly took up his staff and said: "Vertically it exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally it pervades the ten directions.

All the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and all the ancestral masters under heaven are entirely upon the tip of this staff. Transversely and vertically, in every direction, it turns the Great Dharma."
"The wheel! Do you see it? Do you see it? Seeing that you all do not understand, I shall go off into the kingdom of Silla.
He struck his staff down and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: "Spring rain falls, soaking and nourishing all; it reaches every root and sprout, finding its way into every door. What is sweet is sweet, and what is bitter is bitter.
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When meeting face-to-face, one does not hold it out; as soon as the intention arises, one knows it exists.

This too is like gazing ten thousand *li* toward one's hometown. Therefore, Baofu had this to say: 'The spark struck from flint, the flash of lightning—whether you penetrate it or not, you cannot avoid losing your life.
Is there anyone here now who can penetrate it? After a long silence, he said: "Exerting oneself for the sake of the assembly brings disaster from within."

The Gate. Descending from the seat. Ascending the hall. Fire is hot; wind moves and shakes. Water is moist; earth is solid. Yet, within each and every phenomenon, they are distributed according to their roots and leaves.
Thus, clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger; water flows to the moist; fire seeks the dry. But tell me, what about the patch-robed monk?
"What is this? After a long silence, he said: "A thousand form a group; ten thousand form a troop. When weary, they sleep in one place;
when dreaming, each dreams alone. Then he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Having fought long on the battlefields, why have you not achieved fame and merit? The Master said, "Who sent you?
The monk replied, "When the Way prevails, the Imperial decree is not transmitted; when the times are peaceful, one need not sing songs of Great Peace.
The Master said, "Who sent you? He then added, "How enlightened is the sovereign! How excellent are the ministers! The winds blow in season, the rains fall in season, and the five grains ripen."
"The myriad people are at peace. What need is there for anything else? If one can simply accord with worldly conditions, one will naturally conform to the correct principle.
Do you not see that the Patriarchs taught: 'To enter the world and have nothing remaining beyond it'? O practitioners of Chan, do you understand? (After a long silence.)"
He said: "If one attains total non-action within the three realms, why worry that the four seas will not be at peace? He descended from his seat.
Upon ascending the hall for the opening of the Dharma assembly, a monk asked: "Today the Hall of Good Dharma is opened; we pray that the Master proclaim the primary truth."
The Master said, “Why did you not ask sooner? The student stepped forward and said, “I, a student, do not yet understand the Master’s profound intent.
I beg the Master for a skillful means to bestow his compassion once more. The Master said, “Depart, depart! The road to the Western Heaven is long, stretching some one hundred thousand miles.

[The student] asked, “What is the realm of the Dharma-wheel? The Master said, “On the high Mount Guli, clouds emerge halfway up. [The student] stepped forward and asked, “Who is the person within that realm? The Master said:
"Coming and going across the Five Lakes, moving freely as one pleases. A monk asked, "What is the single phrase by which you, the Master, benefit others?
The Master said, "When the rain falls, the mountain colors grow dark. The monk pressed further, "Is this not precisely where you, the Master, benefit others?
The Master said, "Where are your eyes? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. Then he said, "Stop! Stop! Once the Great Elephant has vanished,"

When the rare sounds have vanished into the distance, one must truly transform through lateral penetration and open up the gates of expedient means. Thus, the Tripitaka and the Five Vehicles were established as teachings tailored to specific capacities;
these are like the weapons of a state, employed only when there is no other choice. Subsequently, Bodhidharma came from the West to transmit the mind-seal alone.
The "one flower and five petals" spread throughout the world, yet this is much like holding a deaf person and making them mute. Why is this so? Furthermore—
Each of you possesses a segment of reality that illuminates the past and reaches across the present; it is as vast and expansive as the great void, and as clear and pure as a bright mirror.
It can be verified in the here and now, and truly cannot deceive the eyes of others. But what, precisely, are the eyes of each of you? Can you verify them?
If you can verify them, then the buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and the three vehicles and twelve divisions of the teachings—[all are contained therein].
The six successive patriarchs and all the elder monks of the world have been ground to dust within the eyes of everyone here.

If you cannot verify this for yourself, the mountain in front is the terrace-mountain, and the mountain behind is the main mountain. After a long silence, he again held up the incense and said: "This assembly on this day."
Truly, this is no small matter. Throughout the land and under heaven, who would not rejoice? I dare not further offer prayers for the imperial wind; instead, I shall return with my fellow officials.
Why is this? As the ancients said, "I have long been praying. How much more so for the sagely sovereign and worthy ministers of the present day!
Having stood before the great assembly for some time, I humbly pray that you will all take care of yourselves.

Ascending the hall, he said: "It would truly cause the earth to shake in six ways and the heavens to rain four kinds of flowers. Yet, beneath the gate of the Patriarchs, white clouds stretch for thousands and tens of thousands of miles.
He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Caution is what preserves your virtue; silence is most efficacious. Even if the vast ocean were to change, it would never speak for you.
"Do you understand, monks? "The mouth is the gateway to calamity. He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
Ascending the hall, he raised his staff and said: "Holding the alms bowl toward the world of Fragrant Accumulation—why is there no way out for you to manifest yourself?
Carrying the sun and moon upon the tip of the staff—why are those with eyes as if blind?

Even when it reaches the point where the wind blows and the grass bows, and the resonance accords with the sound, leaving not even a speck of dust behind—this is still a dharma of mutual contention. What about this?"
This is the Dharma of non-contention. [The Master] struck the meditation staff once and descended from the seat.
Entering the hall, he raised the topic, citing the scriptures: "This seeing and its objects are originally the wondrous, pure, and luminous essence of Bodhi. He further cited: "It is also said..."
The forest trees and ponds all resound with the Dharma; their interlacing lights form a lattice like a net of precious threads. How extraordinary are these various virtues of dhyāna!
When the ancient sages spoke thus, they called it "turning back from worldly toil" and opened up skillful means through such indirect expressions. Therefore it is said:
"When I press my finger, the Ocean-Seal emits light; when you momentarily raise your mind, the dust of worldly toil first arises. Do you understand?
For now, let this whisk sweep the world, and let this staff serve as the one who answers questions. [He strikes the meditation seat with the whisk and descends from his seat.]
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "In the midst of this vast expanse, how does one discern the master? The Master said, "A Persian enters a bustling marketplace.
The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then there is no need to sift through the sand. The Master said, "Those who merely parrot the words. The monk then bowed.
The Master said, "If speech does not leave its nest, how can one escape the entanglements? A single cloud hangs across the valley mouth, leaving many people lost."

[The Master] descended from his seat and ascended the hall. "The source of all sentient beings relies upon the ocean of wisdom as its origin; the stream of all conscious creatures takes the Dharma-body as their essence.

It is only because emotions arise that wisdom is obstructed, and because conceptualizations shift that the essence appears diverse. When one realizes the root, emotions vanish; when one knows the mind, the essence is unified."
"Virtuous practitioners of meditation, do you understand? The ancient Buddha intersects with the pillar; the Buddha hall contends forehead-to-forehead with the Heavenly King Hall.
If you still do not understand, he struck the meditation seat and descended from it.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The whisk swallows Mount Sumeru. In ordinary discourse, when Deshan plants his signboard, how do you deliberate upon this in the midst of a bustling marketplace?
After a long silence, he said: "In public, not even a needle is permitted; in private, a carriage and horse may pass. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The golden crow does not necessarily always stand at noon; the jade hare is never dark even at midnight.
What is it like then? The Master said: "To point is to miss. The monk was speechless. The Master said: "Do you understand? The monk said: "I do not understand. The Master said: [Silence].
Upon arriving, he did not light [the lamp]. He asked, "What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground? The Master said, "Do not seek it from others.

He pressed further, saying, "If one does not seek it from others, how can it be attained? The Master said, "It is not far from here to Hengyang. Then he said, "All you venerable practitioners of Chan:"

Once you have entered the monastic groves, you must skillfully consult with spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). These spiritual friends are none other than yourself; do not seek them elsewhere in vain.
The nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is all-pervasive and perfect; the source of the mind is limpid and still. Since there is no door through which to avoid it, what benefit is there in seeking it?

Have you not seen Huangbo cover his ears and Baizhang roll up his mat? It is clear and distinct right here; there is no other message. Gain and loss, right and wrong—all at once melt away like ice. *He!* (A shout)
A shout. Descending from the seat.
Ascending the hall. Xuansha did not cross the ridge; Baoshou did not ford the river. Sudhana visited fifty-three spiritual friends;
Huiyuan gathered eighteen monks and laymen. Xuefeng three times went up to Touzi; Zhiyi [visited] nine...
For ten days we have discussed the *Lotus Sūtra*. Now tell me: is this fellow a jackal howling or a lion’s roar? [He lets out a shout, strikes the meditation seat, and descends from it.]

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he had already descended into the royal palace; before emerging from his mother’s womb, he had finished delivering all sentient beings.
When the Wheel of Dharma reaches this point, there is no use for a mouth. Do you all understand this thoroughly?
If you do understand it thoroughly, the nostrils of all the old monks in the world are entirely in your hands. If you do not understand it either, you will weep until your blood flows."
To flow into useless places is not as good as keeping one's mouth shut and passing through the remainder of spring.

[The Master] descends from his seat. He ascends the hall and says: "If you do not look back, you are already mistaken; if you attempt to deliberate, when in kalpas will you awaken? He then holds up his whisk and says:
Now it has been brought forth. How will you regard it? After a long silence, he said: "If you intend to deliberate, in what kalpa will you awaken?
He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised this passage from the teachings: "During the three seven-day periods, he contemplated these matters:
'I would rather not preach the Dharma and quickly enter nirvana. The Master then gave a shout, saying:

"If at that time someone had come forward and let out such a shout, choking the old barbarian’s throat, would not all under heaven have been hushed and the four barbarian tribes cleared away? But now—"
"I have let it go. Do you all still have 'blood under the skin'? After a long silence, he said, "Exerting one's utmost for the sake of the assembly brings disaster upon one’s own family.
He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The ancient mirror reflects the essence; the essence manifests its own form. The ancient teaching illuminates the mind; the mind reveals its own clarity.

Do you all, practitioners of Chan, understand? When the mind is clear, all phenomena are radiant; when the nature is obscured, all conditions are dark. Where the sun and moon do not reach, there lies a wondrous world of its own.
With a shout, he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ten directions gather together as one; each and every one studies non-action. This is the field where Buddhas are selected;
with an empty mind, one returns having passed the imperial examination. When the ancients spoke thus on this occasion, did the patch-robed monks accept it or not?
If you accept it, where is the eye of the traveling monk? If you do not accept it, how do you speak that turning-phrase? After a long silence, he gave a shout.
A shout. A strike upon the meditation seat. Descending from the seat.
Entering the hall. Where sound and form do not reach, the ailment lies in seeing and hearing; where words and explanations fail, the fault rests with the lips.
Setting aside the phrase regarding the throat, how do you speak? Is there anyone who can say it? If you can say it, you will sit upon the tongues of all people in the world.
If you cannot say it, there is porridge and rice at the foot of the Dharma Wheel Gate. Descent from the seat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "To understand it in such a way is like adding frost to snow. Wait any longer for me to beat these two pieces of skin, and white clouds will stretch for thousands and tens of thousands of miles.
He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If speech does not leave the old nest, how can one transcend the entanglements? White clouds span the mouth of the valley; how many people have been lost to their own source?
Therefore, words cannot unfold the reality of things, and speech cannot meet the needs of the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded."
"You all have come here; on what basis do you claim understanding? After a long silence, he said:
"If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata. Be careful."

Ascending the hall, he raised [the following]: "The scriptures say: 'Forests and groves, ponds and marshes, all proclaim the sound of Dharma; their interlacing lights entwine like a net of precious threads. It also says:
'The ringing of bells and the beating of drums proclaim the truth; the green waters and blue mountains serve to exalt it. O practitioners of Zen, do you understand?
If suddenly a monk were to come forth and say, 'This is a lapse into words,' how would you drive him away?"
He dismissed them. After a long silence, he said: "To weep until one's blood flows is of no use; it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring.
He then ascended the hall and raised the following case: An ancient said, "In studying the Way, one must first have an awakening; it is like having once competed in a swift dragon boat race."
"Though the old pavilion and idle fields / Were won back once, only then did he cease.
When the ancients spoke thus, it was much like being so preoccupied with watching white waves that one loses the oar in hand. Is there anyone among you who can examine this thoroughly?
If you can examine it, save the ancients; if you cannot examine it, the Dharma wheel shall suffer defeat today.
[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Later, while presiding at Yunfeng, he gave this discourse in his *Recorded Sayings*:
"The ancients said: 'When the wind moves, the heart sways; when clouds arise, nature stirs up dust. If you understand today's matter..."
He darkens the person of original nature. For now, let us set aside today’s affairs. What is this person of original nature? After a long silence, he said:
"The crane has nine gao of space, yet its wings find it hard to soar; the horse lacks the thousand-li stride, so its pursuit of the wind is in vain. Adieu.
Ascending the hall on a winter day: The seasonal mark of "clouds written" has arrived; what is there for the mountain folk to discuss?
As soon as the single orb emerges from the sea, all myriad things receive its grace. (He strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and descends.)
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: Master Mingjiao addressed the assembly, saying, "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, do not say that I am not telling you all:
everyone, watch the fire and the candle! The Master said, "Master Mingjiao, an old man, out of affection for his children, was unaware of their ugliness.
This is because the land is vast and the people are few; since you all have been here this summer, I, this old monk, truly did not wish to speak to you."
"You say: 'It is better to cherish your eyebrows. He then descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he said: "The ancients said:
'How can one ascend the ancient path? The Way of the Golden Immortal is what one may rely upon. There is no need to labor over leveling things.'"
"Non-thing" is not yet a complete designation. Now tell me, how would you express this one phrase of complete designation? Yunfeng beats the drum of retreat;
striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he descends from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Linji’s vanguard has let one move pass; Deshan’s subsequent command shall be set aside for a moment.
How do you express that single phrase of solitary revelation, free from partiality? After a long silence, he said, "How lamentable, the end of Zhongli under King Chu!
He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said: 'Every movement reveals the ancient path; one does not fall into the silent mechanism. Do you understand?
The ancients have already overturned such harmoniousness as well. When some fellows hear this, it is like the wind passing through a tree—what remedy is there for them?
He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient case: Xinghua asked the rector Kebin, "Before long, you shall become a teacher who proclaims the Way.
Kebin said, "I will not enter this protective community. Xinghua asked, "Do you refuse to enter because you understand, or because you do not understand?
Kebin said, "I am neither of these. Xinghua then struck him and fined him five strings of cash; having provided him with a meal of steamed rice, he drove him away.
He was discharged from the hospital. Later, however, he became a Dharma heir of Xinghua. The Master said, "Do you understand? When the road is long, one knows the strength of a horse;
when years have passed, one sees the true heart of a person. He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'Words multiply, and one moves further from the Way. But consider this: before words are spoken, where is the Way? He then said:
'If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Wheel.
Striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he descended from the seat."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The teachings state: 'All manner of grasping and rejecting are but saṃsāra.

To attempt to discern Perfect Enlightenment (Samantabhadra-jñāna) without having escaped saṃsāra is for that nature of Perfect Enlightenment to be identical with the cycle of transmigration. There is no way to avoid saṃsāra [in such a state].
Now, when you all reach this point, how do you understand Perfect Enlightenment? After a long silence, he said: "The lotus leaf is round; it is round like..."
Mirror. Its rhombus points are as sharp as awls. [The Master] strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and descends from the seat.
He ascends the hall and says: A monk asked Fayan, "When the autumn wind first stirs, on what can the poor rely?
Fayan said, "If you can recognize kindness, you will know how to repay it. The Master then said: "Do you understand? A single leaf drifting through the void reveals the autumn."
"The Dharma-body must penetrate the clamor and chatter. Next year there will be new branches again; the spring wind that causes such disturbance will never cease.
[He struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.]
Ascending the hall, he said: "The monastic quarters are silent and still as summer practice proceeds; the doors are closed, and people are rightly surprised by my solitude.
Yet I have matters of 'same wind' (tongfeng) of my own; though none come from a thousand miles away, I am willing to acknowledge them.
But what is this matter of 'same wind'? Do you understand? A steamed bun is the everyday meal of a common householder; a single word or half-sentence is the ancient tangle. Yunfeng..."
"You two have no connection. Descend from the seat. [The Master] ascends the hall and says:
"The teaching states: 'The source of returning is non-dual; the expedient means have many gates. The holy nature is all-pervasive;
both following and reversing are expedient means. Do you understand? Therefore it is said: 'Do not rashly ascend the stages or follow the ranks according to one's merit. [He cites a sutra.]
"There are sutra masters; there are treatise masters and commentators on the treatises. Do you think there is any such news within the school of the patch-robed monks?
After a long silence, he said, "Once a word has been uttered, even four horses cannot overtake it. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Where sound and form do not reach, the fault lies in seeing and hearing; where words and explanations fail to arrive, the error rests with the lips and mouth.
Setting aside the throat, lips, and mouth, how would you speak this one phrase? Is there anyone who can say it?
If you can, you will sit upon the tongues of all the world’s masters and the Buddhas of the three periods. If you cannot, you shall only know..."
Following the custom, eat your fill. You can even get three coins to buy straw sandals.
Descend from your seat. Ascend the hall. He cites the teaching: "To know illusion is to leave it; no expedient means are required. To leave illusion is awakening;
there is also no gradual progression. Does the assembly understand? Let it be that Mount Sumeru leaps into your nostrils for now, but you—
Dao asked, "How many years has the Dragon King Sāgara been alive? His flesh weighs a thousand jin, yet his wisdom does not weigh a single zhu.
[The monk] descended from his seat. *Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies*, Volume Forty;
*Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies*, Volume Forty-One.
When Master Yunfeng Yue first resided at Cuiyan, his recorded sayings state that one day in the meditation hall he raised an ancient precedent, asking:
"A former master once said to his attendant, 'After you have finished your inquiry, stand to one side. What is the principle behind this?"
He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Stand over here. The attendant then moved over. The Master said, "Pointless! Pointless!"
Case: A monk asked Xuefeng, “What is the Buddha? Xuefeng said, “Why do you prattle in your sleep?

The Master said, “When the ancients spoke thus, it was called ‘administering medicine according to the illness. It would have been unacceptable to let this pass. Had he not let it pass, what words could you have offered here?
The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him across the mouth with his whisk. Case: Fandeng Chan Master... [text ends]

On the day the Master first opened the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "This mountain monk originally intended to dwell in seclusion among the crags and caves, passing the time with the community;
however, because the Elder of Qingliang has an unresolved case, I have come forth today to analyze it for him."
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the case that cannot be resolved? Dēng struck him and said, "The patriarchs could not resolve it; the calamity reaches the descendants.
The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? Dēng said, "The fault lies with me; the calamity reaches you. The Master [Zhaozhou] said:
"This fellow’s display of bestowing and revoking was indeed like shining before and excelling after. Yet when pressed to the limit, he was again like a dragon [hiding in the mud]."
"Head snake, tail snake. Is there anyone present here who can act as the host for Qingliang? He raised [the whisk] and said:
"The scriptures state that the Dharma-body flows through the five paths; therefore, when sentient beings appear, the Dharma-body does not manifest.
Then he held up the whisk and asked: "This is the whisk; which one is the Dharma-body? He spoke again: "This is the Dharma-body; which one..."
“This is the whisk. Do you understand? The Dharma-body swallows the whisk; the whisk swallows the Dharma-body.

If you do not understand this, it will be mid-spring in the tenth month. Case: One day Huangbo asked Baizhang, “Regarding the matter transmitted from the ancestors, how do you, Master, instruct people?
Baizhang remained sitting as he was. Huangbo said, “For the descendants of future generations...”
"How can this be transmitted? Baizhang said, "I thought you were a man of substance," and he returned to his quarters.
The Master said, "Out of affection for one's child, one does not notice their ugliness. Nevertheless, though it be so, when the law is fully applied, there are no subjects left.
Case: One day, Master Xuansha saw Changsheng and drew a circle. Changsheng said, "No one can get out of this. Xuansha said, "Sentiment..."
"Knowing that you are making your living inside a ghost cave," [Zhaozhou] said. Shengyun asked, "I am just like this; how about you, Master?
Zhaozhou said, "No one can get out of here. Shengyun asked, "I just now spoke in such a way;
why can I not get out? And yet you say you can. Zhaozhou said, "I can get out; you cannot get out. The Master said:
Whether you can speak the Way or not, all is within the circle of Xuansha. Is there anyone now who can escape it? Case:
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "I have newly entered the monastery; I beg the Master for instruction. Zhaozhou said, "Have you finished eating your congee?
The monk replied, "I have finished eating. Zhaozhou said, "Go wash your bowl. At these words, the monk attained great enlightenment.
Later, Yunmen took up the case and said: "Tell me, was there an instruction or not? If you say there was an instruction, what did he say to him?
If you say there was no instruction, why did that monk attain enlightenment? The Master said: "Yunmen does not know good from bad.
To speak in such a manner is much like drawing legs on a snake or growing a beard for a eunuch."—Cuiyan.
That is not so. If this monk were to awaken in such a manner, he would enter hell as swiftly as an arrow shot.
Case: Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying, "The entire universe and the great earth can be gathered up and made as small as a single grain of millet and tossed before you.
