Zithers and lutes, wind through the pines; A whistling rain upon the cypresses. The lion bites the man; The Korean hound chases after clods of earth. Case:
One day, while at the latrine, Zhaozhou saw Wenyuan passing by and called out to him.
"Wenyuan? Yuan responded, "Yes. The State Governor said, "I cannot speak the Buddha-dharma to you while you are on the latrine.
Donglin’s verse:
The old monk was just on the toilet. He did not preach the Buddha-dharma for others;
the stench of excrement and the fragrance of sandalwood were both revealed in this single moment, leaking the secret mechanism between father and son.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Zhaozhou has a secret word; Wenyuan did not conceal it. He brought forth the Great Treasury of Teachings; his merit is truly immeasurable. Case:
One day, while traveling together with Wenyuan, Zhaozhou suddenly pointed to the ground before them and said:
"Let us establish a watch-station here. Yuan then stepped forward, extended both hands, and said, "Hand over the official pass.
Zhou gave him a slap. Yuan said, "The official pass is perfectly clear."
A Verse by Donglin:

The Son of Heaven dwells within the bustling marketplace; The old monk resides amidst the tips of a hundred grasses. Waving his hand as he comes and goes through the imperial streets, He fears not the patrol officers of the fire watch.
Yunmen’s Verse:
One correct and one perverse; one falling and one rising. Wenyuan and Zhaozhou point their fingers from within the leather boot.
Case: One day, while at the Buddha Hall, Zhaozhou saw Wenyuan prostrating to the Buddha and struck him once with his staff.
Wenyuan said, "Prostrating to the Buddha is also a good thing. Zhaozhou said, "A good thing is not as good as having none at all."
The Donglin Verse:

Throughout my life serving my teacher, I have not possessed even a trace of his breath. As for the wondrous nature of the Buddha-dharma and its celestial mechanism, not a single word can be taught to him.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Wenyuan’s practice does not fall into emptiness; From time to time he gazes upon the purple-gold countenance.
Although Zhaozhou’s staff is short, A further circle of light shines behind his head.
Case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "Does even a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou said, "No.
The monk said, "From the Buddhas above down to the ants below, all possess Buddha-nature.
Why then does the dog lack it? Zhaozhou said, "It is because he still possesses karmic consciousness."
Donglin’s Verse:
Passing before the Xuande Gate, Turning one's head brings disaster. If you wish to remain free from trouble, Simply go back and sit inside your house.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Someone asked about the Buddha-nature of a dog. Zhaozhou replied, "It has none. With these words, he extinguished the Hu clan;

yet even so, he was still not a true man of stature. Case: Zhaozhou addressed the assembly, saying: "The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the wooden Buddha does not pass through the fire."
The clay Buddha does not cross the water; the true Buddha sits within the house.
This verse by Donglin [states]:
"The golden Buddha, the wooden Buddha, and the clay Buddha—crossing the furnace, crossing the water, and crossing the fire—all enter Zhaozhou’s red furnace amidst a blazing conflagration."
Refined within the light, it is a single note of "White Snow" and "Yangchun," which no one has been able to harmonize for ten thousand ages.
Yunmen’s verse:
"The ninety-seven kinds of wondrous marks are difficult to depict even with the brush of Gu Kaizhi or Lu Tanwei; Zhaozhou’s eyes are sharp and clear—he sees them."
The heart, liver, and five viscera.
[The Master] raised [this topic]. A monk asked Zhaozhou, “All dharmas return to the One; where does the One return?
Zhaozhou said, “When I was in Qingzhou, I made a robe of cotton cloth that weighed seven *jin*.”
Donglin’s Verse:
Midnight, the ink-black darkness; A thief is caught. Lighting a fire to look at him— It turns out to be Old Wang.
Yunmen’s Verse:
The seven-pound robe of Qingzhou—exerting all one's strength, it cannot be lifted. Once the barrier of Zhaozhou is shattered, everything is simply one’s own.
Case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "I have heard that you, Master, personally met Nanquan—is this true?
Zhaozhou replied, "In Zhenzhou, they grow large radishes."
The Donglin Verse:
A large radish grows in Zhenzhou; There is a reason why master and disciple are in accord. Maitreya is installed within Guanyin Hall;
To the west of Dongyuan is Zhaozhou.
Yunmen’s Verse:
I went to visit the Great Teacher Nanquan Wang; The radish of Zhenzhou has no private secret. He brings it forth to block the mouths of right and wrong;
This "Snowy Melody" and "Spring's Radiance" are not the *Chuci*.
A monk took his leave of Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou asked, “Where are you going? The monk replied, “I am going to the South to study the Buddha-dharma.
Zhaozhou said, “When you reach the South, do not stay where there is a Buddha; pass quickly through places where there is no Buddha.
Even when you encounter people three thousand miles away, do not misrepresent what you have heard. The monk said:
"If that is so, then one does not go," [he said]. Zhou said, "Plucking willow flowers. Plucking willow flowers. Donglin’s verse says:
"Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; where there is no Buddha, run past in haste. Three thousand miles away, pluck the willow flowers."
"Flower. He said, "Come back another day and show this to me.
Yunmen’s verse: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; an iron pestle has been eaten by worms. Where there is no Buddha, pass quickly through; you will run into—"
At Mount Song, he encountered Pòzào Duò. "Do not misquote me from three thousand miles away. Two stone men whisper to one another. "If it is so, then I shall not go.
These words have already spread throughout the world. Plucking the willow flowers.
Plucking the willow flowers. Oṃ mā ni da li hūṃ phaṭ.
Case: Zhaozhou asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk said, “From Xuefeng.
Zhaozhou said, “What words or phrases has Xuefeng spoken lately?
The monk said, “Xuefeng said, ‘The entire earth is the single eye of a śramaṇa; where will you all go to defecate? Zhaozhou said, “Up! (shàng).
When Zuo was about to depart, he said, "Please give a spade to Xuefeng on my behalf.
Donglin’s verse says:
"The great earth is the eye; where can one defecate? The whole world cannot do anything with Old Xue. Zhaozhou sent him a spade."
Only after departing can this talk be made perfectly clear and complete.
Yunmen’s verse says:
"Traveling through dozens of provinces on the road, conveying words and transmitting messages with such elegance; one does not realize that mud has grown beneath one's feet."
*Ci*. (He) stepped on the toe of the man with a awl.
*Ju*. Baoshou asked, "Hudingjiao, do you not agree? Jiao replied, "I dare not.
Baoshou said, "Can you still nail the void? Jiao said, "Please break open the void and bring it here. Baoshou...
He then struck him and said, "In the future, there will be a talkative master who will break it open for you.
Later, Hu Dingjiao recounted this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou asked, "Why were you beaten by him?"
The tongsman asked, "I do not know where the fault lies. Master Zhou said, "Even this single seam cannot be managed;
let alone being told to break it open. The tongsman then understood. Master Zhou then said, "For now, just nail up this seam."
Donglin’s Verse:
The single seam is clearly present; To strike it at the head is difficult. Even if you manage to stitch and hem it, In the end, it will never be perfectly round.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Even if you were able to nail this single seam shut, upon close inspection, you would find yourself no adept. Pity these two old Zen masters;
they go so far as to speak of their own family’s disgrace to worldly people.
Case: There was a monk who, having finished building a funerary pagoda for Shushan, came to inform him.
Shushan asked, "How much money did you give to the craftsmen? The monk replied, "Everything was left to the Master.
Shushan said, "Did you give three coins to the craftsmen? Or did you give two coins? Or..."
He gave a coin to the artisan, saying, "If you can speak [the truth], I will have you build a stupa for me personally.
The monk had no reply. At that time, Luoshan was staying in a hermitage on Mount Dayu. When the monk arrived at Luoshan’s place, Luoshan asked, "Where have you come from?
He replied, "From Shushan. Luoshan asked, "What sayings or phrases have been circulating there recently?"
The monk then recounted the previous conversation. Luoshan asked, "Is there anyone who can say it?
The monk said, "No one has been able to say it yet. Luoshan said, "You go back and report this to Shushan."
When Daling Woshang heard this being cited, he said:
"If you give three coins to the craftsman, you, Master, will certainly not obtain the stupa in this lifetime.
If you give two coins to the craftsman, you and the craftsman will together produce a single hand. If you give one coin to the craftsman, [you will carry it]..."
The artisan’s eyebrows and beard fell off. The monk then returned and related this to Shushan.
Upon hearing these words, Shushan assumed a formal posture of reverence and prostrated toward Mount Dayu, sighing: "I thought there was no one;
it turns out there is an ancient Buddha on Mount Dayu whose radiance shines all the way here. He then turned back...
The monk said, "Your journey to the Great Yü Ridge is like a lotus flower in the eleventh month.
The monk returned and reported this to Luoshan. Luoshan said, "Long ago, tortoise hair was already several zhang long."
Donglin’s Verse:
Striking the collar with the sleeve—no adding, no subtracting; Cutting the lapel from under the arm—there is short and long.
The single Buddha atop Mount Dayu; Shushan twice emitted rays of light.
Yunmen’s Verse:
He excavated the permanent lands of the ten directions, Spending three coins until he laid bare the corpses.
Though the ancient Buddha Luoshan was efficacious, He could not avoid burying his own body in one place.
Case: When Luoshan was at Heyuan, as he was seeing off his fellow practitioner, Elder Jugu, to the gate, Luoshan took up his staff and thrust it forward once.
Jugu had no reply. Luoshan said, "The stone ox guards the ancient road;
one horse does not have two foals. Later, a monk recounted this to Shushan. Shushan said, "Stone..."
The ancient road by the ox pen: one horse gives birth to three tigers. The Donglin Verse:
I do not tread upon the path before the gate; Spring returns once again for another year. Falling flowers, red, fill the ground; Tall grasses, green, stretch to the heavens.

Leaving the gate, we grasp hands and speak of parting; The ancient road stretches far away—once gone, it cannot be pursued.

He left. After the rice gruel was finished, Master Quan asked the kitchen steward, "Where has the practitioner gone?
The steward replied, "He left right then. Quan thereupon smashed the rice gruel pot.
The Donglin Verse:
"The cat and the white ox chant Mahā; how can they compare to Nanquan beating the rice-pot?
Though the Buddha-dharma is not so vast, the monasteries throughout the world cannot do anything about it."
Cloud Gate’s Verse:
Nanquan smashed the idle furniture; Throughout the vast quarters, all take it as a saying to contemplate. Today, for your sake, I raise it up once more:
Vivid and distinct, leaving nothing vague or incomplete.
Case: Master Shoushan held up a bamboo stick and asked a monk, "To call it a 'bamboo stick' is to encounter resistance;
not to call it a 'bamboo stick' is to turn one's back. Tell me, what do you call it?"
Donglin’s Verse:
Holding up his bamboo staff, he asked, "How can you immediately call this the Way? Secret Maguan did not understand; immediately thereafter, he raised his forked staff.
Yunmen’s Verse:
To turn one's back on touch is not protection; it is clearly and directly raised up. Though the "hair-cutting blade" does not move, the ground is covered with swords and spears.
*Jǔ* (Lift!). Xuan Sha asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Ruiyan.
Xuan Sha asked, "What sayings or phrases did Ruiyan have? He replied, "The Master usually calls out, 'O Lord! [He himself...]
[The Master] replied, "Yes. He said, "Stay alert! In the future, do not allow yourself to be deceived by others.
The monk said, "Even though we are both playing with our spirits, you are still slightly ahead of me."
Donglin’s Verse:
One master is dead; one master is alive. If you understand how to play with the vital spirit, you will penetrate and transcend both ends.
Yunmen’s Verse:
The house style of Suiryaku: "Call out, Master! Last night on the Southern Mountain, a tiger bit a great beast. Case:
When Xinghua saw a fellow practitioner approaching, as soon as the monk entered the Dharma Hall, Xinghua gave a shout.
The monk also shouted. Xinghua shouted again. The monk shouted once more. Xinghua stepped forward and raised his staff. The monk shouted again. Xinghua—

Huangbo said, "Look! This blind fellow still dares to act as the master. As the monk hesitated, Huangbo struck him directly out of the Dharma Hall. An attendant monk asked, "What did that monk do to offend you? Huangbo replied: "Look at this blind fellow; he still presumes to be the master.
As the monk hesitated, Huangbo struck him straight out of the Dharma Hall. An attendant monk asked, "What did that monk do to provoke you? Huangbo said:
He just now possessed both the provisional and the real, both illumination and function.
When I crossed my hands before him twice, he was unable to proceed further.
For a blind fellow like this, if I do not strike him, when shall I ever?
Donglin’s verse:
A thunderclap startles heaven and earth; how can one listen while covering the ears? You must know that Old Xinghua’s [action] was half out of human sentiment.
Yunmen’s Verse:
“Holding the Mohe sword in his grasp, the celestial Māras’ hearts fail them. O clear-eyed bhikṣu, cease further conjecture! Case:
Xinghua said to the rector Kebin, “Before long, you shall become a leader of the assembly.”
The Master said, "Guest, you do not enter this monastery. Zhaozhou said, "I do not enter whether I have understood or not understood.
The Guest said, "It is not like that at all. Zhaozhou then struck him and said, "Venerable Kebin, you were defeated in the Dharma-battle;
you shall pay a fine of five strings of cash and provide a full meal for the assembly. When the next day arrived—
One day, after Xinghua had personally struck the gavel, Abbot Kebin, the *weina*, was defeated in a dharma-battle and fined five strings of cash.
He was served a single meal of steamed rice, but he was not permitted to eat it; he was to leave the monastery immediately.
Donglin’s Verse:

In the battle for the Dharma, victory has always been granted to Kebin. Seizing the banner and capturing the drum—these two points are perfectly clear. One must exhaustively apply the Dharma to be free from shame;
This old man intends to speak of this practice in years to come.
Yunmen’s Verse:

The vermilion mountains give birth to the young phoenix; The lioness gives birth to the maned lion. Under the blow of the staff, the eye of Maheśvara— In vain do they boast of the "first-grade faculty.
Case: Xinghua addressed the assembly, saying, "I heard that under the long corridor he also shouted, and later in the rear quarters..."
"Ye-he! My children, do not shout blindly or shout recklessly.

Even if you were to shout so powerfully that Xinghua ascended to the thirty-third heaven and was then dashed back down until he had not a breath of life left, and only after Xinghua had recovered would I say to you, 'It is still not so. Why is this? Because I have not yet—"
"I once scattered real pearls from within the purple silk curtains for you all;
what is the point of you shouting recklessly and wildly in the void?
Donglin’s Verse.
True pearls are scattered within a purple silk curtain; Zen practitioners who pass this down all deceive themselves with empty talk.
Clapping hands and laughing aloud, "Śākyamuni and Maitreya are his slaves!"
Yunmen’s Verse:
Before the assembly, he fully proclaims the Magadha command; how could this be merely opening two flaps of skin? With a shout, the blind donkeys gallop off in a herd;
in a dream, they topple the five Sumeru mountains.
Case: Xinghua ascended the hall and said, "Today, there is no need for 'how' or 'what.
I ask you simply to enter directly with a single blade, and I, Xinghua, will provide witness for you.
At that time, the Elder Minde came forth from the assembly, prostrated, and upon rising, let out a shout. Xinghua also shouted. Minde shouted again, and Xinghua shouted once more.
"Hai! Minde bowed and returned to the assembly. Huihua said, "If it had been anyone else just now, he would not have deserved even a single one of the thirty blows.
Why? Because Minde understands how to employ the 'single shout' so that it does not function merely as a single shout."
Donglin’s Verse:
Entering directly with a single blade—there is no need for further discussion. In the mere interval of deliberation, guest and host are distinguished. It is not that he let Minded pass;
one must know that Xinghua’s staff-head was clear.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Holding hands in the dark, they ascend a high mountain; When dawn breaks, each must travel alone.
Countless guests on the road who have not yet returned— With eyes wide open, they fall into a deep pit.
Jushi’s Three Sages said: "When I meet people, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for the sake of others.
Xinghua said: "When I meet people, I do not come forth; when I come forth, I immediately act for the sake of others."
Donglin’s Verse:
When a person is poor, their wisdom seems short; when a horse is lean, its hair appears long. Lodging alone at Shuangfeng Temple, we burn a single incense stick together.
Yunmen’s Verse:
How could a mirage ever quench thirst? When could a painted cake satisfy hunger? I urge you not to plant thorns;
they will cling to the clothes of your descendants in later generations.
Case: When Nanquan saw Deng Yinfeng approaching, he pointed to a water pitcher and said, "The pitcher is an object;
you must not disturb the object. Bring me some water.
Yinfeng took the pitcher and poured water before Nanquan, whereupon Nanquan ceased his questioning. Guizong said, "Deng Yinfeng, too..."
This is a chaotic exegesis.
Donglin’s verse says:
“Nanquan did not point to the pure pitcher; Yinfeng never spilled water. Leave it to beating tiles and boring through tortoises—this is the Buddha-dharma.”
"It is not here. Yunmen’s verse:

"When there is no film in the eye, there is no need to scrape it away; when there is no dust on the mirror, there is no need to polish it. Trusting your steps, go out the door and walk the Great Path."
On the road, he slung his staff over his shoulder and sang a mountain song.
He cited: Shitou said, "In this way it is not permitted; in that way it is not permitted;
in both this way and that way it is not permitted."
Donglin’s Verse:
The smoke of war has settled across the four seas; News from the Central Plains has been communicated. Lay aside the three-foot sword; Cease playing with the single bow.
Yunmen’s Verse:
What a fine point for discourse! Who can bring it forth? Even if one could bring it forth perfectly, I would not yet dare grant my approval.
Bring it forth! Sansheng asked Xuefeng: "When a golden fish has passed through the net, what does it eat?
Feng said: "Wait until it comes out of the net, and I will tell you. Sansheng said: "Of the fifteen hundred people [in the assembly]..."
"Good friend, you do not even recognize the 'head' (the core pivot) of the teaching. Feng said, "This old monk is burdened by the affairs of the monastic administration.
Donglin’s verse says:
"The scaled dragon has passed through the net, intending to swallow the boat; He has long been surging against the waves, flowing upstream. Yet he is caught by the idle fisherman who draws him in."
Fishing: drifting with the waves and following the currents, all is vast and leisurely.
Yunmen’s verse: "In total death, there is total life; in total life, there is total death. One is a clumsy fellow; the other is a man from Fujian."
The case is cited: Jia Shan said, "After the ape carries its young back behind the green peaks, the bird picks up fallen flowers before the azure cliffs.
Fa Yan said, "For twenty years, I have been taking this as a talk about objective conditions."
Eulogy on Donglin Temple:
Thirty years ago I wandered through this temple; Magnolia blossoms bloomed as the courtyard was newly renovated.
Now, returning once more to where I used to walk, The trees are old and flowerless, and the monks have white hair.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Though understanding through words and concepts is not yet it, I ask again: what is it like right now? Qingliang’s original source has a straight nose-tip;
Jiashan remains with his two eyebrows arched.
Case: Muzhou called to a monk. The monk turned his head. Muzhou said, "A fellow carrying a wooden board.
Donglin’s verse:
Do not be hasty amidst the flash of lightning; do not be distracted by the edge of the sword-wheel. At ease, let go of your entire body.
Entering. One must never, even for a hair’s breadth, commit an offense.
Yunmen’s verse:
Muzhou carries a board; there is no room to blink. Whether wide or narrow, long or short—there is no need to add or subtract.
Case: A monk asked Muzhou, “Can one breath turn over the entire Tripitaka?
Muzhou said, “What kind of *bi-luo-chui* pastry is there? Quickly bring it here!”
The Donglin Verse:
Muzhou accepted only the sharpness of the chisel’s tip; this monk did not see the squareness of the chisel’s head.
Even if one could turn over hundreds of thousands of scriptural treasuries, such offerings as these would still be considered ordinary.
Yunmen’s Verse:

A single breath turns the entire Great Canon; Sudden and gradual, partial and complete, provisional and real— Boundless wondrous meanings shine forth clearly, Yet originally, not a single character is recognized.
Case: In the assembly of Linji, the two head seats of the two halls simultaneously let out a shout.
A monk asked, "Is there still guest and host? Linji said, "Guest and host are clearly distinct."
The Donglin Verse:
When masters meet, there is never error; two by two, they simultaneously watch for the peck and the hatch.
Although guest and host are distinguished within a shout, how can that compare to Puhua shaking his bell?
Yunmen’s Verse:
To repay injustice with equanimity— The King’s Law has no partiality. Though Linji possesses the clear eye, He is but the essence of Huanglong. Case:
Puhua was constantly shaking his bell in the streets and markets, saying: "If you come from the bright side, I strike from the bright side."
"Coming from the dark, he strikes in the dark. Coming from the four quarters and eight directions, he strikes like a whirlwind.
Coming from empty space, he strikes blow for blow. Linji sent his attendant away;
as soon as [Puhua] saw him do so, he grabbed him and said, "What if they did not all come this way? Puhua pushed him away and said:
Tomorrow there is a vegetarian feast at Beiyuan Monastery.
Donglin’s Verse:
One must strive for cleverness; How could one ever have one's name inscribed upon the golden scroll? Take off your head-wrap and go home.
Do not ride your donkey past the gates of others.
Yunmen’s verse:
"The place where the former master revealed his true nature within the assembly; the time when Linji ate vegetables before the hall. These three instances together reveal the tethering post.
So! Pshaw on this beggar who clings to the platform! Case:
One day Mingzhao ascended the hall because the weather was cold. As soon as the assembly had gathered, Mingzhao said, "The wind is quite stiff;
this is not a place for you to settle your body or establish your life. Return for now to a warm room to deliberate."
Having measured [the situation], he returned to the abbot’s quarters. The assembly followed him there and stood in formation.
He called out to them, "As soon as you reach the warm room, you immediately fall asleep. With his staff, he drove them all away at once.
Eulogy by Donglin:
When the wind at the peak is somewhat harsh, it is difficult to stand firm; As soon as the warmth begins to circulate, drowsiness sets in. I laugh instead at Mingzhao, who toils in vain;
Pointlessly, he forces an arrangement between two places.
Yunmen’s Verse:
At midnight, the morning star appears at noon; The deluded still wait for the cock to crow.
Pitifully, they do not know the stench of their own excrement, Yet wish to pick it up again and show it to others.
Case: Baoshou opened the hall for his formal lecture. Sansheng brought forward a monk, and Baoshou struck him.
Sansheng said, "To act as a teacher in such a manner not only blinds this monk’s eyes, but blinds the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
The Donglin Verse:
At the tip of the staff, a whole city was blinded; Sansheng picked up the staff, Baoshou grew angry. The true command can only be raised half-way;
One blind man leads a multitude of blind men along.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Lifting up the first mallet upon Mount Sumeru— The flash of lightning and the spark from flint are far too slow. Where the Elephant King treads, the fox tracks vanish;
When the Lion roars, the hundred beasts tremble with fear.
Case: There was once an ancient worthy who one day did not go to the hall.
When the attendant came to invite him to the hall for the midday meal, the worthy said, "Today I have eaten my fill of oil-cakes at the manor. The attendant said:
"The Master has not been out. De said, "You simply go and ask the master of the manor.
As soon as the attendant stepped outside, he suddenly saw the manor master returning to thank the Master for coming to the manor to eat oil-cakes.
Donglin’s Verse:
It is close at hand, right upon the surface of the lips; yet it lies far beyond lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. How many people in this world fail to get a taste of the sesame cake?
Yunmen’s Verse:
The Abbot did not go to the hall. The Master of the Estate thanked him for his visit. "Once a single character enters the gates of officialdom, even nine oxen cannot pull one out.

Case: Xuansha said, "If we discuss this matter, it is like a plot of land whose boundaries on all four sides have already been demarcated and sold to others; there remains only the tree in the center."
It still belongs to the Old Monk.
*Donglin’s Verse*:
"Ten thousand matters depend on the Old Teacher; the tree does not yet belong to you. The butcher Guang'e attained Buddhahood. The Second Patriarch.
The Great Master pays off his debts.
Yunmen’s verse:
“The grandfather’s fields and gardens have all been sold; not a single boundary marker remains. Alas, there is still the center!”
The tree is troubled by the spring breeze, which never ceases.
[Case] A monk asked Shoushan, "What is the Buddha? Shoushan said, "The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it."
Donglin’s Verse:
Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law share the same lineage; The path to one’s own hometown is but a foot away. How laughable are those who ride a donkey searching for a donkey;
For a lifetime they have mistaken the horse-saddle bridge.
Yunmen’s Verse:
The new bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it; Step by step they follow one another, yet she does not whip it. Returning to the painted hall, no one recognizes her;
From now on, she will be too weary to step out the door again.
Case: When Wujou saw the two senior monks Xuan and Shao approaching, he asked, "Where have you two Chan masters come from recently?
The monks replied, "Jiangxi. Wujou struck him. The monk said, "I have long heard that the Master possesses such a vital pivot of teaching.
Wujou said, "Since you do not understand, let the second one step forward."
"Come! As the monk hesitated, Jiu also struck him, saying: "In the same pit, there is no different soil.
Go to the hall. Donglin’s verse says:
Naked, one thrusts against a white blade; From death, one yet attains life. A single arrow loses its own trace; Ten thousand chariots all lose their tracks.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Fierce flames allow not even a mosquito to alight; How could the great ocean harbor a corpse?
Even one with three heads and six arms— Upon hearing the wind, none fail to raise the flag of surrender.
Case: A monk asked Yunmen, “What is the Buddha? Yunmen said, “A dried-up shit-stick.
Donglin’s Verse:
No need for translations in Tang; No need to transmit them in Sanskrit. The eyes of Maheśvara— Facing each other, yet separated by the Western Heaven.
Yunmen’s Verse:

"Yunmen’s dry dung-spoon completely transcends the Dharma, Reward, and Transformation bodies. Without a single concern, he goes out into the mountains to roam, with a hundred coins hanging from the head of his staff.
Case: A monk asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still any transgression? Yunmen said:
Mount Sumeru.
East Forest Verse:
A single thought not arising is Mount Sumeru; turn your robe inside out and look backward as you step back. It reaches straight up to support heaven and down to support the earth.
The ground refers to the "obtaining" [of realization] prior to any recommendation; it is vast and open.
Yunmen’s verse says:
"Majestic and towering is this single Great Sumeru; its bearing of all is not a matter of coarse physical strength. Even if one does not follow words,"
Meeting [the Buddha], one instead comes face-to-face with a bitter deception.
Case: A monk asked Master Dayu Zhi, "What is the Buddha? Zhi said, "A saw and a scale-weight."
The Donglin Verse:
The saw, the scale-beam, and the hammer are all made of iron; Old Daoyu is once again loquacious. The water flowing down the mountain torrent is too busy;
The clouds atop the ridge peak are never at rest.
Yunmen’s Verse: When asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master immediately replied: "With a scale-club and a saw to cut it apart; Beyond words, he ferries the deluded across. Case:
A monk asked Xinghua, "How is it when [enemies] come from the four directions and the eight quarters? Xinghua said, "Strike!"
At that moment, the monk bowed. Xuefeng said, "Today I went to a village feast and have just returned.
On the way back, I encountered a sudden storm;
I took refuge inside an old shrine and managed to get through it."
Donglin’s Verse:
A sudden gale and torrential rain arrive; Yet one finds shelter within an ancient shrine.
Though one strikes others within the ghost cave, One must swallow charcoal and hide once more.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Within the ancient temple, one avoids it; Beside the piles of paper money, one sighs in secret.
Idle gods and wild ghosts are all struck with fear, Simply because this man recognizes the Sanskrit script.
Case: Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying: "I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion.
I have already met you at Wushan Ridge. I have already met you before the Sangha Hall."
The Donglin Verse:
Everyone says they have personally met him; Yet as before, it is still a dog coming at his cheek.
It would be well to strike them over the head with a great staff, So that the blind man’s eyes might suddenly open.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Wangzhou, Wushan, and the Sangha Hall— The frantic activity of karmic consciousness is beyond endurance.
When the monk’s staff is raised, The five lakes and four seas boil like hot soup.
Case: Jiashan addressed the assembly, saying: "There is no dharma before one's eyes; the intent lies right before one's eyes.
It is not a dharma of the present moment; it is not something that can be reached by the ears or the eyes."
East Lin Ode:
In recent years, all matters have become demonic; As I grow old, idly adding more white hairs. When the Way prevails, the Emperor’s edicts need not be proclaimed;
In times of peace, there is no need to sing songs of the Great Peace.
Yunmen’s Verse:
Do not speak of dreams before a fool; One must seek the seam upon a lump of raw iron. Though I explain it clearly, you act as if deaf;
You do nothing but engage in idle brawling on the outside.

Case: National Teacher Wuye said, "If even a single hair’s breadth of conceptual thought regarding ordinary or sage is not exhausted, one cannot avoid entering the womb of a donkey or the belly of a horse.
Master Baiyun Cheng said, "Even if every last trace of conceptual thought regarding ordinary or sage were purified away, one would still not avoid entering the womb of a donkey."
He went into the belly of a horse.
Donglin’s verse says:
"A single path as straight as a string; heart and hand are even more intimate. When the arrow pierces the shadow of the red sun, only then is one an archer who shoots the eagle."
Yunmen’s Verse:
To shift the body is not to shift the steps; to shift the steps is not to shift the body. The golden lion has run away; the jade qilin is captured.
[This refers to] citing Lingyun’s realization of the Way upon seeing peach blossoms.
Donglin’s Verse:
The peach blossoms seek the sword-wielder; Without speaking, they smile at the spring breeze. With white hair, he has not yet returned; His home lies east of Haimen.
Yunmen’s Verse:
It is commonly said that one awakens to the Way upon seeing peach blossoms; I do not know whether these words are true or false.
Vast and boundless is the universe, filled with countless people—among them all, which man can truly be called a great hero?
Case: Xuansha said, "It is accurate; it is most accurate. I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate.
Donglin’s verse says:
"I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have still not reached the ultimate. How cutting was Xuansha’s word! Behold the peach blossoms by the roadside."
"Red. It is all the blood from the eyes of those separated from their loved ones.
Yunmen’s Verse: "The Ghost Gate is shattered; The sun is at its zenith. One arrow hits the red heart; Throughout the great earth, there is not an inch of soil."

The Master said, "Your servant has crossed the river fourteen times; it was like walking upon level ground. The Emperor said, "I have heard that in antiquity there were those who crossed by floating their bamboo hats."

it turned out to be an Arhat. Upon reaching Tiantai, they encountered a swollen river that could not be crossed. After standing with his staff planted for a long time, the strange monk used his bamboo hat as a boat, climbed upon it, and floated away.
Pointing at him, Huangbo cursed, saying: 'You self-satisfied fellow! Had I known you earlier, I would certainly have beaten you until your bones were broken.'"
The Emperor remarked, "A monk of extraordinary caliber indeed! His spiritual power is so fierce and sharp that it is beyond my reach.
The Master said, "Under the School of our Tradition, we do not value supernatural powers; we value only the clarity of the eye. The Emperor said, "One must indeed be like this to succeed.
Generally speaking, I do not believe in such matters as illusions and marvels. The Master said, "Your Majesty’s sagely wisdom is profoundly clear and penetrating."
[The Emperor] saw it thus. The至尊 (Supreme Honored One) said, "Do not stay for several more days. The Master said, "Your servant has already selected the twenty-fifth day to enter the monastery.
The至尊 said, "Wherever you go, the conditions are ripe. The Master said, "I am deeply moved by Your Majesty’s sacred grace.
The至尊 said, "Every day I recite the *Śūraṅgama-sūtra*, the *Samādhirāja-sūtra*, and Confucian texts; all day long I remain in a state of tranquil detachment, without a single [distraction]."

[The Emperor] said, “This clearly shows that Your Majesty’s sacred learning is renewed daily. Generally speaking, when one reads the scriptures and unrolls the scrolls, one is immediately face-to-face with the ancients;
it truly does not depend on reading much. The Sovereign said, “I constantly keep this in mind, remaining ever-attentive to it.
The Master said, “Your Majesty comes from the stage of a Bodhisattva; therefore, your power of aspiration is firm and steadfast. However, as for all words...”
Whether in silence, movement, or stillness, simply maintain right mindfulness in the present; do not give rise to a second thought.
It is just as when I, your subject, am now facing Your Majesty: how could I know the subtle flow of Your Majesty’s mind?
This very subtle flow is what is called the "stealing mind. If this stealing mind is absent, a second thought will naturally not arise. —The Most Honored One.
The Emperor said, "I have gained this single thought from the Chan Master; it is not without benefit.
The Master said, "In the past, when Zen Master Xuefeng left the mountain to visit Chan Master Lingguang of Jingyan in Xiuzhou, he encountered Lingguang’s passing.
Xuefeng asked his disciples, 'When Lingguang was alive, how did he instruct his students? The disciples replied, 'He would simply say, "Do not give rise [to thoughts]."'"
The Second Thought. His Holiness said, "This one phrase can be used to instruct people on how to apply themselves to practice.

The Master said, "What is called 'striking the head of a stone man with a staff'—*bò bò*—is to discuss the actual reality. His Holiness said, "What karmic conditions are there? Please cite another or two cases.
The Master said, "In the past, the practitioner Zhizai went to visit Caoshan. Caoshan asked, 'What is paper?'"
Regarding the matter of the paper robe: Daowu said, "Once the single fur cloak is hung upon the body, all ten thousand dharmas are as they are.
Yunmen asked, "What is the function beneath the paper robe? Daowu stepped forward, responded with an "Amen," and immediately took it off.
Yunmen said, "You only know how to go like that; you do not know how to come back like this. Daowu suddenly opened his eyes and asked, "The one spiritual true nature does not..."
"Suppose at the time of being in the womb, how would it be? Caoshan said, "It is not yet wondrous. The practitioner asked, "What is wondrous?

Caoshan said, "Do not borrow from others. The practitioner, having paid his respects, departed once more. Caoshan then composed a verse, which says: "The nature of awakening is perfectly luminous, the formless body;
Do not mistakenly draw near or distance yourself through intellectual views. If thoughts differ, you obscure the profound essence; If the mind errs, it deviates from the source."
Adjacent to the Way, the emotional attachments to the myriad dharmas sink into the realm before one; with manifold modes of discernment, one loses one's original truth.
If one fully understands and realizes these words, one is clearly the person of old, free from affairs. The Most Honored One said: "When practicing Chan, one arrives at this point."
Only then can one begin to experience its fruition. The Master said: "The ancients were without interruption in every thought-moment;

only then did they reach this ground of ultimate reality. One does not dare to sit for long. The Emperor took his leave, thanking him for his grace and descending from the hall. On the fifth day of the third month, the Shouhuang Emperor sent a written inquiry, saying:
"Every day I do nothing but sit like a block. What else can I possibly do? I trouble you, Master, to write back to me. The Master [responded].
He replied, "I respectfully receive Your Majesty’s inquiry. Each day I do nothing more than sit like a block of wood; what else could I possibly accomplish?
Your Majesty need only look into this very state of sitting like a block of wood and inquire: 'What is this? If there is anything else, it is merely a superfluous dharma."
Therefore, Master Nantaisi had a verse that says: "Sitting quietly on South Terrace for a single stick of incense, / Throughout the entire day, he remains unmoving and forgets all myriad concerns.
/ This is not merely to stifle the mind and eliminate delusive thoughts; / It is entirely because there is nothing to be pondered. This is where the ancient masters set foot upon solid ground.
Your Majesty has realized this through personal verification; it is not merely a matter of sitting like a block of wood, but extends to all four modes of deportment.
The Dharma of peace and happiness is always spontaneously present for enjoyment. Respectfully submitted. On the sixth day of the fourth month, the Emperor-in-Waiting (Shouhuang) questioned me:
"Lately I have come to realize that there is not much to the Buddha-dharma. To summarize it in a single phrase: it is simply the absence of deluded thoughts.
If deluded thoughts arise, then there is birth and cessation. I do not know whether this statement is correct. The Master replied: "I respectfully receive [Your Majesty’s instruction]..."
Your Majesty’s recent realization that there is not much more to the Buddha-dharma than this is a clear manifestation of Your Majesty’s penetrating insight.

What Your Majesty has called “summarizing it in a single phrase” is simply this: to have no deluded thoughts. If deluded thoughts arise, then there is birth and cessation; this is truly as Your Majesty intends.

Furthermore, if one can reach the state where even delusion and forgetfulness, arising and ceasing, are transcended, then heaven and earth will be revealed in their nakedness, and one’s application of wisdom will be free and unimpeded in all directions.
This is precisely the samādhi of enjoyment. Respectfully submitted.
*Recorded Sayings of Ancient Honored Masters*, Volume 48 (End).
